findings.claim: Element Caching is a merged core feature since 3.32: Performance tab 'Element Cache' option `elementor_element_cache_ttl` (default '24' hours; values disable/1/6/12/24/72/168/336...), output stored in post meta `_elementor_element_cache`, per-widget Advanced > Cache Settings control `_element_cache` ('' Default, 'yes' = Inactive, 'no' = Active); it only reduces server render time on uncached requests and is the most-cited cause of stale widget output, so keep the default TTL but mark booking/filter/cart/language widgets Inactive and rely on the page cache.
findings.detail: 4.3.5 modules/element-cache/module.php (TTL select, `std` '24'); core/base/document.php `CACHE_META_KEY = '_elementor_element_cache'`; includes/base/element-base.php `should_render_shortcode()`: an element is NOT cached when `_element_cache === 'yes'`, when `is_dynamic_content()` is true, when filter `elementor/element/is_dynamic_content` returns true, or when any setting carries a `__dynamic__` tag. Help (2026-09-15): Container, Grid Container, Off Canvas, Section, Column, Inner Section are always cached and cannot be changed; 'Element Caching cannot be used on elements that contain dynamic tags or any other type of dynamic information, such as shortcodes'. Dev update 3.32: merged and active by default; 'Websites facing issues... clear cache from Elementor > Tools or disable... Performance tab'; longer TTL recommended for rarely-updated sites. Elementor blog: internal tests 3.18 vs 3.22 showed 50% TTFB and 40% LCP improvement. WP Rocket doc: 'Element Cache may cause widgets to show incorrect content. You can disable it as WP Rocket handles full-page caching.' Help 'My changes do not appear online' lists Element Caching as a cause. Observed: pallada disabled it (score 86); limnoupolis/onar default; cretaforums/kand/marakaki 24 h.
findings.breaks_when: Third-party widgets that render per-visitor/time-based output in PHP without declaring dynamic (FacetWP publicly marks Elementor Element Caching incompatible); shortcodes typed in Text Editor/Shortcode widgets; server-rendered Polylang/WPML language switcher or translated strings in cached widgets; YITH/Woo Bookings availability or price widgets; forum/recent-activity widgets -> stale up to the TTL; content edited outside Elementor (ACF via dynamic tags is excluded automatically).
findings.how_to_apply: Settings > Performance > Element Cache = 1 Day (1 Week on brochure sites); in the editor set Advanced > Cache Settings = Inactive on JetSmartFilters, booking forms/calendars, WooCommerce cart/mini-cart, language switcher, forum widgets; run Tools > Clear Files & Data after bulk edits (Novamira `elementor-clear-document-cache` purges per document). Changing the TTL option itself purges all Elementor CSS files (core/files/manager.php hook `update_option_elementor_element_cache_ttl`).
findings.how_to_verify: TTFB with page cache bypassed: `curl -o /dev/null -w '%{time_starttransfer}' 'URL?nocache=1'` before/after; `wp post meta get <id> _elementor_element_cache` populated after first view; change a booking price/availability and reload logged-out -> updated; switch language -> correct language; WP Rocket/LiteSpeed cache still purges on Elementor save.
findings.correction: Code confirms: modules/element-cache/module.php `std` '24' with options disable/1/6/12/24/72/168/336/720/8760; core/base/document.php `print_elements()` treats the cache as active whenever the option is not literally 'disable' (`'disable' !== get_option('elementor_element_cache_ttl', '')`), and `set_document_cache()` falls back to 24 h when the option is empty or non-numeric, so a site that never saved the Performance tab IS caching for 24 h. element-base.php `should_render_shortcode()` bypasses the cache when `_element_cache === 'yes'`, `is_dynamic_content()`, the `elementor/element/is_dynamic_content` filter, or any `__dynamic__` setting. Correction: Elementor's own help page (Last Update September 15, 2026) still says 'the feature is inactive by default' and calls it 'an experimental feature', which is stale copy from 3.2x; the plugin must not quote that page for defaults. Also note: WP Rocket's doc simply says to deactivate Element Cache when WP Rocket is active, so the plugin should expose 'disable' as a legitimate choice on page-cached sites rather than only 'keep default'. Risk stays medium.

findings.claim: `e_optimized_markup` ('Optimized Markup', Stable, tag Performance) removes the `.elementor-widget-container` wrapper and other tags; in 4.3.5 it is still default Inactive for existing sites (default Active only for installs >= 3.30.0; the 3.32 attempt to force it on everywhere was reverted), so legacy sites run the heavier DOM; enabling it is a small DOM win that breaks custom CSS/JS and add-ons targeting the old wrappers.
findings.detail: core/experiments/manager.php 4.3.5: description 'Reduce the DOM size by eliminating HTML tags in various elements and widgets. This experiment includes markup changes so it might require updating custom CSS/JS code and cause compatibility issues with third party plugins', `release_status` stable, `default` inactive, `new_site.default_active` true with `minimum_installation_version` 3.30.0. includes/base/widget-base.php switches the controls stack to 'common-optimized' and `has_widget_inner_wrapper()` false; widgets that keep/branch on the wrapper: counter, divider, image-box, image-gallery, progress, shortcode, video, text-path, nested-tabs, nested-accordion, floating buttons/bars, button trait, column `space_between_widgets`. Dev update 3.32: 'UPDATE: The Optimized Markup change was reverted.' Elementor help: sections -> containers cut a 5-widget block from 37 to 23 divs; blog: Flexbox container output −39%, Grid −85% vs sections. Observed: 9/10 sites on; onar (4.2.3, Premium Addons, FA4 shim, score 44) off.
findings.breaks_when: Theme/child CSS, Custom CSS or Custom Code selecting `.elementor-widget-container` (common in agency style overrides), add-on widgets (Premium Addons, older Dynamic.ooo) that assume the wrapper or `data-settings` placement (3.26.2 changelog fixed one such third-party conflict), custom nested tabs/accordion styling.
findings.how_to_apply: Settings > Features > Optimized Markup = Active (option `elementor_experiment-e_optimized_markup` = active). First grep theme, Custom CSS and Custom Code for `elementor-widget-container`; Tools > Clear Files & Data; purge page cache; screenshot key templates. Keep Active on new builds (default for new installs).
findings.how_to_verify: `document.querySelectorAll('.elementor-widget-container').length` -> 0 except for the listed widgets; Lighthouse 'Avoid an excessive DOM size' node count before/after; visual diff of header, footer, hero, forms, tabs at 390 px and 1366 px.

findings.claim: `e_font_icon_svg` ('Inline Font Icons', Stable) stops loading Font Awesome (all.min.css 59 KB + fa-solid-900.woff2 78 KB) and eicons (CSS 22 KB + eicons.woff2 108 KB) by inlining SVG, but it is default Active only for installs >= 3.17.0, and `elementor_load_fa4_shim` = yes re-adds v4-shims (26.7 KB CSS + 15 KB JS) plus a 78 KB FA webfont even when the feature is on, as observed on onar, staging and voreniahorizon.
findings.detail: core/experiments/manager.php: e_font_icon_svg stable, `new_site.default_active` true, `minimum_installation_version` 3.17.0; includes/frontend.php enqueues `elementor-icons` only if the feature is inactive (or in preview); includes/managers/icons.php `LOAD_FA4_SHIM_OPTION_KEY = 'elementor_load_fa4_shim'` -> `enqueue_shim()` (v4-shims css/js). Help 'Inline Font Icons' (2024-03-07): renders SVG inline, no extra requests, does not convert Font Awesome Pro kit icons. Help 'Optimize speed': FA loads per page only for used families (`elementor-icons-fa-solid|regular|brands`) with filters to deregister FA and eicons. Perfmatters recommends Inline Font Icons to fix the 'Ensure text remains visible during webfont load' warning caused by eicons. Observed from public HTML: pallada, limnoupolis, cretaforums, voreniahorizon all report `e_font_icon_svg:true`, yet onar loads fa-solid-900.woff2 (78 KB) and a standalone Font Awesome plugin, voreniahorizon and staging load font-awesome with FA4 shim on.
findings.breaks_when: Content still uses Font Awesome 4 names (`fa fa-*`) -> icons disappear when the shim is turned off; FA Pro Kit users not converted; third-party add-ons that enqueue their own FA keep loading it; custom CSS that styles `i` tags with `color`/`font-size` instead of `svg` fill/width.
findings.how_to_apply: Settings > Features > Inline Font Icons = Active; Settings > Advanced > Load Font Awesome 4 Support = No only after `grep -R 'fa fa-'` over post content and Elementor meta finds nothing (the draft debloat script already checks); deactivate standalone Font Awesome plugins if only Elementor icons are used; for add-on packs, use their own 'load Font Awesome' switch.
findings.how_to_verify: Network: no requests to `/elementor/assets/lib/font-awesome/`, `/eicons/`, `v4-shims`; Lighthouse 'Ensure text remains visible during webfont load' has no eicons/fa entries; Playwright crawl: count `i.fa, i.fas, i.eicon-*` with zero rendered width -> 0; screenshot icon lists, social icons and menu arrows.
sources: https://pallada.gr/ https://limnoupolis.gr/ https://cretaforums.gr/ https://voreniahorizon.gr/ (public HTML experimentalFeatures)

findings.claim: Elementor's `elementor_font_display` option defaults to 'auto' (the Advanced tab 'Google Fonts Load' recommends Swap) and 7 of 9 audited homepages fail Lighthouse's font-display audit; set Swap, use 'Load Google Fonts Locally' (`elementor_local_google_fonts`, default '0' since 3.32.1), cap at 2 families and the weights used, and keep Greek coverage by relying on Google's subset files or Greek+Latin custom .woff2.
findings.detail: includes/fonts.php: `get_option('elementor_font_display','auto')` and `elementor_google_font` (1 Enable / 0 Disable); core/files/fonts/google-font.php: `elementor_local_google_fonts` default '0', downloaded set tracked in `_elementor_local_google_fonts`, files under /wp-content/uploads/elementor/google-fonts/, re-downloaded after cache clear (help, 2026-01-20: optional and Disabled by default since 3.32.1). Help 'Choose a loading method' (2026-01-20): Default/Blocking/Swap/Fallback/Optional; settings.php desc 'Recommended: Swap'. Observed Lighthouse: font_display_fail = 1 on cretaforums, pallada, voreniahorizon, fagitiotiszois, platonos; onar loads 10 Google font files (~360 KB, 5 families) plus a custom icon font; platonos 6 files/3 families (~276 KB); fast sites use 2 families. Perfmatters: disable Elementor Google Fonts with `add_filter('elementor/frontend/print_google_fonts','__return_false')`; Pro custom fonts font-display via `elementor_pro/custom_fonts/font_display` filter then Regenerate CSS. The 'Use Variable Fonts' help (2026-10-01) documents variable font upload (one file for all weights, width/weight axes).
findings.breaks_when: Latin-only self-hosted .woff2 replaces Google's Greek subset -> Greek text falls back to a system font; `elementor_google_font` disabled without the same families as Custom Fonts -> whole site in fallback fonts; 'Optional' on slow 4G -> brand font never shown; Elementor local fonts + Perfmatters local fonts both on -> duplicate downloads.
findings.how_to_apply: Settings > Advanced > Google Fonts Load = Swap; Settings > Performance > Load Google Fonts Locally = Enable, then Tools > Clear Files & Data once (first load downloads); Site Settings > Global Fonts: <= 2 families, only used weights (or one variable font per family); custom fonts: upload Greek+Latin .woff2 (check glyph coverage with fontTools before upload); use either Elementor's or Perfmatters' local-fonts feature, not both.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse font-display audit passes; Network shows <= ~6 woff2 totalling <= ~250 KB from the own domain; screenshot a Greek and a Latin heading at 390 px (both in brand font); `curl` the generated google-fonts CSS and confirm `font-display:swap` and a `greek` unicode-range block for each family.
findings.correction: Defaults confirmed (includes/fonts.php:1881 `get_option('elementor_font_display','auto')`; google-font.php `get_option('elementor_local_google_fonts','0')`; help: 'Starting with Elementor version 3.32.1 ... default setting was switched to Disabled'). Two corrections: (1) 'only the weights used' cannot be enforced through Elementor's Google Fonts path: includes/frontend.php `get_stable_google_fonts_url()` always requests every variant `:100,100italic,...,900,900italic` for each family on the legacy CSS v1 API, so the @font-face CSS always declares 18 variants (browsers download only the ones used, but Load Google Fonts Locally downloads every file to uploads/elementor/google-fonts/). Weight capping only works with Custom Fonts or a variable font upload. (2) Greek handling is now verified: the request adds `&subset=greek` only when `get_locale()` is exactly 'el' (map `'el' => 'greek'`, filterable via `elementor/frontend/google_font_subsets`); the CSS is fetched with a Chrome/114 User-Agent (`UA_STRING`), so Google returns woff2 with per-subset `unicode-range` blocks, and `download_fonts()` preg-matches every `url()` and downloads/rewrites each one, so Greek subset files survive local hosting. On WPML/Polylang sites whose default locale is en_US the subset hint is absent, but the unicode-range blocks still cover Greek. Risk stays low.

findings.claim: Two Performance-tab features are ON by default and overlap with cache plugins: `elementor_optimized_image_loading` (default '1') disables WordPress native lazy-loading, puts `fetchpriority="high"` on the first large image and `loading="lazy"` on the rest; `elementor_lazy_load_background_images` (default '1') hides CSS backgrounds of top-level containers from the 2nd (mobile)/3rd/4th onwards with `background-image:none !important` until an IntersectionObserver fires. Run exactly one lazy-loader; WP Rocket explicitly says to disable both (and Element Cache) when it is active, and LiteSpeed's image lazy-load raised CLS 0 -> 0.107 on staging.
findings.detail: modules/image-loading-optimization/module.php: `add_filter('wp_lazy_loading_enabled','__return_false')`, `stop_core_fetchpriority_high_logic`, `omit_threshold = 3`, attributes added only to images with width+height. modules/lazyload/module.php: inline CSS `.e-con.e-parent:nth-of-type(n+4):not(.e-lazyloaded):not(.e-no-lazyload)` (desktop), n+3 (tablet), n+2 (mobile) with `background-image: none !important`, plus an inline IntersectionObserver script; opt-out class `e-no-lazyload`. Help 'Optimized Image Loading' (2026-09-25): 'typically improves page loading times by 5-10%', not applied above the fold; help 'Lazy loading': all background images except the first. WP Rocket doc: deactivate Optimized Image Loading, Lazy Load Background Images, Element Cache because its 'Optimize critical images' cannot exclude from third-party lazyload and it already lazy-loads CSS backgrounds. Perfmatters: 'we've seen Elementor improperly add fetch on images below the fold' -> turn off Optimize Image Loading; Perfmatters lazy CSS backgrounds via class `perfmatters-lazy-css-bg` on the Elementor container. LiteSpeed docs: 'Add Missing Sizes' and 'Responsive Placeholder' reduce layout shift but only work with Lazy Load Images ON; the agency's staging test showed CLS 0.107 with LiteSpeed lazy images.
findings.breaks_when: Hero is a background image on the 2nd+ top-level container on mobile -> hidden until JS, LCP regresses; two lazy-loaders on the same img -> `loading=lazy` or placeholder on the LCP image, CLS from placeholders without dimensions; Elementor fetchpriority on a below-fold image -> wasted bandwidth; cache plugin's 'critical images' preload fights Elementor's lazy attributes.
findings.how_to_apply: Pick one: (a) keep Elementor's two features and turn OFF the cache plugin's image lazy-load (LiteSpeed Media > Lazy Load Images OFF; WP Rocket LazyLoad images off; Perfmatters Lazy Loading off), or (b) use WP Rocket/Perfmatters/FlyingPress lazy-load and set both Elementor options to Disable. Always: hero as Image widget with Lazy Load = No and explicit dimensions (or `fetchpriority=high`), add CSS class `e-no-lazyload` to any above-fold container with a background image; if LiteSpeed lazy stays on, enable Media > Responsive Placeholder + Add Missing Sizes and exclude the hero via Lazy Load Image Excludes.
findings.how_to_verify: View source: LCP `` has `fetchpriority="high"` and no `loading="lazy"`, and only one `fetchpriority="high"` per page; either no `background-image: none !important` block or the hero container carries `e-no-lazyload`; Lighthouse CLS <= 0.02 and no 'Largest Contentful Paint image was lazily loaded' warning; Playwright screenshot at DOMContentLoaded shows the hero background.
findings.correction: The background lazy-load thresholds are viewport-HEIGHT media queries, not device breakpoints: default `.e-con.e-parent:nth-of-type(n+4)`, `@media (max-height:1024px)` -> n+3, `@media (max-height:640px)` -> n+2, all `:not(.e-lazyloaded):not(.e-no-lazyload)`, observer rootMargin 200px. Lighthouse/PSI mobile emulates 412x823 (confirmed in the local runs' configSettings.screenEmulation), so in PSI the 3rd top-level container onwards is hidden, not the 2nd; a hero in the 2nd container only disappears on phones <= 640 px tall (landscape, small devices). Also sharpen the image half: the module only rewrites `` tags passing through `the_content`/`wp_content_img_tag` that already carry width AND height, treats the first 3 such images as in-viewport (omit_threshold 3), and adds a single `fetchpriority="high"` only when width*height >= 50,000 px (filter `elementor/image-loading-optimization/min_priority_img_pixels`); CSS backgrounds are untouched. So an Image widget without dimensions or a hero rendered by a Theme Builder header gets no fetchpriority. WP Rocket's advice confirmed verbatim; LiteSpeed 'Add Missing Sizes ... works only when Lazy Load Images is ON' and 'Responsive Placeholder ... when the images have width and height attributes' confirmed; Perfmatters: 'we've seen Elementor improperly add fetch on images below the fold'. Risk stays medium.

findings.claim: The v4 Atomic Editor is the only structural weight reduction: Elementor states Atomic Elements 'use pure HTML tags that render without additional wrapper layers' and share CSS via Global Classes; the one controlled v3-vs-v4 comparison found (third-party, 2026-09-23) measured −65–67% DOM nodes, −85–89% CSS bytes, LCP −0.4–0.7 s, JS −5%, PageSpeed +16–17; v4 is default-on only for installs created on >= 4.0.0 (`e_opt_in_v4` and `e_atomic_elements` are hidden experiments, default inactive otherwise), and 4.3.x carries two open server-side costs (#37016 Cache_Validity option bloat, #36205 editor request bursts).
findings.detail: 4.0 beta discussion (2026-03-16): new installs start with Atomic Elements, Variables, Classes, Components on; existing sites unchanged; toggle at WP Admin > Elementor > Editor > Settings > Atomic Editor; FAQ: 'pure HTML tags... without additional wrapper layers', gains 'may vary' when mixing v3 and v4. Changelog 4.0.0: 'Updated Atomic Editor status to Stable', 'Enabled Atomic Editor by default for new websites', 'Improved performance and ordering of Global Classes styles on the frontend'; 4.2.0 Grid; 4.3.0 Accordion, Background Video, Default Styles, nav/main tags, nested elements auto-wrapped in Flexbox; 3.33.0 'Replaced the legacy V3 container wrapper with the optimized V4 wrapper'. 4.3.5 source: opt-in.php `e_opt_in_v4` alpha hidden, `new_site` >= 4.0.0 default_active; atomic-widgets/module.php `e_atomic_elements` beta hidden, same new_site rule; atomic CSS compiled to files by Atomic_Styles_Manager/CSS_Files_Manager with Cache_Validity; Interactions depend on assets/lib/motion/motion.min.js (128,346 B raw). snapelement benchmark (same host, WP Rocket, Hello theme, 30 daily PSI runs): homepage DOM 1,847 -> 612, CSS 342 KB -> 47 KB, JS 285 -> 271 KB, TTFB unchanged, INP −8–15 ms; caveat: no third-party scripts. #37016 (open; 4.2.1–4.3.4): Cache_Validity 'local' tree grows one child per rendered post, 3,965 children/767 KB, ~168 array copies, '483 + 456 + 205 = 1,144 ms per uncached render' on a WPML 21-language site; second report 5.56 MB options, 871 ms in enqueue_styles(); workaround cron deleting the options. #36205 (open): editor fires 667–891 requests per load, HTTP 508/500 on shared hosting. Observed: only limnoupolis has `e_atomic_elements:true`; kand reports the atomic runtime unavailable with the experiment OFF. Pro: Atomic Forms (4.0), Loop (4.2), Interactions.
findings.breaks_when: Atomic elements inside v3 Loop/Posts widgets lose styles (#36212 open since 4.1); v3 add-on packs keep their wrappers so mixed pages gain little; large/multilingual sites (WPML, thousands of documents) accumulate Cache_Validity options -> TTFB +0.5–1.1 s on uncached renders; shared hosting -> editor 508s; Core 4.3 with Pro < 4.3 (version-coupling finding).
findings.how_to_apply: Build mode for new sites: install Elementor >= 4.3.5 + Pro >= 4.3.2 fresh so v4 defaults on; build with Flexbox/Div Block/Heading/Paragraph/Image/Button/Atomic Accordion/Tabs/Form/Loop; use Global Classes (limit 1000) for repeated styles; no v3 add-on packs; Interactions only below the fold. Existing sites: do not flip `e_atomic_elements` on production; rebuild one template on staging and measure. Monitor `wp option list --search='elementor_atomic*'` (or `SELECT option_name, LENGTH(option_value)` for Cache_Validity options) on WPML/large sites until #37016 is fixed.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse DOM size, CSS bytes and LCP for a v3 page vs its v4 rebuild with identical images; page source `elementorFrontendConfig.experimentalFeatures` shows `e_atomic_elements:true`; editor opens in < 10 s on the target host; option sizes stable month over month; styles intact inside loops.

findings.claim: Exact 4.3.5 core experiment inventory (option key `elementor_experiment-<name>` = active|inactive|default): e_font_icon_svg (stable; new installs >= 3.17 active), additional_custom_breakpoints (stable, active), container (stable, inactive; new >= 3.16 active; deactivation hides content), e_optimized_markup (stable, inactive; new >= 3.30 active), e_optimized_css_files (alpha, inactive), nested-elements (stable, active, hidden), e_atomic_elements (beta, hidden, inactive; new >= 4.0 active), e_opt_in_v4 (alpha, hidden; new >= 4.0 active), landing-pages (beta, active), import-export-customization (beta, active, hidden, immutable), markdown_rendering (alpha, inactive, 4.1.0); e_assets_manager and e_page_audit are hidden editor-side experiments with no front-end effect; Pro flags seen live on 4.3.4 sites: e_pro_atomic_form, e_pro_collection_loop, mega-menu, theme_builder_v2 (Pro defaults not verifiable, closed source).
findings.detail: core/experiments/manager.php 4.3.5 `OPTION_PREFIX = 'elementor_experiment-'`, states default/active/inactive, release statuses dev/alpha/beta/stable, `hidden` flag, `new_site.minimum_installation_version` logic; add_default_features() lists the five core ones; modules/nested-elements/module.php (stable, active, hidden); modules/atomic-widgets (e_atomic_elements, e_list/e_icon_button/e_accordion/e_svg_library dev hidden), opt-in.php (e_opt_in_v4); modules/assets-manager/module.php `e_assets_manager` 'Dynamic Assets Management' dev hidden inactive: dequeues editor/preview assets only (hooks elementor/editor|preview/after_enqueue_*); modules/audits/module.php `e_page_audit` beta hidden inactive: editor audit panel ('editor-audits' app; 4.4.0 PRs still building its UI); modules/markdown-render `markdown_rendering`; app/app.php import-export-customization (mutable false) and e_onboarding; modules/landing-pages. Experiments no longer present in 4.3.5 (merged/removed): e_optimized_assets_loading, e_optimized_css_loading, e_element_cache, e_lazyload, e_image_loading_optimization. Help 'Activate Elementor experimental features' (2026-09-15): Features tab, statuses, 'Some Features are activated by default for NEW sites only', 'Elementor acts as if the feature has never existed' when deactivated. Live public HTML (`elementorFrontendConfig.experimentalFeatures`) on pallada 4.3.4: e_font_icon_svg, additional_custom_breakpoints, container, e_optimized_markup, nested-elements, import-export-customization, e_pro_atomic_form, e_pro_collection_loop, mega-menu all true; limnoupolis 4.3.5 adds theme_builder_v2, hello-theme-header-footer, e_atomic_elements, e_opt_in_v4.
findings.breaks_when: Deactivating `container`, `nested-elements` or `e_atomic_elements` on a site that used them -> blank front end ('My changes do not appear online' doc warning); toggling hidden dev experiments via the option is unsupported; e_assets_manager/e_page_audit do nothing for visitors.
findings.how_to_apply: Audit: read `elementorFrontendConfig.experimentalFeatures` from the public HTML (no login needed) and `wp option list --search='elementor_experiment-*'`; change via Settings > Features or `wp option update elementor_experiment-<name> active|inactive`; never toggle e_assets_manager/e_page_audit for performance; treat Pro experiments as read-only unless a Pro doc says otherwise.
findings.how_to_verify: After purge, page source `experimentalFeatures` JSON reflects the change; `wp option get elementor_experiment-<name>`; home + 2 inner pages render identically in screenshots.

https://pallada.gr/ https://limnoupolis.gr/ https://cretaforums.gr/ https://voreniahorizon.gr/ (public HTML experimentalFeatures)

findings.claim: Elementor deletes every file in uploads/elementor/css/ on `activated_plugin`, `deactivated_plugin`, `switch_theme`, element-cache TTL change and on every `upgrader_process_complete` — which WordPress also fires on mere update checks and translation updates — so warm page caches/CDNs serve HTML that references deleted CSS and visitors get unstyled pages (#35983 open, 'We are investigating', reproduced on 4.3.2; #32226 race leaves stylesheets missing on first load); the alpha experiment `e_optimized_css_files` (default inactive, off on all 10 sites) is where 4.3.5 gates the fix (skip non-genuine upgrader events, one purge per request, `elementor/files/base_dir|base_url` filters).
findings.detail: core/files/manager.php 4.3.5: `register_site_changed_hooks()` (the five hooks), `on_upgrader_process_complete()` returns early only `if ( is_optimized_css_files_active() && ! is_genuine_update( $hook_extra ) )`; `clear_cache()` deduped per request only when active; experiment description 'Keeps external CSS files available and consistent for sites behind page caching or a CDN', RELEASE_STATUS_ALPHA; core/files/base.php adds `elementor/files/base_dir` and `elementor/files/base_url` filters ('@since 4.4.0', only when active). Related changelog: Pro 4.3.0 'Page-specific CSS may be missing on the first visit after automatic CSS cleanup'; core 4.3.2 'Page styles may not load correctly after being regenerated'; 4.3.4 'Widget styles can be missing when rendered inside saved Templates'; #37217 (4.2.4): Image Carousel only inside a template renders without swiper/e-swiper CSS, workaround `wp_enqueue_style('swiper'); wp_enqueue_style('e-swiper');`. #35983: handler chain ended in a LiteSpeed purge_all; regeneration is lazy (needs an uncached PHP render), CDN can cache 404s; `wp elementor flush-css --regenerate` rebuilds post CSS only; internal print method protects post CSS but not shared files. #32226: race between two near-simultaneous requests after regeneration (prefetch) leaves `_elementor_css` meta empty -> `<link>` not enqueued; worse with object cache.
findings.breaks_when: Page cache/CDN TTL longer than the gap between a purge (any plugin/theme update, update check, translation update) and the next uncached render; object cache without meta refresh; carousels/slides only inside Theme Builder/Loop/saved templates; cache plugins that do not hook Elementor's purge.
findings.how_to_apply: Safe path: after any plugin/theme/translation update run Tools > Clear Files & Data (or `wp elementor flush-css`) and then purge page cache + CDN in that order; automate with a post-update hook and an uptime check that fetches one post-*.css. Staging test: Settings > Features > Optimized CSS Files = Active and confirm uploads/elementor/css survives an update check. For template-only carousels enqueue swiper/e-swiper from the child theme. Keep CSS Print Method external.
findings.how_to_verify: `ls wp-content/uploads/elementor/css | wc -l` before/after `wp cron event run wp_update_plugins` and a translation update; fetch cached pages logged-out and `curl -I` every `uploads/elementor/css/*.css` -> 200; Playwright screenshots of header/footer after updates; no 404s for /uploads/elementor/css/ in server logs.

findings.claim: Per-widget cost in 4.3 (gzip, measured on the agency's sites and the 4.3.5 tree): Swiper 38 KB JS + 4–5 KB CSS (Image/Loop/Media/Testimonial Carousel, Slides, Nested Carousel, container background slideshow); Lottie 60 KB JS + the JSON per animation (Pro); Google Maps widget is a third-party iframe (already `loading="lazy"`) that costs ~1 MB when visible; Video widget loads the YouTube/Vimeo player unless its 'Lazy Load' toggle is on (thumbnail until click); lightbox 27 KB chunk + dialog 4 KB whenever an image/gallery links to media with the global lightbox on; Nested Tabs 13 KB; Counter 7.5 KB + jQuery numerator; WP Menu/Mega Menu smartmenus 7 KB + mega-menu CSS 2.7 KB; Pro Form 5.4 KB chunk plus reCAPTCHA if enabled; popups render on every page their conditions match. Each has a lighter alternative.
findings.detail: Sizes from GETs on pallada.gr and Lighthouse network items (swiper.min.js 38,152 B gz; lottie.min.js 60,581 B gz / 252,588 raw; chunks/lightbox-lightbox.min.js 27–28 KB; chunks/nested-tabs.min.js 13–14 KB; chunks/counter.min.js 7.2–7.5 KB; chunks/video.min.js 8–9 KB; jquery.smartmenus 6,867 B; widget-mega-menu.min.css 2,712 B; Pro form bundle 5,432 B). Source: includes/widgets/google-maps.php outputs `<iframe loading="lazy"`; includes/widgets/video.php has the `lazy_load` control; includes/widgets/counter.php depends on jquery-numerator; image-carousel.php depends on swiper + `e-swiper`/`widget-image-carousel` CSS; core/kits settings-lightbox.php `global_image_lightbox`. Help Video widget (2026-09-15): Lazy Load 'load the video widget data only after the visitor scrolls' / 'only once someone hits the play button'; self-hosted Preload = Meta/Auto/None. Help Lottie (2026-09-15): 'toggle Lazy Load on... only load when it becomes visible'. Help Optimize speed: 'external scripts, for example Google Maps, Facebook share count, Avatar images, considerably slows down a page load'. Help Popups: conditions decide where the popup is used. Perfmatters: iframe/video lazy-load and 'YouTube Preview Thumbnails' work with Elementor Atomic YouTube elements and legacy Video widgets (their test: −58% page size). Observed: limnoupolis has 84 video widgets and its home loads lightbox + nested-tabs + counter chunks; voreniahorizon's home also loads Dynamic.ooo plyr 37 KB + velocity 17 KB + tippy 9 KB + popper 8 KB.
findings.breaks_when: Unloading swiper where a carousel exists -> broken slider; global lightbox off -> gallery images open as plain files; lazy video on an autoplaying hero -> black box until click; static map image without a link -> no interactivity; popups with 'On Page Load' triggers on landing pages -> LCP/CLS and consent conflicts.
findings.how_to_apply: Builder rules: hero = Image widget (Lazy Load No, dimensions set) or v4 Image; carousels/sliders/videos/maps/Lottie only below the fold with the widget's Lazy Load on; Site Settings > Lightbox > Image Lightbox off unless galleries; counters replaced by headings with the number; Lottie JSON < 50 KB with Lazy Load; Google Maps below the fold or a static map image linking to Google Maps; popups with tight conditions, no page-load popups on landing pages; Pro Form with honeypot instead of reCAPTCHA where spam allows; Perfmatters 'YouTube Preview Thumbnails' for video-heavy pages.
findings.how_to_verify: Network on the homepage: no swiper.min.js, lottie.min.js, lightbox chunk unless the element is above the fold; Lighthouse 'Third-party usage' lists no maps/youtube before scroll; Playwright click-through: every carousel swipes, lightbox opens, video plays, form submits, popup opens on its trigger.

findings.claim: Cache-plugin CSS features remove Elementor's render-blocking CSS but need Elementor-specific guards: exclude `/wp-content/plugins/elementor/assets/css/` from async/defer/RUCSS and regenerate critical CSS (Elementor's own FOUC guidance, 2026-08-27, which also says turn Cloudflare Rocket Loader off and never use Internal Embedding to fix FOUC); in LiteSpeed, Critical CSS/UCSS/VPI only work with QUIC.cloud, 'CSS Per URL' must stay ON for page builders, 'UCSS Inline' silently disables 'Load CSS Asynchronously', and CSS/JS Combine is discouraged; FlyingPress 'Lazy Render' applies `content-visibility:auto` below the fold automatically and must exclude JS-dependent elements by keyword.
findings.detail: Elementor FOUC doc steps: locate Defer CSS / Load CSS Asynchronously / Remove Unused CSS, add `/wp-content/plugins/elementor/assets/css/` to excluded files, regenerate Critical CSS, Rocket Loader off, enable font preloading, purge; FAQ: Internal Embedding 'can create conflicts with site caching mechanisms and degrade overall performance'. LiteSpeed docs (pageopt): CSS Combine OFF default; Generate UCSS is a QUIC.cloud service used with CSS Combine; 'If UCSS Inline is enabled, the Load CSS Asynchronously setting is ignored and treated as OFF'; 'Load CSS Asynchronously uses the QUIC.cloud Page Optimization service... If you choose not to use QUIC.cloud services, CSS will not load asynchronously'; CSS Per URL ON: setting OFF 'may result in incorrect CSS styling if your site uses a page builder'; Font Display Optimization appends font-display; Lazy Load Images OFF default with Responsive Placeholder and Add Missing Sizes for layout shift; Localize Resources for Google/Facebook scripts; Load JS Deferred vs Delayed. WP Rocket: Elementor post CSS excluded from minify; cache purge synchronized with Elementor. FlyingPress Lazy Render (2025-05-21): cloud optimizer picks below-fold elements, `content-visibility: auto`, keyword exclusions (no regex), 'elements which rely heavily on JavaScript may not render properly'. Observed: cretaforums (FlyingPress, internal CSS) 74/LCP 4.4 s; limnoupolis (LiteSpeed with every optimisation off) 27; staging after LiteSpeed lazy images CLS 0.107.
findings.breaks_when: RUCSS/UCSS drop selectors added only by JS (`.elementor-active`, `.e-active`, `.elementor-sticky--active`, `.elementor-popup-modal`, swiper state classes, `.elementor-invisible` reveal) -> broken tabs/menus/popups/sticky until safelisted; async CSS without critical CSS -> FOUC; Combine with Elementor post CSS -> every editor save invalidates the bundle and disk grows; Rocket Loader reorders Elementor JS; LiteSpeed lazy images without dimensions -> CLS.
findings.how_to_apply: LiteSpeed: CSS Minify ON, CSS Combine OFF, Generate UCSS + Load CSS Asynchronously only with QUIC.cloud and CSS Per URL ON, UCSS Selector Allowlist with the Elementor state classes above, Font Display Optimization = Swap, Lazy Load Images OFF (or ON with Responsive Placeholder + Add Missing Sizes), Localize Resources for gtag/fbevents, Load JS Deferred = Deferred. WP Rocket: RUCSS with Elementor safelist, Delay JS one-click Elementor exclusions, its LazyLoad instead of Elementor's. FlyingPress: Remove Unused CSS + Lazy Render with exclusions for popups, menus, forms, booking calendars. Perfmatters Script Manager: unload plugin CSS not used on the page (jQuery UI, booking calendar, WooCommerce on brochure pages).
findings.how_to_verify: WebPageTest filmstrip: no unstyled frame; Lighthouse render-blocking list free of Elementor CSS; click-through script: hover states, dropdown/mega menu, tabs, accordion, popup, sticky header all work with RUCSS/UCSS on; CLS <= 0.02 with lazy images; after an editor save `curl -sI` the combined/UCSS file -> 200.

findings.claim: Elementor's own widgets, fonts and icons load their assets only on pages that use them (official FAQ), so Element Manager's 'Deactivate Unused Elements' mostly declutters the editor; the measurable waste comes from third-party add-on packs (Premium Addons, Dynamic.ooo, JetSmartFilters/JetTabs, EmbedPress, standalone Font Awesome plugins) that enqueue libraries site-wide — e.g. Dynamic.ooo's plyr + velocity + tippy + popper (~72 KB gzip) on voreniahorizon's homepage — and from duplicate plugins (two image optimisers, two popup tools, FA plugin next to Elementor).
findings.detail: Help 'Do unused widgets, fonts, or icons slow down my page?' (2024-01-29): 'Elementor does not load widget-specific assets in pages where the widget is not in use, except for a small amount of basic CSS and Javascript that should not be fragmented... Some third-party plugins may allow disabling of their widgets as they may require actively disabling to prevent them from loading assets even when not in use.' Help 'Element Manager' (2026-01-20): Scan Element Usage, Deactivate Unused Elements (applies to ALL unused even when filtered), warning that disabling used elements 'could even break your site'; option stored via Options::get_disabled_elements (modules/element-manager). Developers 'Scripts & Styles': register assets and let Elementor enqueue dynamically. Pro 3.31: ribbon styles loaded only when used (Elementor trend to conditional CSS). Audit: marakaki has 131 widgets disabled + Perfmatters and only ~13 KB Elementor assets on its home; voreniahorizon add-ons (Dynamic.ooo) load plyr.polyfilled.min.js 37.4 KB, velocity 17.4 KB, tippy 9.4 KB, popper 8 KB; onar runs Premium Addons + PRO, Dynamic.ooo, Font Awesome plugin, FA4 shim.
findings.breaks_when: Deactivating an element still used in a template, popup or loop item -> blank area (verify templates after the usage scan); unloading add-on CSS/JS via Script Manager on a page that opens a modal/filter using it; removing the FA plugin while a non-Elementor part of the theme uses it.
findings.how_to_apply: Element Manager > Scan Element Usage > Deactivate Unused Elements, then click through templates; in add-on packs disable unused widgets in their own module settings (Premium Addons > Elements, Dynamic.ooo > Features, JetPlugins > Widgets/Skins); replace a lone add-on widget with a core/v4 equivalent and deactivate the pack; Perfmatters Script Manager with regex for the pack's handles on pages that do not use it; one image optimiser, one popup tool, no FA plugin.
findings.how_to_verify: Network filtered by `/plugins/<pack>/` on home, an inner page and a booking page before/after; Lighthouse 'Reduce unused CSS/JS' entries for the pack gone; visual click-through of every page that uses the pack's widgets (filters, tabs, galleries, menus).

findings.claim: Keep Core and Pro on matching 4.3.x (Core >= 4.3.5 of 2026-10-13, Pro >= 4.3.2 of 2026-10-13): Core 4.3.1 marked the `nested-elements` experiment hidden, and Pro <= 3.29 'Mega Menu' listing it as a dependency throws `Dependency_Exception: Depending on a hidden experiment is not allowed` on every page (#37443, closed 'not planned': update Pro; 4.3.2 relaxed the check); 4.3.4 fixed 'Dropdown menus do not open on the frontend due to missing feature dependencies'; Pro 4.3.1 fixed Global Widgets losing Content/Style tabs (#37436) and PHP warnings with WooCommerce (#37389).
findings.detail: Core changelog: 4.3.0 (2026-09-22) MCP, Background Video, Accordion, Default Styles, raised minimum Chrome/Firefox/Safari; 4.3.1 top bar translations; 4.3.2 (09-24) 'Improved update stability between Elementor Core and Pro', HTTP Basic Auth fix, 'Page styles may not load correctly after being regenerated'; 4.3.4 (10-05) dropdown fix, 'Widget styles can be missing when rendered inside saved Templates', 'Elementor update can fail during version upgrade'; 4.3.5 (10-13) Internal CSS fix (#37468). Pro: 4.3.0 Loop taxonomy filters/alternating templates/empty states, 'Page-specific CSS may be missing on the first visit after automatic CSS cleanup'; 4.3.1 (09-30) #37389, #37436; 4.3.2 (10-13) form security, loop term filters. 4.3.5 source: nested-elements `hidden => true`, Pro mega-menu depends on it; manager.php `is_removed_or_hidden_dependency` / `warn_removed_or_hidden_dependency`. The Plus Addons write-up (2026-09-29) documents the Reddit cases (Core auto-updated to 4.3.0 while Pro stayed on 3.28.3), the WP-CLI recovery sequence (`wp plugin deactivate elementor-pro elementor; wp plugin update elementor; wp plugin update elementor-pro; wp plugin activate elementor elementor-pro`) and rollback via Elementor > Editor > Tools > Version Control. Observed: onar still on 4.2.3 with Pro 4.2.x; others 4.3.3–4.3.5 with Pro 4.2.2–4.3.1 (not all matched).
findings.breaks_when: Core auto-updates while Pro's licence is disconnected/expired (Pro stays on 3.x or 4.2.x); rolling back only one of the two plugins; mega menus or nested elements on a site where Pro lags Core by a major version.
findings.how_to_apply: Update Pro and Core together on staging first; wait for the .1/.2 patch on feature releases (4.3.0 needed 4.3.2 within 48 h); after updating run Tools > Clear Files & Data and purge caches; disable auto-updates where the Pro licence is not connected; move onar from 4.2.3 to 4.3.5 + Pro 4.3.2 in one maintenance window with FA4 shim and Premium Addons re-tested.
findings.how_to_verify: `wp plugin list --name=elementor* --fields=name,version,status` shows matching 4.3.x; load home and a mega-menu page logged-out, open dropdowns and nested tabs; PHP error log empty after update; `wp eval 'var_dump(\Elementor\Plugin::$instance->experiments->is_feature_active("nested-elements"));'` true.

findings.claim: Flexbox containers cut Elementor's structural DOM versus sections (Elementor's own 5-widget example: 37 -> 23 divs, 105 -> 76 lines; blog: Flexbox output −39%, Grid −85%), but each extra nesting level adds a div plus per-container CSS in post CSS, and 4.3 auto-wraps nested elements in a Flexbox container; the audited sites nest 6–9 levels while Elementor publishes no depth limit, so the plugin should enforce <= 4 levels and < 1,500 DOM nodes as a build budget, knowing DOM size was not the limiting factor on these sites.
findings.detail: Help 'Analyze Flexbox container performance' (2026-05-18) table: Section 37 div elements / 105 lines vs Container 23 / 76 ('Total Reduction 14 / 29'); help 'Improve your page performance': two sections replaced by one container using flex direction/alignment/wrap. Changelog 4.3.0 'Improved nested elements by auto-wrapping them in a Flexbox Container'; 4.2.0 'Grid containers can cause slower Editor performance on complex pages' (fix); 3.35.0 'Nested Accordion optimizations with Grid in Chrome browser'. manager.php: deactivating `container` -> 'Container-based content will be hidden from your site and may not be recoverable'. Audit: nesting depth 6–9 and 89–854 containers per site; Lighthouse DOM counts pallada 2,024 nodes (score 86), cretaforums 1,224, limnoupolis 703 (score 27) — JS/LCP dominate, not DOM. snapelement's v3 analysis attributes ~65% of v3 DOM to structural wrappers.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break; the risk is only the `container` experiment being deactivated on a container-built site (content hidden).
findings.how_to_apply: Build with containers only (never sections/columns); one parent container per visual band; columns via child containers with flex wrap/gap rather than container-in-container-in-container; spacing via padding not wrapper containers; header/footer templates as single containers; v4 Div Block/Flexbox when building atomic. Audit metric: Novamira `elementor-get-content` nesting depth <= 4 for new pages.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse 'Avoid an excessive DOM size' (< 1,500 nodes, max child count and depth reported); `document.querySelectorAll('.e-con').length` and maximum `.e-con` ancestry depth per page via Playwright; compare before/after a template rebuild.

findings.claim: `elementor_optimized_gutenberg_loading` (Performance tab 'Optimized Gutenberg Loading', default '1') dequeues `wp-block-library`, `wp-block-library-theme`, `wc-block-style` and `wc-blocks-style` only on singular posts that are built with Elementor and contain no Gutenberg blocks; it is already on by default, so expect no extra gain from touching it, and it cannot affect WooCommerce block Cart/Checkout pages (not Elementor-built).
findings.detail: modules/gutenberg/module.php 4.3.5: `get_option('elementor_optimized_gutenberg_loading','1')`, `dequeue_assets()` at priority 999 guarded by `should_dequeue_gutenberg_assets()` = post exists AND `is_built_with_elementor($post)` AND NOT `is_gutenberg_in_post($post)`. Help 'Optimized Gutenberg Loading' (2024-06-23) and settings desc 'Reduce unnecessary render-blocking loads by dequeuing unused Gutenberg block editor scripts and styles'. Elementor blog: also replaced waypoint.js with native JS and trims empty widget parts.
findings.breaks_when: An Elementor-built page embeds a shortcode or WP widget whose output is block markup relying on wp-block-library CSS (e.g. a reusable block via shortcode plugin) -> unstyled; archive/shop pages are unaffected (not singular posts).
findings.how_to_apply: Leave Settings > Performance > Optimized Gutenberg Loading = Enable; if a block-styled shortcode breaks, set Disable or enqueue `wp-block-library` conditionally in the child theme for that page.
findings.how_to_verify: `wp-block-library` CSS absent on Elementor pages and present on the WooCommerce block Cart/Checkout pages; Lighthouse 'Reduce unused CSS' has no block-library entry on Elementor pages; screenshot any shortcode-embedded content.

findings.claim: v4 Interactions assets (motion.min.js, 128 KB raw, plus the elementor-interactions bundle) are registered on every page when Atomic Elements is active but enqueued only on pages where at least one element has an interaction, so enabling v4 does not add that cost to interaction-free pages.
findings.detail: modules/interactions/module.php registers `motion-js` (assets/lib/motion/motion.min.js, version 11.13.5), `elementor-interactions-shared-utils` and `elementor-interactions` on `elementor/frontend/after_register_scripts` with no enqueue. modules/interactions/interactions-frontend-handler.php collects interactions per document on `elementor/frontend/builder_content_data` (header, footer, post content; cached in post meta via Interactions_Postmeta) and in `print_interactions_data()` (wp_footer priority 1) returns early `if ( empty( $elements_with_interactions ) )`; only otherwise does `enqueue_interactions_assets()` call `wp_enqueue_script( HANDLE_MOTION_JS )` and `wp_enqueue_script( HANDLE_FRONTEND )` and print the JSON config. Because the scripts are enqueued at wp_footer they load late (after HTML), so an above-the-fold v4 entrance Interaction behaves like a v3 entrance animation: the element waits for JS.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break; the cost only appears on pages that actually use Interactions, where it is ~128 KB raw of motion.js plus the bundle.
findings.how_to_apply: Build rule for v4 sites: Interactions are free until used; keep them off hero/LCP elements and audit with the per-page check below rather than globally forbidding the feature.
findings.how_to_verify: On a v4 page without interactions, Network shows no request for /elementor/assets/lib/motion/motion.min.js and no inline `elementorInteractions` config in the footer; add one interaction below the fold and both appear.

findings.claim: Elementor's Google Fonts CSS always declares all 18 weight/style variants per family and passes `&subset=greek` only when the WordPress locale is exactly 'el'; weight capping therefore has to be done with Custom Fonts (one Greek+Latin variable .woff2 per family) or by disabling Elementor's Google Fonts and self-hosting via Perfmatters, not through Site Settings.
findings.detail: includes/frontend.php `get_stable_google_fonts_url()` builds `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=<Family>:100,100italic,200,200italic,300,300italic,400,400italic,500,500italic,600,600italic,700,700italic,800,800italic,900,900italic|...&display=<elementor_font_display>` and appends `&subset=` from a locale map (`'el' => 'greek'`, `'ru_RU' => 'cyrillic'`, ... filter `elementor/frontend/google_font_subsets`). Google's v1 API served to Elementor's Chrome/114 UA (core/files/fonts/google-font.php `UA_STRING`) returns woff2 @font-face blocks per subset with `unicode-range`, so browsers fetch only the subsets and weights actually used, but the CSS payload lists 18 variants x N subsets per family, and 'Load Google Fonts Locally' downloads every one of those files (download_fonts() loops over every `url()`), i.e. dozens of woff2 files per family on disk. Elementor's own 'Use Variable Fonts' help (2026-10-01, cited by the researcher) is the supported path to one file for all weights.
findings.breaks_when: Custom font uploaded as Latin-only woff2 -> Greek falls back to system font; Elementor Google Fonts disabled (`elementor/frontend/print_google_fonts` false) without re-declaring the same family names as Custom Fonts -> whole site in fallback fonts.
findings.how_to_apply: Per family: subset a variable font to latin+greek with fontTools (`pyftsubset Font[wght].ttf --unicodes='U+0000-00FF,U+0370-03FF,U+1F00-1FFF' --flavor=woff2`), upload under Elementor > Custom Fonts with the same family name used in Global Fonts, set Google Fonts Load = Swap; or keep Google Fonts and accept the 18-variant CSS (browsers still download only used weights). Verify the locale: on Greek-default sites WPLANG should be `el` so the subset hint is sent.
findings.how_to_verify: `curl -A 'Mozilla/5.0 ... Chrome/114...' '<the fonts.googleapis.com URL from page source>' | grep -c 'unicode-range'` shows greek blocks; after switching to custom fonts, Network shows <= 2 woff2 per family and Greek + Latin headings render in the brand font at 390 px.

findings.claim: Under Lighthouse/PSI mobile emulation (412x823, DPR 1.75) Elementor's background lazy-load rule in force is the `max-height:1024px` one (`nth-of-type(n+3)`), so only a hero placed in the 3rd or later top-level container is hidden in PSI; the n+2 rule applies to real phones <= 640 px tall (landscape, small/old devices) and is invisible to Lighthouse.
findings.detail: modules/lazyload/module.php emits default `n+4`, `@media screen and (max-height: 1024px)` -> `n+3`, `@media screen and (max-height: 640px)` -> `n+2`; local Lighthouse 12.8.2 runs report `screenEmulation: {mobile: true, width: 412, height: 823, deviceScaleFactor: 1.75}`. Consequence for the audit script: a PSI-clean page can still show a blank hero background on a landscape phone until the IntersectionObserver (rootMargin 200px) fires after DOMContentLoaded.
findings.breaks_when: Header template + announcement bar + hero means the hero is the 3rd `.e-con.e-parent` -> hidden in PSI; on <= 640 px tall viewports the 2nd container's background is hidden until JS runs.
findings.how_to_apply: Add CSS class `e-no-lazyload` to every top-level container that can be in the first viewport on any device (hero and anything above it), or disable 'Lazy Load Background Images' when the cache plugin lazy-loads CSS backgrounds (WP Rocket/Perfmatters/FlyingPress).
findings.how_to_verify: Playwright at 412x823 and at 844x390 (landscape): screenshot at DOMContentLoaded with JS disabled; hero background visible in both; `getComputedStyle(hero).backgroundImage !== 'none'`.

findings.claim: Elementor's main branch is already versioned 4.4.0 (unreleased; wordpress.org current = 4.3.5, 2026-10-13), and the `elementor/files/base_dir|base_url` filters and the e_optimized_css_files guards are '@since 4.4.0' code, so the plugin should pin its rules to 4.3.5 and re-check the CSS-purge finding when 4.4.0 ships.
findings.detail: raw elementor.php on main: `Version: 4.4.0`, `define('ELEMENTOR_VERSION','4.4.0')`; api.wordpress.org/plugins/info/1.0/elementor.json: version 4.3.5, last_updated 2026-10-13 12:48pm GMT, requires_php 7.4, tested 7.1.3. Any raw 'main' file quoted by the researcher (manager.php, lazyload, image-loading-optimization) is 4.4.0-dev; the experiment defaults match the 4.3.5 tag but could change before release. No 4.4.0 beta announcement was findable by search on 2026-10-15.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break; stale knowledge-base entries if 4.4.0 flips e_optimized_css_files to beta/active or changes Element Cache defaults.
findings.how_to_apply: Store `elementor_core_pinned_version: 4.3.5` and `elementor_pro_pinned_version: 4.3.2` in the plugin references; on each run compare `wp plugin get elementor --field=version` against the pin and re-fetch changelog.txt when newer.
findings.how_to_verify: `curl -s https://api.wordpress.org/plugins/info/1.0/elementor.json | jq .version` equals the pin; changelog.txt top entry matches.

findings.claim: LiteSpeed offers two Elementor-safe escape hatches the researcher omitted: a `data-no-defer="1"` attribute (or filter `litespeed_optm_gm_js_exc`) to keep a script out of Guest Mode defer/delay, and 'Localize Resources' (default OFF) to self-host gtag/fbevents so they can be minified/deferred like local files.
findings.detail: docs.litespeedtech.com pageopt: Guest Mode JS Excludes 'Other ways to do the same thing include: Using the API filter litespeed_optm_gm_js_exc. Marking elements in HTML with the data-no-defer="1" attribute'; Localize Resources 'OFF ... Set Localize Resources to ON to copy the resources to your local system, where they can be optimized as needed ... works only with HTTPS URLs'. Also relevant: Lazy Load Images 'When you turn this option ON, the WordPress core Lazy Load feature is automatically disabled' and Elementor's Optimized Image Loading also disables core lazy-load (`wp_lazy_loading_enabled` false), which is why two loaders double-mark images.
findings.breaks_when: Localizing a vendor script that is version-pinned by URL -> stale copy until LiteSpeed refreshes; data-no-defer on Elementor inline configs is unnecessary (Guest Mode excludes should target the file paths from the Perfmatters list instead).
findings.how_to_apply: LiteSpeed > Page Optimization > Tuning > Guest Mode JS Excludes: paste the Perfmatters Elementor list (frontend.min.js, frontend-modules.min.js, elements-handlers.min.js, webpack runtimes, jquery, elementorFrontendConfig, ElementorProFrontendConfig); Localization: Localize Resources ON with the default recommended URL list (gtag/gtm/fbevents) only after confirming the cookie banner still blocks them pre-consent.
findings.how_to_verify: Guest Mode first view: hero visible without interaction; Tag Assistant shows GTM firing from the local copy; consent tool still gates GA4/FB until accept.

title: Cache and optimizer plugins with Elementor: a safe/unsafe settings matrix
summary: On these 10 sites the cache plugin is either doing nothing (every optimisation off) or doing the dangerous things first (Guest Mode, lazy-load with no VPI, combine). The matrix below is consistent across all five vendors' own docs (all opened, dated 2025-2026): page cache, browser cache, object cache, minify, DNS prefetch and self-hosted fonts are safe to auto-enable; lazy-load images needs an above-the-fold exclusion mechanism (VPI / Optimize critical images / Exclude leading images / FlyingPress cloud detection) or it raises LCP and CLS, which is exactly the 0 to 0.107 CLS regression seen on staging; Remove Unused CSS and Delay JS give the largest PageSpeed gains (render-blocking CSS and 5 GTM tags are the top audits on the slow sites) but are the two features every vendor documents as breaking Elementor entrance animations, popups, sticky headers, menus, sliders and booking calendars, so they must ship with the Elementor exclusion lists quoted below and a click-through test, never as a blind toggle. Options that must never be auto-enabled: CSS/JS Combine (every vendor says it breaks Delay JS and RUCSS and fills disk with Elementor's per-post CSS), LiteSpeed Guest Mode + Guest Optimization (official docs warn of momentary wrong language/pricing and it masks real problems; a dated April 2026 field report shows an Elementor slider site dropping 31 points and CLS 0.087 to 0.896), "delay all"/"load after interaction" JS modes without exclusions, Cloudflare Rocket Loader, Elementor's own Optimized Image Loading / Lazy Load Background Images alongside a plugin lazy-loader, and W3TC Minify in Auto / Combine mode. Only one plugin may own each function: WP Rocket disables its RUCSS if Perfmatters RUCSS is on, FlyingPress force-disables overlapping Perfmatters features, LiteSpeed lists W3TC and WP Rocket as conflicts, and Perfmatters' own LiteSpeed guide says turn all Page Optimization and Guest Mode off and let Perfmatters do the front end. Recommended order: page/browser/object cache and Woo/booking exclusions, then minify + font self-hosting (with Greek subset), then defer JS, then lazy-load images with hero protection, then delay third-party scripts only, then RUCSS with the Elementor safelist, then (optionally) delay-all JS with the Elementor exclusion list, then script-manager unloading; measure mobile PSI, CLS and a fixed click-through list after each step. Version note: FlyingPress's official changelog ends the 4.x line at 4.16.4 (Feb 2025) and is at 5.6.5 (Aug 2026); the observed "4.22.1" does not exist there and must be re-checked.
critic_notes: Method: WebFetch could not resolve any external host from this container (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so every page listed as a source was downloaded with curl through the session proxy using the researcher's own text-extraction script (copied to critic_fetch.py) into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/critic_cache/ and read locally; quotes come from those fresh copies, not from the researcher's cache. Elementor 4.3.5 setting names and defaults were verified from the GitHub main-branch source (already carrying @since 4.4.0 annotations, so treat as 4.3.5+). The FlyingPress fork finding comes from read-only Novamira calls (list-directory, read-file) on cretaforums.gr only; voreniahorizon.gr was not re-read and is assumed identical from the audit's shared '4.22.1'. Nothing was written to any site. Not re-opened: StackHarbor/Savvy LiteSpeed-Woo guides, BoldGrid minify forum threads, wordpress.org LiteSpeed/Elementor threads, WoodMart/WP Booking Calendar threads, the jrmora VPI post (grepped from the researcher's copy only), Freshy's Element Cache case (page returned 220 bytes); those claims stand on the researcher's copies. Dead links found: perfmatters.io/docs/elementor/ (404), boldgrid.com/support/w3-total-cache/w3-total-cache-and-elementor/ (404; remove-cssjs/ is also 404, live URL is remove-css-js/), polylang.pro and wpml.org caching pages (404), developers.elementor.com widget-output-caching (empty response). The PSI API quota in the scratchpad is exhausted (psi.json shows 429), so no new PageSpeed measurements were possible. Open questions remaining: Greek unicode-range in WP Rocket / FlyingPress-fork font output (not tested on a live Greek page); whether YITH/WooCommerce Bookings/JetSmartFilters widgets return is_dynamic_content()=false; whether the LiteSpeed hosts are LSWS Enterprise (ESI) or OpenLiteSpeed. Skipped: W3TC Pro feature pages beyond Delay Scripts and Remove CSS/JS, and FlyingPress 5.x docs beyond those cited, since no audited site runs official FlyingPress 5. Risk for the user: the fork's update host (downloads.cretaforce.gr) is a third-party supply chain for two production sites and should be reviewed by the agency.

findings.claim: Only one plugin may own each optimisation function, and the enabling order must be cache first, Delay-all JS and Remove Unused CSS last; three of the audited sites run two optimisers with overlapping features.
findings.detail: Every vendor documents this. LiteSpeed's Third Party page lists W3 Total Cache, WP Rocket, Asset CleanUp ("Not compatible with LSCache's Page Optimization features and Guest Mode") and Cookie Notice & Compliance for GDPR ("Interferes with LSCache's JavaScript Delay functionality") as conflicts (page dated July 27 2026). Perfmatters' LiteSpeed guide: "turn off both Guest Mode and Guest Optimization" and "Under Page Optimization, turn off every setting", keep only cache, TTL (recommends 2592000 s), Object cache, Browser cache. WP Rocket: "Remove Unused CSS is automatically disabled when ... Perfmatters' Remove Unused CSS are active". FlyingPress: "automatically disables conflicting optimizations in ... Perfmatters, ShortPixel AI, SiteGround Optimizer" and "use FlyingPress as your only optimization plugin". Observed stack: marakaki.com and pallada.gr run W3TC + Perfmatters, onar-seaside-lounge.gr runs LiteSpeed + Perfmatters. Recommended split when two plugins coexist: cache plugin owns page cache, browser cache, object cache, CDN; Perfmatters owns minify, defer/delay, RUCSS, lazy load, fonts, script manager. Enabling order (each step measured before the next): 1) page cache + browser cache + object cache + Woo/booking excludes; 2) CSS/JS minify, HTML minify, remove emoji, self-host Google Fonts with Greek subset; 3) defer JS; 4) lazy-load images + iframes with above-the-fold protection; 5) delay third-party scripts only (GTM, pixel, chat); 6) Remove Unused CSS with the Elementor safelist; 7) optional delay-all JS with the Elementor exclusion list; 8) per-page unloading with the script manager in test mode.
findings.breaks_when: Two plugins lazy-load, minify or delay the same assets: images never appear or need a mouse move (WP Rocket 1655 lists third-party lazyload + Delay JS as the first common issue), combined files 404, Used CSS generated from already-combined CSS (WP Rocket 1718: "Any combination of CSS/JavaScript by other plugins/themes needs to be disabled").
findings.how_to_apply: Inventory which plugin has each toggle on (LiteSpeed > Page Optimization tabs; Perfmatters > Assets/CSS/JavaScript/Lazy Loading; W3TC > General Settings > Minify / User Experience; FlyingPress > Optimizations). Disable duplicates so each function has exactly one owner. For LiteSpeed + Perfmatters follow perfmatters.io/docs/litespeed-cache-settings/: General > Guest Mode OFF, Guest Optimization OFF; Page Optimization all OFF (optionally HTML Minify); Cache > TTL 2592000; Object cache ON; Browser cache ON. For W3TC + Perfmatters: keep W3TC Page Cache (Disk: Enhanced), Browser Cache, Object Cache; turn off W3TC Minify and Lazy Load. Then enable features in the order above, one per deploy.
findings.how_to_verify: After each step: run PSI mobile 3x on home + one product/booking page + one inner page and record score, LCP, CLS, TBT; view source and confirm each asset is rewritten by exactly one plugin (one of data-lazyloaded / data-rocket-lazy / perfmatters-lazy / loading=lazy, not two); run the fixed click-through list (mobile menu, popup, slider, sticky header, form submit, booking date pick, add-to-cart, language switch) in an incognito window at 390px; check DevTools console for ReferenceError.

findings.claim: Delay JavaScript until interaction is the single biggest TBT/score lever for the slow sites (5 GTM tags, FB pixel) but is the feature most documented to break Elementor; ship it in 'specified scripts only' mode first, and 'delay all' only with the Elementor exclusion list below.
findings.detail: Perfmatters (doc current, plugin 2.6.9 Oct 6 2026): two behaviours, "Only delay specified scripts" and "Delay all scripts" ("by far the most aggressive option"); delay strings for GTM: /gtm.js, /gtag/js, gtag(, /gtm-, /gtm.; Facebook: fbevents.js, fbq(; optional "Delay timeout" 15 s (filter perfmatters_delay_js_timeout). Its Elementor exclusion list: jquery.min.js, jquery.smartmenus.min.js, jquery.sticky.min.js, webpack.runtime.min.js, webpack-pro.runtime.min.js, /elementor/assets/js/frontend.min.js, /elementor-pro/assets/js/frontend.min.js, frontend-modules.min.js, elements-handlers.min.js, elementorFrontendConfig, ElementorProFrontendConfig, imagesloaded.min.js, hooks.min.js, i18n.min.js ("If you're not using a lot of animations, you might not need any exclusions"); Elementor search: webpack-pro.runtime.min.js, webpack.runtime.min.js, elements-handlers.min.js, jquery.smartmenus.min.js; TOC widget: /wp-includes/js/dist/hooks.min.js, /wp-includes/js/dist/i18n.min.js, /elementor/assets/lib/waypoints/waypoints.min.js; JetMenu: /elementor-pro/, /elementor/, /jet-menu/, jetMenuPublicSettings etc.; WooCommerce product gallery: flexslider, single-product.min.js, slick, waypoint. Changelog: quick exclusion got swiper (2.3.9), e-gallery (2.5.1), hooks/i18n (2.6.9). WP Rocket 3.23.5.1 (Oct 2 2026): "Delay JavaScript execution" with One-click exclusions (tick the Elementor boxes, doc 1745 updated Apr 22 2026), "Excluded JavaScript Files", nowprocket attribute, "Safe Mode for Delay JavaScript Execution" excludes /wp-content/, /wp-includes/, jQuery and wp_add_inline_script output ("not recommended ... last resource"); Combine JS is force-disabled when Delay is on; 3.18.1 introduced layout issues fixed in 3.18.3. LiteSpeed 7.9.1: Page Optimization > JS Settings > "Load JS Deferred: Delayed", Tuning > "JS Deferred/Delayed Excludes" and "JS Delayed Includes" (partial strings, no wildcards). FlyingPress 5.x docs (Jun 2025): "Delay All JavaScript" has three modes: Defer loading, Load when idle (recommended), Load after interaction ("not suitable if your site has sliders, animations, menus, or other interactive elements in the above-the-fold area"); separate "Load Third-party Scripts on Interaction" (auto-detects external domains) and "Delay Specific Scripts on Interaction" (keyword list: googletagmanager.com, google-analytics.com, fbevents.js, static.hotjar.com, clarity.ms ...). W3TC 2.10: "Delay Scripts" is Pro only, Performance > General Settings > User Experience, a Delay List matched exactly against script attributes plus a Timeout; matched scripts are excluded from Minify.
findings.breaks_when: Delay-all is enabled on a page with above-the-fold JS-dependent UI: Elementor entrance animations stay invisible (elementor-invisible class never removed until interaction), popups don't open, mobile menu needs a double tap, sticky header doesn't stick, Swiper/loop carousels don't initialise (WoodMart thread June 2026: off-canvas cart, sticky add-to-cart and lazy images all broke, only Safe Mode fixed it), cookie banner missing from the PSI screenshot, booking calendar shows 'loading' (WP Booking Calendar requires excluding /booking(.*)/(.*) and (.*)_wpbc(.*)), consent-mode defaults fire after GTM. Also breaks when a theme preloader is on (spinner until interaction) and when combine JS is on anywhere.
findings.how_to_apply: Step A (safe): Perfmatters > JavaScript > Delay JavaScript ON, behaviour "Only delay specified scripts", list the GTM/gtag/fbevents strings above; or FlyingPress > Load Third-party Scripts on Interaction ON; or WP Rocket Delay JS with every Elementor/Woo/cookie-banner One-click box ticked; or LiteSpeed JS Delayed Includes with gtm.js, gtag/js, fbevents.js while Load JS Deferred stays 'Deferred'. Step B (optional): switch to Delay all / 'Load after interaction' / LiteSpeed 'Delayed' only after adding the Elementor list, the cookie-banner strings and the booking plugin paths, and after the Step C click-through passes; use WP Rocket Safe Mode / Perfmatters exclusions of /themes/ /plugins/ /wp-includes/ only as a diagnostic.
findings.how_to_verify: Incognito at 390px with no mouse movement: hero, menu, first popup trigger, slider and cookie banner must all render before any interaction; PSI screenshot filmstrip shows the banner and hero. DevTools console: no 'Uncaught ReferenceError: jQuery is not defined' / 'elementorFrontend is not defined'; search source for data-rocket-type / pmdelayedscript / data-lazyloaded to confirm which scripts are delayed. Compare TBT and 'Reduce unused JavaScript' before/after; confirm GA4 realtime still records a pageview (enable the 15 s timeout if the marketer needs pageviews without interaction).
findings.correction: FlyingPress's three modes ('Defer loading / Load when idle / Load after interaction') and auto-detecting 'Load Third-party Scripts on Interaction' are 5.x cloud features (docs dated June 25 / May 21, 2025). cretaforums.gr runs a CretaForce fork of FlyingPress 4.x (header 'Version: 4.22.1', 'Update URI: https://downloads.cretaforce.gr/wordpress/flying-press/'); its src/Config.php exposes only js_defer (bool), js_delay (bool) with js_delay_method = 'selected' | 'all', js_delay_selected (keyword list, default includes googletagmanager.com, google-analytics.com, fbevents.js, static.hotjar.com, clarity.ms, grecaptcha.execute, cookie-law-info) and js_delay_all_excludes. On those sites Step A = keep js_delay_method 'selected' (already default) and Step B = 'all' plus the Elementor exclusion list; there is no 'idle' mode. Risk stays high for delay-all.

findings.claim: Remove Unused CSS (Perfmatters/WP Rocket/FlyingPress) or UCSS+CCSS (LiteSpeed via QUIC.cloud) removes the render-blocking CSS that Elementor sites carry, but every vendor documents the same failure class on Elementor: styles that are only visible after interaction (hover menus, popups, sliders, tabs, sticky header, entrance animations) get dropped, so it must ship with a safelist and a side-by-side check.
findings.detail: Perfmatters 2.6.x: CSS > "Remove Unused CSS"; "Used CSS Method" Inline (best PSI) or File; "Stylesheet Behavior" Delay (default, recommended) / Async / Remove ("advanced users"); "Excluded Stylesheets" and "Excluded Selectors"; documented Elementor safelist: #elementor-device-mode and .elementor-sticky--active (sticky menu), a flexbox-container pseudo-element CSS fix for banners; built-ins added for Elementor animations (1.9.x/2.x), background slideshow (2.5.5), and "Elementor's new local and global per-document stylesheets" (2.6.9, Oct 2026); used CSS is generated per page, once for posts, per Woo product type; requires CSS combine OFF in other plugins and recommends Elementor CSS as external file. WP Rocket: "Remove Unused CSS" under Optimize CSS delivery; asynchronous SaaS generation (visits ?wpr_imagedimensions=1&nowprocket=1&no_optimize=1, 45 s timeout, must allow-list WP-Rocket-SaaS user agents/IPs, Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode off, real cron recommended); result in <style id="wpr-usedcss">; "CSS safelist" accepts classes, IDs, files, @FontFamily, (.*) patterns; test with (.*) first; Mobile Cache creates separate mobile Used CSS; invalid Used CSS <150 bytes is discarded; helper to set 10 KB minimum. FlyingPress: "Remove Unused CSS" inlines <style id="flying-press-css">, rest loaded when idle; "Include CSS Selectors" (selectors only, not file names) for "Dynamically injected (popups, modals, sliders), Hidden on initial load (tabs, dropdowns), Shown only after interaction (menus on hover)"; recommends Elementor CSS as external files. LiteSpeed 7.9.1: "Generate UCSS" requires "CSS Combine" ON and QUIC.cloud quota; "UCSS Inline" (then Load CSS Asynchronously is ignored); "UCSS Selector Allowlist" (selector as written in CSS; pseudo-classes like :hover are ignored, add the base selector), "UCSS URI Excludes", "UCSS Inline Excluded Files"; separate "Load CSS Asynchronously" generates Critical CSS (CCSS) with "CSS Per URL" ON ("may result in incorrect CSS styling if your site uses a page builder" when OFF), "Separate CCSS Cache Post Types" default page; warns of disk use (one file per page, two with Cache Mobile); UCSS troubleshooting is the Inspect-compare method with /?LSCWP_CTRL=before_optm. W3TC 2.10 has no automatic unused-CSS removal; Pro "Remove CSS/JS" is a manual Remove List per URL/content match and Pro "Eliminate render-blocking CSS" inlines combined CSS.
findings.breaks_when: Any selector not present in the initial render is needed later: Elementor popups, mega-menu sub-menus, sticky header active state (.elementor-sticky--active), Swiper/Loop carousel slides, tabs/accordions, entrance-animation keyframes, Woo variation forms, JetSmartFilters results, cookie banner; mobile-only styles when only desktop Used CSS is generated; the generator is blocked by a firewall/bot challenge (randomly broken CSS); CSS/JS combine is active in another plugin; Elementor CSS Print Method is Inline (nothing external to analyse).
findings.how_to_apply: Preconditions: Elementor > Settings > Performance > CSS Print Method = External File; no CSS combine anywhere; only one RUCSS engine. Perfmatters: CSS > Remove Unused CSS ON, Used CSS Method Inline, Stylesheet Behavior Delay, Excluded Selectors: #elementor-device-mode, .elementor-sticky--active, .elementor-invisible, .elementor-popup-modal, .dialog-widget, .e-n-menu, .elementor-sticky, .swiper (start broad, then narrow); exclude /cart/, /checkout/ pages via the meta box (already auto-excluded). WP Rocket: File Optimization > Optimize CSS delivery > Remove Unused CSS, enable Preload and Mobile Cache, safelist the same selectors plus @FontName if a font vanishes. FlyingPress: Remove Unused CSS ON, Include CSS Selectors with the same list. LiteSpeed: only if QUIC.cloud is funded: CSS Combine ON + Generate UCSS ON + UCSS Inline ON + Cache Mobile ON; add selectors to UCSS Selector Allowlist; otherwise leave UCSS/CCSS off and use Perfmatters.
findings.how_to_verify: Open the page normally and with ?nowprocket (WP Rocket) / ?perfmattersoff (Perfmatters, logged in) / /?LSCWP_CTRL=before_optm (LiteSpeed) side by side; Inspect the header, a popup after opening it, the sticky header after scrolling, a slider slide and the mobile menu, and diff the applied rules. Confirm the Used CSS block exists (wpr-usedcss / flying-press-css / perfmatters used CSS file) on both desktop and mobile UA. PSI mobile: 'Eliminate render-blocking resources' and 'Reduce unused CSS' should drop to near zero; CLS must not rise (FOUC from async CSS shows as CLS). Re-run after every Elementor global style change and clear Used CSS.
findings.correction: (1) LiteSpeed's bundled data/ucss_whitelist.txt has zero Elementor entries (only .pace-inactive and .et_pb_number_counter.active), so on LiteSpeed the whole Elementor safelist is manual. (2) Elementor 4 'Atomic/V4' elements (experiments e_opt_in_v4 / e_atomic_elements seen in the audit) print class-based CSS during the render pass; a June 4, 2026 practitioner guide calls LiteSpeed UCSS 'the most common Atomic-CSS culprit' and cites Elementor GitHub issue #35397 (popups opened by a runtime trigger lose V4 CSS). Perfmatters only added 'built-in Remove Unused CSS exclusions for Elementor's new local and global per-document stylesheets' in 2.6.9 (10.06.2026); WP Rocket, LiteSpeed and FlyingPress document no equivalent, so RUCSS risk is high on pages using V4 elements. (3) Elementor 4.3.5 (2026-10-13) fixed 'Page editing can fail when Internal CSS Embedding is enabled', one more reason for CSS Print Method = External File. The FlyingPress fork's equivalent key is css_rucss_method (default 'async').

findings.claim: Lazy-loading images is safe only when the LCP/hero and other above-the-fold images are excluded and dimensions are enforced; enabling a plugin lazy-loader blindly raised CLS from 0 to 0.107 on staging and will also lengthen LCP.
findings.detail: LiteSpeed 7.9.1: Media Settings > "Lazy Load Images" (disables WP core lazy load), "Responsive Placeholder" ON (needs width/height), "Add Missing Sizes" ON (works only with Lazy Load ON), "Lazy Load iframes"; VPI tab: "Viewport Images" ON + "Viewport Images Cron" ON (QUIC.cloud service; detects visible images at 1300x900 desktop and 480x800 mobile per URL, excludes them from lazy load and preloads them; 7.9 added fetchpriority=high to VPI preloads; per-post override in the LiteSpeed Options metabox); Media Excludes: "Lazy Load Image Excludes", "Lazy Load Image Class Name Excludes", "Lazy Load Image Parent Class Name Excludes", "Lazy Load URI Excludes" (partial strings, no wildcards). Without VPI nothing protects the hero. Perfmatters: Lazy Loading > Images, "Exclude Leading Images" N (count while logged out; does not apply to background images), "Exclude by Parent Selector" (advanced), no-lazy class, perfmatters_lazyload_excluded_attributes filter, "Viewport threshold" (0px default; 300px+ on ad-heavy sites), "DOM Monitoring" only for AJAX/infinite scroll, "CSS Background Images" with Background Selectors or the perfmatters-lazy-css-bg class on an Elementor container; Preload critical images automatically excludes those images. WP Rocket: Media > LazyLoad, "Excluded images or iframes" accepts filename, any img attribute, container class for background images, CSS filename (excludes all images in it); Elementor image widget has no class on the img, so use filenames or the add-class-to-elementor-image plugin with no-lazy (doc updated May 14 2025); "Optimize critical images" preloads the LCP image and prevents its lazyload; "LazyLoad for CSS background images" (threshold 300px, "not fully compatible with combined CSS third party features"). FlyingPress 5.x: "Lazy Load Images, Videos, and Iframes" uses native loading=lazy, cloud optimizer marks above-the-fold media loading=eager and preloads key images; exclusions by keyword in the tag; "Properly Size Images" adds width/height. W3TC 2.10.7: General Settings > User Experience > Lazy Load Images, exclusions by class/URL, "Process background images" (a stored-XSS CVE affected this option up to 2.10.5; 2.10.6 fixed 'Match background styles as top-level attributes only'); no above-the-fold detection. Elementor's own "Optimized Image Loading" already adds fetchpriority=high to the LCP image and loading=lazy below; it must be off when a plugin lazy-loads (WP Rocket 1745, LiteSpeed thirdparty).
findings.breaks_when: Hero, logo, first slide or above-the-fold gallery is lazy-loaded (LCP element shows loading=lazy, LCP rises, CLS rises if no dimensions); images inside Swiper/loop carousels or AJAX-filtered grids never load without DOM monitoring; Elementor background-image containers (sections/columns) are untouched by img-based lazyloaders and double-processed when Elementor 'Lazy Load Background Images' is also on; Jeg Kit image-splitting widget glitched under WP Rocket lazyload (wordpress.org thread); the lazyload script itself is deferred/delayed (Perfmatters: images show as SVG data URI until /perfmatters/js/lazyload.min.js is excluded from defer).
findings.how_to_apply: Turn off Elementor > Settings > Performance > Optimized Image Loading and Features > Lazy Load Background Images, and WP core/other lazyloaders. LiteSpeed: enable Lazy Load Images only together with Viewport Images + VPI Cron (requires QUIC.cloud), Responsive Placeholder ON, Add Missing Sizes ON, and add .elementor-widget-image img and wp-post-image to Lazy Load Image Excludes as a safety net (wpmet guide), or leave Lazy Load Images OFF and let Perfmatters do it. Perfmatters: Images ON, Exclude Leading Images = number of images in the first mobile screen (usually 2-3), Add Missing Image Dimensions ON, iFrames and Videos ON + YouTube Preview Thumbnails ON, Fetch Priority high on the hero. WP Rocket: LazyLoad ON + Optimize critical images ON + Add missing image dimensions ON; exclude hero filename. FlyingPress: Lazy load ON, Properly size images ON, add the hero filename to Exclusions if PSI still flags it.
