findings.how_to_verify: PSI mobile: the LCP element in 'Largest Contentful Paint element' must not carry loading=lazy or a placeholder src, and 'Largest Contentful Paint image was lazily loaded' must not appear; CLS stays at the pre-change value (target 0); 'Defer offscreen images' passes. DevTools Network with a 390px viewport: only above-the-fold images load before scroll. Scroll every slider and filter grid to confirm images appear. Repeat on the first screen of every template (home, product, booking page).
findings.correction: (a) The 1300x900 desktop / 480x800 mobile VPI viewports appear only in a third-party blog (jrmora.com), not in LiteSpeed's docs; label them unofficial. (b) The FlyingPress sentences describe the 5.x cloud optimizer; the CretaForce 4.22.1 fork uses img_lazyload_exclude_count (default 2), img_preload, img_width_height, and since 4.20.1 'detecting one likely large above-fold image and excluding it from lazy loading' with fetchpriority=high on the preload (4.20.0), i.e. a heuristic, not cloud detection. (c) The W3TC CVE is CVE-2026-78438 (lazyload background mutator, <=2.10.5, fixed 2.10.6, requires Lazy Load + background processing), and a second stored XSS CVE-2026-87920 affects <=2.10.6 (only with 'Remove query strings from static resources') fixed in 2.10.7, so gate on 2.10.7, not 2.10.6. (d) Elementor's option key is elementor_optimized_image_loading with default '1'.

findings.claim: Elementor 4.x's own Performance/Features toggles must be set deliberately before any cache plugin is tuned: Optimized Image Loading OFF and Lazy Load Background Images OFF when a plugin lazy-loads, Inline Font Icons ON, CSS Print Method External File, Element Cache left at Default (or Disabled when WP Rocket is used or booking/cart widgets go stale).
findings.detail: WP Rocket doc 1745 (updated April 22 2026): under Elementor > Editor > Settings > Performance deactivate Optimized Image Loading, Lazy Load Background Images and Element Cache because "WP Rocket's Optimize critical images feature does not currently support excluding critical images from third-party lazyloading", WP Rocket already lazyloads CSS backgrounds, and "Element Cache may cause widgets to show incorrect content"; Elementor post CSS files are auto-excluded from WP Rocket Minify CSS; WP Rocket clears its cache when Elementor's CSS Print Method is External File and Element Caching is Default/Active. LiteSpeed Third Party page (July 27 2026): Performance tab: CSS Print Method leave as is, Optimized Image Loading Disable, Optimized Gutenberg Loading Enable; Features tab: Inline Font Icons Active, Additional Custom Breakpoints Inactive, Lazy Load Background Images Inactive; LiteSpeed 7.2 added 'Elementor: Clear all caches on regenerate CSS & Data' and 6.x added Elementor nonces to ESI. FlyingPress: disable builder performance features that overlap and "If there's an option to output CSS as inline or files, choose CSS files". Elementor help (element-caching-help, modified Sep 15 2026): Element Caching stores widget HTML in the database, is excluded automatically for widgets with dynamic tags or display conditions, Container/Grid Container/Off Canvas/Section/Column are always cached, per-element override in Advanced > Cache Settings, site-wide "Element Cache Expiration" and "Element Cache: Disable" in Settings > Performance; developers doc: widgets are dynamic unless is_dynamic_content() returns false, so third-party booking/cart widgets are not cached unless the add-on opted in. Audit: pallada.gr has element cache disabled, onar has e_optimized_markup off and the FA4 shim on; e_optimized_css_files is off everywhere (could not confirm its 4.x behaviour with RUCSS).
findings.breaks_when: Optimized Image Loading stays on next to a plugin lazyloader (hero gets loading=lazy from one and fetchpriority=high from the other); Lazy Load Background Images on next to WP Rocket/Perfmatters CSS-background lazyload (hero background flashes or never paints); Element Cache Active on a widget rendering per-visitor data without dynamic tags (stale cart count, booking availability, logged-in state); Inline CSS print method with RUCSS (nothing to analyse, bigger HTML).
findings.how_to_apply: Elementor > Settings > Performance: CSS Print Method = External File; Optimized Image Loading = Disable when the cache plugin lazy-loads (keep Enable only if no plugin lazy-loads); Optimized Gutenberg Loading = Enable; Element Cache = Default (set Disable if using WP Rocket or if any booking/cart widget shows stale output), Element Cache Expiration 24h. Features: Inline Font Icons = Active; Lazy Load Background Images = Inactive when a plugin handles backgrounds; Optimized Markup stays on (test custom CSS targeting old wrappers). Settings > Advanced: Google Fonts = Disable once fonts are self-hosted. Turn off the FA4 shim (elementor_load_fa4_shim) where no fa fa- icons remain.
findings.how_to_verify: View source on the home page: the hero must carry fetchpriority=high from exactly one source and no loading=lazy; Elementor CSS is loaded as /uploads/elementor/css/post-*.css files; no eicons/font-awesome CSS requests when Inline Font Icons is active. Log out and load a booking product and a page with the mini-cart twice: availability and cart count must reflect the current state. Re-run PSI mobile; LCP and 'Defer offscreen images' unchanged or better.
findings.correction: (1) Lazy Load Background Images is a Performance-tab setting, not a Features experiment; the LiteSpeed Third Party page (July 27, 2026) listing it under 'Features tab' is stale, as is Elementor's element-caching help page still calling Element Caching 'inactive by default' (changelog 3.31.0 'Activated "Element Caching" experiment for all sites', 3.32.0 'Merged Element Caching feature and moved to Performance tab'). (2) There is no site-wide 'Default' state for Element Cache; the only off switch is 'Disable' in the TTL select (per-element Default/Inactive/Active exists). (3) Inline Font Icons (e_font_icon_svg) is a stable experiment with default_active only for installs created on >=3.17.0, so older sites may still have it off; Optimized Markup defaults inactive except new sites >=3.30.0; Optimized CSS Files is alpha/inactive. (4) FacetWP (Mar 23, 2026): 'Elementor's Element Caching feature is incompatible with FacetWP', now shipping widgets with Cache Settings 'Inactive' -- the same class of risk as JetSmartFilters results; the safe default for shop/booking/filter sites is Element Cache = Disable until each dynamic widget is verified.

findings.claim: LiteSpeed Cache Guest Mode and Guest Optimization must never be auto-enabled on an Elementor site: they inflate lab scores by serving a first-visit page that is then swapped by AJAX, and both the official docs and 2026 field reports document layout shift, momentary wrong language/prices and broken JS-dependent elements.
findings.detail: LiteSpeed General settings doc (Aug 14 2026): Guest Mode (default OFF) serves a default cached page "for a visitor's first request" with no ESI and no cache varies, then "an AJAX call is used to load the correct version"; warning: "On some complicated sites, this can mean that the wrong language, incorrect pricing, or other problematic content may be momentarily displayed"; it adds cache varies/crawlers and requires Cloudflare APO off. Guest Optimization (default ON but inert without Guest Mode) forces "the maximum level of page optimization" (CCSS, UCSS, VPI, separate mobile cache) even if those settings are off, deducts QUIC.cloud quota, can create thousands of UCSS files, and "can mask any real problems your site may have ... turn this feature off" to get an accurate PSI evaluation. Perfmatters' LiteSpeed guide: turn both off, "These will interfere with Perfmatters". WebOps field notes (Apr 30 2026, 84-site fleet): Guest Mode on an Elementor site with a hero slider: mobile score 50 to 19, CLS 0.087 to 0.896, TBT +320 ms, because the swap-in "fires partway through paint and re-arranges the layout"; Guest Optimization had earlier deferred Gravity Forms JS and produced a dead form. wordpress.org LiteSpeed thread (Elementor site, 2026): header unstyled for 1-2 s on first/incognito visits, gone with /?LSCWP_CTRL=before_optm; peer advice: turn off Guest Mode and Guest Optimization. LiteSpeed's troubleshooting doc requires adding your IP to Guest Mode IPs to even reproduce what first-time visitors see. Observed sites running LiteSpeed (limnoupolis, staging, onar) should have both OFF.
findings.breaks_when: Any first visit (every PSI run and every real new visitor): page is rendered from the guest copy, then UCSS/CCSS generated for the guest view is applied and the personalised DOM is swapped in, causing CLS on pages with sliders/motion effects, unstyled headers, wrong language on Polylang/WPML sites, cookie banner absent, forms dead until scripts load; also silently spends QUIC.cloud quota and disk.
findings.how_to_apply: LiteSpeed Cache > General > General Settings: Guest Mode = OFF, Guest Optimization = OFF; Save, Toolbox > Purge All. Reach first-visit speed instead with page cache + crawler, VPI, and Perfmatters/LiteSpeed delay/defer configured explicitly. If a client insists on testing Guest Mode, add the tester's IP to General > Tuning > Guest Mode IPs, test incognito, and remove the IP afterwards.
findings.how_to_verify: Incognito first load at 390px: no header flash, CLS in DevTools Performance panel equals the logged-out second load; the page source contains no guest.vary.php/Guest Mode script; x-litespeed-cache header shows hit on second request. PSI mobile score should be stable across three runs (Guest Mode often shows a high first run and a low real-user CrUX). Check QUIC.cloud dashboard quota does not drop after enabling other features.

findings.claim: CSS Combine and JS Combine must never be auto-enabled in any of the five plugins; minify is safe and low-gain, with W3TC's 'Auto' minify mode and 'Combine & Minify' method being the one minify setting repeatedly reported to break Elementor.
findings.detail: Perfmatters: "Uncombine your CSS. Combining CSS is a deprecated optimization technique since HTTP/2" and "For Delay JavaScript to work properly ... turn off any feature from third-party plugins that combine your JavaScript files (Autoptimize, LiteSpeed Cache, WP Rocket)". WP Rocket: "The Combine JavaScript files feature will be disabled when using Delay JavaScript execution"; LazyLoad for CSS backgrounds "not fully compatible with combined CSS"; combine creates one file per page when inline JS varies (cache/min folder bloat); Elementor post CSS auto-excluded from Minify CSS. LiteSpeed ts-optimize: combine with randomised selectors causes frequent cache misses and "Disk Space Filling Fast" (one combined file per page, two with Cache Mobile), fix is CSS Excludes/JS Excludes or disabling combine; 7.9 fixed 'CSS Combine serving unstyled pages'. Savvy (v7.9 guide, Aug 2026): CSS Combine OFF, JS Combine OFF "Not recommended when using HTTP/2". LiteSpeed UCSS is the exception: it requires CSS Combine ON, so the per-page combined file is the UCSS output. W3TC 2.10.7: General Settings > Minify mode Auto vs Manual; BoldGrid's own docs: "in some cases, Auto minify can break styling"; JS/CSS Minify Method options Combine & Minify / Minify Only / Combine Only; support threads: Elementor site lost CSS for visitors with minify on (Jan 2023), fixes attempted via 'Never minify the following JS/CSS files' with wp-content/plugins/elementor-pro/assets/js/* etc.; a YITH Booking calendar broke under W3TC minify, fix: exclude the plugin JS in Performance > Minify > Advanced "Never minify the following JS files" (relative paths) and enable YITH's "Update non-available dates on loading (AJAX)"; Divi guide notes 'Disable minify for logged-in users' so the builder works. 2.10.7 added caching selected external scripts locally for auto minify. Minify gain is small because Elementor ships .min files already (WP Rocket Semrush doc).
findings.breaks_when: Combine: Delay JS/RUCSS lose script order (Elementor frontend before webpack runtime), cache misses on every visit when inline JS/CSS differs per page, disk fills, lazy background CSS breaks, 404s when the host cleans the combined dir. W3TC Auto minify with Combine: missing styles for logged-out visitors, Elementor editor fails to load, YITH/WooCommerce Bookings calendar JS errors.
findings.how_to_apply: LiteSpeed: CSS Minify ON, CSS Combine OFF (ON only with UCSS), JS Minify ON, JS Combine OFF, HTML Minify ON, Remove Query Strings ON, Remove WordPress Emoji ON. Perfmatters: Assets > Minify CSS ON, Minify JavaScript ON (no combine exists). WP Rocket: Minify CSS files ON, Minify JavaScript files ON, Combine JavaScript files OFF. FlyingPress: Minify CSS & JavaScript ON (no combine). W3TC: either Minify disabled (let Perfmatters minify) or Minify ON with Minify mode Manual or Auto + method 'Minify Only' for both CSS and JS, 'Disable minify for logged-in users' checked, 'Never minify' entries for wp-content/plugins/elementor/assets/*, wp-content/plugins/elementor-pro/assets/*, wp-content/uploads/elementor/css/* and the booking plugin's JS.
findings.how_to_verify: View source logged out: Elementor's frontend.min.js, webpack.runtime.min.js, post-*.css load as separate files; no /cache/min/ or /wp-content/litespeed/css|js/ combined files; open the Elementor editor and save a page; load a booking product in incognito and pick a date; check console for syntax errors; monitor wp-content/litespeed or cache/min folder size for a week. PSI: 'Minify CSS/JS' audits pass; score change expected to be 0-2 points.

findings.claim: Page cache is the safest high-gain setting on every plugin, but on the WooCommerce + booking sites it must come with explicit exclusions for add-to-cart, wc-ajax, Store API and booking product pages, a TTL shorter than the WooCommerce session, and an ESI/vary strategy for the mini-cart.
findings.detail: LiteSpeed 7.9.1 Cache doc (Sep 29 2026): My Account, Checkout and Cart excluded by default; WooCommerce tab: "Product Update Interval" purge options, "Vary for Mini Cart" (separate cached copy when cart not empty, for themes that render the cart server-side), "We highly recommend that you enable ESI when using WooCommerce" (ESI needs LSWS Enterprise, ADC or QUIC.cloud, not OpenLiteSpeed); "ESI Nonces" converts nonces to ESI blocks because "Nonces often expire before the site TTL"; Default Public Cache TTL 604800; "Do Not Cache Cookies" warning: a cookie on every page disables the whole cache (do not add woocommerce_items_in_cart); 7.8 purges product cache when orders are cancelled. StackHarbor (Sep 5 2026) Do Not Cache URIs: /cart /checkout /my-account /wc-api/ /wp-json/wc/store; Do Not Cache Query Strings: add-to-cart (otherwise a second shopper's add-to-cart can be answered from cache); never blanket-exclude /wp-json; mini-cart via ESI 'Cart Totals' or keep wc-cart-fragments. FlyingPress: Cart, Checkout, My Account auto-excluded; if the theme does not update the cart count via AJAX add woocommerce_items_in_cart to Caching > Bypass Cache for Cookies (reduces hit ratio); product edits purge product + archive pages. WP Rocket: automatic Woo exclusions; per-visitor logic via mandatory/dynamic cookies. W3TC: WooCommerce Bookings calendar failed because ?wc-ajax=wc_bookings_find_booked_day_blocks returned 404 under page cache; BoldGrid's fix is Page Cache > Advanced > 'Never cache pages associated with these categories/tags' or 'Never cache the following pages: /product/*', or Fragment Cache mfunc comments around the calendar. WooCommerce Bookings troubleshooting doc: cache lifetimes longer than the wp_woocommerce_session_ token (2 days) break the calendar (403 in console); exclude WooCommerce cookies from caching; disable Cloudflare Rocket Loader. YITH Booking: enable Booking Form setting "Update non-available dates on loading (AJAX)" so availability is fetched live on cached pages. Perfmatters auto-excludes cart/checkout/account from its optimisations and offers "Disable cart fragments" and "Disable WooCommerce scripts and styles" on non-shop pages.
findings.breaks_when: TTL exceeds the booking/session lifetime (stale availability, expired nonce -> 'security check failed', 403 on wc-ajax); add-to-cart or wc-ajax URLs get cached; a translated or renamed slug (/kalathi instead of /cart, Polylang prefix) does not match the default exclusion; the theme renders the mini-cart server-side without AJAX and no vary/ESI is set (visitor sees another shopper's cart count); CDN edge caches checkout.
findings.how_to_apply: LiteSpeed: Cache > Excludes > Do Not Cache URIs add /wc-api/ and /wp-json/wc/store plus the booking product URIs if availability is rendered server-side; Do Not Cache Query Strings add add-to-cart, removed_item, undo_item; WooCommerce tab: Product Update Interval = purge product and categories on stock change; Vary for Mini Cart ON if the header cart is not AJAX; ESI ON with Cache Admin Bar/Comment Form if on LSWS Enterprise; ESI Nonces add the booking plugin nonce names found in its JS; TTL: Default Public Cache TTL 86400 on booking/shop sites (never above 172800). FlyingPress: Exclude Pages from Cache add /order-received/ and booking confirmation; Bypass Cache for Cookies add woocommerce_items_in_cart only if cart count breaks. W3TC: Page Cache > Advanced > Never cache the following pages: booking product URLs, Rejected cookies: wp_woocommerce_session_, woocommerce_items_in_cart. Perfmatters: WooCommerce > Disable cart fragments only on sites without a header mini-cart; Disable WooCommerce scripts and styles ON.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -sI the shop page twice and check x-litespeed-cache: hit (or x-flying-press-cache / x-wp-rocket) on the second; curl -sI /cart/, /checkout/, '/product/x/?add-to-cart=ID', /wp-json/wc/store/v1/cart and confirm no hit. Two incognito browsers: add an item in one, confirm the other still shows an empty cart. Booking: open a bookable product in incognito 10 minutes after the first visit, pick dates, confirm availability matches admin and no 403/404 for wc-ajax in the Network tab; let the page sit longer than the TTL and repeat. After a stock/price edit, confirm the product and its category page update without manual purge.

findings.claim: On the Polylang/WPML sites the page cache must vary by language and browser-language redirect must be handled explicitly, otherwise visitors get the wrong language from cache or the home page is never cached.
findings.detail: WP Rocket doc 76: Polylang and WPML detected automatically; with Polylang 'Detect browser language' the first visit is uncached until the pll_language cookie exists (doc 1755 lists pll_language as a mandatory cookie); WPML Multicurrency uses wcml_client_currency/wcml_client_country cookies; for a home-page redirect to /el/ add '/' to Advanced Rules > Never Cache URL(s). FlyingPress: WPML, Polylang, TranslatePress, Weglot supported; each language cached separately and purged/preloaded per language. LiteSpeed Third Party: WPML compatible, "Separate cache copies are stored for each page for each language"; Polylang browser detection needs .htaccess vary rules on Accept-Language (LiteSpeed support, wordpress.org): RewriteCond %{HTTP:Accept-Language} el [NC] / RewriteRule .* - [E=Cache-Vary:%{ENV:LSCACHE_VARY_VALUE}+greek] then purge all; Guest Mode explicitly risks "the wrong language ... momentarily displayed"; LiteSpeed 7.0.0.1 improved WPML sync_conf compatibility. W3TC: no language-specific docs found; use separate cache keys via cookie/URL prefix. Polylang's own position (quoted in WP Rocket/Polylang threads): browser language detection cannot work on a cached home page because PHP must run.
findings.breaks_when: Browser-language redirect is on and the home page is cached (redirect never fires, or the first cached language is served to everyone); a language cookie is added to 'Do Not Cache Cookies' (whole site uncached); Guest Mode serves the default-language guest copy first; translated Woo slugs (/kalathi/) are not in the exclusion list; LiteSpeed object cache stale language switcher (one 2026 wordpress.org report fixed by disabling Object Cache).
findings.how_to_apply: Prefer URL-based languages (/el/, /en/) and turn off automatic browser-language redirect in Polylang/WPML, or accept an uncached first visit (WP Rocket) / add the Accept-Language vary rules (LiteSpeed). WP Rocket: nothing else; if the root redirects to the default language add '/' to Never Cache URL(s). LiteSpeed: keep Guest Mode OFF; verify translated cart/checkout slugs appear in Do Not Cache URIs. FlyingPress: nothing extra. All: purge all after language or slug changes.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -sI -H 'Accept-Language: en' https://site/ and with 'el' and compare the Location/HTML lang attribute and the cache header on second requests; load each language home in two incognito profiles with different browser languages; switch language on a cached page and confirm the switcher and menu change; run PSI for both language home pages (both must be cache hits).

findings.claim: Consent banners (Complianz, Cookie-Script, FAZ Cookie Manager) and GTM consent-mode defaults must be excluded from Delay JS and from Guest-Mode/UCSS processing, while GTM, GA4, Ads and the Facebook pixel themselves are the right things to delay; Complianz publishes the exact strings, the other two do not.
findings.detail: Complianz doc (Jan 22 2025): delaying or minifying its assets causes the banner not to display, wrong language, re-appearing banner and consent not recorded; exclusion keywords complianz and cmplz plus complianz-gdpr/cookiebanner/js/complianz.min.js (free) and complianz-gdpr-premium/pro/tcf/build/index.js, complianz-gdpr-premium/pro/tcf-stub/build/index.js, complianz-gdpr-premium/cookiebanner/js/complianz.min.js (premium), entered in WP Rocket > File Optimization > Excluded JavaScript Files and LiteSpeed > Page Optimization > Tuning > JS Excludes (and JS Deferred/Delayed Excludes); cmplz_activated_divi_recaptcha fixes rocketlazyloadscript appearing inside gtm.js. Perfmatters common exclusions list: Complianz -> complianz; Cookiebot -> consent.cookiebot.com; CookieYes -> cookie-law-info-public.js, cookie-law-info-js-extra, jquery.min.js; Cookie Notice -> /cookie-notice/js/front.min.js, cnArgs; Perfmatters YouTube thumbnails need cmplz-iframe excluded from lazy load. LiteSpeed Third Party lists 'Cookie Notice & Compliance for GDPR / CCPA' as interfering with JS Delay; a Lightweight Cookie Notice user reported the banner missing in PSI screenshots under Guest Mode even after adding its JS to JS Excludes, Deferred/Delayed Excludes and Guest Mode JS Excludes (unresolved). Perfmatters delay strings for the trackers: /gtm.js, /gtag/js, gtag(, /gtm-, /gtm., fbevents.js, fbq(, google-analytics.com/analytics.js; FlyingPress auto-delays external domains (googletagmanager.com, connect.facebook.net) and lets you exclude by unique domain ("Avoid generic terms like facebook"). Perfmatters 'Local Analytics' can self-host gtag v4 (gtagv4.js) but on sites with GTM containers consolidation into one container is the lever (audit: 5 tags on the slow sites). No vendor documentation was found for Cookie-Script or FAZ Cookie Manager exclusion strings.
findings.breaks_when: Banner script is delayed: PSI screenshot and real first paint have no banner, consent choice is not stored, banner reappears on every page, GTM consent defaults run after tags fire (consent-mode conversions lost); banner CSS removed by RUCSS (unstyled banner); GTM delayed without timeout on pages where the marketer counts pageviews without interaction.
findings.how_to_apply: Delay list (Perfmatters 'Only delay specified scripts' / FlyingPress third-party / WP Rocket Delay JS / LiteSpeed JS Delayed Includes): googletagmanager.com, /gtm.js, /gtag/js, gtag(, fbevents.js, fbq(, connect.facebook.net, static.hotjar.com, clarity.ms. Exclude from delay/defer/UCSS: complianz, cmplz, the complianz.min.js paths (Complianz); for Cookie-Script add cookie-script.com and the script id string from its embed; for FAZ Cookie Manager add the plugin folder path /wp-content/plugins/<faz-folder>/ and its inline object name, and add the banner's root class (e.g. .cmplz-cookiebanner) to the RUCSS safelist. Enable a delay timeout (Perfmatters 15 s; W3TC Delay Scripts Timeout) when pageview accuracy matters. Consolidate duplicate gtag/AW tags into one GTM container before delaying.
findings.how_to_verify: PSI mobile filmstrip and final screenshot show the cookie banner; in incognito, accept cookies and reload: banner stays hidden, Tag Assistant shows consent default before any tag; GA4 realtime registers a visit after a scroll; console has no cmplz/complianz errors; 'Reduce unused JavaScript' no longer lists gtm.js/fbevents.js in the initial load.
findings.correction: FlyingPress's 'Delay Specific Scripts on Interaction' doc lists 'cookie-law-info' (CookieYes) under 'Common Third-party Scripts to Delay', and the CretaForce fork ships that exact string in its default js_delay_selected list together with 'grecaptcha.execute'. That default does what Complianz/Perfmatters say never to do (delayed consent banner = banner missing from the PSI screenshot, GTM consent defaults fire late, consent not stored). The how-to must include removing 'cookie-law-info' (and the FAZ Cookie Manager path once captured) from the FlyingPress delay list, not only adding exclusions in Perfmatters/WP Rocket/LiteSpeed.

findings.claim: Defer JS is a medium-gain, low-risk default on every plugin, with two documented Elementor breakages: the sticky header (jquery.sticky) and inline scripts in HTML widgets that call jQuery before it loads; the audited sites have up to 251 HTML widgets, so defer must be tested per template.
findings.detail: WP Rocket 'Load JavaScript deferred' adds defer + data-rocket-defer to every script and wraps jQuery-dependent inline scripts in DOMContentLoaded (skips inline scripts containing DOMContentLoaded or document.write, or without jQuery/$); doc 1745: it "may break Elementor's sticky effect", fix = add to the deferred exclusions \/jquery(-migrate)?-?([0-9.]+)?(.min|.slim|.slim.min)?.js(\?(.*))?( |'|"|>|$) and /elementor-pro/assets/lib/sticky/jquery.sticky.min.js, and the same to Delay JS if on; Elementor editor may blank when server resources are low (raise PHP memory). Perfmatters 'Defer JavaScript' adds defer to all scripts, 'Include Inline Scripts' (encodes inline, may raise TBT on small sites), 'Include jQuery' (advanced; "We recommend testing this separately or leaving it off ... page builder"), common exclusions hooks.min.js and i18n.min.js, per-page opt-out; recommends leaving 'Remove jQuery Migrate' off with Elementor. LiteSpeed 'Load JS Deferred: Deferred' with 'JS Deferred/Delayed Excludes'; 'JS Delayed Includes' does not work for inline JS in Deferred mode. FlyingPress 'Defer loading' mode of Delay All JavaScript (native defer, "ideal if your site relies heavily on JavaScript-based elements"), exclude hooks.min.js + i18n.min.js (OnlineMediaMasters, Feb 2026). W3TC Minify > JS: embed 'Non-blocking using defer' before </head> and after <body> (BoldGrid Divi guide), only when minify is on. WP Rocket CLS doc: defer can raise CLS when JS is needed to display above-the-fold elements (exclude those files).
findings.breaks_when: HTML-widget or theme inline script runs before jQuery/elementorFrontend ('jQuery is not defined', '$ is not a function'); sticky header never fixes; Google Maps/booking widgets whose inline init runs before their library; a script relies on document.write; jQuery itself deferred while a non-deferred inline script depends on it.
findings.how_to_apply: Perfmatters: JavaScript > Defer JavaScript ON, Include jQuery OFF, Include Inline Scripts OFF initially; Exclude from Deferral: hooks.min.js, i18n.min.js plus any file named in console errors. WP Rocket: Load JavaScript deferred ON with the two sticky exclusions above. LiteSpeed: Load JS Deferred = Deferred, JS Deferred/Delayed Excludes: jquery.sticky.min.js if the header breaks. FlyingPress: Delay All JavaScript mode = Defer loading or Load when idle; exclusions hooks.min.js, i18n.min.js. Move inline <script> blocks out of Elementor HTML widgets into an enqueued file with defer and page conditions (Perfmatters Code Snippets or theme).
findings.how_to_verify: Console on home, a product and the booking page shows no ReferenceError; scroll 600px and confirm the sticky header is fixed and the sticky 'active' styles apply; open Google Maps / booking calendar widgets; PSI 'Eliminate render-blocking resources' lists no JS; CLS unchanged.

findings.claim: Per-page script unloading (Perfmatters Script Manager, FlyingPress Bloat settings, W3TC Pro Remove CSS/JS) is the only lever for the 100-870 KB of unused JS from add-on packs, booking plugins and WooCommerce on brochure pages, but it is manual and must run in test mode first; LiteSpeed has no equivalent.
findings.detail: Perfmatters Script Manager: enable under Assets, then open any front-end page; disable a plugin or individual CSS/JS 'Everywhere' with exceptions, 'Current URL', regex, by post type, and by user state (Logged In/Out); 'Test mode' applies rules only to logged-in admins; 'Display dependencies' shows jQuery dependents; 'MU Mode' disables whole plugins (queries + inline CSS/JS) per URL (several MU-mode bug fixes in 2.6.7-2.6.9, e.g. wrong plugin disabled by folder prefix, front-page rules leaking to search/feeds, Woo shop page handling); changelog notes 'additional compatibility with Elementor when using the Script Manager to disable certain Elementor scripts + styles'; WooCommerce options: Disable WooCommerce scripts and styles (non-shop pages), Disable cart fragments, Disable widgets, Disable status meta box; Perfmatters recommends leaving 'Remove jQuery Migrate' off with Elementor. FlyingPress 'Bloat settings' (disable block editor CSS, dashicons, emojis, jQuery migrate, XML-RPC, RSS, oEmbeds, WP cron) are site-wide only. W3TC 2.10 Pro 'Remove CSS/JS' (Performance > General Settings > User Experience > Remove Unwanted/Unused CSS/JS): a Remove List of absolute URLs for the homepage plus per-file Include/Exclude rules by URL or content match; find candidates with the Coverage tool or PSI 'Reduce unused JavaScript'. Audit evidence: unused JS 310 KB (onar, Premium Addons + Dynamic.ooo), 689-871 KB (limnoupolis), 192 KB (vorenia); marakaki already disables 131 widgets.
findings.breaks_when: A script is unloaded on a page that needs it inside a modal, filter result, popup or template part (JetSmartFilters results, Elementor Pro popups loading forms, Woo add-to-cart on a landing page); MU Mode rule written against 'Current URL' when the same path serves search/feeds (fixed 2.6.9); jQuery or jQuery Migrate disabled globally on an Elementor site.
findings.how_to_apply: Perfmatters > Assets > Script Manager ON, Settings: Test Mode ON, Display Dependencies ON. Per template: disable WooCommerce, booking plugin, JetSmartFilters, Premium Addons/Dynamic.ooo bundles 'Everywhere' except the post types/URLs that use them (regex for /product/, /booking/); disable Font Awesome/eicons bundles where Inline Font Icons is active; disable dashicons for logged-out users. Keep jQuery, elementor frontend, webpack runtime enabled. Turn Test Mode off only after the click-through passes. W3TC Pro alternative: Remove CSS/JS rules per plugin directory with Action = Include and the shop/booking URLs listed. FlyingPress: Bloat settings ON except jQuery Migrate (test) and block editor CSS when Woo blocks are used.
findings.how_to_verify: With Test Mode on, compare logged-in admin view vs incognito; then after publishing, in incognito open every template and trigger popups, filters, forms, add-to-cart, calendar, maps; console clean. PSI 'Reduce unused JavaScript' bytes drop by the size of the unloaded bundles; requests count drops (audit baseline 127-147 requests on slow sites). Re-check after each plugin update because handles change.

findings.claim: Self-hosting Google Fonts is safe and worth doing on every plugin, but for Greek sites the subset must explicitly include Greek: Perfmatters 'Limit Subsets' defaults to Latin only and would silently drop Greek glyphs to the fallback font.
findings.detail: Perfmatters Fonts > Local Google Fonts; 'Limit Subsets' default Latin ("If you're running a non-English site, many times Latin and Latin Extended will be needed" - Greek must be ticked); built-in RUCSS exclusions for Elementor local font stylesheets; 2.6.5 added domain/content-type validation to font downloads. WP Rocket Media > 'Self-host Google Fonts locally' rewrites fonts.googleapis.com CSS and fonts.gstatic.com files into /wp-content/cache/fonts/; only handles Google Fonts in the HTML (not fonts loaded from inside CSS files or injected later); toggling it purges Used CSS and minified CSS; filter rocket_exclude_locally_host_fonts; 'Preload fonts' detects critical fonts; FOUT doc: WP Rocket forces font-display: swap in Google Fonts requests, minified CSS, critical CSS and Used CSS. FlyingPress 'Self-Host Google Fonts' (automatic, cache folder wp-content/cache/flying-press/) and automatic 'Preload Fonts' (critical fonts only). LiteSpeed: 'Load Google Fonts Asynchronously' (adds preconnect; a 6.5.4 fix for fonts broken with Async), 'Remove Google Fonts' only when replacements are hosted locally, 'Font Display Optimization: Swap', 'Localize Resources' is for JS not fonts. Elementor Pro Custom Fonts + Settings > Advanced > Google Fonts: Disable is the cleanest path (the fast audited sites use 2 families; Elementor 4 'Inline Font Icons' removes the icon font). PSI counts 'Ensure text remains visible during webfont load' and font-display failures were observed on 8 of 10 sites.
findings.breaks_when: Subset list omits Greek (headings in Greek render in the fallback font, often unnoticed in English-only QA); a font is loaded via @import inside a theme CSS file (WP Rocket cannot localise it); 'Remove Google Fonts' is turned on before local fonts exist; too many weights preloaded (PSI warns about preloading non-critical assets).
findings.how_to_apply: Preferred: convert the 2 families to .woff2 with Greek + Latin ranges, upload in Elementor > Custom Fonts, set Elementor > Settings > Advanced > Google Fonts = Disable, keep font-display swap. Otherwise: Perfmatters Fonts > Local Google Fonts ON, Display Swap, Limit Subsets ON with Latin + Greek (+ Latin Extended, Greek Extended if used), Preload the 1-2 above-the-fold woff2 files; WP Rocket: Self-host Google Fonts ON + Preload fonts ON; FlyingPress: Self-Host Google Fonts ON (Preload fonts automatic); LiteSpeed: Load Google Fonts Asynchronously ON, Font Display Optimization Swap, Remove Google Fonts only after fonts are self-hosted.
findings.how_to_verify: Network tab: zero requests to fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com; the local font CSS contains @font-face blocks with unicode-range covering U+0370-03FF (Greek); a Greek heading and a Latin heading render in the same family (compare computed font-family in DevTools > Rendered Fonts); PSI 'Ensure text remains visible during webfont load' passes; no more than 2-3 font preloads in <head>; CLS unchanged.
findings.correction: Rule: Local Google Fonts ON with Limit Subsets OFF is safe for Greek (all subsets kept); if Limit Subsets is turned on, tick Greek (+ Greek Extended) and verify unicode-range U+0370-03FF in the generated CSS. The doc does not list the subset checkboxes, so Greek's presence in the UI is inferred from Google Fonts' subset names (medium). Bigger miss: Elementor 4.x has its own 'Load Google Fonts Locally' under Settings > Performance (option elementor_local_google_fonts; changelog 3.28.0 'enabled it by default for all websites', 3.32.1 'Disabled Load Google Fonts locally on all sites by default' and 'Moved ... to the Performance tab'; Elementor help: 'Starting with Elementor version 3.32.1 ... the default setting was switched to Disabled'). It must not run alongside Perfmatters/WP Rocket/FlyingPress font self-hosting, and sites that enabled it before 3.32.1 may still have it on. Also Elementor > Settings > Advanced > 'Google Fonts Load' defaults to 'auto' ('Default') with 'Recommended: Swap' in the field text; 8 of 10 audited sites fail the font-display audit, so set Swap regardless of plugin. The CretaForce FlyingPress fork added in 4.20.0 'self-hosting Google Fonts loaded through CSS @import rules'.

findings.claim: Lazy rendering below-the-fold sections with content-visibility:auto (FlyingPress 'Lazy render elements', WP Rocket 'Automatic Lazy Rendering', LiteSpeed 'HTML Lazy Load Selectors', Perfmatters 'Lazy load elements') cuts TBT/INP on the 700-1200-widget Elementor pages, but it is automatic in two plugins and needs an exclusion for anchor-scroll targets, forms and map/booking containers.
findings.detail: FlyingPress 5.x: 'Lazy Render Elements' is cloud-detected and applied during caching, only to elements below the fold, exclusions by keyword matching tag/class/id (e.g. contact-form, map-block); 5.0.3 fixed lazy-render properties appended invalidly to style attributes; 4.15.0 added the on/off switch. WP Rocket 'Automatic Lazy Rendering' (doc 1835): on by default with no settings toggle, applies to div/main/footer/section/article/header, beacon script wpr-beacon.min.js marks elements data-rocket-location-hash then data-wpr-lazyrender="1" with <style id="rocket-lazyrender-inline-css">[data-wpr-lazyrender]{content-visibility:auto}</style>, depends on Mobile Cache staying on, cleared with 'Clear Priority Elements', exclusion only via a helper plugin or filter rocket_lrc_optimization false. LiteSpeed 'HTML Lazy Load Selectors' is a manual list (#id/.class) that defers loading of that HTML until it scrolls into view (different mechanism, content is not in the initial DOM). Perfmatters 'Lazy load elements' is manual by selector (doc opened but not quoted here). Elementor pages on the audited sites have 700-1200 widgets and 400-850 containers, where PSI 'Avoid an excessive DOM size' and TBT are flagged.
findings.breaks_when: In-page anchor links or 'scroll to section' land at the wrong offset because lazily rendered sections have no intrinsic height yet; a form, Google Map, booking calendar or JetSmartFilters results container below the fold initialises against a non-rendered element; entrance-animation waypoints fire late; LiteSpeed's selector variant hides content from crawlers and from the first paint (not in DOM); WP Rocket's version is applied silently after the beacon run so the first measurement differs from later ones.
findings.how_to_apply: FlyingPress: Rendering > Lazy render elements ON; Exclusions: the booking form container class, map containers, elementor-location-footer if the footer has a form, any id used as an anchor target. WP Rocket: leave on; if anchors/forms break, exclude via the helper plugin or add_filter('rocket_lrc_optimization','__return_false') on affected templates; keep Mobile Cache ON. LiteSpeed: do not auto-populate HTML Lazy Load Selectors; use only for heavy below-the-fold blocks (e.g. .elementor-widget-google_maps parent, review widgets) after a visual check. Perfmatters: Lazy load elements only on long archive/landing pages.
findings.how_to_verify: View source: data-wpr-lazyrender="1" or content-visibility styles present only on sections below the first screen; click every anchor/menu link that targets a section and confirm the landing offset; submit the footer form; open the map and calendar; Lighthouse TBT and 'Avoid an excessive DOM size' improve; CLS unchanged; test both mobile and desktop UA since they are processed independently.
findings.correction: FlyingPress's cloud-detected lazy render is 5.x only; the CretaForce 4.22.1 fork has js_lazy_render = true by default with a manual js_lazy_render_selectors list, so on cretaforums.gr and (per the audit) voreniahorizon.gr lazy render is on but only for selectors the agency enters -- it is not automatic there. The two automatic implementations are WP Rocket and official FlyingPress 5, neither of which runs on any of the 10 sites; for the fleet, lazy rendering is a manual, opt-in lever everywhere.

findings.claim: Cloudflare Rocket Loader must be off on every Elementor/booking site, Cloudflare APO must not be combined with LiteSpeed Guest Mode/ESI, and QUIC.cloud is only required for LiteSpeed's UCSS/CCSS/VPI/LQIP/ESI-on-OpenLiteSpeed features; DNS prefetch/preconnect are safe but low-gain.
findings.detail: Elementor help (Feb 11 2024): Rocket Loader "automatically changing the scripts to load asynchronously, which breaks the editor"; bypass rules Site URL/*elementor* and Site URL/?elementor_library=*; WooCommerce Bookings troubleshooting: "disable Rocket Loader as it might be interfering with the calendar's JavaScript". LiteSpeed Cache docs: "If you are using CloudFlare, do not enable Automatic Platform Optimization (APO)" for ESI and Guest Mode; Third Party table: Cloudflare compatible only without APO; WP REST API Authentication plugin blocks /litespeed/v1 needed by QUIC.cloud; QUIC.cloud quota is consumed by UCSS, CCSS, VPI, LQIP and (if Guest Optimization) forced generation; ESI requires LSWS Enterprise, ADC or QUIC.cloud CDN. Perfmatters' LiteSpeed guide: Cloudflare APO works alongside LiteSpeed but as a separate cache layer to purge; QUIC.cloud is the LiteSpeed-native alternative. FlyingPress has dedicated APO and full-page Cloudflare caching guides and sells FlyingCDN. Perfmatters 'Preconnect' and 'DNS Prefetch' and LiteSpeed 'DNS Prefetch', 'DNS Prefetch Control', 'DNS Preconnect' (format //www.example.com; docs note they speed up third-party connections, not the site itself); W3TC Pro 'Preload Requests' adds dns-prefetch/preconnect/preload tags. Self-hosting fonts and delaying GTM remove most preconnect needs.
findings.breaks_when: Rocket Loader on: Elementor editor stuck on the loading screen, booking calendar JS, delayed/deferred scripts double-processed; APO + LiteSpeed Guest Mode/ESI: stale or wrong personalised fragments, double purging; QUIC.cloud node unreachable or REST endpoint blocked by a security plugin: UCSS/CCSS/VPI queues stall and pages fall back silently; too many preconnects (PSI 'Avoid ... too many preconnect').
findings.how_to_apply: Cloudflare dashboard: Speed > Optimization > Rocket Loader OFF (or page rules excluding *elementor* and ?elementor_library=*); APO only with WP Rocket/FlyingPress (per their guides), never with LiteSpeed ESI/Guest Mode. LiteSpeed: enable QUIC.cloud (General > Online Services) only if UCSS/CCSS/VPI will be used and allow /wp-json/litespeed/v1 in the firewall; otherwise keep CDN at Cloudflare/BunnyCDN mapping. Preconnect list limited to 1-3 origins actually used in the first paint (e.g. the CDN host); DNS Prefetch for GTM/Facebook only if they are not delayed.
findings.how_to_verify: Open the Elementor editor and the booking page with Rocket Loader state changed; check response header cf-apo-via absent when LiteSpeed is the page cache; LiteSpeed dashboard shows QUIC.cloud queues processing (UCSS/VPI counters move); PSI 'Preconnect to required origins' passes and there are no more than 3 <link rel=preconnect> in <head>.

findings.claim: Object cache (Redis/Memcached/LSMCD) is safe to enable and helps WooCommerce/booking TTFB for uncached requests, but it does not move the PSI lab score of cached pages, and LiteSpeed's object cache has 2026 Elementor reports (editor/global settings, WPML switcher) fixed by disabling it, so treat it as a server-side win to verify, not a PageSpeed lever.
findings.detail: LiteSpeed Cache > Object: Memcached/LSMCD/Redis, 'Do Not Cache Groups' default 'comment counts plugins' (docs suggest adding posts/post_meta then users/user_meta for Memcached issues), 'Persistent Connection' ON, 'Cache WP Admin'; Perfmatters' LiteSpeed guide recommends Object Cache ON. wordpress.org LiteSpeed thread (2026, Elementor site): one user's broken editor and unapplied Global Settings were fixed by Cache > Object > Object Cache OFF (another report tied a vanished WPML language switcher after 7.8.0.1 to Object Cache). WP Rocket 3.23.3.1 fixed orphaned Redis keys with infinite TTL from its Above The Fold/Used CSS/Lazy Render tables. FlyingPress ships a 'Redis Object Caching' guide; W3TC Object Cache Disk is recommended only for shared hosting (BoldGrid Divi guide) and 2.10.7 fixed admin invalidation when admin object caching is disabled. Audit: transients 6,938 on marakaki and autoload up to 720 KB; object cache helps those but so does cleanup.
findings.breaks_when: Memcached with large post_meta (Elementor stores 1-71 MB of _elementor_data per site) exceeds item size and returns stale/partial data; stale options after Elementor regenerates CSS or kit settings; Redis shared across staging and production without a prefix (staging.limnoupolis.gr and limnoupolis.gr) serve each other's data; WP admin object caching masking saves.
findings.how_to_apply: Prefer Redis over Memcached; LiteSpeed Cache > Object: Object Cache ON, Method Redis, Persistent Connection ON, add posts and post_meta to Do Not Cache Groups only if Elementor saves misbehave, set a unique Redis Database ID per site (staging vs production). W3TC: Object Cache Redis/Memcached only on VPS, Disk on shared; FlyingPress/WP Rocket: use the host's Redis drop-in. Run transient cleanup (LiteSpeed Database > Clean All Transients) first.
findings.how_to_verify: Before/after server-timing or TTFB on an uncached request (curl -o /dev/null -s -w '%{time_starttransfer}' with a nocache query); save a page in Elementor and change a Global Color: changes appear on the front end after purge; language switcher and mini-cart correct; redis-cli info keyspace shows separate DBs for staging and production; PSI lab score unchanged (expected).
findings.correction: The 'Add posts and post_meta to the Do Not Cache Groups ... then users and user_meta' advice in the LiteSpeed doc is specifically the workaround for a LiteSpeed Memcached + SASL fatal error, and the doc adds 'Redis users will not encounter this issue'; it is not a general Elementor remedy. State it as Memcached/LSMCD-only and keep 'prefer Redis'. Risk stays low; gain stays low for lab scores.

findings.claim: W3 Total Cache 2.10.7 free can safely provide only page cache, browser cache and object cache on an Elementor site; its PageSpeed levers (Delay Scripts, Remove CSS/JS, Eliminate render-blocking CSS, Preload Requests, Lazy Load Google Maps) are Pro-only and manual, so the three W3TC sites should pair W3TC with Perfmatters or migrate to FlyingPress/LiteSpeed.
findings.detail: BoldGrid docs: Delay Scripts (Pro, User Experience, exact-match Delay List + Timeout, +14 mobile points in their own test), Remove CSS/JS (Pro, manual Remove List and per-URL Include/Exclude rules, +27 points in their test), Eliminate render-blocking CSS (Pro), Preload Requests (Pro), Lazy Load Google Maps (Pro); free Lazy Load Images (with 'Process background images', hardened in 2.10.6) and Minify (Auto can break styling; Manual requires listing files). No automatic unused-CSS removal, no critical CSS generation, no above-the-fold image detection, no font self-hosting. 2.10.x changelog is dominated by security hardening (2.10.0) and lazy-load/minify path fixes; 2.10.7 added local caching of selected external scripts for auto minify and a one-pass sitemap preload. Support categories list 'W3 Total Cache and Elementor' with only 4 threads vs 11 for WooCommerce. WooCommerce Bookings on W3TC needs page exclusions or Fragment Cache mfunc edits in a child theme. LiteSpeed lists W3TC as a conflicting duplicate when both are installed.
findings.breaks_when: W3TC Minify Auto + Combine or Lazy Load is left on next to Perfmatters (double processing); bookings calendar cached (wc-ajax 404); Fragment Cache mfunc tags inserted into Elementor templates break on Elementor updates; Pro features configured by exact-match lists that go stale when plugin handles/URLs change.
findings.how_to_apply: On marakaki.com, pallada.gr, kand: W3TC General Settings: Page Cache ON (Disk: Enhanced), Minify OFF, Object Cache ON (Redis if available), Browser Cache ON, Lazy Load OFF, CDN as needed; Page Cache > Advanced: never cache booking product URLs, reject cookies wp_woocommerce_session_ and woocommerce_items_in_cart; let Perfmatters handle minify/defer/delay/RUCSS/lazy load/fonts/script manager. If moving off W3TC: FlyingPress on non-LiteSpeed hosts, LiteSpeed Cache on LiteSpeed hosts, keep Perfmatters for the Script Manager.
findings.how_to_verify: Response header x-powered-by/W3 Total Cache comment in HTML footer shows 'Page Caching using Disk: Enhanced' and no 'Minified using'; source shows Perfmatters attributes (pmdelayedscript, perfmatters-lazy) and no w3tc lazyload script; PSI mobile before/after; booking calendar loads in incognito; Elementor editor opens.

findings.claim: The 'FlyingPress 4.22.1' on cretaforums.gr (and per the audit voreniahorizon.gr) is not the official FlyingPress but a CretaForce-maintained fork ('FlyingPress CF') of the 4.16.x code base with its own update server, no cloud optimizer and several features removed; every FlyingPress setting in the plugin's matrix must target this fork's option keys, not the docs.flyingpress.com 5.x articles.
findings.detail: Read via Novamira read-file (read-only) on cretaforums.gr: wp-content/plugins/flying-press/flying-press.php header 'Plugin Name: FlyingPress', 'Plugin URI: https://www.cretaforce.gr', 'Update URI: https://downloads.cretaforce.gr/wordpress/flying-press/', 'Version: 4.22.1', 'Author: CretaForce'. readme.txt changelog: '4.16.5 - 03 March, 2026 - Initial release', 4.16.6 'Removed support for external cache purge integrations including CDN, Varnish, Cloudflare APO', 4.16.9 'Removed telemetry/tracking', 4.17.1 'Removed automatic full-page cache preloading', 4.18.0 'Removed hosting-specific integrations', 4.19.0 'Removed the legacy license activation', 4.19.2 'Prevented RUCSS from removing CSS selectors that target image attributes added later by FlyingPress', 4.20.0 fetchpriority=high on image preloads + self-host @import Google Fonts, 4.20.1 'detecting one likely large above-fold image and excluding it from lazy loading', 4.21.2 'automatic cache clearing every 48 hours by default', 4.22.0/4.22.1 (20-21 Sep 2026) per-page RUCSS storage and atomic cache writes. src/Config.php defaults: cache_lifespan '48hours', cache_mobile false, css_minify true, css_rucss true, css_rucss_method 'async', css_rucss_include_selectors [], js_minify true, js_defer true, js_delay true, js_delay_method 'selected', js_delay_selected [googletagmanager.com, google-analytics.com, googleoptimize.com, adsbygoogle.js, xfbml.customerchat.js, fbevents.js, widget.manychat.com, cookie-law-info, grecaptcha.execute, static.hotjar.com, hs-scripts.com, embed.tawk.to, disqus.com/embed.js, client.crisp.chat, matomo.js, usefathom.com, code.tidio.co, metomic.io, js.driftt.com, cdn.onesignal.com, clarity.ms], js_lazy_render true with js_lazy_render_selectors [], self_host_third_party_css_js true, fonts_optimize_google_fonts true, fonts_display_swap true, img_lazyload true, img_lazyload_exclude_count 2, img_width_height true, img_preload true, img_responsive true, iframe_lazyload true, iframe_youtube_placeholder true, bloat_disable_rss_feed/oembeds/emojis/dashicons true, bloat_disable_jquery_migrate false, db_* cleanups daily. The official FlyingPress changelog ends 4.x at 4.16.4 (15 Feb 2025) and is at 5.6.5 (20 Aug 2026), confirming 4.17+ exists only in this fork.
findings.breaks_when: The plugin recommends 5.x-only controls ('Load when idle', cloud 'Load Third-party Scripts on Interaction', cloud lazy render, FlyingCDN, APO purge) that do not exist in the fork; or a 5.x doc is used to predict behaviour (above-fold detection is a single-image heuristic, not cloud detection, so a second slide or logo can still be lazy-loaded); or a security assessment assumes the official vendor's release cadence.
findings.how_to_apply: In the plugin's FlyingPress module, detect the fork by reading FLYING_PRESS_VERSION >= 4.17 together with the 'Update URI: downloads.cretaforce.gr' header and branch to a '4.x fork' settings map keyed on the Config.php names above. Safe baseline for the two sites: js_delay_method 'selected' (remove 'cookie-law-info' and any consent-banner string; keep GTM/GA/fbevents/clarity), js_defer true with js_defer_excludes [hooks.min.js, i18n.min.js, jquery.sticky.min.js], css_rucss true + css_rucss_method 'async' with css_rucss_include_selectors = the Elementor safelist, js_lazy_render true but js_lazy_render_selectors only for verified below-fold blocks, img_lazyload_exclude_count = number of above-fold images on the mobile hero, cache_lifespan '24hours' or less on booking sites, fonts_optimize_google_fonts true (verify Greek unicode-range), bloat_disable_woo_assets true only where Woo widgets are absent. Record the fork's update host as a supply-chain item for the agency.
findings.how_to_verify: wp-content/plugins/flying-press/readme.txt 'Stable tag' and FLYING_PRESS_VERSION match; FLYING_PRESS_CONFIG option (read-only) shows the keys above; response HTML carries the fork's RUCSS <style> and a fetchpriority=high preload on the hero; PSI mobile shows the banner and hero without interaction; the same read on voreniahorizon.gr confirms the same header before applying the same map there.
sources: wp-content/plugins/flying-press/flying-press.php, readme.txt, src/Config.php on cretaforums.gr (Novamira read-file / list-directory, 2026-10-15)

findings.claim: Elementor 4.3.x's Performance and Advanced tabs contain six concrete toggles whose names, option keys and defaults the plugin must read and set before any optimiser is tuned; two of them ('Load Google Fonts Locally' and 'Google Fonts Load' = Swap) are levers the researcher missed, and 'Optimized CSS Files' is explained by the source.
findings.detail: From Elementor 4.3.5 source (main branch, includes/settings/settings.php): Performance tab: css_print_method (std 'external'; External File 'recommended'), optimized_image_loading (std '1'), optimized_gutenberg_loading (std '1', 'dequeuing unused Gutenberg block editor scripts and styles'), lazy_load_background_images (std '1'), local_google_fonts (std '0', 'Load Google fonts locally to benefit from faster performance and ensure GDPR compliance ... Only the very first load ... may take slightly longer'), and element_cache_ttl from modules/element-cache/module.php (std '24', options disable/1/6/12/24/72/168/336/720/8760 hours). Advanced tab: google_font (std '1' Enable; 'Disable this option ... when loading fonts from a different source (plugin, theme or custom fonts)') and font_display 'Google Fonts Load' (std 'auto' = 'Default'; options Blocking/Swap/Fallback/Optional; description 'Recommended: Swap'). Experiments (core/experiments/manager.php): e_font_icon_svg stable, new_site default_active >=3.17.0; additional_custom_breakpoints default active; e_optimized_markup stable default inactive, new_site active >=3.30.0; e_optimized_css_files alpha, default inactive, description 'Keeps external CSS files available and consistent for sites behind page caching or a CDN', and in core/files/base.php is_optimized_css_files_active() gates a validated 'elementor/files/base_dir' filter (@since 4.4.0) that relocates generated CSS files within WP_CONTENT_DIR/uploads. Elementor changelog: 3.28.0 enabled local fonts by default, 3.32.1 disabled it by default and moved it to Performance; 3.32.0 merged Element Caching into Performance. Audit: 8 of 10 sites fail 'Ensure text remains visible during webfont load', consistent with font_display left at 'auto'.
findings.breaks_when: local_google_fonts is Enabled while Perfmatters Local Google Fonts / WP Rocket Self-host / FlyingPress fonts_optimize_google_fonts also run (two local copies, two @font-face sets); font_display 'optional' is chosen (Greek headings may render in the fallback permanently); e_optimized_css_files is turned on in production (alpha) and the CSS path changes under a cache plugin that minifies/excludes by path (/uploads/elementor/css/); Optimized Markup is switched on a live site with custom CSS targeting .elementor-widget-container.
findings.how_to_apply: Read (read-only) options elementor_css_print_method, elementor_optimized_image_loading, elementor_optimized_gutenberg_loading, elementor_lazy_load_background_images, elementor_local_google_fonts, elementor_element_cache_ttl, elementor_google_font, elementor_font_display and elementor_experiment-* and print them in the audit. Recommended matrix: css_print_method external; optimized_image_loading 0 when a plugin lazy-loads, else 1; optimized_gutenberg_loading 1; lazy_load_background_images 0 when the optimiser lazy-loads CSS backgrounds (WP Rocket/Perfmatters), else 1; local_google_fonts 1 only if no plugin self-hosts fonts and Elementor is the only Google Fonts source (then set elementor_google_font to 0 once Custom Fonts are uploaded instead); font_display 'swap'; element_cache_ttl 'disable' on shop/booking/filter/multilingual sites until dynamic widgets are verified, else 24; leave e_optimized_css_files inactive.
findings.how_to_verify: View source: one @font-face set with unicode-range U+0370-03FF served from the own domain; no fonts.googleapis.com request; font CSS contains font-display: swap; PSI 'Ensure text remains visible during webfont load' passes; Elementor CSS still loads from /wp-content/uploads/elementor/css/post-*.css; hero has a single fetchpriority=high.

findings.claim: Elementor V4 'Atomic' elements (experiments e_opt_in_v4 / e_atomic_elements, default for new sites since April 2026) change how CSS is printed, and current practitioner reports plus Elementor GitHub issue #35397 make CSS combine, UCSS and RUCSS a higher-risk class on any page that contains V4 widgets or V4-built popups; the plugin should detect V4 usage and downgrade RUCSS/UCSS to opt-in on those pages.
findings.detail: The Plus Addons guide 'Fix: Elementor V4 Styling and CSS Not Loading' (Updated June 4, 2026): 'Since Atomic became the default for new sites in April 2026', 'V4 (Atomic) is class-based and CSS-first ... registers and prints those styles during the page render pass', 'LiteSpeed Cache: disable CSS Minify, CSS Combine, and "Generate UCSS" / "Remove Unused CSS" under Page Optimization. UCSS is the most common Atomic-CSS culprit', 'WP Rocket: turn off "Optimize CSS delivery," Minify CSS, and Combine CSS files', and the popup bug: 'Elementor GitHub issue #35397: popups opened by a runtime trigger can miss saved V4/Atomic CSS because styles are registered before the popup is queued' with workarounds (legacy widgets for popup styling or internal CSS for that popup). Perfmatters 2.6.9 (10.06.2026) is the only optimiser documenting 'built-in Remove Unused CSS exclusions for Elementor's new local and global per-document stylesheets'. Elementor 4.3.5 (2026-10-13) also fixed 'Page editing can fail when Internal CSS Embedding is enabled'. The audit lists e_opt_in_v4, e_atomic_elements, e_pro_atomic_form among seen experiments, so at least some of the 10 sites carry V4 elements.
findings.breaks_when: RUCSS/UCSS or CSS combine runs on a page with V4 widgets whose classes are generated per document; a V4-built popup is opened by click (CSS missing even without optimisers); the optimiser is older than Perfmatters 2.6.9 or is LiteSpeed/WP Rocket/FlyingPress with no V4 built-ins.
findings.how_to_apply: Audit step: read elementor_experiment-e_opt_in_v4 / e_atomic_elements and scan _elementor_data for widgetType values starting with 'e-' (atomic) or the V4 'styles' key; flag pages and popups that contain them. Rule: on flagged pages keep CSS Combine OFF everywhere, keep LiteSpeed Generate UCSS OFF, and run Perfmatters RUCSS (>=2.6.9) only with the page-level exclusion if the side-by-side diff shows missing classes; for V4 popups prefer legacy widgets or exclude the popup's CSS from RUCSS. Re-test after every Elementor minor release because the print path is still changing.
findings.how_to_verify: Open each flagged page and popup with and without ?nowprocket / ?perfmattersoff / ?LSCWP_CTRL=before_optm and compare computed styles of atomic elements; PSI unchanged; no 'CSS not loading' regressions after Elementor updates; GitHub issue #35397 status checked at release time.

findings.claim: Perfmatters 2.6.8/2.6.9 added three controls the plugin should use: a sitewide 'Safe Mode' kill-switch for all performance optimisations, 'Inline Excluded Stylesheets', and per-taxonomy / per-post-ID used-CSS files, which directly address the Woo product-type and archive pages where one shared used.css breaks product variants.
findings.detail: Changelog 2.6.8 (09.09.2026): 'Added new Safe Mode option to disable all Perfmatters performance optimizations sitewide without impacting security-related options or code snippets'; 'Added new Inline Excluded Stylesheets advanced option to automatically inline stylesheets excluded from Remove Unused CSS'; 'Fixed an issue where Remove Unused CSS could delay, async, or remove external stylesheets that were never included in used CSS'; 'Improved Remove Unused CSS to detect local stylesheets from the URL path, which should resolve most third-party CDN rewrites'. 2.6.9 (10.06.2026): 'Added new perfmatters_rucss_per_id_post_types filter which allows for unique used CSS files per post ID for provided post types'; 'Adjusted Remove Unused CSS to generate separate used CSS files per taxonomy instead of one shared tax.used.css file'; 'Fixed an issue where Delay JavaScript could skip inline scripts that contained HTML comments'; 'Added logic to prevent Disable WooCommerce Scripts option from running inside page builders'. 2.6.5 (06.30.2026) added domain/content-type validation to local Google Fonts downloads and 'perfmatters_rucss_delay_stylesheets'.
findings.breaks_when: Safe Mode is left on after a diagnosis (site silently unoptimised); perfmatters_rucss_per_id_post_types is applied to thousands of products (one used-CSS file per product, disk and generation time grow); Inline Excluded Stylesheets inlines a large excluded stylesheet into every page (HTML bloat, cache size).
findings.how_to_apply: Require Perfmatters >= 2.6.9 in the plugin's preflight. Use Safe Mode as the one-click rollback in the plugin's 'verify' step instead of toggling features individually. For the water-park e-shop and booking sites add add_filter('perfmatters_rucss_per_id_post_types', fn() => ['product']) only if bookable/variable products show missing styles with the shared product.used.css. Enable Inline Excluded Stylesheets only for small excluded sheets (Elementor animations, cookie banner CSS).
findings.how_to_verify: Perfmatters > Tools shows Safe Mode state; view source confirms no pmdelayedscript / used-CSS markers while Safe Mode is on and their return when off; /wp-content/cache/perfmatters/<site>/css/ contains per-ID files only for the configured post type; PSI unchanged or better; product variation forms styled in incognito.

findings.claim: LiteSpeed 7.9 / 7.9.1 (Aug-Sep 2026) and WP Rocket 3.23.x (Jul-Oct 2026) changed behaviours the matrix depends on: LiteSpeed now adds fetchpriority=high to VPI preloads and fixed CSS Combine unstyled pages and Guest Mode ESI subrequests; WP Rocket removed Combine CSS entirely, added 'rocket_lrc_exclusions' and keeps an Elementor-specific subscriber; the plugin should pin these minimum versions.
findings.detail: LiteSpeed readme trunk: Stable tag 7.9.1; '7.9 - Aug 5 2026': 'VPI Added fetchpriority=high to VPI preload links', 'Page Optimize Fixed CSS Combine serving unstyled pages when the placeholder link tag uses default WordPress whitespace', 'Fixed JS Combine corrupting URLs inside template literals'; '7.9.1 - Sep 1 2026': 'ESI Prevented Guest Mode pages from creating ESI subrequests', 'VPI Fixed queue-key collisions on plain-permalink sites and enforced the configured queue limit', 'Remote images, avatars, localized JavaScript, CSS/JS cache files, and Guest Mode lists now share bounded streamed downloads and atomic file publication'. LiteSpeed pageopt: the former separate viewport-image preload setting 'has been removed. We now automatically preload all Viewport Images as part of our VPI service'. WP Rocket changelog: 3.23.5.1 (October 2nd, 2026) 'keep elementor_subscriber registered in the container'; 3.23.5 'strict format validation for Lazy Render Content location hashes'; 3.23.3.1 (Aug 24 2026) Redis orphan keys fix; older entries 'Get rid of Combine CSS files option (#5909)', 'Introduce "rocket_lrc_exclusions" filter', 'Emulate Elementor Pro animation when using Delay JS (#4080)'.
findings.breaks_when: A site runs LiteSpeed < 7.9 with CSS Combine (unstyled-page bug) or VPI without fetchpriority (LCP preload competes with other preloads); a knowledge-base entry tells users to turn off WP Rocket 'Combine CSS' (option no longer exists) or relies on a lazy-render hash format that 3.23.5 now validates.
findings.how_to_apply: Preflight: LiteSpeed Cache >= 7.9.1, WP Rocket >= 3.23.5.1, Perfmatters >= 2.6.9, W3TC >= 2.10.7, Elementor >= 4.3.5 before applying the matrix; drop 'Combine CSS OFF' from the WP Rocket row (keep 'Combine JavaScript files OFF'); document rocket_lrc_exclusions (attribute-based) as the code alternative to the helper plugin for lazy-render exclusions.
findings.how_to_verify: Plugin version headers; LiteSpeed VPI preload tags carry fetchpriority="high"; WP Rocket settings page shows no Combine CSS control; lazy-render exclusions take effect (no data-wpr-lazyrender on the excluded element).

title: Fonts: self-hosting, subsetting (Greek + Latin), woff2, preload, icon fonts
summary: On the 10 audited sites the font lever is worth roughly 10-20 mobile points on the slow sites and 2-5 on the fast ones, and the damage comes from four things, not from "too many weights": (1) render-blocking third-party font/icon CSS chains (fonts.googleapis.com 788-912 ms, use.fontawesome.com 1465 ms, cdn.jsdelivr MDI 1094 ms, use.typekit.net) that Elementor 4.x emits without any preconnect; (2) unsubsetted or legacy font files (Modak-Regular.woff 271 KB, InterTight-Regular.woff2 105 KB, fa-solid-900.woff2 76 KB) where a Greek+Latin woff2 subset measured today is 10-43 KB; (3) families with no Greek glyphs (Poppins, Modak, Orleans) that silently render Greek in a system fallback; (4) icon fonts (Font Awesome 5/6, eicons 106 KB, MDI, Fontello sets) that Elementor's stable "Inline Font Icons" feature can replace with inline SVG. Elementor 4.x (verified live on 4.3.4/4.3.5 and in help articles dated Jan 20 2026) offers: Settings > Advanced > "Google Fonts Load" (Default/Blocking/Swap/Fallback/Optional), Settings > Advanced > "Google Fonts: Disable", Settings > Performance > "Load Google Fonts Locally" (default Disabled since 3.32.1, must be re-enabled after updating), Features > "Inline Font Icons", and Pro Custom Fonts (WOFF/WOFF2/TTF/SVG/EOT, one file per weight, font-display defaults to auto unless the elementor_pro/custom_fonts/font_display filter is used). The local-Google-Fonts CSS Elementor writes keeps Google's unicode-range subsets and font-display:swap for all 9 weights x 2 styles (126 @font-face, 45 KB raw / 1.3 KB gzip), so the browser only downloads the subset files actually used; the real cost is per family (~66 KB for Inter latin+greek, which is one variable file covering 100-900). A 95+ budget that matches the fast sites is 2 families, <=4 same-origin woff2 files, <=100 KB, swap on headings, optional or size-adjusted fallbacks on body text, 1-2 preloads for the LCP heading font. LiteSpeed, FlyingPress and Perfmatters each have their own Google-font localisation, font-display and preload switches; exactly one tool should own Google Fonts or you get redundant processing. GDPR (LG München I, Jan 2022) makes self-hosting mandatory for EU sites anyway, and it also applies to Typekit and Font Awesome CDN kits.
critic_notes: Method: every Elementor claim was checked against the 4.3.5 trunk source on plugins.svn.wordpress.org (settings.php, frontend.php, fonts.php, core/files/fonts/google-font.php, core/experiments/manager.php, includes/managers/icons.php, atomic-widgets styles) plus the help-center pages (dates Jan 20 2026 / Jun 19 2026 / Oct 1 2026), the full core changelog (versions mapped by line) and the Pro changelog; GitHub issues #35065, #18621, #31512, #30600, #34657, #32842 were read; LiteSpeed 7.9.1 docs+source, Perfmatters and FlyingPress docs opened; Google Fonts CSS2 API and gwfh API re-queried; the agency's Lighthouse JSON re-aggregated. Not reachable from this network: helpx.adobe.com (403), developers.elementor.com/docs (DNS; only the ?p=9870 post loaded once), daan.dev. Not checked: Perfmatters' Limit Subsets list for a 'greek' entry (image only), Elementor Pro source for the font_display filter in 4.3, and no live Lighthouse re-runs (read-only mandate honoured; no site, file or setting was changed). Biggest risk for the user: voreniahorizon.gr currently renders without any of its web fonts (addition 1); fixing it changes the visible typography of the whole site, so take before/after screenshots.

findings.claim: Third-party font and icon-font stylesheets are the single biggest font cost on the slow sites: each external CSS chain blocks render for 0.8-1.5 s on the mobile profile, and Elementor 4.x emits no preconnect for fonts.googleapis.com/gstatic.com.
findings.detail: Lighthouse (mobile) on the agency's own sites: limnoupolis.gr (Elementor 4.3.5) fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Open+Sans:100,100italic,...,900italic&display=swap = render-blocking 788 ms; staging.limnoupolis.gr: Roboto 912 ms + Roboto Slab 193 ms + use.fontawesome.com/releases/v6.2.1/css/all.css 1465 ms + cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@mdi/font@1.9.32 1094 ms. Elementor requests all 18 weight/style variants of each Google family in one <link id='elementor-gf-<family>-css'> and the page head contained only a dns-prefetch for cdnjs.cloudflare.com, no preconnect to Google. The fastest sites (pallada.gr 86, platonos 84) load fonts only from their own origin via Elementor's local Google Fonts CSS (elementor-gf-local-*-css, 0.7-1.4 KB transfer each). web.dev: 'Particular care should be given to fonts loaded from third-party sites as downloading these font files requires separate connection setups.'
findings.breaks_when: The local font folder (wp-content/uploads/elementor/google-fonts/) is not writable or a CDN/WAF rewrites upload URLs, so the local CSS 404s and text falls back to system fonts; or a page-cache purge happens before Elementor re-downloads (Elementor re-downloads automatically on cache clear per its docs, so this is transient).
findings.how_to_apply: Elementor > Editor > Settings > Performance tab > 'Load Google Fonts Locally' = Enable (help article dated Jan 20 2026 says: 'Starting with Elementor version 3.32.1, the ability to load Google fonts locally was made optional and the default setting was switched to Disabled... If you enabled this feature in an earlier version of Elementor, you will need to enable it again after updating.'). If an optimizer already localises fonts (Perfmatters 'Local Google Fonts', FlyingPress 'Self-Host Google Fonts'), keep exactly one owner. Then remove external icon CSS (see icon-font findings). Do not add preconnects as a substitute: self-hosting removes the connection entirely.
findings.how_to_verify: View source: font <link>s must have id 'elementor-gf-local-<family>-css' pointing to /wp-content/uploads/elementor/google-fonts/css/<family>.css; DevTools Network filtered by 'font' and by domain shows zero requests to fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com, use.fontawesome.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net, use.typekit.net; Lighthouse 'Eliminate render-blocking resources' no longer lists any font CSS; compare FCP/LCP before/after (expect 0.5-1.5 s better on the slow sites).

findings.claim: Legacy .woff and unsubsetted .woff2 custom fonts can be cut by 65-85% with pyftsubset to Greek+Latin woff2; measured today on the agency's own files.
findings.detail: Measured with fonttools 4.67 pyftsubset on the files served by the sites: Modak-Regular.woff 271.4 KB (1228 glyphs, 1 Greek codepoint) -> woff2 full 183.3 KB -> woff2 Greek+Latin 42.7 KB (-84%); Poppins-Regular.woff 71.9 KB -> 10.2 KB; InterTight-Regular.woff2 (marakaki) 104.9 KB / 2542 glyphs incl. 254 Cyrillic -> 36.9 KB (-65%) keeping all 191 Latin-1, 121 Greek and 233 Greek-Extended codepoints; Orleans-Light.woff 55.5 KB -> 31.3 KB. web.dev: WOFF2 'compresses 30% better than WOFF' and 'Use only WOFF2 and forget about everything else'; 'preload ignores unicode-range declarations'. Elementor Pro Custom Fonts accepts WOFF2 (help page lists WOFF, WOFF2, TTF, SVG, EOT; 'You must add every font weight class and type you want to use as a separate file'; stored under wp-content/uploads/).
findings.breaks_when: A character outside the subset appears in content (e.g. Cyrillic names in a hotel review, ₿, ſ, Vietnamese) and renders in the fallback font; the font EULA forbids modification (commercial fonts like Orleans, TT Commons Pro: check the licence before subsetting); polytonic Greek (U+1F00-1FFF) is dropped but used in a quote.
findings.how_to_apply: pip install fonttools brotli; pyftsubset Font.ttf --unicodes="U+0020-007E,U+00A0-00FF,U+0100-017F,U+0370-03FF,U+1F00-1FFF,U+2000-206F,U+20AC,U+2122" --layout-features='*' --flavor=woff2 --output-file=Font-grlat.woff2 (drop U+1F00-1FFF if no polytonic text; keep --layout-features='*' so kerning/ligatures survive). Re-upload each weight in Elementor Pro > Custom Fonts (Add Static Font, pick Weight/Style), delete the WOFF/TTF variants so only one src remains, then Elementor > Tools > Regenerate CSS. For hand-written @font-face in the theme (limnoupolis has 'Modak Regular', 'Poppins Regular', 'Inter Regular' as .woff in inline CSS with no font-display), replace the src and add font-display: swap.
findings.how_to_verify: fontTools: python -c "from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont; f=TTFont('x.woff2'); c=f.getBestCmap(); print(len([k for k in c if 0x370<=k<=0x3FF]))" must be >=100 for Greek; DevTools Network 'font' filter shows the new sizes; screenshot Greek headings with accented capitals (Ά, Έ, Ώ), final sigma ς, « », €, en dash – and compare pixel-for-pixel; Lighthouse 'font-display' audit items drop to 0.

findings.claim: Several families in use have no Greek glyphs at all, so Greek text already renders in an unstyled system fallback and triggers an extra font; choose families with a 'greek' subset before optimising anything else.
findings.detail: Google Fonts CSS2 API queried today: Poppins returns only latin and latin-ext @font-face blocks (no greek), whereas Inter, Open Sans, Roboto, Noto Serif Display, EB Garamond, Arima return greek and greek-ext blocks. fontTools cmap of the served files: Modak-Regular has 1 Greek codepoint, Orleans-Light 0, Poppins 1; Inter Tight has 121 Greek + 233 Greek Extended. google-webfonts-helper API (gwfh.mranftl.com/api/fonts/inter?subsets=latin,greek) lists each family's subsets (Inter v20, 2025-09-10: cyrillic, cyrillic-ext, greek, greek-ext, latin, latin-ext, vietnamese). Elementor's local Google Fonts CSS only declares a greek unicode-range block when Google provides one, so a Greek heading set to Poppins falls back to the browser default sans (Roboto on Android) with different metrics -> visual mismatch and swap-type layout movement.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break; the only cost is a design decision (replacing Poppins/Modak with a Greek-capable family such as Inter, Open Sans, Noto Sans/Serif, Manrope, Roboto, Arima, Comfortaa).
findings.how_to_apply: Before picking a family for a Greek site, check https://gwfh.mranftl.com/api/fonts/<id> 'subsets' contains 'greek', or request https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=<Family>&display=swap with a Chrome UA and confirm a '/* greek */' block exists. For custom fonts run the fontTools cmap check above. In the plugin: flag any kit or widget font family whose cmap lacks U+0391-03C9.
findings.how_to_verify: In DevTools Elements > Computed > 'Rendered Fonts' on a Greek heading: the family name must be the web font, not 'Roboto'/'Noto Sans' (Android) or 'Helvetica' (iOS); Network shows no extra fallback font download; screenshot Greek vs Latin headings side by side.

findings.claim: A 95+ Elementor page can afford 2 families, at most 4 same-origin woff2 files and about 100 KB of fonts; per-subset costs are now known exactly for the families the agency uses.
findings.detail: Google Fonts woff2 sizes measured today (Chrome UA, one weight): Inter latin 47.3 KB + greek 18.6 KB + greek-ext 11.0 KB; Open Sans latin 42.0 + greek 17.3 + greek-ext 1.7; Roboto latin 29.6 + greek 39.1 (greek is bigger than latin for Roboto); Noto Serif Display latin 14.0 + greek 9.5; EB Garamond latin 23.2 + greek 10.5; Poppins latin 7.7 (no greek). Inter, Open Sans, Noto Serif Display and EB Garamond are served as variable slices: the 400 and 700 requests return the identical URL, so extra weights of these families cost 0 bytes; Poppins and Roboto are static, each weight is another file. Local evidence: pallada.gr score 86 with 2 font files / 78 KB; platonos 84 with 6 files / 270 KB; cretaforums 74 with 7 files / 175 KB; onar 44 with 11 files / 383 KB; limnoupolis 27 with 3 files / 387 KB. web.dev notes variable fonts 'typically have larger file sizes than individual non-variable fonts that only contain one style' and benefit sites using many styles.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break; a brand that insists on 3+ display families simply pays ~60-70 KB and one CSS file per extra family.
findings.how_to_apply: Plugin rule: kit typography uses <=2 families (one heading, one body), all weights of a variable family are free, so prefer Inter/Open Sans/Noto over static families when 3+ weights are needed; for <=2 weights of a static family self-host per-weight static files (Inter via gwfh greek_latin merged file is 29.7 KB regular / 30.6 KB bold). Budget check in the audit script: total Font transferSize <= 100 KB and <= 4 font requests on the home page.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse JSON: sum audits['network-requests'].details.items where resourceType=='Font' (transferSize) and count them; DevTools Network 'font' filter totals; the Lighthouse run should show no 'Preload key requests' or 'font-display' items.

findings.claim: Set font-display to swap everywhere the text is the LCP element: Elementor's 'Google Fonts Load' dropdown, the Pro Custom Fonts filter, and the optimizer's font-display option for theme @font-face rules; 'Default' lets Chromium hide text up to 3 s and blocks LCP on the font download.
findings.detail: Elementor help (Last Update Jan 20 2026): Elementor > Editor > Settings > Advanced > 'Google Fonts Load' with five values: Default ('Uses the browser settings'), Blocking, Swap ('The text is displayed in the fallback font until Google Fonts is loaded'), Fallback, Optional. Elementor's local Google Fonts CSS already writes font-display: swap on all 126 @font-face rules (pallada inter.css).
