Pro Custom Fonts default to font-display auto; Elementor Pro 2.7 added filter elementor_pro/custom_fonts/font_display (args: $current_value default 'auto', $font_family, $font_data), requires re-saving each custom font and Elementor > Tools > Regenerate CSS (developers.elementor.com was unreachable from this network; details from two independent search summaries, treat as medium). web.dev: Chromium and Firefox 'block text rendering for up to 3 seconds if the associated web font has not loaded', and for LCP 'If you set a font-display value of anything other than auto or block, then text will always be visible during load, and LCP won't be blocked on an additional network request.' Local evidence: LCP element is an <h1> on kand, fagitiotiszois, voreniahorizon; Lighthouse font-display failures: limnoupolis Poppins/Modak .woff 140-181 ms, onar custom icon font 243 ms, kand Typekit 430 ms + 154 ms.
findings.breaks_when: Swap produces a visible font flash and, if fallback metrics differ a lot (display fonts like Modak vs Arial), a layout shift on slow connections; headings with text-transform/letter-spacing tuned to the web font may wrap differently for ~100-500 ms.
findings.how_to_apply: Elementor > Editor > Settings > Advanced > Google Fonts Load = Swap. For Pro Custom Fonts add in the theme or a snippet: add_filter('elementor_pro/custom_fonts/font_display', function($v,$family,$data){ return 'swap'; }, 10, 3); then re-save each font under Elementor > Custom Fonts and Tools > Regenerate CSS. For theme/inline @font-face use LiteSpeed Cache > Page Optimization > CSS Settings > 'Font Display Optimization' = Swap (option optm-css_font_display, values Default|Swap, source says 'Swap is recommended'; it appends font-display to all @font-face before caching CSS) or edit the theme CSS. Perfmatters 'Display Swap' only appends display=swap to Google Fonts links and to its own local stylesheet; FlyingPress 'Use System Fonts First' applies a system stack until the custom font loads.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse 'Ensure text remains visible during webfont load' passes with 0 items (note: Lighthouse cannot check third-party origins and reports 'unable to automatically check the font-display values' for Typekit/CDN fonts); DevTools > Network > font CSS shows font-display: swap in every @font-face; LCP element in Lighthouse stays the <h1> and its 'resource load delay' subpart shrinks; record a throttled load video and confirm text is visible before fonts arrive.
findings.correction: Three corrections. (1) Elementor's 'Google Fonts Load' (option elementor_font_display) has std 'auto' in includes/settings/settings.php; changelog 3.8.0 (2022-10-30) switched new sites to Swap, so sites created before that still sit on Default. (2) The local Google Fonts CSS is NOT 'already swap': Google_Font::get_google_fonts_remote_url() reuses get_stable_google_fonts_url(), which appends &display=<setting>; with Default (auto) Google emits no font-display line at all (verified: css?family=Inter:400&display=auto returns 0 font-display rules, display=swap returns swap). pallada's 126 swap rules exist only because that site's setting is Swap. (3) Changing the setting fires update_option_elementor_font_display -> Google_Font::clear_cache(), which unlinks every file in uploads/elementor/google-fonts/{css,fonts} and deletes _elementor_local_google_fonts, so the first front-end view after saving re-downloads all fonts (purge page cache afterwards, expect one slow load). Pro filter confirmed from the Elementor Pro 2.7 developer post (Aug 19 2019): add_filter('elementor_pro/custom_fonts/font_display', fn($current_value,$font_family,$data)=>'swap',10,3), default 'auto', then Elementor > Tools > Regenerate CSS. Risk stays low.

findings.claim: Enable Elementor's stable 'Inline Font Icons' feature and drop the Font Awesome 4 shim: it removes fa-solid-900.woff2 (76 KB), fontawesome.min.css (58 KB raw) and eicons.woff2 (106 KB) by rendering icons as inline SVG.
findings.detail: Elementor help 'Improve performance features' (Last Update June 19 2026) lists under 'Stable features found in the Features tab': 'Inline font Icons: Renders icons as inline SVG without loading the Font-Awesome and the eicons libraries and their related CSS files and fonts.' The Inline Font Icons article (Mar 7 2024) adds: 'This feature does not convert Font Awesome Pro icons.' Measured files from Elementor 4.2.3 (onar-seaside-lounge.gr, feature off, FA4 shim on): assets/lib/font-awesome/webfonts/fa-solid-900.woff2 76.4 KB (1004 glyphs), css/fontawesome.min.css 58 KB raw / 12.4 KB gzip, assets/lib/eicons/fonts/eicons.woff2 105.5 KB (514 glyphs), elementor-icons.min.css 22 KB raw / 4.5 KB gzip; voreniahorizon loads font-awesome/js/v4-shims.min.js 4.6 KB because elementor_load_fa4_shim=yes. web.dev: 'When possible, replace icon fonts with SVGs, which is also better for accessibility.' Known regressions reported on GitHub (SVG fill colours not applied #35065, Icon List styling #18621, Reviews stars #31512 - found via search, pages not opened from this network).
findings.breaks_when: Font Awesome Pro kit icons are used (not converted); third-party add-ons (Premium Addons, Dynamic.ooo, JetSmartFilters) render icons via <i class='fa'> in their own templates and still need the FA CSS; custom Elementor icon sets (Fontello/IcoMoon zips) remain icon fonts; icon colour on hover/active states may need fill instead of color; FA4 class names (fa fa-xxx) in HTML widgets or theme stop rendering when the FA4 shim is turned off.
findings.how_to_apply: Elementor > Settings > Features > 'Inline Font Icons' = Active. Elementor > Settings > Advanced > 'Font Awesome 4 Support' = No only after grepping post_content and theme templates for 'fa fa-' (the debloat script already checks). Clear page cache and Elementor > Tools > Regenerate CSS.
findings.how_to_verify: DevTools Network 'font' filter: no fa-*.woff2, eicons.woff2 or elementor-icons*.css; grep rendered HTML for '<svg' inside .elementor-icon; click through Icon, Icon Box, Icon List, Social Icons, Nav Menu dropdown arrows, Reviews/Testimonial stars, Accordion/Toggle chevrons, Post Navigation arrows, and hover states on mobile and desktop; compare screenshots before/after.
findings.correction: Correct on mechanism and savings, but add: (a) default state answered from core/experiments/manager.php - e_font_icon_svg is release_status stable with new_site default_active = true only for installs whose first Elementor version was >= 3.17.0 (changelog: default-on for new sites in 3.18.0, stable in 3.20.0); sites installed earlier (onar, limnoupolis) stay Inactive until toggled. (b) Open regressions as of Oct 2026: #31512 (Pro Reviews widget stars invisible for logged-out visitors when the feature is on, Elementor 3.29.2, triaged as bug Aug 2025, still open); #18621 (Icon List icon colour/size, open since 2022, users report fixes both by enabling and disabling the feature); #35065 (SVG ignores 'color', needs fill; closed 'not planned' Mar 2026 on 3.35.6). Pro changelog shows repeated fixes in this area (Post Navigation, Button alignment, Menu dropdown caret, Form select icon, Link in Bio), so the feature is mainstream but widget-by-widget QA is mandatory. (c) Lighthouse on onar shows the FA file served as fa-solid-900.woff (76 KB), not woff2. Keep risk medium.

findings.claim: Separate icon plugins loading CDN CSS (official Font Awesome plugin kit, Material Design Icons) duplicate Elementor's icons and cost ~2.5 s of render-blocking on mobile; remove them or dequeue their handles.
findings.detail: staging.limnoupolis.gr Lighthouse: use.fontawesome.com/releases/v6.2.1/css/all.css 24.2 KB render-blocking 1465 ms + v4-shims.css 4.7 KB + local font-awesome/v6.2.1/css/svg-with-js.css; cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@mdi/font@1.9.32/css/materialdesignicons.min.css 15.1 KB render-blocking 1094 ms plus a second MDI copy from cdn.materialdesignicons.com (two MDI stylesheets, versions pinned to WordPress 7.1.3 query string, i.e. enqueued by a theme/plugin). The audit summary flags 'Font Awesome plugin' active on staging.limnoupolis and onar next to Elementor's bundled Font Awesome. Each is a third-party connection plus a stylesheet the browser must fetch before first paint.
findings.breaks_when: Content, theme templates, forum (cretaforums) or booking plugins output <i class='fa ...'> / 'mdi mdi-...' markup that relied on the CDN CSS: those icons become empty squares or vanish; FA6-only icon names used in HTML widgets are not in Elementor's bundled FA5.
findings.how_to_apply: 1) grep wp_posts.post_content, theme templates and plugin templates for 'class="fa', 'fa-solid', 'fab ', 'mdi-'. 2) If none outside Elementor icon controls: deactivate the Font Awesome plugin; find the MDI enqueue (handle in Perfmatters Script Manager or Query Monitor) and disable it site-wide via Perfmatters Script Manager or wp_dequeue_style in the child theme. 3) If a few icons are needed, replace them with inline SVG (Elementor Icon widget > Upload SVG requires Settings > Advanced > 'Enable Unfiltered File Uploads').
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse 'Eliminate render-blocking resources' no longer lists use.fontawesome.com or materialdesignicons; Network shows no requests to those hosts; visual sweep of header, footer, social icons, forum post actions, booking widgets, cookie banner icons.

findings.claim: Preload only the LCP heading font (1-2 same-origin woff2 files), never the whole set: FlyingPress does it automatically, Perfmatters via Preloading > Preload, LiteSpeed has no font-preload UI.
findings.detail: web.dev optimize-lcp: the preload scanner can discover the LCP resource when 'The LCP element is a text node that requires a web font to render, and the font is loaded using <link rel="preload">'. web.dev font-best-practices warns 'preload ignores unicode-range declarations' and 'should only be used to load a single font format', and that overuse takes bandwidth from other resources; Lighthouse docs: 'overusing preloads can negatively impact load metrics. We recommend performing A/B testing'. FlyingPress 'Preload Fonts' (doc May 21 2025): 'Our cloud optimizer automatically detects the fonts used during the initial render... preloaded using <link rel="preload">... Works for local fonts and supported third-party fonts (e.g. Google Fonts)... no setup required.' Perfmatters Preloading > Preload: full URL + type font (+ device, location, priority), emits <link rel='preload' href='font.woff2' as='font' type='font/woff2' crossorigin>; Chrome has a 'soft limit' of two preloads at top priority. LiteSpeed Cache docs list no font preload option. On the audited sites the LCP is an <h1> on 3 of 9 pages, so the heading font's latin (and greek) files are the candidates.
findings.breaks_when: The preloaded URL changes (Elementor regenerates local Google Fonts with new hashed filenames after a cache clear; Perfmatters local fonts moved) so the preload is wasted and Chrome logs 'was preloaded using link preload but not used'; more than 2 font preloads push the hero image down the waterfall and worsen LCP; preloading the greek file on Latin-only pages downloads ~19 KB uselessly.
findings.how_to_apply: Identify the LCP element (Lighthouse 'Largest Contentful Paint element'); if it is text, take the exact woff2 URLs from the local font CSS for that family/weight (latin, plus greek on Greek pages). FlyingPress: nothing to configure. Perfmatters: Preloading > Preload > URL, type 'font', device 'all', optionally location = front/post ID. LiteSpeed-only sites: add in the child theme on wp_head priority 1: <link rel="preload" href="<woff2 url>" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>. Pair with font-display: swap (or optional) on that face.
findings.how_to_verify: DevTools Network: the font request's Initiator column is 'preload' and it starts right after the HTML, before any CSS finishes; Console has no 'preloaded but not used' warning; Lighthouse LCP subparts (Performance panel > LCP by phase) show resource load delay near 0 ms; A/B two Lighthouse runs (with/without preload) and keep it only if LCP improves.
findings.correction: The breaks_when is wrong about Elementor: local font filenames are substr(sha1(<gstatic font URL>),0,8) (Google_Font::get_unique_font_id), so a cache clear/re-download reproduces the SAME filename; the name changes only when Google bumps the family version (e.g. opensans v44 -> v45) or when the site domain changes (URLs are absolute, see additions). Also mandatory: the preload tag needs crossorigin or 'Fonts preloaded without the crossorigin attribute will be fetched twice' (web.dev), and Chrome logs unused preloads ~3 s after load. The 'soft limit of two' is not in any opened source; practitioner guidance is 'your most important font or two'. FlyingPress 'Preload Fonts' (May 21 2025) and 'Self-Host Google Fonts' docs confirmed; LiteSpeed pageopt docs list no font preload option (confirmed). Preloading the Greek slice on Greek pages is right because preload ignores unicode-range (web.dev).

findings.claim: Font-swap CLS is small on these sites today (CLS 0-0.005 on 8 of 9 pages) but display fonts and slow 3G can shift; the fix is font-display: optional for body text or a size-adjusted local() fallback, both of which Elementor can only take through Custom CSS.
findings.detail: web.dev font-display table: Block 2-3 s block/infinite swap; Swap 0 ms/infinite; Fallback 100 ms/3 s; Optional 100 ms/none. Recommendation: 'Performance: Use font-display: optional... text render is delayed for no longer than 100ms and there's assurance that there isn't font-swap related layout shifts... use font-display: swap for branding and other visually distinctive page elements. Use font-display: optional for fonts used in body text.' Chrome blog 'Improved font fallbacks': ascent-override, descent-override, line-gap-override and size-adjust let a local() fallback match the web font's dimensions ('reduces or eliminates layout shifts caused by font swapping'); for ~90% of Google Fonts the overrides are OS-independent. Generator: screenspan.net/fallback (upload brand font, pick web-safe fallback, outputs @font-face with size-adjust/ascent-override/descent-override/line-gap-override). Elementor's typography control emits 'font-family: "<Family>", <generic>' and offers no fallback stack, so the adjusted fallback must be injected via CSS. Local evidence: limnoupolis CLS 0.103 comes from lazy-loaded hero image, not fonts; pallada CLS 0.002 with swap and no preload.
findings.breaks_when: font-display: optional on a slow first visit keeps the system font for the whole page view (brand font appears only on the next navigation) - unacceptable for hero headings, fine for body copy; a wrong size-adjust makes fallback text visibly larger/smaller for a few hundred ms; Custom CSS overriding font-family loses Elementor responsive typography control if selectors are too broad.
findings.how_to_apply: Option A (simple): keep swap for headings, set optional for the body family: in Elementor's local Google Fonts CSS this is not configurable per family, so use Elementor > Editor > Settings > Advanced > Google Fonts Load = Optional only on sites whose headings are a Pro custom font (custom fonts use the filter, so they can stay swap). Option B: generate a fallback with screenspan.net/fallback for the heading font, add to Site Settings > Custom CSS (Pro): @font-face{font-family:'Inter Fallback';src:local('Arial');size-adjust:107%;ascent-override:90%;descent-override:22%;line-gap-override:0%} and body,.elementor-heading-title{font-family:'Inter','Inter Fallback',sans-serif}. Measure before choosing: only act if DevTools shows font-related layout shifts.
findings.how_to_verify: DevTools Performance panel > Layout Shifts track under throttled 'Slow 4G' with cache disabled: no shift attributed to text nodes after fonts load; Lighthouse CLS stays <= 0.01 across 3 runs; toggle the web font in Elements > Rendered Fonts and compare line counts of the hero heading in fallback vs web font (same number of lines = no shift).

findings.claim: Adobe Fonts (Typekit) on two dev sites cost 193 KB and 43 KB of third-party fonts plus two CDN stylesheets and fail the font-display audit; set font-display in the Adobe web project or replace with a licensed self-hosted/open font, because Typekit files cannot be self-hosted.
findings.detail: Lighthouse: fagitiotiszois.dev6 loads use.typekit.net/btd2hql.css + p.typekit.net beacon + 4 fonts of 46-51 KB (193 KB total, tt-commons-pro); kand.dev6 loads use.typekit.net/fcw7vbu.css + 2 fonts 22 KB (helvetica-neue-world) flagged 'font-display' 430 ms and 154 ms. Perfmatters doc: 'The above feature only works with Google Fonts. However, if you're using Adobe Fonts, you can add swap by updating your web project.' Adobe's help page (helpx.adobe.com/fonts/using/font-display-settings.html) returned HTTP 403 from this network; search summary of it: Edit Project > choose a font-display value in the sidebar, default auto, applied to the existing embed code within minutes, support added September 2020 (medium confidence). Lighthouse cannot read third-party @font-face and marks the origin as unable to check.
findings.breaks_when: The brand contract requires TT Commons Pro / Helvetica Neue World: Adobe Fonts licence does not allow downloading the files, so the only lawful self-host is buying a web licence from the foundry; swapping to a look-alike open font changes the design; GDPR: Typekit transmits the visitor IP to Adobe (US) like Google Fonts does.
findings.how_to_apply: Short term: fonts.adobe.com > Web Projects > Edit Project > font-display = swap, then purge cache; add <link rel="preconnect" href="https://use.typekit.net" crossorigin> via Perfmatters Preloading > Preconnect. Long term for new builds: pick an open Greek-capable family and self-host via Elementor Pro Custom Fonts; if the client owns a webfont licence (TT Commons Pro is sold with self-hosting web licences by TypeType), upload the woff2 subset instead and remove the Typekit embed.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -s https://use.typekit.net/<kit>.css | grep -c 'font-display:swap' equals the number of @font-face rules; Lighthouse font-display audit has no typekit items; Network shows no use.typekit.net when the font is self-hosted; headings still render in the brand font (Rendered Fonts panel).

findings.claim: Elementor's local Google Fonts CSS declares every weight and subset (126 @font-face per family) but costs only ~1.3 KB gzipped and lets the browser download just the latin+greek files it needs, so 'remove unused weights' is wasted effort in Elementor 4.x; the real lever is the number of families and per-widget families.
findings.detail: pallada.gr /wp-content/uploads/elementor/google-fonts/css/inter.css: 45,036 bytes raw, 1,259 bytes gzip, 126 @font-face = 9 weights x 2 styles x 7 unicode-range subsets (latin, latin-ext, greek, greek-ext, cyrillic, cyrillic-ext, vietnamese), each with font-display: swap and the same unicode-range Google serves. The browser fetched only 2 Inter files on cretaforums (latin 47.1 KB, 518 glyphs; greek 18.6 KB, 144 glyphs) despite the 126 declarations. The remote variant (limnoupolis) requests css?family=Open+Sans:100,100italic,...,900italic&display=swap (3.0 KB) and downloads only the one Open Sans file used (42.5 KB). Note: the help article says fonts are stored in /wp-content/uploads/elementor/fonts/, but live 4.3.x sites use /wp-content/uploads/elementor/google-fonts/{css,fonts}/. The audit shows widget-level families adding 3-5 extra families (limnoupolis: +Inter, Comfortaa, Roboto, Lato; marakaki: +Noto Serif, Ysabeau, Roboto, Inter, Open Sans): every extra family used on a page is one more CSS file plus ~20-70 KB of woff2.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break.
findings.how_to_apply: Audit rule: count distinct font families per page (kit + widget overrides) rather than weights; in the builder set typography only in Site Settings > Global Fonts and leave widget 'Family' at Default; in debloat, list widgets whose settings contain typography_font_family that differs from the kit and propose resetting them (data change, needs approval). Perfmatters 'Limit Subsets' (Latin + Greek) only trims the CSS of Perfmatters-local fonts ('80% decrease in the font CSS size when selecting one specific subset') and is unnecessary when Elementor hosts the fonts.
findings.how_to_verify: Count <link id^='elementor-gf-'> in the page source (target <= 2); DevTools Network 'font' count <= 4; audit.php 'usage' fonts list shows only the kit families.

findings.claim: Once fonts are self-hosted via Pro Custom Fonts, set Elementor > Settings > Advanced > 'Google Fonts' = Disable so stray widget-level Google families can never trigger a Google request again (marakaki already does this).
findings.detail: Elementor help 'Disable Google Fonts' (Last Update Jan 20 2026): 'From WP Admin, navigate to Elementor>Editor>Settings... Select the Advanced tab. In the pane, from the Google Fonts dropdown menu, select Disable... Google Fonts will not load on your site.' The article explicitly cites 'legal issues connected to the use of Google Fonts' as a reason. Audit summary: marakaki.com has 'Google fonts OFF (self-hosted)' and its home page loads only 3 self-hosted files. Side effect reported in WordPress.org support (search result, not opened): Google families disappear from the editor font list and widgets still set to them fall back to the generic family.
findings.breaks_when: Any widget, popup, template or kit setting still references a Google family (audit found 3-5 such families per site): those texts silently change to the generic sans/serif fallback - run the per-widget font audit and re-point them to the custom font first; third-party add-ons that call Elementor's Google font list may show an empty font dropdown.
findings.how_to_apply: 1) Upload the chosen families as woff2 in Elementor Pro > Custom Fonts. 2) Site Settings > Global Fonts: set all four globals to the custom fonts. 3) Fix widget overrides (audit list). 4) Elementor > Editor > Settings > Advanced > Google Fonts = Disable; Save; Tools > Regenerate CSS; purge cache.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -s <url> | grep -c -E 'fonts\.googleapis|fonts\.gstatic|elementor-gf-' returns 0 on home, a product page, a blog post and a popup-bearing page; visual diff of 5 key pages before/after; Elements > Rendered Fonts shows the custom family.

findings.claim: Only one tool may own Google Fonts: Elementor's 'Load Google Fonts Locally', Perfmatters 'Local Google Fonts', FlyingPress 'Self-Host Google Fonts' and LiteSpeed's 'Load Google Fonts Asynchronously'/'Remove Google Fonts' overlap, and 'Remove Google Fonts' without a local replacement changes the design.
findings.detail: LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1 (docs + plugin source): Page Optimization > Optimization: 'Load Google Fonts Asynchronously' (optm-ggfonts_async, OFF) - 'loads Google Fonts asynchronously without loading the other CSS that way. It also implements a preconnect to Google'; 'Remove Google Fonts' (optm-ggfonts_rm, OFF) - 'removes all Google Fonts from your site. Be sure to test it. Unless you have suitable replacement fonts stored locally, your site's style could change dramatically'; CSS Settings > 'Font Display Optimization' (optm-css_font_display, Default|Swap). LiteSpeed 'Localize Resources' is for external JavaScript, not fonts. Perfmatters Fonts: 'Disable Google Fonts', 'Display Swap', 'Local Google Fonts' (downloads to /wp-content/cache/perfmatters/<domain>/fonts/ and links xxxx.google-fonts.css; print method File or Inline; 'Limit Subsets'; 'CDN URL'; 'Clear Local Fonts'; removes existing preconnect/dns-prefetch to Google; does not catch @import url fonts). FlyingPress (May 21 2025): 'Self-Host Google Fonts' detects fonts.googleapis.com/fonts.gstatic.com during page caching and serves from wp-content/cache/flying-press/; 'Preload Fonts' auto; 'Use System Fonts First'. Elementor 'Load Google Fonts Locally' rewrites its own links to same-origin CSS, after which the optimizers' Google-font features find nothing to process (harmless), but two localisers both ON means fonts are downloaded twice into two cache folders and preloads may point at the wrong copy.
findings.breaks_when: LiteSpeed 'Remove Google Fonts' ON while Elementor still relies on Google Fonts (limnoupolis) -> all text falls to generic fonts; LiteSpeed 'Load Google Fonts Asynchronously' ON adds a flash of unstyled text and does nothing once fonts are local; Perfmatters 'Disable Google Fonts' ON with Elementor local fonts is a no-op but confuses debugging; Perfmatters local + FlyingPress self-host on the same site (both active on none of the audited sites, but plugin stacks drift).
findings.how_to_apply: Decision table for the plugin: LiteSpeed sites -> Elementor 'Load Google Fonts Locally' = Enable, LiteSpeed ggfonts_async OFF, ggfonts_rm OFF, Font Display Optimization = Swap. FlyingPress sites -> either Elementor local (then FlyingPress self-host is idle) or FlyingPress self-host; keep FlyingPress Preload Fonts ON. Perfmatters sites -> Elementor local Enable, Perfmatters Local Google Fonts OFF, Display Swap irrelevant, use Perfmatters only for Preload and Script Manager; or the reverse (Perfmatters Local + Limit Subsets latin,greek + Inline print method) with Elementor local Disabled. Never turn on two localisers.
findings.how_to_verify: Page source contains exactly one family stylesheet per family and it is same-origin; wp-content/uploads/elementor/google-fonts/ and wp-content/cache/perfmatters|flying-press/ are not both populated with fonts; Lighthouse third-party summary lists no font hosts; visual check that typography is unchanged.
findings.correction: Add two facts. (1) Perfmatters' own doc says 'If you're using Elementor version 3.30 or higher, they now host your Google Fonts locally for you automatically' - stale since Elementor 3.32.1 (2025-09-16) 'Disabled Load Google Fonts locally on all sites by default'; on a 4.x site with the Elementor toggle off, Perfmatters Local Google Fonts is a legitimate owner. (2) FlyingPress does not merely idle next to Elementor local fonts: on voreniahorizon.gr the elementor-gf-local-* <link>s point to wp-content/cache/flying-press/<hash>.ebgaramond.css (FlyingPress re-serves Elementor's local CSS from its own cache), so a stale Elementor font CSS also needs a FlyingPress purge. LiteSpeed options confirmed in 7.9.1 docs and source: optm-ggfonts_async (OFF; 'also implements a preconnect'), optm-ggfonts_rm (OFF; 'your site's style could change dramatically'), optm-css_font_display switch Default|Swap ('Swap is recommended'). The researcher's decision table stands.

findings.claim: GDPR makes self-hosting mandatory for these EU (Greek) sites: LG München I ruled in January 2022 that loading Google Fonts from Google's servers transmits the visitor's IP without legal basis (EUR 100 damages, EUR 250,000 threatened per further infringement), and the same logic applies to Typekit and Font Awesome CDN kits.
findings.detail: WP Tavern (Feb 3 2022) quoting the Munich regional court (case 3 O 17493/20): 'The automatic transmission of the IP address by the defendant to Google was an inadmissible encroachment on the plaintiff's general personality rights under data protection law... since it is possible to use the fonts without connecting to Google'; damages EUR 100; 'threatens a fine of EUR 250,000.00 for each case of infringement or, alternatively, six months imprisonment'. Elementor's own Jan 2026 docs now give 'Privacy concerns: GDPR and other data protection laws may restrict the transfer of user information to Google' as a reason for 'Load Google Fonts Locally', and 'Disable Google Fonts' cites 'legal issues'. Perfmatters doc: 'Usage of Google Fonts violates GDPR, unless you host them locally.' On the audited sites use.typekit.net, p.typekit.net (beacon), use.fontawesome.com and cdn.jsdelivr.net are also contacted before consent.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break; relevant when a cookie banner (Complianz/Cookie-Script) is configured to block Google Fonts until consent, which would delay fonts and cause FOUT - self-hosting removes that dependency.
findings.how_to_apply: Treat any request to fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com, use.typekit.net, p.typekit.net, use.fontawesome.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net (fonts/icons) as a release blocker in the audit; fix with Elementor local fonts / Pro Custom Fonts / Inline Font Icons as above; for Adobe Fonts obtain a self-host licence or change family.
findings.how_to_verify: Load the home page in a fresh profile without accepting the cookie banner and export the HAR: no font/CSS requests to the hosts above; repeat for a Greek and an English page and a WooCommerce product page.

findings.claim: google-webfonts-helper is the fastest way to get Greek+Latin woff2 files for Pro Custom Fonts without a subsetting toolchain: one merged greek_latin file per weight (Inter regular 29.7 KB, bold 30.6 KB) or a ready zip.
findings.detail: gwfh.mranftl.com/api/fonts/inter?subsets=latin,greek returns storeID 'greek_latin', version v20 (lastModified 2025-09-10), subsetMap greek:true latin:true, and per-variant woff2 URLs from fonts.gstatic.com that are Google's own merged latin+greek static instances; downloaded sizes: regular 29,668 bytes, 700 30,556 bytes. The zip endpoint /api/fonts/inter?download=zip&subsets=latin,greek&variants=regular,700&formats=woff2 returned HTTP 200, 60,479 bytes. Compared with Google's own split files (Inter latin 47.3 KB + greek 18.6 KB variable), two static merged weights total ~60 KB, equal to the variable pair, so for <=2 weights static self-hosting costs nothing extra; for 3+ weights the variable file wins (needs a custom @font-face, see open questions on variable-font upload in Pro).
findings.breaks_when: Latin-only pages download the Greek glyphs too (~+10 KB, no unicode-range split); gwfh builds can lag Google's live version (WP Tavern commenters noticed size differences), so hinting/glyph updates may differ from the Google-served copy; latin-ext (Polish, Turkish names) is excluded unless added to subsets.
findings.how_to_apply: Pick family on gwfh.mranftl.com, tick Charsets latin + greek (+ latin-ext if needed), select 2-3 weights, choose 'Modern Browsers' (woff2 only), download; upload each file as a weight in Elementor Pro > Custom Fonts; apply the font-display filter (swap); set Global Fonts; disable Google Fonts in Elementor. Automatable with curl against the API for the plugin's builder flow.
findings.how_to_verify: fontTools cmap check shows >=100 Greek codepoints and 190 Latin-1; Network shows one woff2 per weight (~30 KB for Inter) and no Google hosts; Greek/English headings render identically on Android Chrome and iOS Safari screenshots.
findings.correction: The gwfh facts check out (API: inter v20, lastModified 2025-09-10, storeID greek_latin). But the 'open question' about variable fonts is answerable and changes the advice: Elementor Pro DOES have 'Add Variable Font' (Elementor > Editor > Custom Elements > Custom Fonts; help page 'Use Variable Fonts' updated Oct 1 2026; introduced in Pro 3.24) - but the upload flow accepts a TTF ('click Select ttf file') and you must enter min/max weight/width. A variable TTF is several times larger than a woff2 slice (Inter variable TTF ~800 KB vs ~30 KB per static greek_latin woff2), so for performance the plugin should keep recommending 2-3 static woff2 weights via Add Static Font and treat the variable upload as a design-only option. Pro 4.0.0 (2026-03-30) added custom fonts to Atomic Editor typography and 4.2.0 fixed custom-font names with spaces, so Custom Fonts work in V4 elements too.

findings.claim: Custom Elementor icon sets (Fontello/IcoMoon zips) and theme icon fonts (Glyphicons) stay icon fonts even with Inline Font Icons on, fail the font-display audit, and should be replaced by uploaded SVGs for the handful of icons a hotel/villa site needs.
findings.detail: onar-seaside-lounge.gr loads /wp-content/uploads/elementor/custom-icons/kritiagro_icons/font/kritiagro_icons.woff2 (3 KB) flagged by Lighthouse font-display 243 ms; limnoupolis inline CSS declares @font-face 'Glyphicons Halflings' with woff2+woff+ttf sources from the theme. Elementor's 'Inline Font Icons' help only promises to avoid loading 'the Font-Awesome and the eicons libraries'. web.dev: 'The font-display strategies that work well for conventional web fonts don't work as well for icon fonts... icon fonts are more likely to cause significant layout shifts... When possible, replace icon fonts with SVGs.' Elementor's Icon control accepts an uploaded SVG once Settings > Advanced > 'Enable Unfiltered File Uploads' is on (Elementor sanitises SVG on upload).
findings.breaks_when: An icon set is used in dozens of widgets (re-pointing each to an SVG is manual work); SVG upload is blocked by hosting security or a hardening plugin; theme CSS references the Glyphicons class names in non-Elementor templates (forum, booking forms).
findings.how_to_apply: List custom icon set usage from Elementor data (icon.library != fa-solid/fa-regular/fa-brands); export the needed glyphs as SVG from the Fontello/IcoMoon project, upload via Icon control > Upload SVG; delete the custom icon set under Elementor > Custom Icons; for theme fonts remove the @font-face and dequeue the CSS when no element uses the classes. Until then, at least add font-display: swap to those @font-face rules (LiteSpeed Font Display Optimization = Swap does it automatically for cached CSS).
findings.how_to_verify: Network 'font' filter shows no custom-icons/*.woff2 or glyphicons*; Lighthouse font-display audit empty; icons render identically (screenshot compare) and are keyboard/screen-reader accessible (inline SVG with aria-hidden or title).

findings.claim: voreniahorizon.gr is serving NO web fonts today: Elementor's local Google Fonts CSS hard-codes absolute URLs of the domain at download time, the site moved from villavorenia.gr, and every font request 301-redirects to the new home page, so EB Garamond, Inter Tight and Lexend Deca all render in fallback fonts.
findings.detail: Verified today: voreniahorizon.gr home page links elementor-gf-local-ebgaramond/intertight/lexenddeca CSS (served from wp-content/cache/flying-press/<hash>.<family>.css); inside, all url() point to https://villavorenia.gr/wp-content/uploads/elementor/google-fonts/fonts/ebgaramond-xxxxxxxx.woff2; the untouched Elementor file /wp-content/uploads/elementor/google-fonts/css/ebgaramond.css on the new domain has the same old-domain URLs; curl of one font URL returns HTTP 301 to https://voreniahorizon.gr/ (HTML). The agency's Lighthouse run shows all 4 font requests with statusCode -1 and 0 bytes. Root cause: Google_Font::download_fonts stores the absolute upload URL in the CSS; a domain change without Elementor's 'Clear Files & Data' leaves stale URLs (changelog 3.28.1: 'Font URL is not updating after domain change' fix only applies when the cache is cleared; issue #30600 confirms 'Google Fonts are now cleared once you Clear Files and Data, and re-downloaded when the page is visited'). Related open bug #34657 (Feb-Jun 2026, 3.35.x): stale _elementor_local_google_fonts option keeps printing elementor-gf-local-* links after the toggle is turned off, causing 404s and in one report an 80-second load.
findings.breaks_when: Clearing Elementor files triggers a first-view re-download of every Google family (slow first load, needs write access to wp-content/uploads/elementor/google-fonts/); if the server cannot reach fonts.googleapis.com the code falls back to the Google CDN link (enqueue_from_cdn) - check the page source afterwards.
findings.how_to_apply: Elementor > Tools > General > 'Clear Files & Data' (or Regenerate CSS & Data), load the home page once as a visitor, then purge FlyingPress (its cache re-serves the Elementor CSS). For any migration/staging-to-live step in the plugin: after Replace URL always run Clear Files & Data and then purge the page cache. Audit rule: fetch every elementor-gf-local-* CSS and fail if any url() host differs from the site host or if _elementor_local_google_fonts exists while elementor_local_google_fonts = 0.
findings.how_to_verify: curl the three *.css files and grep url(): hosts must equal voreniahorizon.gr; DevTools Network 'font' filter shows 200 responses with content-type font/woff2; Elements > Computed > Rendered Fonts on the h1 shows 'EB Garamond' not a system serif; re-run Lighthouse: font requests have statusCode 200 and the font-display audit still passes; compare screenshots (the whole typography of the site will change back to the design).

findings.claim: Elementor's 'Load Google Fonts Locally' has a precise lifecycle the plugin should encode: option elementor_local_google_fonts (default '0' since 3.32.1), files under uploads/elementor/google-fonts/{css,fonts}, filenames = first 8 hex of sha1(gstatic URL), cache cleared by Clear Files & Data, by toggling the option, and by changing Google Fonts Load; on fetch failure it silently falls back to the Google CDN.
findings.detail: From Elementor 4.3.5 trunk: Google_Font::enqueue() returns the local style if the CSS file exists, otherwise, when get_option('elementor_local_google_fonts','0') is truthy, it fetches the Google CSS with a Chrome UA, downloads each url() into fonts/, writes css/<family>.css and records state in option _elementor_local_google_fonts; if the remote fetch fails it enqueues the fonts.googleapis.com link instead (handle elementor-gf-<family>, so a site can mix local and remote families). clear_cache() unlinks everything in both folders and deletes _elementor_local_google_fonts; it is hooked to add/update_option elementor_local_google_fonts, update_option_elementor_font_display and to Files_Manager::clear_cache (Tools > Clear Files & Data, plugin activation/deactivation, theme switch). Changelog: introduced 3.27.0 (2025-01-20), default-on 3.28.0, merged into core 3.30.0, default-off for all sites 3.32.1 (2025-09-16), notice added 3.32.4. Help page 'Elementor and Google fonts' (Jan 20 2026) still says /uploads/elementor/fonts/ - wrong path.
findings.breaks_when: Mixed state: if one family's remote fetch failed once, that family is served from Google while others are local (GDPR + extra connection); a page-cache plugin caching the HTML before the first download leaves <link> tags pointing at the CDN until purge; sites whose uploads folder is read-only never localise and the setting looks 'on' while doing nothing.
findings.how_to_apply: Audit script: read options elementor_local_google_fonts, _elementor_local_google_fonts, elementor_font_display, elementor_google_font and list files in uploads/elementor/google-fonts/css; flag any front-end <link id='elementor-gf-*'> without '-local-'. After enabling the toggle: visit the home, a product page and a Greek post as a logged-out visitor, then purge page cache. Document in the plugin that 'Regenerate CSS & Data' re-downloads fonts (one slow first view).
findings.how_to_verify: ls wp-content/uploads/elementor/google-fonts/css/ lists one <family>.css per family in use; page source has only elementor-gf-local-* font links; Lighthouse third-party summary has no fonts.googleapis.com/gstatic.com.

findings.claim: Elementor exposes three PHP filters that let the plugin enforce font policy in a must-use plugin without touching the UI: elementor/frontend/print_google_fonts (kill all Google requests), elementor/frontend/google_font_subsets (locale -> subset map; 'el' => 'greek' is built in), and elementor_pro/custom_fonts/font_display (swap for Pro custom fonts).
findings.detail: includes/frontend.php: apply_filters('elementor/frontend/print_google_fonts', $print_google_fonts) gates enqueue_google_fonts(); apply_filters('elementor/frontend/google_font_subsets', $subsets) with default map including 'el' => 'greek' appended as &subset= to the legacy css?family= URL. Elementor Pro 2.7 developer post (Aug 19 2019): add_filter('elementor_pro/custom_fonts/font_display', function($current_value,$font_family,$data){ return 'swap'; },10,3); default 'auto'; 'you will need to regenerate the CSS via Elementor > Tools > Regenerate CSS'. The Pro filter is not referenced in any 4.x changelog entry as removed; the Pro 4.x changelog only mentions custom-font fixes (4.2.0 names with spaces, 4.0.0 Atomic typography support), so treat 'still works in Pro 4.3' as likely but unverified against Pro source (Pro is closed source).
findings.breaks_when: print_google_fonts=false while widgets still use Google families (same effect as 'Google Fonts = Disable'); the Pro filter has no effect until each font's CSS is regenerated.
findings.how_to_apply: Ship an optional mu-plugin: add_filter('elementor_pro/custom_fonts/font_display', fn()=>'swap', 10, 3); and, for sites fully on Pro Custom Fonts, add_filter('elementor/frontend/print_google_fonts','__return_false'); then Elementor > Tools > Regenerate CSS & Data and purge cache.
findings.how_to_verify: View the Pro custom-fonts CSS (post-css/*.css or inline) and confirm 'font-display: swap' on every @font-face; page source has zero fonts.googleapis.com links.

findings.claim: Audit rule for 'Inline Font Icons': its effective default depends on the site's first-installed Elementor version (>= 3.17.0 => active by default), so read option elementor_experiment-e_font_icon_svg and elementor_install_history instead of assuming 4.x = on.
findings.detail: core/experiments/manager.php registers e_font_icon_svg with release_status stable, 'new_site' => ['default_active' => true, 'minimum_installation_version' => '3.17.0']; older installs resolve 'default' to inactive. Changelog: experiment introduced 3.1.0 era ('Font Awesome Inline SVG'), default-on for new sites 3.18.0 (2023-12-04), stable 3.20.0 (2024-03-11). Observed: onar (Elementor 4.2.3, old install) has it off and loads fa-solid-900.woff 76 KB; the 3.33 system-info dump the researcher saw ('Active by default') was from a newer install. Icons_Manager also keeps the FA4 shim option elementor_load_fa4_shim and renders uploaded SVGs via Svg::get_inline_svg when icon library == 'svg'.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break (read-only audit rule); the risks are those of enabling the feature (see verdict 6).
findings.how_to_apply: audit.php: add 'elementor_experiment-e_font_icon_svg' to the options list and report effective state = option value, or when 'default', compare the first version in elementor_install_history to 3.17.0. Debloat: propose activation only after the widget sweep listed in verdict 6.
findings.how_to_verify: Elementor > Settings > Features shows the computed state; front end stops loading fontawesome/eicons CSS and fonts (Network 'font' filter) when active.

findings.claim: V4 atomic elements route font-family values through the same enqueue path as V3 (Styles_Renderer::maybe_enqueue_font -> Font_Family_Prop_Type -> Frontend::enqueue_google_fonts), and Pro 4.0.0 added custom fonts to Atomic typography, so the local/Google/custom-font decisions above apply unchanged to V4 pages; V4 typography still offers no fallback stack UI.
findings.detail: modules/atomic-widgets/styles/styles-renderer.php: maybe_enqueue_font() resolves a Font_Enqueueable prop type and calls the on_font_enqueue callback with the family name; modules/atomic-widgets/styles/style-fonts.php stores enqueued families per style in option elementor_atomic_styles_fonts-<style_key>. Pro changelog 4.0.0 (2026-03-30): 'Added support for custom fonts in typography controls - Atomic Editor'; 4.2.0: 'Fix: Custom Font names with spaces or special characters do not work in the Font Family control - Atomic Editor'. Help 'Style tab Typography' (V4, Jul 1 2025) lists only Font family/weight/size etc., no fallback control. The exact callback target (whether it is Frontend::enqueue_google_fonts) was not traced to the line, hence medium confidence.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break.
findings.how_to_apply: In the builder skill, keep typography in V4 Variables/Classes (one body, one heading family) rather than per-element; for a size-adjusted fallback use a global CSS class/Custom CSS as in verdict 9. Audit: include options matching elementor_atomic_styles_fonts-* when counting families per page.
findings.how_to_verify: On a V4 page view source: font <link> ids are the same elementor-gf-local-* handles as V3 pages; count of distinct families <= 2.

title: Images, hero/LCP, video and sliders
summary: On the audited sites the LCP problem is almost never "image too big" and almost always "LCP resource discovered or prioritised late": limnoupolis.gr's hero carries loading="lazy" (LCP 7.7 s, Load Delay 4.3 s), staging.limnoupolis.gr and marakaki.com use a container CSS background as hero (LCP 10.2 s / 5.2 s, Load Delay 8.4 s / 2.2 s because the URL only exists in post-NNN.css), while the fast sites (pallada 86, platonos 84) have text or static-image heroes. Elementor 4.3.x's "Optimized Image Loading" (option elementor_optimized_image_loading, default on) replaces WordPress core logic with its own: it disables wp_lazy_loading_enabled and core fetchpriority, buffers header-to-content HTML, leaves only the first 3 that have width+height eager, and gives fetchpriority="high" to the first of those with >= 50,000 px² - so a header logo (marakaki 768x124, limnoupolis 2352.png/1-768x512.png) takes the high slot and a hero that is the 4th image is lazy-loaded. The omit threshold (3) is hard-coded; only elementor/image-loading-optimization/min_priority_img_pixels is filterable, and footer-template images are not processed at all (they load eagerly). The robust fixes are: make the hero a real (Image widget, not container background), force fetchpriority="high"/loading="eager" on it via wp_get_attachment_image_attributes keyed by attachment ID (Elementor honours explicit values), or let one page-optimiser own the above-the-fold logic (Perfmatters "Preload Critical Images"/"Fetch Priority", FlyingPress cloud detection, LiteSpeed VPI) and turn the others off. Elementor's second default-on feature, "Lazy Load Background Images", hides background-image on every top-level container from the 3rd one down (2nd on viewports <= 640 px high) until an IntersectionObserver fires after DOMContentLoaded; a hero that is not the first or second .e-con.e-parent is delayed, and class e-no-lazyload is the escape hatch. Background images always use the full-size upload unless "Image Resolution" is changed on the media control, and the control is responsive, so a separate mobile image (e.g. 800 px AVIF/WebP) is possible. Video: the container background-video handler skips entirely on the "mobile" device mode unless "Play On Mobile" is on, so a hero video costs nothing in mobile Lighthouse unless that toggle is set - two sites (kand, voreniahorizon) do load an .mp4 on mobile; the Video widget's "Lazy Load" + "Image Overlay" combination is a facade that defers the YouTube API to click, and hosted video gets preload="metadata" by default (set "None" + Poster). Image Carousel (Swiper) renders hand-built tags with no width/height/loading attributes and an optional Swiper data-src lazyload, so any above-the-fold carousel is both a CLS and LCP-discovery hazard; web.dev advises a static first slide. Format conversion is a smaller lever on these sites (modern-image-formats savings <= 9 KiB): WordPress 6.5+ natively supports AVIF, and Converter for Media (AVIF is PRO), ShortPixel, Imagify, TinyPNG, Elementor Image Optimizer and LiteSpeed/QUIC.cloud all convert; pick one, never two (limnoupolis runs TinyPNG + Converter for Media). JS lazy-loaders (LiteSpeed) must be paired with "Responsive Placeholder" + "Add Missing Sizes" + VPI/excludes or they add CLS (the 0 -> 0.107 staging result) and LCP delay.
critic_notes: Method: re-read the Elementor main-branch sources (ILO module, lazyload module, image-size.php, image.php, image-carousel.php, video.php, background-video.js, container.php, background.php, media.php, atomic-image twig, atomic-youtube.php), read Elementor Pro 4.3.1 and Elementor 4.3.4 files directly from voreniahorizon.gr via Novamira read-only read-file/list-directory (slides.php, media-carousel.php, loop-carousel.php, image-transformer.php, image-src-transformer.php, image-prop-type.php, image-sizes.php), opened the cited web.dev / Chrome / Perfmatters / FlyingPress / LiteSpeed / WP Rocket / Elementor help / Zinruss / Make-Core pages via curl (WebFetch DNS failed for every host in this session), and parsed the 10 local Lighthouse JSON runs. Open questions status: (1) Pro Slides/Loop/Media Carousel markup - RESOLVED (addition 3). (2) V4 atomic Image rendering - RESOLVED: does not use wp_get_attachment_image (addition 2). (3) FlyingPress fetchpriority on preloads - still unknown; the May 2025 lazy-load article says 'preloads key above-the-fold images' but never mentions fetchpriority; the 'Preload critical images' article URL now 404s. (4) Perfmatters labels - verified: 'Add Missing Image Dimensions' (own doc, Lazy Loading submenu, no lazy required, not for external images), 'Viewport threshold' + perfmatters_lazyload_threshold filter, 'Fade in', 'CSS Background Images', 'Exclude leading images', 'YouTube Preview Thumbnails', 'Disable Core Fetch'. (5) ILO buffer vs Pro header - not directly verified, but limnoupolis header images carrying fetchpriority=high (researcher's evidence) implies the buffer captured the header there; hook-order risk remains theoretical. (6) VPI quota - not checked. (7) Image converter benchmark - not done. (8) Lighthouse lcp-lazy-loaded doc - confirmed 404 on developer.chrome.com; use web.dev/articles/lcp-lazy-loading or the Lighthouse JSON audit id instead. Not checked: developer.wordpress.org hook pages, Make-Core 6.5 AVIF note, the other image-converter plugin pages, handlers/video.js and background-slideshow.js, Elementor help 'section-background-video-options'. Risk for the user: Pro widget markup was read from one site's Pro 4.3.1 copy; verify again after Pro updates, and the Elementor main branch may be ahead of the installed 4.2.3-4.3.5 versions for the ILO/lazyload modules (the installed 4.3.4 atomic-image files matched main). Local scratch copies of everything opened are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/critic-img/.

findings.claim: Elementor 4.3.x 'Optimized Image Loading' lazy-loads every after the third one that has width+height and gives fetchpriority="high" to the first image >= 50,000 px² - so a header logo consumes the high slot and a hero that is the 4th image on the page gets loading="lazy" and becomes a late LCP.
findings.detail: modules/image-loading-optimization/module.php (main branch, 4.3.x): option elementor_optimized_image_loading default '1'; constructor adds `add_filter('wp_lazy_loading_enabled','__return_false')` and calls `wp_high_priority_element_flag(false)` on init (WP core lazy and fetchpriority are both switched off); ob_start at get_header, flushed at the_content priority 0, plus filter wp_content_img_tag. `$omit_threshold = 3` (hard-coded, no filter), `$min_priority_img_pixels = 50000` (filter elementor/image-loading-optimization/min_priority_img_pixels). Images without ` width="` and ` height="` are returned untouched (no lazy, no priority). Explicit loading="eager"/fetchpriority="high" already present are honoured and do not count toward the 3. Local evidence: limnoupolis.gr LCP element is `` (lcp-lazy-loaded audit fails, LCP 7.7 s, Load Delay 4.27 s) while header images 2352.png and 1-768x512.png load at priority High; marakaki.com gives High to the 768x124 logo. Elementor's help page (Last Update Sept 25 2026) only says lazy loading is not applied to above-the-fold images - the actual rule is a positional count of 3.
findings.breaks_when: Raising min_priority_img_pixels above the logo size is safe; but if you force fetchpriority=high on more than 1-2 images Chrome's prioritisation stops helping (web.dev). If the header has >= 3 raster with dimensions (logo + flags + icons), the hero still gets lazy unless you also set loading=eager on it explicitly. Changing the option does not purge caches - flush LiteSpeed/FlyingPress/W3TC after.
findings.how_to_apply: Diagnose: view-source on mobile UA, find the hero , check for loading="lazy" and which image carries fetchpriority="high". Fix A (snippet, mu-plugin): `add_filter('wp_get_attachment_image_attributes', function($attr,$att){ if( in_array($att->ID, [15401 /* hero IDs */], true) ){ $attr['loading']='eager'; $attr['fetchpriority']='high'; } return $attr; }, 10, 2);` - Elementor's module sees the explicit values, keeps them, and does not spend a slot. Fix B (one-liner so the logo cannot take the slot): `add_filter('elementor/image-loading-optimization/min_priority_img_pixels', fn() => 200000);` (logo 768x124 = 95,232 px² < 200k; hero 800x384 = 307,200 px² qualifies). Fix C: give header logos an SVG/inline logo (no width/height → not counted). Fix D: Elementor > Settings > Performance > Optimized Image Loading = Disable and let Perfmatters/FlyingPress/LiteSpeed VPI own above-the-fold logic (then WP core's wp_omit_loading_attr_threshold and wp_min_priority_img_pixels filters apply again).
findings.how_to_verify: PageSpeed Insights mobile: 'Largest Contentful Paint image was lazily loaded' audit must disappear and 'LCP request discovery' insight must show all three checks green; DevTools Network: hero image Priority = High and requested in the first ~5 requests after HTML; Lighthouse JSON audits['lcp-lazy-loaded'].score == 1 and audits['largest-contentful-paint-element'] phases: Load Delay < 300 ms. Visual check: logo still appears before text (it stays eager, only priority changes).

findings.claim: A hero built as a container Background Image is invisible to the browser's preload scanner because its URL lives only in post-NNN.css; converting the hero to an Image widget (or preloading the background with fetchpriority=high) removes 2-8 s of LCP load delay on the audited sites.
findings.detail: staging.limnoupolis.gr: LCP element is `div.e-con ... data-settings={background_background:classic}`; Lighthouse initiator chain shows the image was requested by `post-13852.css` (pathLength 3), LCP 10.2 s with Load Delay 8.4 s. marakaki.com: same pattern via Dynamic.ooo `data-dce-background-image-url`, Load Delay 2.2 s. web.dev Optimize LCP (updated 2025-03-31): resources referenced only from external CSS are not discoverable; preload them with ``, and 'Never lazy-load your LCP image'. Chrome 'LCP request discovery' insight (2025-10-08): fetchpriority=high on the img or on its preload, discoverable from HTML, no loading=lazy; when preloading set fetchpriority=high on both. Zinruss (June 2026) documents the same Elementor-specific failure and gives the preload-via-wp_head and +object-fit refactor. Background group control (background.php) emits `background-image: url("{{URL}}")` with no img tag.
findings.breaks_when: Preload URL must be byte-identical to the one the CSS requests (CDN rewriting, WebP/AVIF rewriting by Converter for Media/ShortPixel, or responsive mobile background image changes the URL) - a mismatch downloads two images. Preloading a desktop image on mobile wastes bandwidth: use imagesrcset/imagesizes or Perfmatters per-device preload with 'Mobile' only if separate mobile cache exists. Refactoring to an Image widget changes layout (text overlay needs the container with position:relative and the image absolutely positioned with object-fit:cover, or a Grid container with stacked cells).
findings.how_to_apply: Preferred (build-time rule): hero = Flexbox/Grid container with an Image widget (Image Resolution = a 1.5-2x-of-mobile-width size, e.g. 'large' 1024 px or a custom 1200 px) + overlay text; CSS `.hero img{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover}`. Retrofit: keep background but add a preload: Perfmatters > Preloading > Preload > URL of the exact background file, type Image, Priority 'High', Location 'front' (or post ID), device All/Mobile; or snippet `add_action('wp_head', function(){ if(is_front_page()) echo '<link rel="preload" as="image" href="https://.../hero-800.webp" imagesrcset="https://.../hero-800.webp 800w, https://.../hero-1600.webp 1600w" imagesizes="100vw" fetchpriority="high">'; }, 1);`. Also make sure the container is not hidden by Lazy Load Background Images (see finding on e-no-lazyload).
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse JSON audits['prioritize-lcp-image'] score 1 and initiatorPath pathLength == 2 (HTML → image); LCP phases: Load Delay < 300 ms, Load Time < 600 ms; Network panel shows the hero as one of the first 3 image requests at Priority High with no duplicate download (filter by filename, expect exactly 1 request). Screenshot mobile 412x823 before/after to confirm identical rendering.
findings.correction: 'Image Resolution = ... or a custom 1200 px' must NOT mean Elementor's built-in 'Custom' option. In includes/controls/groups/image-size.php get_attachment_image_html() only calls wp_get_attachment_image() when the size key is in get_intermediate_image_sizes()+'full'; any other value ('custom' dimensions, or static render mode) falls into a hand-built `` with NO width/height, NO srcset and a hard-coded loading="lazy" that ILO/Perfmatters will honour. Use a registered size (add_image_size + image_size_names_choose) instead. Corrected risk: low (unchanged) once that rule is followed.

findings.claim: Elementor's default-on 'Lazy Load Background Images' hides background-image on the 3rd top-level container and below (2nd and below when viewport height <= 640 px) until an IntersectionObserver fires after DOMContentLoaded; a hero that is not the first/second .e-con.e-parent is delayed, and `e-no-lazyload` on the container is the exemption.
findings.detail: modules/lazyload/module.php: option elementor_lazy_load_background_images default '1'; wp_head CSS `.e-con.e-parent:nth-of-type(n+4):not(.e-lazyloaded):not(.e-no-lazyload), ... * { background-image: none !important; }`, `@media (max-height:1024px)` → n+3, `@media (max-height:640px)` → n+2; wp_footer script observes `.e-con.e-parent:not(.e-lazyloaded)` with rootMargin 200px and adds `.e-lazyloaded` on DOMContentLoaded or `elementor/lazyload/observe`. Lighthouse mobile emulates 412x823 → the 1024 rule applies: only the first two top-level containers keep their backgrounds at first paint. The rule also hits all descendants (`*`), so widgets with background images inside the 3rd container are hidden too. Settings label: Elementor > Settings > Performance > 'Lazy Load Background Images' ('all background images except the first one').
findings.breaks_when: Pages with an announcement bar container + header-in-page container + hero container (hero is 3rd) → hero bg appears only after DOMContentLoaded, i.e. after all parser-blocking JS (GTM, three.js). Disabling the option globally makes every background image eager (bandwidth), so prefer the class. Elementor Pro header/footer template containers are separate parents and do not count.
findings.how_to_apply: Per page: select the hero container > Advanced > CSS Classes: add `e-no-lazyload`. Keep the hero as the first or second top-level container (merge notice bars into the header template). Build rule for new sites: top-level container #1 = hero. Global switch only if needed: Elementor > Settings > Performance > Lazy Load Background Images = Disable (option elementor_lazy_load_background_images = 0).
findings.how_to_verify: View source: hero container must have class e-no-lazyload or be nth-of-type <= 2 among `.e-con.e-parent` siblings; DevTools > Elements on mobile emulation at first paint: computed background-image on the hero is a url(), not none; Lighthouse filmstrip shows hero image in the first frame after FCP; LCP Load Delay drops.
tools: Elementor setting: Lazy Load Background Images
findings.correction: Default rule `.e-con.e-parent:nth-of-type(n+4)` hides the 4th container and below (viewport height > 1024 px, i.e. desktop); `@media (max-height:1024px)` -> n+3 (3rd and below; this is what Lighthouse mobile 412x823 hits); `@media (max-height:640px)` -> n+2 (2nd and below; landscape phones). So on desktop the hero may be 3rd and still show; on mobile it must be 1st or 2nd. nth-of-type counts sibling elements of the same tag (div) inside the `.elementor` wrapper, so any non-container div inserted before the hero by a plugin shifts the count. Help page (Last Update December 17, 2024) describes it as 'all background images except the first one', which is imprecise.

findings.claim: Only one layer should decide lazy-load/preload/fetchpriority for above-the-fold images; with Elementor ILO + a cache plugin's lazy-load both active, the hero gets loading="lazy" from Elementor and a JS placeholder from the optimiser, and each plugin has a specific exclusion mechanism that must be used.
findings.detail: Perfmatters (docs): its lazy loader is a 2.5 KB JS library; enabling it disables WP native lazy; options 'Images', 'iFrames and Videos', 'Exclude Leading Images' (count from top, 'does not work on background images'), 'Exclude from Lazy Loading' (URL or attribute fragment), class `no-lazy`, viewport threshold (filter perfmatters_lazyload_threshold), 'DOM Monitoring', 'CSS Background Images' with Background Selectors or class `perfmatters-lazy-css-bg`; 'Preload Critical Images' (0-5, recommends 2-3 because Chrome has a soft limit of two preloads at the top of the waterfall) auto-excludes those images from lazy; filters perfmatters_critical_image_exclusions, perfmatters_preloads. 'Fetch Priority' feature: add class/ID/filename, High/Low, 'Search by Parent Selector' (target the hero container class), per device/location; images with fetchpriority are auto-excluded from Perfmatters lazy. FlyingPress (docs 2025): cloud optimizer detects above-the-fold media, marks it loading="eager" and preloads it; exclusions by any keyword in the tag; uses native loading=lazy (Chrome loads lazy images 1250 px/2500 px before viewport). LiteSpeed Cache 7.x: Page Optimization > Media: 'Lazy Load Images' (OFF default, disables WP core lazy when ON), 'Lazy Load iframes', 'Responsive Placeholder', 'Add Missing Sizes' (only with lazy ON), Media Excludes: 'Lazy Load Image Excludes', 'Lazy Load Image Class Name Excludes', 'Lazy Load Image Parent Class Name Excludes', 'Lazy Load URI Excludes'; VPI tab: 'Viewport Images' + 'Viewport Images Cron' (QUIC.cloud quota; viewport images are excluded from lazy AND preloaded; 'Preload Featured Image' removed in favour of VPI). WP Rocket (reference pattern): 'Optimize critical images' auto-preloads the LCP image with fetchpriority=high, excludes above-fold images from lazy, per device via Mobile Cache.
findings.breaks_when: Two lazy loaders active (Elementor ILO + LiteSpeed/Perfmatters) → hero carries loading=lazy AND data-src; exclusions in one plugin do not remove the other's attribute (Perfmatters only removes core/ILO lazy on images it preloads or that have fetchpriority). LiteSpeed lazy without VPI/excludes lazy-loads the hero and logo; Perfmatters 'Exclude Leading Images' counted while logged in gives the wrong number (admin bar images); FlyingPress above-the-fold detection is per cloud run - a redesigned hero needs a re-run/cache purge.
findings.how_to_apply: Pick ONE owner per site. Sites with Perfmatters (marakaki, onar, pallada): Perfmatters > Lazy Loading: Images ON, iFrames and Videos ON, YouTube Preview Thumbnails ON, Exclude Leading Images = count of real above the fold on mobile (typically 2-3), Preloading > Preload Critical Images = 2; then Elementor > Settings > Performance > Optimized Image Loading = Disable (so Elementor does not inject loading=lazy on the hero first). Sites with FlyingPress (cretaforums, voreniahorizon): FlyingPress > Images > Lazy load ON (keep native), add logo/hero keyword to exclusions only if the cloud detection misses them; disable Elementor ILO. Sites with LiteSpeed (limnoupolis, onar): if you enable Lazy Load Images also enable Responsive Placeholder + Add Missing Sizes + VPI (+ VPI Cron) and put the hero/logo filenames in 'Lazy Load Image Excludes'; otherwise leave LiteSpeed lazy OFF and keep Elementor ILO with the hero fix from finding 1.
findings.how_to_verify: Rendered mobile HTML: hero has neither loading="lazy" nor data-src/data-lazyloaded; exactly one `` per critical image; Lighthouse 'lcp-lazy-loaded' passes; 'offscreen-images' savings should go to ~0 KiB (below-fold images deferred) while CLS stays <= 0.01; compare the network request count before/after on the home page (should drop by the number of below-fold images).

findings.claim: Container background images always use the full-size upload unless 'Image Resolution' is changed in the media control, and the background image control is responsive - so a mobile-specific 800-900 px WebP/AVIF background is available in the editor without code.
findings.detail: background.php: field `image` is `Controls_Manager::MEDIA` with `'responsive' => true` and `'has_sizes' => true`; media.php renders an 'Image Resolution' select (data-setting="size") whose empty default is 'Full'. Image widget default is `'default' => 'large'` (image-size.php group control, label 'Image Resolution'), rendered through wp_get_attachment_image() so srcset/sizes exist; backgrounds get a single URL. Lighthouse evidence: voreniahorizon.gr hero image `vorenia-horizon-aerial-09.webp` full size 172 KB at width=1920 served into a 412 px viewport; kand.dev6 `kand-gold-rings-on-hand.webp` 280 KB full-size, no srcset, 273 KB waste; fagitiotiszois 1,101 KiB 'Properly size images' savings. Chrome 'Improve image delivery' insight flags bytes-to-pixel ratio and recommends responsive sizes + AVIF/WebP.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break. Caveat: a background 'Image Resolution' of 'large' (1024 px) on a 1920 px desktop hero looks soft at DPR 2 - use the responsive switcher to set Full/custom on desktop and a smaller size on tablet/mobile; custom sizes need regeneration for old uploads (WP generates intermediate sizes at upload only).
findings.how_to_apply: Editor: Container > Style > Background > Image: set 'Image Resolution' = Large or a registered custom size, then click the responsive switcher next to 'Image' and choose a different (smaller, pre-cropped) image for Mobile. For new sites register sizes in the theme: `add_image_size('hero-mobile', 900, 1200, true); add_image_size('hero-desktop', 1920, 1080, true);` and make them selectable: `add_filter('image_size_names_choose', fn($s) => $s + ['hero-mobile' => 'Hero mobile', 'hero-desktop' => 'Hero desktop']);`. Upload hero masters <= 2560 px (WP big_image_size_threshold) and let the optimiser create WebP/AVIF for all sizes.
findings.how_to_verify: PSI mobile 'Properly size images' lists no hero/background entry; Network shows the mobile URL (e.g. -900x1200.webp) < 120 KB; audits['uses-responsive-images'] wastedBytes for the hero == 0; visually compare at 412 px and at 1920 px (no blur).

findings.claim: Elementor's container Background Video handler does not create a player at all when 'Play On Mobile' is off and the device mode is mobile, so a hero video costs nothing in mobile Lighthouse unless that toggle is on - two audited sites do load an .mp4 on mobile and should use the Background Fallback image instead.
findings.detail: assets/dev/js/frontend/handlers/background-video.js: run() returns early when `! elementSettings.background_play_on_mobile && 'mobile' === elementorFrontend.getCurrentDeviceMode()`; no IntersectionObserver - on desktop/tablet the hosted <video> gets its src immediately on init, YouTube waits for the IFrame API (`onApiReady`), Vimeo creates `new Vimeo.Player` with autoplay/muted/background; `background_privacy_mode` switches to youtube-nocookie.com. container.php adds class `elementor-hidden-mobile` to the wrapper when play_on_mobile is off. Controls (background.php): 'Video Link', 'Start Time', 'End Time', 'Play Once', 'Play On Mobile', 'Privacy Mode', 'Background Fallback' ("cover image will replace the background video in case that the video could not be loaded", output as `background: url() 50% 50%; background-size: cover`). Elementor help (Last Update Oct 26 2025) notes autoplay fails under power-saving/Data Saver. Lighthouse mobile: kand.dev6 loads kand-hero-editorial.mp4 (82 KB) and voreniahorizon.gr Main-Video-Final.mp4 (262 KB) on a 412 px viewport; limnoupolis loads no media on mobile. Device mode 'mobile' follows Elementor breakpoints (default <= 767 px), so tablets still load the video.
findings.breaks_when: Turning 'Play On Mobile' off removes the video on phones - the Background Fallback image must be set or the hero shows a flat colour. The fallback image is itself a CSS background (not preload-scanner discoverable) - preload it or layer an Image widget under the video. YouTube/Vimeo background videos add third-party JS/iframes on desktop (TBT) - prefer a self-hosted, muted, <= 1.5 MB MP4/WebM trimmed to 8-12 s.
findings.how_to_apply: Container > Style > Background > Video: 'Play On Mobile' = No; 'Background Fallback' = the mobile hero image (same file you preload with fetchpriority=high); 'Privacy Mode' = Yes for YouTube; prefer self-hosted MP4 (H.264, 1280x720, CRF 28-30, no audio track). For desktop keep the video but reduce TBT by avoiding YouTube/Vimeo as background source. Build rule: no autoplay video in the mobile hero; a static image hero is what the two fastest audited sites use.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse mobile JSON: no network-requests item with resourceType 'Media' or '.mp4' in URL; third-party summary shows no youtube.com/vimeo.com on mobile; TBT drops; the hero area still shows the fallback image in the filmstrip; desktop Lighthouse still plays the video (manual check in a 1366 px window).
tools: Elementor Background Video: Play On Mobile, Background Fallback, Privacy Mode
findings.correction: THREE audited sites load an MP4 on the 412 px mobile run, not two - kand.dev6 (kand-hero-editorial.mp4), voreniahorizon.gr (Main-Video-Final.mp4) and onar-seaside-lounge.gr (onar-seaside-lounge.mp4). Whether those are Elementor background videos with Play On Mobile on, Video widgets, or theme/Dynamic.ooo markup was not verified per site - check each before assuming the toggle is the fix.

findings.claim: The Elementor Video widget's 'Lazy Load' switch plus an 'Image Overlay' is a true facade (YouTube API only loads on click); without an overlay, lazy load only means IntersectionObserver, which does nothing for an above-the-fold video; the V4 atomic YouTube element has a 'Lazy load' prop defaulting to false.
findings.detail: includes/widgets/video.php: control `lazy_load` ('Lazy Load') shown for video_type youtube or when show_image_overlay is set; `get_embed_options()['lazy_load']`; help text: 'load the video widget data only after the visitor scrolls and the video appears in the viewport'. handlers/video.js: with lazy_load the handler uses `elementorModules.utils.Scroll.scrollObserver` on the parent and loads the YouTube API on intersection; if `show_image_overlay && image_overlay.url` the API load is skipped at init and happens on click of `.elementor-custom-embed-image-overlay`; for non-YouTube iframes a `data-lazy-load` URL is assigned to src on play. atomic-youtube.php (Editor V4): `'lazyload' => Boolean_Prop_Type::make()->default(false)` with a 'Lazy load' switch. Lighthouse 'third-party-facades' audit (Chrome docs) flags YouTube embedded player when loaded eagerly and recommends facades (lite-youtube or lazy iframe loaders). Perfmatters 'YouTube Preview Thumbnails' does the same swap site-wide and explicitly supports 'Elementor Atomic YouTube elements and legacy Elementor video widgets' (their test: -99.63 % TBT, -44 % LCP). limnoupolis.gr has 84 video widgets in its documents.
findings.breaks_when: Autoplay + overlay: the first click plays (OK), but an autoplaying above-the-fold YouTube hero cannot be faced - it loads the player immediately. Image Overlay uses the Image Size control - pick 'medium_large/large' or the thumbnail is full-size. Perfmatters YouTube Preview Thumbnails requires 'iFrames and Videos' lazy ON and may double-wrap an Elementor overlay (pick one). Lightbox mode is unaffected.
findings.how_to_apply: Every Video widget: Image Overlay = Yes with a WebP/AVIF thumbnail (Image Resolution 'large'), Lazy Load = Yes, Privacy Mode = Yes, Play Icon = Yes; never Autoplay for YouTube/Vimeo in the hero. V4 atomic YouTube element: enable 'Lazy load'. Site-wide alternative: Perfmatters > Lazy Loading > iFrames and Videos ON + YouTube Preview Thumbnails ON. Hosted video (Video widget type 'Self Hosted'): Preload = 'None' (control `preload`, default 'metadata'; hidden when Autoplay is on) and set Poster.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse 'third-party-facades' audit passes (no youtube.com requests before interaction); Network on load: zero requests to youtube.com/ytimg.com/vimeo.com; clicking the overlay starts the video within one click (verify on iOS Safari too, where autoplay-on-click must remain a user gesture). TBT drops on pages with videos.
tools: Elementor Video widget: Lazy Load, Image Overlay, Privacy Mode, Preload, Poster
findings.correction: The Image Overlay goes through the same Group_Control_Image_Size::print_attachment_image_html path as the Image widget, so choosing 'Custom' resolution for the overlay yields `` with no width/height - for an above-the-fold video facade pick a registered size (medium_large/large) so the poster is sized and not lazy.

findings.claim: Hosted <video> above the fold should ship with a poster (preloaded with fetchpriority=high) and preload="none"; the Video widget defaults to preload="metadata" and hides the Preload control when Autoplay is on, and newer browsers honour loading="lazy" on <video>.
findings.detail: video.php `get_hosted_params()`: outputs autoplay/loop/controls booleans, `preload` from the 'Preload' select (Metadata | Auto | None, default 'metadata', condition autoplay = ''), `muted`, `playsinline` only when 'Play On Mobile' is on, `controlsList=nodownload`, `poster` from the 'Poster' media control; rendered as `<video class="elementor-video" src=... >`. web.dev 'Lazy loading video' (updated 2026-07-02): browsers started supporting `loading="lazy"` on media elements (poster and media lazy, autoplay deferred until near viewport); `preload="none"` + poster is the only reliable way to avoid downloading video bytes because metadata is fetched with Content-Range and may not be at the file start; a video that is the LCP element should use a poster and `<link rel="preload" as="image" fetchpriority="high">` for it since poster has no fetchpriority. web.dev 'Fast playback with preload': Chrome default is metadata since Chrome 64. WP Rocket's doc confirms a poster can be preloaded but not given fetchpriority.
findings.breaks_when: Autoplay muted loops (GIF replacement) need the bytes anyway - preload none only delays start; keep them below the fold or use loading="lazy" on the element. Elementor has no 'loading' control for <video>; adding it needs an HTML widget or output filter. iOS requires playsinline for inline autoplay ('Play On Mobile' adds it).
findings.how_to_apply: Video widget (Self Hosted): Preload = None, Poster = optimized WebP/AVIF frame, Autoplay off in the hero. If a muted autoplay loop is required above the fold: keep it <= 1 MB, 720p, and preload its poster: Perfmatters > Preloading > Preload the poster URL as Image, Priority High. Below the fold: add `loading="lazy"` via an HTML widget `<video loading="lazy" preload="none" poster=... autoplay muted loop playsinline>`.
findings.how_to_verify: Network on first load (mobile): no range request for the .mp4 when Preload=None (0 bytes of video until play); poster request Priority High and complete before LCP; Lighthouse LCP element becomes the poster /video with Load Delay < 300 ms; TBT unchanged or lower.
tools: Elementor Video widget: Preload, Poster, Play On Mobile

findings.claim: Elementor's Image Carousel renders hand-built tags with no width/height/loading/fetchpriority attributes and an optional Swiper data-src 'Lazyload', so an above-the-fold carousel is a CLS source and an undiscoverable LCP; web.dev recommends a static first slide and no autoplay above the fold.
findings.detail:
includes/widgets/image-carousel.php (WebFetch summary): image URL via Group_Control_Image_Size::get_attachment_image_src() ('thumbnail_size'), `` built as a string with only class, src (or `data-src` + class `swiper-lazy` + `
` when `lazyload` = yes), alt; no width/height/loading/fetchpriority; autoplay default 'yes', autoplay_speed 5000, slides_to_show 1-10, scripts 'swiper'. Container background slideshow (background.php `slideshow_lazyload`, handlers/background-slideshow.js) uses Swiper lazy too. voreniahorizon.gr Lighthouse shows `` images of 130-190 KB at priority Low. web.dev carousel best practices: above-the-fold carousels often contain the LCP element; autoplay slide transitions can produce 'infinite CLS'; LCP candidates keep changing in autoplay carousels until first interaction; recommendation: load the first slide statically and lazy-load the rest. web.dev fetch-priority: in a carousel only the first visible image needs fetchpriority=high, the rest fetchpriority=low. Elementor Pro Slides/Loop Carousel source is not public; their hero use is unverified here (see open questions).
findings.breaks_when: Replacing a hero slider with a static Image widget changes design (agree with client); if the slider stays, disabling 'Lazyload' makes all slides download (bandwidth) - acceptable for 3-4 slides with proper Image Resolution. Perfmatters 'DOM Monitoring' is needed if its lazy loader must handle cloned Swiper loop slides. LiteSpeed 'Add Missing Sizes' can add width/height to these imgs only when its lazy load is ON.
findings.how_to_apply: Build rule: no carousel/slider in the mobile hero; use Image widget + text. Existing sites: Image Carousel widget > Additional Options: Autoplay = No above the fold (or Pause on Interaction), Lazyload = No for an above-the-fold carousel, Image Size = 'large'/custom instead of Full; set the carousel container a fixed min-height or CSS `aspect-ratio` on `.elementor-image-carousel-wrapper` to reserve space; below the fold keep Lazyload = Yes. For hero sliders in Elementor Pro Slides, prefer a single static first slide (or preload the first slide image with fetchpriority=high) - verify the first slide's markup per site.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse 'unsized-images' lists no carousel ; 'layout-shifts' shows no slide element; CLS <= 0.01 across a 10 s mobile trace with autoplay running (DevTools Performance > Layout Shifts); LCP element is stable across 3 runs (same node) and its request is High priority.

findings.claim: WordPress 6.5+ supports AVIF natively (upload + generation via image_editor_output_format) and 6.7 adds sizes="auto" to lazy images; the conversion plugins differ mainly in cost model and delivery method, and running two converters (limnoupolis: TinyPNG + Converter for Media) gains nothing.
findings.detail: Make/Core 6.5 dev note: AVIF ~50 % smaller than JPEG, supported by all major browsers; requires Imagick/GD AVIF support (check Tools > Site Health > Info > Media Handling); `image_editor_output_format` filter can map image/jpeg → image/avif at upload; `wp_editor_set_quality` sets AVIF quality. 6.7 dev note: WP prepends `auto,` to sizes only for loading="lazy" images (so eager LCP images keep the theme's sizes string, default `(max-width: Wpx) 100vw, Wpx`); disable with `add_filter('wp_img_tag_add_auto_sizes','__return_false')`.
