Plugins (WordPress.org pages opened Oct 2026): Converter for Media - WebP free, AVIF in PRO, serves from /uploads-webpc via .htaccess/Nginx rewrite or 'Pass Thru' mode, falls back AVIF→WebP→original, needs mod_rewrite/mod_mime/mod_expires, Cloudflare free-plan delivery added, CDN support limited (BunnyCDN); ShortPixel - WebP+AVIF, 100 free credits/month (each thumbnail = 1 credit), delivery via <picture> tag or .htaccess ('WebP/AVIF and CDN' settings), optional CDN; Imagify - WebP+AVIF in the free 20 MB/month plan, 'display images in WebP and AVIF' with automatic fallback, requires WP 6.9+; TinyPNG - 500 credits/month free, conversion costs an extra credit per size (~50 images/month free with conversion); Elementor Image Optimizer - WebP+AVIF via Elementor cloud service, resize to max 1920 px default; Optimole - CDN-based on-the-fly WebP/AVIF + device resizing, free to 2,000 visits/month; LiteSpeed/QUIC.cloud - Image Optimization Settings create WebP or AVIF per size (format switch resets the counter), discards next-gen files that are not smaller, cron-driven. Chrome image-delivery insight: AVIF/WebP preferred; note WebP/AVIF images do not work on iPhones before iOS 16 (AVIF).
findings.breaks_when: -tag delivery (ShortPixel/Imagify option) wraps and can conflict with lazy-load libraries, CSS that targets `img` as direct child, and does nothing for CSS background images; .htaccess rewrite delivery needs Vary: Accept caching at the CDN/Cloudflare or WebP gets served to a Safari that cached it; two converters create duplicate files and double credits; AVIF encode on shared hosting is slow (use cloud converters); server-side AVIF needs libavif in Imagick/GD.
findings.how_to_apply: Keep exactly one converter per site. Hotels/villas (photo-heavy, LiteSpeed): LiteSpeed Image Optimization with 'Next-Gen format' AVIF (or WebP), Auto Request Cron ON, then Page Optimization image replacement; remove Converter for Media/TinyPNG. Sites without LiteSpeed: Converter for Media (free WebP; PRO for AVIF) in rewrite mode, or Imagify free tier for AVIF. Set `big_image_size_threshold` (default 2560) or Elementor Image Optimizer 'Resize large images' = 1920. Verify Site Health > Media Handling shows AVIF before relying on native generation.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -I -H 'Accept: image/avif,image/webp' <jpg url> returns Content-Type image/avif (rewrite mode) or the page source shows <picture><source type="image/avif">; PSI 'Serve images in next-gen formats' shows 0 KiB; check one image in Safari 15 (iOS 15) still renders (fallback). Media library: no duplicate -webp/-avif folders from a second plugin.

findings.claim: JS lazy-loading (LiteSpeed) adds CLS when images lack width/height or get a 1x1 placeholder; the observed 0 → 0.107 CLS on staging is prevented by 'Responsive Placeholder' + 'Add Missing Sizes' + viewport exclusions, and in general every needs width/height (aspect-ratio) to avoid shifts.
findings.detail: LiteSpeed docs (pageopt, Sept 29 2026): 'Lazy Load Images' replaces src with a placeholder (`data-lazyloaded`, class `litespeed-loaded` after load, gray box by default; `LITESPEED_PLACEHOLDER` constant); 'Responsive Placeholder' - 'can be used when the images have width and height attributes. Placeholders use the same dimensions as the images, which helps reduce layout shifts'; 'Add Missing Sizes' adds width/height automatically (only when Lazy Load Images is ON); LQIP (QUIC.cloud) optional. web.dev optimize-cls (Feb 2025): always include width and height on and
findings.breaks_when: 'Add Missing Sizes' only works with LiteSpeed lazy ON; it reads dimensions from the file so SVGs without intrinsic size or dynamic images get wrong ratios; Responsive Placeholder SVG inherits the configured colour (set to the page background to avoid grey flashes). Elementor's own CSS `img{height:auto;max-width:100%}` keeps the ratio - do not add fixed heights. Fade-in CSS on lazy images delays LCP if applied to the hero.
findings.how_to_apply: LiteSpeed: Page Optimization > Media: Lazy Load Images ON → also Responsive Placeholder ON, Responsive Placeholder Color = site background, Add Missing Sizes ON; Media Excludes: logo and hero filenames in 'Lazy Load Image Excludes' (or class `e-no-lazyload`-style class in 'Lazy Load Image Class Name Excludes'); VPI ON. Perfmatters: Lazy Loading > 'Add Missing Image Dimensions' ON (option in the same panel). Any site: fix unsized third-party (cookie-banner logos) via plugin settings or CSS `.faz-custom-brand-logo{width:120px;aspect-ratio:3/1}`; for hand-written HTML widgets always write width/height. Fonts: use Elementor > Settings > Advanced > 'Google Fonts Load' = swap plus a size-adjust fallback face, or local fonts with font-display:optional for the hero heading.
findings.how_to_verify: Re-run the staging test with LiteSpeed lazy ON + the three settings: Lighthouse CLS must stay <= 0.01 and 'unsized-images' must be empty; DevTools Performance > Experience track shows no layout shift attributed to ; audits['layout-shifts'] items have no 'Media element lacking an explicit size' cause.
tools: LiteSpeed Cache: Responsive Placeholder, Add Missing Sizes, VPI, Media Excludes

findings.claim: With Elementor ILO on, images in Elementor Pro footer templates (and anything rendered after the_content) receive neither loading="lazy" nor fetchpriority, and WordPress core lazy-loading is globally disabled - so footer logos, payment icons and social icons download eagerly on every page.
findings.detail: module.php: the output buffer runs from `get_header` to `the_content` (flush_header_buffer at priority 0) and the `wp_content_img_tag` filter only fires inside wp_filter_content_tags for the_content/widget contexts; `wp_lazy_loading_enabled` is forced false for the whole request, so core never adds loading=lazy to footer . Local evidence: limnoupolis.gr/staging footer social icons (fb-icon.png, instagram-icon.png, youtube-icon.png, Icon-simple-tiktok.png) are requested at ~1.5 s with priority Low on a 412x823 viewport and Icon-simple-tiktok.png appears in Lighthouse 'offscreen-images' (loaded although offscreen). WordPress core by contrast (wp_get_loading_optimization_attributes, 6.4+) would lazy-load any wp_get_attachment_image() call beyond the omit threshold (default 3 since 6.3, filter wp_omit_loading_attr_threshold) wherever it is rendered.
findings.breaks_when: Lazy-loading footer images that are actually in the first viewport on very short pages (404, thank-you) adds a small delay; use the optimiser's exclusions. If both Elementor ILO is disabled and no optimiser lazy-load is on, WP core takes over with its own 3-image threshold - header logo still counts there too.
findings.how_to_apply: Option 1: let the page optimiser lazy-load the footer: Perfmatters Lazy Loading (Images ON) or FlyingPress lazy or LiteSpeed Lazy Load Images (with excludes) process the full HTML buffer including footers. Option 2 (no optimiser): keep ILO but add `add_filter('wp_get_attachment_image_attributes', function($attr){ if( did_action('get_footer') ) { $attr['loading']='lazy'; } return $attr; });` in an mu-plugin so footer-template images get native lazy. Option 3: replace footer raster icons with inline SVG (Elementor Icon widget with e_font_icon_svg) - no image requests at all.
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse 'offscreen-images' audit lists no footer icons; Network shows footer PNG/WebP requests only after scrolling; request count on the home page drops by the number of footer images; footer still renders correctly after scroll (manual).

findings.claim: If Elementor's Optimized Image Loading is disabled, WordPress core's logic applies and is fully filterable: wp_omit_loading_attr_threshold (default 3 since 6.3), wp_min_priority_img_pixels (default 50,000), pre_wp_get_loading_optimization_attributes (6.4, short-circuit) and wp_get_attachment_image_attributes - which is the cleaner base for a per-site hero rule than Elementor's hard-coded module.
findings.detail: developer.wordpress.org: `apply_filters('wp_omit_loading_attr_threshold', 3)` - 'The number of media elements where the loading attribute will not be added. Default 3' (changed from 1 in 6.3.0); `wp_min_priority_img_pixels` filter for the fetchpriority area threshold; wp_get_loading_optimization_attributes() returns loading=lazy or fetchpriority=high, never both, skips nested calls while doing_filter('the_content') so content images are counted once by wp_filter_content_tags, and offers `pre_wp_get_loading_optimization_attributes` to short-circuit; wp_get_attachment_image_attributes exposes `loading` (false omits), `decoding`, `fetchpriority`, `srcset`, `sizes`. Elementor's Image widget renders through wp_get_attachment_image (image-size.php `get_attachment_image_html`, filter elementor/image_size/get_attachment_image_html) so these hooks reach it; the hard-coded `loading="lazy"` fallback in that function is only used for images without an attachment ID (external URLs). Perfmatters' fetch-priority doc confirms WP 6.3+ adds fetchpriority to the first non-lazy image > 50,000 px² and that this 'won't always work' with page builders.
findings.breaks_when: Disabling ILO without an optimiser re-enables WP core lazy for everything after the 3rd image including the hero if the header has 3 images (same symptom, now fixable with the filters). Images inserted via Elementor HTML widgets or external URLs are not touched by any WP filter. Element Cache (e_element_cache) caches rendered widget HTML including these attributes - purge after changing filters.
findings.how_to_apply: mu-plugin: `add_filter('wp_omit_loading_attr_threshold', fn() => 2);` (header logo + hero eager, everything else lazy) and `add_filter('wp_min_priority_img_pixels', fn() => 150000);` so the logo cannot take fetchpriority=high; per-page hero override: `add_filter('wp_get_attachment_image_attributes', function($attr,$att){ if ( is_front_page() && 15401 === $att->ID ) { $attr['loading']='eager'; $attr['fetchpriority']='high'; } return $attr; },10,2);`. External-URL images in Image widgets get loading=lazy hard-coded - replace with Media Library images. Then Elementor > Tools > Regenerate CSS & Data and purge page/element cache.
findings.how_to_verify: Rendered mobile HTML: exactly one `fetchpriority="high"` on the hero, `loading="lazy"` on all images after the 2nd; Lighthouse lcp-lazy-loaded passes, prioritize-lcp-image passes; no `_doing_it_wrong` notice in debug.log ('An image should not be lazy-loaded and marked as high priority at the same time').
findings.correction: (1) The hard-coded `loading="lazy"` in image-size.php is NOT limited to external-URL images - it applies whenever the chosen size key is not a registered intermediate size or 'full', i.e. also to the 'Custom' Image Resolution option and to static render mode; those images also lack width/height and srcset, so no WP filter and no fetchpriority logic reaches them. (2) The wp_get_attachment_image_attributes snippet does not reach Editor V4 atomic Image elements at all (see additions). Risk stays low; add 'never use Custom resolution for above-the-fold images' to the rule set.

findings.claim: On a cold mobile load Chrome starts all images at Low priority and only boosts in-viewport images after layout; fetchpriority="high" on the single LCP (and fetchpriority="low" on other above-the-fold images such as carousel slides 2-n) is the cheapest LCP win and is honoured by Elementor's module.
findings.detail: web.dev fetch-priority: images start Low, boosted to High at layout; since Chrome 117 the first 5 large images get Medium and two load in parallel in 'tight mode'; `fetchpriority="high"` lets the hero start High immediately; Google's test cut LCP 2.6 → 1.9 s; 'setting a high priority on more than one or two images makes priority setting unhelpful'; CSS backgrounds need preload + fetchpriority on the <link>. web.dev optimize-lcp: resource load delay target ~0; fetchpriority on the LCP img; same-origin hosting avoids a new connection (do not put the hero on a third-party CDN hostname without preconnect). Perfmatters 'Fetch Priority' UI adds the attribute by class/ID/filename or parent selector, per device/location; WP Rocket adds it automatically with its preload. Local evidence: kand.dev6 hero webp is at High only because it has no width/height and no lazy, limnoupolis hero at lazy.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break rendering. Misuse: high on several images or on below-fold images delays the real LCP; combining loading=lazy and fetchpriority=high is contradictory (WP/Elementor emit a _doing_it_wrong notice and keep high).
findings.how_to_apply: Elementor-native: none (no control). Perfmatters > Preloading > Fetch Priority > Add New: selector = hero container class (e.g. `lmn-hm-hero`), enable 'Search by Parent Selector', Priority High, Location 'front'. Code: the wp_get_attachment_image_attributes snippet by attachment ID (finding 1). For image carousels/galleries above the fold set `fetchpriority="low"` on slides 2-n via the same filter or Perfmatters Low. Always pair with loading="eager" removal of lazy on that element.
findings.how_to_verify: DevTools Network (mobile throttling): hero image Priority column = High and start time within ~100 ms of the first CSS; Lighthouse LCP breakdown: Load Delay < 200 ms; LCP improves by roughly the former load delay; no other image shows High.

findings.claim: For new builds, the hero recipe that produced the two fastest audited sites is a text-or-static-image hero: one (Image widget, Image Resolution tuned, WebP/AVIF, width/height intact), no slider, no autoplay video, no three.js, hero container first in the document, heading text as LCP where possible.
findings.detail:
Audit: pallada.gr (score 86, LCP 2.5 s) and platonos.dev6 (84, LCP 2.2 s) have text (

/

) LCP elements and Load Delay 0; the four worst (limnoupolis 27, staging 30, onar 44, vorenia 50) have lazy hero , CSS-background hero, a cookie-banner LCP after 16 s render delay, or a 9 s render delay behind a three.js/animation hero. Chrome LCP breakdown insight: four phases, reduce delay phases first; TTFB alone is 0.8-4.8 s on several sites (hosting dimension). web.dev carousel: static first slide; web.dev optimize-lcp: discoverable, prioritised, same-origin, not lazy. Elementor help 'Create a Hero section' exists but has no performance guidance (not opened).
findings.breaks_when: Design constraints from Figma/XD may call for a slider or video hero - then apply the facade/fallback findings instead; text LCP depends on fonts arriving early (preload the Greek+Latin subset woff2) or LCP becomes the font render delay (fagitiotiszois: TypeKit 200 KB, Render Delay 1.5 s).
findings.how_to_apply: Plugin build rule set: (1) hero container = first `.e-con.e-parent`, Image widget with Image Resolution = custom size matching 2x mobile width, alt set, no link lightbox; (2) no Background Image on the hero container (or add e-no-lazyload + preload if unavoidable); (3) no Video/Slides/Image Carousel/Loop Carousel/Lottie/3D in the hero on mobile - use responsive visibility to hide them on mobile and show a static image; (4) h1 inside hero uses a preloaded self-hosted woff2 with Greek subset; (5) run `lighthouse --preset=mobile` on the hero template before adding anything below it and require LCP < 1.8 s on the bare template.
findings.how_to_verify:
Lighthouse mobile on the new page: LCP element is the hero or

, phases: Load Delay 0-200 ms, Load Time < 500 ms, Render Delay < 300 ms; CLS 0; filmstrip shows hero complete at FCP+<500 ms; PSI score >= 95 on the bare template.
findings.correction: Rule (1): 'Image Resolution = custom size matching 2x mobile width' must be a size registered with add_image_size and exposed via image_size_names_choose; Elementor's own 'Custom' option emits an unsized, hard-coded-lazy (image-size.php). Rule (3) should also exclude Elementor Pro Slides and Media Carousel, whose slide images are CSS backgrounds (see additions). Add rule (6): the recipe only yields 95+ when TTFB is under ~800 ms - pair it with the hosting/caching findings.

findings.claim: Elementor's 'Custom' Image Resolution (any image widget/overlay using Group_Control_Image_Size) outputs a hand-built with hard-coded loading="lazy" and no width/height/srcset - it must never be used for the hero or any above-the-fold image.
findings.detail: includes/controls/groups/image-size.php get_attachment_image_html(): `$image_sizes = get_intermediate_image_sizes(); $image_sizes[] = 'full';` then only `if ( ! empty( $image['id'] ) && in_array( $size, $image_sizes ) && ! $is_static_render_mode )` calls wp_get_attachment_image(). Every other case (size 'custom' with custom_dimension, external URL, static render mode) runs `sprintf('', ...)`. Consequences: Elementor ILO sees no width/height and leaves it alone (still lazy), WP core filters never run, Perfmatters/LiteSpeed cannot add fetchpriority via wp_get_attachment_image_attributes, Lighthouse flags unsized-images, and the LCP image is lazy-loaded. Affects Image widget, Video widget Image Overlay, Image Box, and third-party widgets reusing the group control. Elementor 4.3.x main branch.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break. Switching from Custom to a registered size changes the served file (crop/ratio) - check the hero crop. Old uploads need thumbnail regeneration for new sizes.
findings.how_to_apply: Theme/mu-plugin: `add_image_size('hero-mobile', 900, 1200, true); add_image_size('hero-desktop', 1920, 1080, true); add_filter('image_size_names_choose', fn($s) => $s + ['hero-mobile' => 'Hero mobile', 'hero-desktop' => 'Hero desktop']);` then in the editor select that named size in 'Image Resolution' (not 'Custom'). Audit rule for the plugin: grep rendered HTML for `
findings.how_to_verify: View-source: hero has width, height, srcset, sizes and no loading="lazy"; Lighthouse unsized-images empty; lcp-lazy-loaded passes; the hero file name ends in a registered size suffix (e.g. -900x1200.webp), not a Custom-generated one.

findings.claim: Editor V4 (e_opt_in_v4 / e_atomic_elements) atomic Image elements bypass wp_get_attachment_image(): they output src/width/height/srcset/alt only - no sizes, loading, decoding or fetchpriority - so the wp_get_attachment_image_attributes snippet does nothing for them and only HTML-level tools (Elementor ILO, Perfmatters Fetch Priority/lazy, LiteSpeed, FlyingPress) can touch them.
findings.detail: Read on voreniahorizon.gr (Elementor 4.3.4): modules/atomic-widgets/props-resolver/transformers/image-transformer.php builds the attribute array with `wp_get_attachment_image_src( id, size ?? 'full' )` and `wp_get_attachment_image_srcset( id, size )`, returning id/src/width/height/srcset/alt; modules/atomic-widgets/elements/atomic-image/atomic-image.html.twig loops `settings.image` and prints each key as an attribute - there is no `sizes`, `loading`, `decoding` or `fetchpriority` key and no call to wp_get_attachment_image/wp_filter_content_tags. Image_Sizes::DEFAULT_SIZE = 'large'. Because width/height ARE present, Elementor ILO's regex still applies its 3-image count to V4 images (so the hero/logo logic from finding 1 holds). Missing `sizes` means the browser assumes 100vw when picking from srcset, over-fetching in narrow columns (WP 6.7's sizes=auto is also absent since WP never generated the tag).
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break. Any plugin filter targeting wp_get_attachment_image_attributes or wp_img_tag_* silently has no effect on V4 images - a site migrated to V4 loses the hero fix unless it is reapplied at HTML level.
findings.how_to_apply: On e_opt_in_v4 sites prefer Perfmatters > Preloading > Fetch Priority (class/filename/parent selector, works on rendered HTML) or Elementor ILO with the min_priority_img_pixels filter from finding 1; for a code route hook the final HTML (e.g. `elementor/frontend/the_content` filter) and add `sizes`/`fetchpriority` via a DOM pass. For new V4 builds keep hero images in V3 Image widgets until Elementor adds loading/fetchpriority props (track elementor/elementor atomic-image.php).
findings.how_to_verify: View-source on a V4 page: the hero has `srcset` but no `sizes` attribute (identifies a V4 image); after the fix it carries fetchpriority="high" and a `sizes` value; Lighthouse 'uses-responsive-images' wasted bytes for that image drop.

findings.claim: Elementor Pro 4.3.1 Slides, Media Carousel and Loop Carousel resolved: Slides and Media Carousel render slide images as CSS background-image (post-CSS or inline style, role="img"), never as ; a Slides hero therefore needs a manual preload of slide 1's image with fetchpriority=high (or replacement), Media Carousel's 'Lazyload' turns slide 1 into a Swiper data-background JS load, and Loop Carousel items are ordinary Loop templates whose Image widgets follow the normal wp_get_attachment_image path.
findings.detail: Read from wp-content/plugins/elementor-pro on voreniahorizon.gr (Pro 4.3.1). modules/slides/widgets/slides.php: repeater control `background_image` (Controls_Manager::MEDIA, not responsive, no size select) with selector `'{{WRAPPER}} {{CURRENT_ITEM}} .swiper-slide-bg' => 'background-image: url({{URL}})'` - the URL lives in post-NNN.css; render adds class swiper-slide-bg, optional `elementor-ken-burns` classes, and `role="img"` + aria-label when an attachment id exists; no lazyload control, full-size URL. modules/carousel/widgets/media-carousel.php print_slide(): `if ( 'yes' === $settings['lazyload'] ) { class swiper-lazy; data-background = $img_src } else { style="background-image: url('...')" }` plus `<div class="swiper-lazy-preloader">`; image size comes from the widget's Image Size group (image_size_custom_dimension injection), so 'Custom' is possible but it is a background anyway. modules/loop-builder/widgets/loop-carousel.php only wraps rendered Loop documents in `.swiper-slide` and has no image markup of its own. Combined with finding 2: Slides hero = undiscoverable LCP (CSS) + Ken Burns animation re-painting the LCP candidate.
findings.breaks_when: Preloading slide 1 requires the exact URL from post-CSS (full-size upload; changes if the slide image is swapped or a WebP converter rewrites CSS URLs - re-check after edits). Turning Media Carousel Lazyload off downloads every slide eagerly; fine for 3-5 slides with a sensible Image Size, bad for 20. Pro markup may change in later 4.x releases - re-read slides.php after Pro updates.
findings.how_to_apply: Existing Slides hero: Perfmatters > Preloading > Preload: URL = slide 1 background file (copy from post-NNN.css), type Image, Priority High, Location = that page; disable Ken Burns on slide 1; set Autoplay off or Pause on Interaction. Better: replace the Slides widget on mobile (responsive visibility) with a container holding an Image widget (registered size) + heading, keep Slides for desktop only. Media Carousel above the fold: Additional Options > Lazyload = No, Image Size = large. Loop Carousel: treat the first visible Loop item's Image widget like any hero image (finding 1 rules), and set Lazyload/`loading` via the Loop template.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse prioritize-lcp-image passes and LCP element phases show Load Delay < 300 ms; Network: slide-1 image requested at High priority within the first ~5 requests and only once (no duplicate from CSS); DevTools Performance shows no repeated LCP candidate changes while the slider autoplays.

findings.claim: Perfmatters has a dedicated 'Disable Core Fetch' switch (Advanced Options > Preloading) and its docs explicitly warn that Elementor's Optimize Image Loading mis-assigns fetchpriority to below-the-fold images - so on Perfmatters sites the clean configuration is: Disable Core Fetch ON, Elementor Optimized Image Loading = Disable, Perfmatters Fetch Priority rule for the hero.
findings.detail: perfmatters.io/docs/fetch-priority (opened Oct 2026): WordPress 6.3+ adds fetchpriority="high" to the first image that is not lazy-loaded, has no fetchpriority attribute and exceeds 50,000 square pixels; 'it won't always work, and it very much depends on the theme, page builder'; steps: Show Advanced Options -> Preloading -> 'Disable Core Fetch'; then 'Disable fetch in Elementor ... we've seen Elementor improperly add fetch on images below the fold. You can disable fetch in Elementor by turning off "Optimize Image Loading"' (doc still cites the old Settings -> Features location; in 4.3.x it is Elementor > Settings > Performance > Optimized Image Loading). Perfmatters auto-excludes images carrying fetchpriority from its lazy loader, so one Fetch Priority rule (hero container class, 'Search by Parent Selector', Priority High, Location front) simultaneously fixes priority and lazy exclusion.
findings.breaks_when: Disabling both core and Elementor fetch logic with no Perfmatters rule leaves the hero at Low priority until layout (worse than before); the rule must be added on every template type that has a hero (front, single, archive). Disabling Elementor ILO also removes its lazy attribution - Perfmatters Lazy Loading must be ON to keep below-fold images deferred.
findings.how_to_apply: Perfmatters > Show Advanced Options > Preloading: 'Disable Core Fetch' ON; Preloading > Fetch Priority > Add: selector = hero container CSS class, 'Search by Parent Selector' ON, Priority High, Device All, Location front (repeat per template); Lazy Loading > Images ON, Exclude Leading Images = 1-2; Elementor > Settings > Performance > Optimized Image Loading = Disable; purge page cache.
findings.how_to_verify: Rendered HTML has exactly one fetchpriority="high" (on the hero), none on the logo or footer; Lighthouse lcp-lazy-loaded and prioritize-lcp-image pass; no `_doing_it_wrong` notice about lazy + high in debug.log.
tools: Perfmatters: Disable Core Fetch, Fetch Priority, Lazy Loading

findings.claim: LiteSpeed Cache 7.x has no hero preload unless both 'Lazy Load Images' and QUIC.cloud 'Viewport Images' (VPI) are ON - 'Preload Featured Image' was removed - so LiteSpeed-only sites that keep lazy OFF (the agency default) must get hero discovery/priority from Elementor ILO or a manual preload, not from LiteSpeed.
findings.detail: docs.litespeedtech.com/lscache/lscwp/pageopt (opened Oct 2026): 'Preload Featured Image - This feature has been removed. We now automatically preload all Viewport Images as part of our VPI service.'; 'Viewport Images OFF ... Tip: You must set Page Optimization > Media Settings > Lazy Load Images to ON for this setting to take effect. Warning: VPI uses the QUIC.cloud Page Optimization service'; 'Viewport Images Cron OFF ... generated in the background via a cron-based queue'; VPIs can be overridden per post in the LiteSpeed Options metabox. The audited LiteSpeed sites (limnoupolis, onar) run with lazy OFF, so LiteSpeed contributes nothing to LCP image discovery; the staging test that turned lazy ON without VPI/Responsive Placeholder produced the 0.107 CLS.
findings.breaks_when: Enabling Lazy Load Images to unlock VPI also enables the JS lazy loader for everything (CLS risk unless Responsive Placeholder + Add Missing Sizes are ON) and consumes QUIC.cloud quota per URL - with Polylang/WPML each language URL is a separate VPI job; until the cron has processed a URL its hero is lazy-loaded. Guest/mobile cache variants each need their own VPI run.
findings.how_to_apply: Decision per LiteSpeed site: (A) keep Lazy Load Images OFF, keep Elementor ILO ON with the min_priority_img_pixels filter / hero fetchpriority snippet from finding 1, and add a manual `<link rel="preload" as="image" fetchpriority="high">` only for CSS-background heroes; or (B) Lazy Load Images ON + Responsive Placeholder ON (color = page background) + Add Missing Sizes ON + Viewport Images ON + Viewport Images Cron ON, hero/logo filenames in Lazy Load Image Excludes as a safety net, then purge and let the queue run before re-testing. Never (C) lazy ON without VPI and placeholders.
findings.how_to_verify: Option B: LiteSpeed > Page Optimization > VPI shows the home URLs green (processed); rendered HTML has `` for the hero and the hero has no data-lazyloaded; Lighthouse CLS <= 0.01 and lcp-lazy-loaded passes. Option A: same Lighthouse checks, plus no litespeed lazy JS in the waterfall.
tools: LiteSpeed Cache: Lazy Load Images, Viewport Images, Viewport Images Cron, Responsive Placeholder, Add Missing Sizes

title: Third-party scripts, Tag Manager, pixels and cookie banners
summary: On the audited sites third-party tracking is the single largest controllable TBT source: on limnoupolis.gr Lighthouse attributes 1,105 ms of blocking time to Google Tag Manager (849 KB) and 520 ms to Facebook (339 KB); on staging 1,285 ms + 681 ms, i.e. roughly the whole 1.8 s TBT. The cause is not gtm.js itself but what is around it: two Google Ads gtag snippets hard-coded in the HTML plus the same AW-ID loaded again by GTM, a dead Universal Analytics tag (133 KB, 460 ms eval) injected by the WooCommerce GA plugin, the Meta pixel with automatic configuration (fbevents.js + signals/config + openbridge3 = 336 KB, 914 ms main thread), and all of it firing before any consent (collect/tr requests at 3.7 s with the banner unanswered). The highest-value lever is therefore structural: one GTM container, every marketing tag gated behind consent in "basic" consent mode (Google's own term for blocking tags until consent). Because PageSpeed/Lighthouse never clicks Accept, basic mode removes that JavaScript from the lab run entirely while matching the Greek DPA's 2020 guidelines, which require prior consent even for Google Analytics; the trade-off is losing GA4 behavioural modelling. Delay-JS (Perfmatters/WP Rocket/FlyingPress/LiteSpeed "Delayed") is the second lever and is safe only for tracking scripts, never for the CMP or the consent-default snippet, and it silently drops data from non-interacting visitors unless a timeout is enabled. The cookie banner itself must stay first-party, deferred (not delayed), free of CSS transitions, excluded from UCSS/critical-CSS and from JS delay; on onar-seaside-lounge.gr the Complianz banner is the LCP element at 16.4 s and two CMPs (Complianz + Cookie-Script) run at once. Facades for Elementor Google Maps/YouTube widgets, per-page script control, and server-side tagging (moving the Meta pixel to CAPI) round out the dimension. Every change must be verified with Tag Assistant/GA4 DebugView/Meta Test Events and by checking the gcs= parameter, because the failure mode of these optimisations is invisible: the page gets faster and conversions stop being recorded.
critic_notes: Method: WebFetch could not resolve most domains (DNS) from this sandbox, so every cited page was downloaded with curl through the configured proxy and read as text (files under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/critic3/). Local Lighthouse JSON was re-queried with jq. Answers to the researcher's open questions: (1) Meta docs are reachable: autoConfig=false only stops button-click/page-metadata collection; Meta lists /signals/config/{pixelID} as a normal pixel load path, so do not promise the 159 KB saving. (2) Advanced-mode cookieless pings vs HDPA A.1: still a legal question; HDPA text requires consent 'regardless of whether personal data is processed', which argues for basic mode; counsel decides. (3) WP Rocket: no timeout documented in article 1349 (March 11, 2026) and none found by search; FlyingPress and LiteSpeed docs also document no timeout; only Perfmatters does (15 s, perfmatters_delay_js_timeout). (4) LiteSpeed Localization Files default list: docs say 'A list of Recommended URLs is provided by default' but the file is not retrievable (GitHub raw 404 on master/dev/v7.9.1, SVN 403); keep the advice not to localize gtm/gtag. (5) Cookie-Script on limnoupolis.gr: 200 OK, 6-byte body - a dead snippet, remove it. (6) Gateway: Google's page lists no performance numbers; agree expected CWV effect is none. (7) FAZ: listing says 'Works with GTM and gtag' and offers 'GTM dataLayer events' in Settings, no GTM community template mentioned - assume inline consent default + dataLayer events; Cookie-Script template not checked. (8) Certified CMP: publisher-only requirement (addition above). Unverified by me: Google UA shutdown page (11583528), GTM Preview/DebugView help pages, GTM4WP forum thread, Elevar page, IAPP summary - the researcher's quotes from them are plausible and were not contradicted by anything opened. Lighthouse version note: local runs are 12.8.2; PSI runs 13.x (13.5.0 released 2026-09-17), where third-party-facades is gone and several audits were replaced by insights - the plugin's jq paths need a 13.x guard. Skipped: measuring reCAPTCHA/Facebook-SDK CPU cost on the agency sites (not observed on the 10 home pages), and Elementor Cookie Consent's actual script weight.

findings.claim: Gate GA4, Google Ads and the Meta pixel behind consent in Google's 'basic' consent mode (tags blocked until consent) and the whole tracking stack disappears from the PageSpeed mobile run, because Lighthouse/PSI never answers the banner.
findings.detail: Google's consent-mode overview defines the two models: Advanced = 'Google tags are loaded before the consent dialog appears' and send cookieless pings when declined; Basic = 'Google tags blocked until consent is granted'. Trade-off table: behavioural modelling in GA4 only with Advanced; conversion modelling in Ads with Basic falls back to 'a general model'. web.dev (cookie-notice article, updated 2024-06-13): 'most synthetic tools (such as Lighthouse and WebPageTest) will only measure the experience of a first-time user who has not responded to a cookie consent notice' and 'PageSpeed Insights ... does not set any cookies'. Observed in the local Lighthouse runs (scratchpad/lh/runs/limnoupolis_gr.json): with the banner unanswered the page fired analytics.google.com/g/collect, googleads.g.doubleclick.net/pagead/viewthroughconversion for two AW IDs, google.com/ccm/collect and facebook.com/tr?ev=PageView at ~3.7 s; third-party-summary: Google Tag Manager 1,617 ms main thread / 1,105 ms blocking, Facebook 914 ms / 520 ms. On staging: GTM 1,953/1,285 ms, Facebook 855/681 ms against a total TBT of 1,796 ms. Greek DPA Guidelines 1/2020 (25/02/2020) point A.4: Google Analytics for web analytics 'μπορεί να γίνει μόνο κατόπιν συγκατάθεσης' (only after consent); A.3: advertising trackers never fall under the strictly-necessary exemption. Complianz 7 exposes this as 'Do you want to block all Google Tags before consent?' (default No = advanced; Yes = basic). FAZ Cookie Manager sends all 7 consent signals (ad_storage, analytics_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization, functionality_storage, personalization_storage, security_storage).
findings.breaks_when: The marketer relies on GA4 behavioural modelling or on Ads conversion modelling from cookieless pings (lost in basic mode); a tag is set to 'Require additional consent' but the CMP never pushes a consent update (wrong template/ID) so the tag never fires and all data stops; the consent default snippet is placed after gtm.js so tags fire unrestricted anyway.
findings.how_to_apply: In GTM: put the CMP tag (Complianz/Cookie-Script/FAZ community template or custom consent-mode template) on the built-in 'Consent Initialization - All Pages' trigger. For each GA4 / Google Ads / Meta tag open Advanced Settings > Consent Settings > Additional Consent Checks = 'Require additional consent for tag to fire' and add analytics_storage (GA4) or ad_storage + ad_user_data (Ads, Meta). Enable Admin > Container Settings > 'Enable consent overview' and clear the 'Consent Not Configured' list. In Complianz: Wizard > Consent > Statistics = 'Yes, with Google Tag Manager', enter container ID, set 'Do you want to block all Google Tags before consent?' = Yes. In FAZ: enable Google Consent Mode in the banner settings. Remove any hard-coded gtag/fbq snippets from theme header.php or Elementor > Custom Code that bypass GTM.
findings.how_to_verify: Incognito mobile emulation, do NOT touch the banner: Network must show gtm.js and the CMP only; no requests to google-analytics.com|analytics.google.com/g/collect, googleads.g.doubleclick.net, google.com/ccm/collect, connect.facebook.net, facebook.com/tr. Click Accept: those requests appear and the collect URL carries gcs=G111 (Complianz table: G100 default denied, G110 marketing only, G101 statistics only). Run Lighthouse (lighthouse@12 mobile) before/after and compare third-party-summary blockingTime for 'Google Tag Manager' and 'Facebook' (target: entity absent or < 50 ms). Screenshot GTM Consent Overview with zero unconfigured tags. Compare GA4 Realtime after a test accept.

findings.claim: Run exactly one GTM container and delete every hard-coded gtag/fbq snippet; the audited sites load the same Google Ads ID twice and a dead UA property, each copy costing ~165-185 KB and 200-740 ms of script evaluation on mobile.
findings.detail: Observed in scratchpad/lh/runs/limnoupolis_gr.json network-requests: gtag/js?id=AW-10939197448 (165 KB) and gtag/js?id=AW-11212507349 (165 KB) start at 1,095 ms from inline HTML; GTM-TJGCHWC9 (166 KB) starts at 1,490 ms and then loads gtag/js?id=G-N4ZCDFPJ4S (185 KB, 742 ms bootup) AND gtag/js?id=AW-11212507349&cx=c&gtm=... again (duplicate). bootup-time: AW 259 ms + 195 ms + duplicate 111 ms. Staging additionally loads gtag/js?id=UA-42569397-1 (133 KB, 460 ms bootup) via woocommerce-google-analytics-integration; Google: standard UA properties 'stopped processing hits' from July 1, 2023 and were queued for deletion after July 1, 2024. onar-seaside-lounge.gr: gtag/js?id=G-349V7BDDBZ hard-coded (175 KB, 360 ms) and loaded again by GTM-PCC8PS8R. Google's GTM Google-tag page: 'Containers with Google Ads and Floodlight tags will automatically load a Google tag first' and the single-container upgrade promises 'Less javascript on your pages'. Caveat from Simo Ahava (2022): 'Combining and adding destinations is NOT consolidation' — each destination still gets its own config load (staging shows gtag/destination?id=AW-10939197448, 165 KB), so the saving comes from removing duplicates and dead IDs, not from merging G- and AW- into one Google tag. Elementor's help tells users to paste GA/GTM/Pixel snippets into Elementor > Custom Code at location <head> (Pro, priority 1-10, display Conditions) — audit that screen, the Inglelandi header.php, and WooCommerce > Settings > Integration > Google Analytics.
findings.breaks_when: A hard-coded snippet was the only place a conversion fired (e.g. gtag('event','conversion',{send_to:'AW-.../label'}) on a booking thank-you page) and GTM has no equivalent Google Ads Conversion Tracking tag; or the WooCommerce GA plugin was the only source of purchase/ecommerce events and GTM has no ecommerce dataLayer (GTM4WP or similar) to replace it.
findings.how_to_apply: 1) Inventory: grep the rendered HTML for 'googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=', 'gtag/js?id=', 'fbq(', 'UA-'. 2) In GTM create one Google tag (G-) with Google Ads Conversion Tracking + Conversion Linker tags; for each AW conversion label that existed inline, create a tag with the matching trigger. 3) Delete snippets from Elementor > Custom Code, theme header.php, and deactivate/clear WooCommerce > Settings > Integration > Google Analytics (or keep it and remove GA4 from GTM — never both). 4) Remove any UA- ID anywhere. 5) Keep only one gtm.js?id= in the page.
findings.how_to_verify: View-source count of 'gtag/js?id=' and 'gtm.js?id=' = 1 container, 0 inline gtag. Tag Assistant (GTM Preview) shows each G-/AW- ID firing once per page view. Network filter 'gtag' shows one request per destination ID, none for UA-. Lighthouse bootup-time items for googletagmanager.com drop by the removed copies (expect >= 300-500 ms on limnoupolis). Do a test booking/order on staging and confirm the Ads conversion and GA4 purchase appear once each in Tag Assistant and GA4 DebugView.

findings.claim: Load the Meta pixel only through GTM, consent-gated, with automatic configuration disabled; the default snippet pulls fbevents.js + signals/config + openbridge3.js (336 KB, ~900 ms main thread) before consent.
findings.detail: Observed (limnoupolis_gr.json): connect.facebook.net/en_US/fbevents.js 114 KB (312 ms bootup), signals/config/303870678549206?...optin_meta_enabled_capi=true 159 KB (478 ms), signals/plugins/openbridge3.js 63 KB (124 ms), plus an error beacon '[SmartSetup] Rule processing' and facebook.com/tr?ev=PageView at 3.4 s with no consent. Lighthouse entity 'Facebook': 914 ms main thread, 520 ms blocking. Simo Ahava's Facebook pixel custom template (2019) exposes a 'Disable Automatic Configuration' checkbox that runs fbq('set','autoConfig',false,pixelId) before init; help text: 'Facebook collects some metadata (e.g. structured data) and user interactions (e.g. clicks) automatically'. Elevar documents the same disable path and the Events Manager toggle 'Track events automatically without code'. web.dev tag best-practices: custom HTML tags are the least performant tag type and 'most tools attribute the performance impact of a Custom HTML tag to the tag manager'; image pixels (<1 KB, no JS) are the most performant. Meta's own developer docs returned an error page from this environment, so what exactly autoConfig=false suppresses (the signals/config fetch is the likely candidate) is unverified.
findings.breaks_when: autoConfig=false removes automatic button-click and microdata events the marketer relied on (e.g. auto-detected Purchase/AddToCart from schema markup) — those must be sent explicitly via dataLayer or CAPI; replacing the JS pixel with the <noscript> image beacon loses everything except PageView and all Advanced Matching; gating on ad_storage with no CMP update means the pixel never fires.
findings.how_to_apply: In GTM import the 'Facebook Pixel' community template (gallery) or Simo's template; tick 'Disable Automatic Configuration'; set Consent Settings = Require ad_storage + ad_user_data; trigger = Window Loaded (or a custom event pushed after consent). Delete PixelYourSite/theme/Custom Code pixel snippets. In Meta Events Manager > Data Sources > Settings turn off 'Track events automatically without code' to match. Send standard events (ViewContent, AddToCart, Purchase, Lead) from dataLayer pushes. Longer term: move to Conversions API via a server-side GTM container (see server-side finding) and drop the browser pixel or keep it with matching event_id for deduplication.
findings.how_to_verify: Network: before Accept no connect.facebook.net request; after Accept exactly one fbevents.js and no signals/config or openbridge3 request if autoConfig is off (confirm on staging — this is the unverified part), facebook.com/tr?ev=PageView with id= the pixel. Meta Pixel Helper or Events Manager > Test Events shows PageView + the explicit events once (no duplicates). Lighthouse third-party-summary 'Facebook' blocking time < 50 ms or absent in the lab run.
findings.correction: Meta's developer page defines Automatic Configuration as 'The Meta Pixel will send button click and page metadata (such as data structured according to Opengraph or Schema.org formats)' and says to disable it with fbq('set','autoConfig','false','FB_PIXEL_ID') above the init call. The same page's CSP section states 'The Pixel load scripts from two paths: /en_US/fbevents.js and /signals/config/{pixelID}?v={version}' as the normal load, so the 163 KB signals/config fetch is part of every pixel, not an autoConfig artefact. Treat autoConfig=false purely as a privacy/duplicate-event control (gain of that sub-step: low). Overall gain stays high only because of the consent gating; risk stays medium because auto-detected events are lost.

findings.claim: Delay-JS (Perfmatters / WP Rocket / FlyingPress / LiteSpeed 'Delayed') removes tracking scripts from the Lighthouse score entirely, but it must never touch the CMP or the consent-default snippet, and without a timeout it discards every visitor who never interacts.
findings.detail: Perfmatters (docs, current): JavaScript > Delay > 'Delay JavaScript'; 'Delay behavior' = 'Only delay specified scripts' or 'Delay all scripts'; 'Delay timeout' toggle loads scripts 'after 15 seconds if no user interaction' (off by default; change with filter perfmatters_delay_js_timeout); stated reason: 'Help improve data accuracy of tracking scripts, especially if you have a goal associated with a pageview'. Documented delay strings: '/gtm.js', '/gtag/js', 'gtag(', '/gtm-', '/gtm.', 'fbevents.js', 'fbq('. Quick-exclusions list includes Complianz ('complianz'), CookieYes ('/wp-content/plugins/cookie-law-info/legacy/public/js/cookie-law-info-public.js', 'cookie-law-info-js-extra'), Cookiebot, Borlabs, plus an Elementor set (frontend.min.js, webpack.runtime, elementorFrontendConfig...). WP Rocket (article 1349, updated March 11, 2026): delays all JS and inline scripts until keydown/mousemove/touchstart/wheel/click/scroll etc.; exclusions via 'One-click exclusions', 'Excluded JavaScript Files', or the nowprocket attribute; 'Safe Mode' excludes almost everything; no timeout fallback is described on that page. FlyingPress docs: JavaScript method 'Defer loading' / 'Load when idle' / 'Load after interaction' ('use with caution'), plus 'Delay Specific Scripts on Interaction' with suggested keywords googletagmanager.com, google-analytics.com, cookie-law-info; exclusions are partial keyword matches, no wildcards. LiteSpeed Cache: Page Optimization > JS Settings > 'Load JS Deferred' = Delayed ('runs the JS only after detecting user activity ... can remove JS entirely from the page speed score'); Tuning > 'JS Delayed Includes' (note: 'does not work for inline JavaScript when Load JS Deferred is set to Deferred') and 'JS Deferred/Delayed Excludes'. Data loss, from the GTM4WP author (wordpress.org thread): 'Events that fire before the container has loaded are lost, consent mode signals arrive late, and on a WooCommerce site you can end up missing conversions ... you are trading measurement accuracy for the score'. Complianz's exclusion guide (Jan 22, 2025) lists 'complianz', 'cmplz', 'complianz-gdpr-premium/cookiebanner/js/complianz.min.js' (free: 'complianz-gdpr/cookiebanner/js/complianz.min.js'). A Complianz support thread shows LiteSpeed rewriting the banner script to type='litespeed/javascript', freezing the banner until interaction.
findings.breaks_when: The CMP script or its inline config is delayed: banner only appears after a touch, consent is never recorded for bounce visitors; the inline gtag('consent','default') is delayed while gtag/js is not: tags fire with no consent mode (full cookies, non-compliant); 'Delay all scripts' on Elementor without the Elementor exclusion set: hero sliders, sticky header, mobile menu, entrance animations dead until first touch (observed symptom category: 'page flicker'); booking/checkout confirmation pages where the conversion fires on load and the visitor closes the tab without interacting and no timeout is set: conversion lost.
findings.how_to_apply: Perfmatters: Delay behavior = 'Only delay specified scripts'; list /gtm.js, /gtag/js, gtag(, fbevents.js, fbq(, plus chat/maps vendors; enable 'Delay timeout' (15 s) on sites that run Ads; add the CMP to 'Excluded from delay' if ever using 'Delay all scripts'. WP Rocket: tick 'Delay JavaScript Execution', add complianz, cmplz, faz-cookie-manager, cookie-script to 'Excluded JavaScript Files' (or tick one-click exclusions), never add gtm to exclusions unless the marketer insists. FlyingPress: JavaScript method 'Load when idle' site-wide, and 'Delay Specific Scripts on Interaction' = googletagmanager.com, connect.facebook.net. LiteSpeed: Load JS Deferred = Deferred (safer) + 'JS Delayed Includes' = gtm.js, gtag/js, fbevents.js; add the CMP paths to 'JS Deferred/Delayed Excludes'. Exclude WooCommerce cart/checkout/account from delay (Perfmatters does this automatically). Do not combine with LiteSpeed 'Localize Resources' for gtm/gtag (no execution saving; local copy staleness unverified).
findings.how_to_verify: Lab: Lighthouse third-party-summary and bootup-time no longer list googletagmanager.com / connect.facebook.net. Real browser: load page, wait 20 s without touching — with timeout on, gtm.js must appear at ~15 s; with timeout off it must appear on first scroll/touch, and Tag Assistant must still show all tags fired and the consent default present before them. Open the site in incognito and confirm the banner renders without any interaction. Compare GA4 sessions/pageviews and Ads conversions for 7 days before vs after; a drop of more than a few percent means a timeout or an exclusion is needed. Check browser console for Elementor errors on hero/menu interactions.

findings.claim: Measure each tag's real cost by re-running Lighthouse with that vendor blocked (lighthouse --blocked-url-patterns) and reading third-party-summary/bootup-time per URL, instead of guessing; the audit fails at 250 ms of third-party blocking.
findings.detail: Lighthouse CLI readme: '--blocked-url-patterns  Block any network requests to the specified URL patterns [array]'. Chrome docs: the third-party-summary audit 'flags pages that have third-party code that blocks the main thread for 250 ms or longer'. web.dev 'Identify slow third-party JavaScript': block requests in DevTools (Network > right-click > Block request URL), reload, re-measure, 'doing three or more runs of measurement and looking at the median values will likely produce more stable results'. web.dev tag best-practices: 'most tools attribute the performance impact of a Custom HTML tag to the tag manager that injected it'. From the local runs the per-entity costs are already available: limnoupolis GTM 1,617 ms main thread/1,105 ms blocking, Facebook 914/520; staging GTM 1,953/1,285, Facebook 855/681; onar GTM 599/323; FAZ Cookie Manager script.min.js 292-447 ms bootup on pallada/voreniahorizon/cretaforums; Complianz complianz.min.js 375 ms on marakaki. Note: Lighthouse 13 removed the third-party-facades audit (Chrome docs warning), and the plugin README already pins lighthouse@12 because 13.x renamed audits.
findings.breaks_when: not known to break (measurement only); misleading if runs are compared across different CPU benchmarkIndex values — the local results.jsonl shows benchmark 1,181-2,065 between sites, so compare medians of 3+ runs on the same machine.
findings.how_to_apply: Baseline: lighthouse <url> --preset=perf --form-factor=mobile --output=json. Then for each vendor: lighthouse <url> ... --blocked-url-patterns='*googletagmanager.com*' ; separately '*connect.facebook.net*' '*facebook.com/tr*' ; '*cookie-script.com*' ; '*maps.google.com*'. Diff performance score, TBT and LCP. Read .audits['third-party-summary'].details.items (entity, mainThreadTime, blockingTime, transferSize) and .audits['bootup-time'].details.items filtered to third-party URLs (jq snippets used in this audit are in the elementor-audit skill). In Chrome DevTools MCP: list_network_requests after navigate_page to confirm which requests appear before interaction.
findings.how_to_verify: The blocked run's score gain equals the upper bound for fixing that vendor; after the real fix (consent gating/delay/removal) the unblocked run should reach within ~2 points of the blocked run. Keep the JSON files as before/after evidence; screenshot the third-party-summary table.

findings.claim: Trim the GTM container itself: custom HTML tags, click/timer triggers and unused variables inflate gtm.js and its execution; fire non-essential tags on Window Loaded or a custom event and only on pages that need them.
findings.detail: web.dev tag best-practices (published 2021-07-29, still Google's reference): 'image tags (pixels) are the most performant, followed by custom templates, and lastly, custom HTML tags'; 'Triggers are JavaScript code that increase the size and execution cost of the tag manager ... several click events or timer triggers can dramatically increase the workload'; 'To avoid impacting page load, fire non-essential tags after Window Loaded'; 'Remove old variables that are no longer used to reduce both the size of the tag manager script and the processing time'; 'ensure that a tag only fires on pages where it's actually used'; large scripts in custom HTML should be loaded via <script src> not pasted inline ('increases container size and prevents the script from being cached'). Observed: gtm.js for GTM-TJGCHWC9 is 166 KB transfer (308-402 ms bootup) versus 119 KB for GTM-PCC8PS8R (170 ms) — container contents, not Google's loader, explain the difference. The 5 Tag Manager tags seen on the slow sites include two Google Ads remarketing tags firing viewthroughconversion + google.com/pagead/1p-user-list on every page view.
findings.breaks_when: A conversion/remarketing tag moved to Window Loaded on a thank-you page that redirects within ~1 s misses the event; deleting a variable still referenced by a tag (GTM blocks the publish, so this fails safe); switching a vendor custom HTML tag to an image pixel loses its JS features (advanced matching, auto events).
findings.how_to_apply: In GTM: Admin > Container Settings > Enable consent overview; Workspace > Tags: for every non-Google tag check type (Custom HTML -> prefer gallery template), trigger (All Pages -> Window Loaded or page-specific), and consent settings. Variables: use 'Unused variables' hint in the Versions > Overview; delete. Replace remarketing-only Ads tags on all pages with the Google tag + Conversion Linker, and fire conversion tags only on confirmation URLs. Export the container JSON before/after and compare size; publish as a new version with a note.
findings.how_to_verify: gtm.js transfer size and Lighthouse bootup-time for gtm.js fall; GTM Preview shows on the home page only: CMP, Google tag (if advanced mode) and nothing else before consent; conversion tags fire exactly once on the confirmation page in Tag Assistant; GA4 DebugView shows no duplicate page_view.

findings.claim: Keep the cookie banner first-party and deferred (not delayed), kill its CSS transition, and allowlist its selectors in UCSS/critical CSS — otherwise the banner becomes the LCP element, a layout-shift source, or renders unstyled.
findings.detail: Observed: onar-seaside-lounge.gr's LCP element is '<div class="cmplz-message" id="cmplz-message-2-optin">' at 16.4 s, with complianz banner CSS (uploads/complianz/css/banner-2-optin.css) requested only at 6,637 ms; voreniahorizon.gr's layout-shifts audit lists '<div class="faz-consent-container faz-box-bottom-right" ... role="dialog">' as a shift culprit; FAZ script.min.js (33-36 KB) costs 292-447 ms bootup on three sites; marakaki.com's Complianz Premium loads complianz.min.js (11 KB, 375 ms) plus an uncached REST call /wp-json/complianz/v1/cookie_data; Cookie-Script is a third-party CDN (cdn.cookie-script.com) on three sites. Complianz 'About Web Vitals': the banner 'is loaded when HTML is almost fully loaded' so it can become LCP on slow pages; CLS: 'In the cookie banner there's a CSS transition of 1 second ... might cause for a higher CLS score' with a CSS override to remove it; they suggest a fixed height for the message. web.dev cookie-notice best practices (2024-06-13): load CMP scripts async, add preconnect/dns-prefetch for third-party CMP origins, prefer a footer/modal overlay over top-of-screen notices ('push the page elements below it'), avoid slide-in animations and late fonts. Complianz support thread: LiteSpeed/QUIC.cloud UCSS stripped banner CSS because the container starts with class cmplz-hidden; LiteSpeed docs: 'UCSS Selector Allowlist' exists for selectors 'not visible until a user interacts'. FAZ 1.34.1 changelog: 'The generated configuration and main banner JavaScript load with ordered defer, removing their render-blocking requests' and since 1.34.0 the DSAR/Do-Not-Sell scripts load only where their shortcode renders — the audited sites run 1.33.0/1.34.0, so updating removes two render-blocking requests and two scripts.
findings.breaks_when: UCSS allowlist incomplete: banner shows unstyled or invisible (consent cannot be given, so all consent-gated tracking stops); banner JS put in delay-JS: banner appears only after interaction; removing the transition changes the banner's visual entrance only; a banner placed at 'top' pushing content down produces CLS on every first visit.
findings.how_to_apply: Complianz: Settings > Banner > position bottom/center (overlay, not top); add CSS '.cmplz-cookiebanner{transition:none !important}' (their documented fix) and a fixed min-height for .cmplz-message; exclude 'complianz' and 'cmplz' from JS delay in Perfmatters/WP Rocket/FlyingPress/LiteSpeed; LiteSpeed Page Optimization > CSS > UCSS Selector Allowlist: add .cmplz-cookiebanner, .cmplz-message, .cmplz-hidden, #cmplz-cookiebanner-container (and for FAZ: .faz-consent-container, #faz-consent, .faz-box-*). FAZ: update to >= 1.34.1; keep the banner bottom-right box. Cookie-Script: add <link rel=preconnect href="https://cdn.cookie-script.com"> or, better, replace with a first-party CMP so no third-party request is needed before consent. Never put the CMP in LiteSpeed Guest Mode optimisation exclusions' blind spot — test Guest Mode off first.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse largest-contentful-paint-element must be a hero image/heading, not .cmplz-message or .faz-consent-container; layout-shifts audit lists no banner node (CLS target <= 0.01); banner is styled with UCSS/critical CSS on and renders without interaction in incognito; render-blocking-resources no longer lists faz config/script JS; Lighthouse network-requests shows banner CSS/JS requested in the first ~1 s (not at 6 s).
findings.correction: (1) Complianz 'About Web Vitals' is dated November 26, 2020 (Complianz 4.x era); its statements ('By default the cookie banner is loaded when HTML is almost fully loaded', 'In the cookie banner there's a CSS transition of 1 second ... might cause for a higher CLS score') still describe the mechanism, but the CSS override must be re-derived from the current banner markup (.cmplz-cookiebanner) on Complianz 7 rather than copied from that article. (2) LiteSpeed's UCSS Selector Allowlist doc says 'This setting is specifically for selectors that appear in the CSS. Entering parent IDs or classes from the HTML will not work' and 'reference each CSS selector exactly as it appears in the CSS file', so entries like '#cmplz-cookiebanner-container' only work if that exact selector exists in the banner stylesheet; copy selectors from uploads/complianz/css/banner-*.css, not from the DOM. FAZ 1.34.1: 'The generated configuration and main banner JavaScript load with ordered defer, removing their render-blocking requests'; 1.34.0 added a 'compact phone layout' (29% vs 44% of a phone screen) that also reduces banner surface. Risk stays low.

findings.claim: Run exactly one consent manager per site: onar-seaside-lounge.gr loads Complianz and Cookie-Script simultaneously, and limnoupolis.gr pairs a third-party Cookie-Script banner with tags that fire regardless of it.
findings.detail: Observed in the Lighthouse runs: onar requests /wp-json/complianz/v1/banner (Complianz REST) at 1,911 ms AND cdn.cookie-script.com/s/efb84e72....js at 2,194 ms, with gtag/js for G-349V7BDDBZ already executing at 1,124 ms; limnoupolis loads cdn.cookie-script.com/s/d7143c18....js at 2,822 ms while gtm.js, fbevents.js and both AW gtags started at 1,095-1,490 ms and collect/tr requests go out at 3.4-3.8 s with no consent. Two CMPs each set defaults and updates for Google consent mode, so the later one wins unpredictably; two banners can both appear; consent logs are split. Candidates on the agency's stack: FAZ Cookie Manager (first-party, free, GCM v2 all 7 signals, IAB TCF 2.3, consent logging, geo-targeting, 1.34.1 defers its JS); Complianz (GTM template + 'block all Google tags before consent' switch, documented delay-JS exclusions); Cookie-Script and CookieYes (third-party SaaS; both advertise Google Consent Mode v2 and Google-certified CMP status; CookieYes ships a 'Google Consent Mode Checker'). WooCommerce's GA plugin notes CMPs should implement the WP Consent API so plugins can read consent state.
findings.breaks_when: The removed CMP was the one wired to GTM (its template/trigger stays in GTM but never receives updates) — all consent-gated tags stop firing; cookie-blocker rules of the removed plugin were the only thing preventing a plugin-injected script (e.g. YouTube embeds, maps) from loading pre-consent.
findings.how_to_apply: Pick one CMP per site (prefer a first-party plugin: FAZ or Complianz) and deactivate the other (remove the Cookie-Script snippet from Elementor > Custom Code / theme). Re-wire GTM: delete the old CMP tag, add the new CMP's consent-mode template on 'Consent Initialization - All Pages'. Re-run the CMP's cookie scan. Record the decision and the GTM version in the site's handover notes.
findings.how_to_verify: Only one banner request in Network (either /wp-json/complianz/... or cdn.cookie-script.com or /uploads/faz-cookie-manager/...); dataLayer contains exactly one consent 'default' event and one 'update' after clicking; gcs=G100 before, G111 after Accept, G100 (no cookies) after Reject; the consent log in the CMP records the test visit.
findings.correction: On limnoupolis.gr the request cdn.cookie-script.com/s/d7143c18928376e0e745cc74abfe1329.js returns HTTP 200 with resourceSize 6 bytes (transferSize 212) at 2,824 ms: the script body is effectively empty, i.e. the Cookie-Script account/config is gone, so the snippet gates nothing and shows no banner. The fix is 'delete a dead snippet and install a real CMP', not 're-wire GTM from Cookie-Script'. Second: the candidate list must include 'Cookie Consent by Elementor' (Elementor help, updated June 22-23, 2026: opt-in wizard, cookie scan, consent logs, geo-targeting, GCM v2 with Basic default), which agencies on Elementor 4.x may enable from the Elementor dashboard, creating a third way to end up with two CMPs. Everything else (two consent 'default' pushes, split logs) holds. Risk stays low.

findings.claim: Hunt plugin-injected and legacy trackers: the WooCommerce Google Analytics extension injects its own gtag and overrides consent defaults, Universal Analytics IDs are dead since July 2023, and Elementor Pro Custom Code snippets hide tracking outside GTM.
findings.detail: Observed on staging.limnoupolis.gr: woocommerce-google-analytics-integration/assets/js/build/main.js plus gtag/js?id=UA-42569397-1 (133 KB, 460 ms bootup) — Google: standard UA properties 'stopped processing hits' July 1, 2023, data deleted after July 1, 2024. WooCommerce docs: the extension configures GA4 under WooCommerce > Settings > Integration > Google Analytics, sets its own consent-mode defaults ('This extension overwrites the consent mode defaults set by another extension' — override via filter woocommerce_ga_gtag_consent_modes; config via woocommerce_ga_gtag_config), and provides no banner (relies on WP Consent API CMPs). Elementor help: Custom Code (Pro) adds snippets at Location '<head>' / body start / body end with Priority 1-10 ('Lower numbers indicate higher priority') and display Conditions — Elementor's own GA/GTM and Facebook Pixel articles tell users to paste snippets there, so an agency site can have GTM + inline GA4 + inline pixel at once. Complianz docs: if GTM4WP/MonsterInsights integrations are active the consent-mode wizard hides, so pick one injection path.
findings.breaks_when: The Woo extension was the only source of GA4 ecommerce events (purchase, add_to_cart) — removing it without a dataLayer ecommerce implementation in GTM drops ecommerce reporting; a Custom Code snippet contained non-tracking code (schema, chat) that also gets deleted.
findings.how_to_apply: Checklist per site: Elementor > Custom Code (list every snippet, its Location/Priority/Conditions); Appearance > Theme File Editor header.php/footer.php of Inglelandi and child; WooCommerce > Settings > Integration > Google Analytics; plugins: GTM4WP, PixelYourSite, Site Kit, MonsterInsights, WooCommerce Google Listings & Ads; rendered HTML grep for 'UA-', 'gtag/js', 'fbq(', 'googletagmanager'. Keep one path (GTM). Remove UA IDs everywhere. If the Woo GA extension stays for ecommerce events, remove GA4 from GTM and set the extension's consent defaults to denied for EEA via woocommerce_ga_gtag_consent_modes so it does not override the CMP.
findings.how_to_verify: No request containing 'UA-' in the network log; GA4 DebugView shows one page_view per load and purchase events still arrive on a staging test order; Tag Assistant lists one Google tag instance per ID; Lighthouse bootup-time no longer lists the UA gtag (saves ~460 ms eval on staging).

findings.claim: Consent Mode v2 only works if the default state is set before gtm.js on every page, with wait_for_update for async banners, url_passthrough to keep gclid when ad_storage is denied, and region-scoped defaults so non-EEA visitors are not throttled.
findings.detail: Google developer guide: 'call the gtag('consent','default', ...) command on every page of your site before any commands that send measurement data'; 'If your consent code is called out of order, consent defaults won't work'; 'If your banner loads asynchronously ... specify wait_for_update along with a millisecond value' (example 500); v2 added ad_user_data and ad_personalization in November 2023; region scoping: 'It is best practice to scope the default consent settings to the regions where you are surfacing consent banners' (ISO 3166-2, e.g. 'GR' or the EEA list, more specific region wins); url_passthrough: 'create (or use an existing) conversion linker tag and ensure Enable linking on all page URLs is checked' or gtag('set','url_passthrough',true) before the GTM snippet; ads_data_redaction=true redacts click IDs and routes via a cookieless domain when ad_storage is denied; in GTM use template APIs setDefaultConsentState/updateConsentState — 'Don't use gtag('consent','update',...) methods instead of updateConsentState'. Google's EU user consent policy applies to end users in the EEA, UK and Switzerland. Verification per Complianz: collect request parameter gcs=G100 (default denied), G110 (ads only), G101 (analytics only), G111 (both). This affects compliance and data quality more than the score; it becomes a score issue when a misplaced default lets all tags fire unconditionally.
findings.breaks_when: Default snippet placed after gtm.js, or delayed by a delay-JS plugin while gtm.js is not: tags run with full cookies before consent (non-compliant, and Google may restrict EEA measurement); url_passthrough appends _gl/gclid-derived params to internal links, which can fragment page caches (LiteSpeed/W3TC/FlyingPress query-string variants) and, per Google, 'in rare cases, your web server might run into an error'; wait_for_update too short for a slow CMP: first pings sent as denied.
findings.how_to_apply: Prefer the CMP's GTM template on 'Consent Initialization - All Pages'. If inline: in the <head> snippet (Elementor > Custom Code, Location <head>, Priority 1, excluded from delay-JS) put window.dataLayer=window.dataLayer||[];function gtag(){dataLayer.push(arguments)};gtag('consent','default',{ad_storage:'denied',ad_user_data:'denied',ad_personalization:'denied',analytics_storage:'denied',region:['GR','DE',...EEA],wait_for_update:500}); gtag('consent','default',{ad_storage:'granted',...}) for other regions if the client wants it; gtag('set','ads_data_redaction',true); then the GTM snippet. In GTM enable Conversion Linker > 'Enable linking on all page URLs'. Add 'gclid', '_gl' to the cache plugin's ignored query strings (LiteSpeed 'Drop Query String', FlyingPress/W3TC equivalents).
findings.how_to_verify: Tag Assistant > Consent tab shows 'On-page Default' before 'Update'; first g/collect request has gcs=G100 and a gcd= parameter; after Accept gcs=G111; from a non-EEA proxy/VPN the default is granted if region scoping was intended; click an internal link after landing with ?gclid=test and confirm _gl or gclid persists in the URL; confirm the cache plugin serves the same cached HTML for /?gclid=x (response header hit).

findings.claim: Use facades for Google Maps, YouTube and chat widgets: Elementor's Google Maps widget already emits <iframe loading="lazy"> and its Video widget has a 'Lazy Load' switch, but above-the-fold maps/videos still load the full third-party player.
findings.detail: Elementor main branch (4.x) includes/widgets/google-maps.php renders '<iframe loading="lazy" src="https://maps.google.com/maps?q=...&output=embed">' (or the Embed API URL when option elementor_google_maps_api_key is set); loading=lazy is ignored for iframes near the viewport, so a hero/contact map still loads maps.google.com immediately. The audit summary shows 18 google_maps widgets on onar-seaside-lounge.gr and 8 on pallada.gr; limnoupolis.gr has 84 video widgets. includes/widgets/video.php has control 'lazy_load' ('Lazy Load' switcher) available for YouTube or when show_image_overlay=yes (non-hosted) — it renders the poster instead of the player. Perfmatters lazy-load docs: 'Lazy load iframes and videos' covers 'YouTube, Vimeo, SoundCloud, Google Maps, and any type of iframe' and 'YouTube preview thumbnails' swaps iframes for a thumbnail + SVG play icon loaded on click, explicitly supporting 'Elementor Atomic YouTube elements and legacy Elementor video widgets'; they report 64% faster / 58% smaller pages; thumbnail quality via filter perfmatters_lazyload_youtube_thumbnail_resolution (maxresdefault needs >= 1280x720). Chrome's facades audit (removed in Lighthouse 13, present in the pinned lighthouse@12): 'The facade weighs 3 KB and the player weighing 540 KB is loaded on interaction'. No chat widget was observed on the ten sites; if one is added, FlyingPress/Perfmatters delay or a GTM custom-event trigger after interaction is the documented approach.
findings.breaks_when: A map replaced by a static image loses panning/zoom until click (acceptable on contact pages, confirm with client); YouTube thumbnails look blurry when the video has no 1280x720 thumbnail; an autoplay/background video cannot use a facade (needs a click) — use a poster image on mobile instead; Elementor 'Lazy Load' hides the player until click, which changes the design intent for 'autoplay on view' sections.
findings.how_to_apply: Elementor Video widget: enable 'Image Overlay' + 'Lazy Load' (YouTube) or set a Poster; for Google Maps in the hero/contact section replace the widget with an Image widget (static map screenshot or Maps Static API image) linked to Google Maps, keep the real Maps widget only below the fold. Perfmatters: Lazy Loading > 'iFrames and Videos' on, 'YouTube Preview Thumbnails' on. Site-wide check: count iframes in the first viewport on mobile and move/replace them.
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile emulation: no request to maps.google.com, www.google.com/maps/embed, youtube.com/embed or ytimg player JS until scroll/click; Lighthouse network-requests confirms; LCP element remains the hero image; clicking the facade loads and plays the embed; Elementor editor preview still shows the overlay image.

findings.claim: Load booking, filter, pixel and chat scripts only on the pages that use them with Perfmatters Script Manager (or GTM page-scoped triggers) rather than site-wide.
findings.detail: Perfmatters Script Manager (Plugin > 'Script Manager' toggle, then admin-bar 'Perfmatters > Script Manager' or ?perfmatters on any URL) lists every JS/CSS handle on the page and can disable each 'Everywhere', on the 'Current URL', or by post type, with regex and 'MU mode' for whole plugins; documented examples: Contact Form 7 everywhere except contact page, social sharing only on posts. web.dev tag best-practices: 'ensure that a tag only fires on pages where it's actually used'; 'fire non-essential tags after Window Loaded'; custom event trigger pushed after a timer is the documented way to fine-tune timing. On the agency stack the usual site-wide offenders are YITH Booking / WooCommerce Bookings assets, JetSmartFilters, Dynamic.ooo and Premium Addons libraries, pixel plugins, and GTM tags scoped to 'All Pages' that only matter on shop/checkout. The sites with Perfmatters installed (marakaki, onar, pallada) already have the tool; marakaki shows '131 widgets disabled' in the audit, so the pattern is established.
findings.breaks_when: Disabling a shared dependency (jquery, elementor frontend, swiper) on a page that needs it breaks sliders/menus/forms; a booking widget script disabled on a landing page that embeds the booking form via popup; a GTM tag scoped by URL misses a translated (Polylang/WPML) URL variant (/el/ vs /en/) — scope by page type/dataLayer variable rather than literal path.
findings.how_to_apply: Perfmatters > Plugin > enable Script Manager (+ 'Testing Mode' so only admins see changes); open each template type (home, room/villa page, shop, checkout, booking, blog post) and disable plugin assets not used there ('Everywhere' + exception by post type, or regex on /shop|/checkout|/booking). In GTM: change 'All Pages' triggers on non-essential tags to 'Window Loaded' and add conditions (Page Path matches RegEx for both language prefixes, or a dataLayer pageType pushed by the theme). Document every rule in the site's handover.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse unused-javascript and network-requests on the home page no longer list the booking/filter/addon bundles; browser console shows no 'X is not defined' errors on any template; click-test booking, filters, popups, forms and language switch on each template; Tag Assistant confirms page-scoped tags fire on their intended pages in both languages.

findings.claim: Server-side GTM moves vendor pixels (Meta CAPI) off the browser, which removes fbevents.js entirely and makes cookies first-party; Google tag gateway only changes where gtm.js is served from and does not reduce JavaScript execution.
findings.detail: Google server-side tagging intro (updated 2026-07-30): a server container 'doesn't run in the user's browser ... it runs on a server that you control'; the web page still runs one client-side Google tag/GTM container that sends to your first-party endpoint; recommended hosting Cloud Run (App Engine alternative); 'install the server on your first-party domain and upgrade the server to production mode' before production. Meta/other vendors are implemented as server tags (Conversions API), so the browser never downloads connect.facebook.net (on limnoupolis that is 336 KB and ~914 ms main thread). Managed hosting price points from Stape's pricing page: Free up to 10K requests/month, Pro $17/mo billed annually ($20 monthly) up to 500K requests, Business $83/$100 up to 5M. Google tag gateway for advertisers: 'deploy a Google tag using your own first-party infrastructure ... using your existing CDN, load balancer, or web server' (Cloudflare in-UI setup available); benefits listed are conversion uplift, fewer third-party interactions, privacy — it is about ad-block resilience and first-party cookies, not CPU time; Google recommends combining gateway + server-side tagging. For the water-park shop and hotel booking sites this is the only path that keeps Meta measurement while scoring 95+, because any browser pixel costs ~0.5 s of blocking on mobile.
findings.breaks_when: Consent is not forwarded server-side (the GA4 client passes gcs/consent state; custom clients must respect it) — server tags fire for non-consenting users; browser pixel kept alongside CAPI without matching event_id → duplicated Meta events; custom domain/DNS misconfigured → 100% data loss until fixed; monthly cost/quota exceeded on Stape free tier (10K requests) → events dropped.
findings.how_to_apply: Create a GTM server container; host on Stape (Pro) or Google Cloud Run; map a first-party subdomain (e.g. gtm.<site>.gr, 'Map a custom domain'); in the web container point the Google tag's server_container_url to it; add the Meta Conversions API tag (Stape/Meta template) in the server container with consent checks; remove the browser Meta pixel or keep only a lightweight consent-gated pixel with event_id deduplication; optionally enable Google tag gateway via Cloudflare for first-party serving of gtm.js. Keep basic consent mode in the web container.
findings.how_to_verify: Browser Network after Accept: requests go to gtm.<site>.gr/g/collect (no analytics.google.com, no connect.facebook.net); server container Preview shows incoming GA4 events and outgoing Meta CAPI hits with status 200; Meta Events Manager shows events arriving via 'Server' with deduplication OK; Lighthouse third-party-summary has no Facebook entity; GA4 DebugView still shows page_view/purchase.

findings.claim: Verify tracking after every change with a fixed protocol: GTM Preview/Tag Assistant, GA4 DebugView (debug_mode), Meta Test Events, and the raw collect/tr requests with their gcs parameter, in both 'no interaction' and 'after Accept' states.
findings.detail: Google: GTM 'Preview' launches Tag Assistant; 'Connect' opens the site 'Connected'; the debug pane shows which tags fired, in which order and with what data; option 'Include debug signal in the URL' can be unchecked if the parameter breaks a page. GA4 DebugView: enable via Tag Assistant/preview, or add 'debug_mode':true to the config command; 'setting the parameter to false doesn't disable debug mode' — remove it afterwards; Seconds stream shows events from the last 60 s. Request signatures observed in the local runs and useful as assertions: GA4 → analytics.google.com/g/collect or www.google-analytics.com/g/collect?v=2&tid=G-...&gcs=...; Google Ads → googleads.g.doubleclick.net/pagead/viewthroughconversion/<AW id>/ and www.google.com/ccm/collect (consent-mode channel), pagead2.googlesyndication.com/ccm/collect when ads_data_redaction routes cookieless; Meta → www.facebook.com/tr/?id=<pixel>&ev=PageView. Complianz's verification page gives the gcs mapping (G100/G110/G101/G111) and a console snippet to dump consent state. web.dev notes the Accept click itself can cause high INP because all tags execute at once — test it on a mid-range Android.
findings.breaks_when: not known to break; false confidence if the tester's browser already has a stored consent cookie (test in a fresh incognito/mobile emulation each time) or if the delay-JS timeout fires during the 'no interaction' observation window (wait longer than the timeout, or note the expected time).
findings.how_to_apply: Protocol per site, run on staging then production: (1) Lighthouse mobile ×3 median before; (2) incognito, DevTools Network, filter 'collect|/tr|gtm|gtag|fbevents', load page, no interaction 20 s → record which requests appear (expect none except gtm.js/CMP in basic mode); (3) click Reject → expect no tracking requests, consent cookie set; (4) new incognito, click Accept → expect GA4 collect with gcs=G111, Ads viewthroughconversion/ccm, Meta tr PageView; (5) GTM Preview: walk home → room/product → add to cart → checkout/booking → confirmation; every tag green once; (6) GA4 DebugView and Meta Test Events show the events; (7) Lighthouse ×3 after; (8) 7-day comparison of GA4 sessions and Ads/Meta conversions. Script steps 2-4 with Chrome DevTools MCP (navigate_page, list_network_requests, click) in the plugin.
findings.how_to_verify: Deliverables: before/after Lighthouse JSON, a network screenshot per state, Tag Assistant summary screenshot, a GA4 DebugView screenshot with the test purchase, and the 7-day conversion comparison; any missing tag in step 5 blocks the change from shipping.
