The biggest sources of false alarms on Elementor sites are entrance animations (elementor-invisible/animated classes, 12-68 per home page on the audited sites), Swiper carousels, autoplay video, three different cookie banners (Complianz, FAZ, Cookie-Script) and Lighthouse's own noise; each has a specific stabiliser documented below. Lighthouse must be read as a median of 5 sequential runs, with the 30 percent weight of TBT in mind and the benchmarkIndex checked, otherwise a 5-10 point swing will be mistaken for a regression (or hide one); metric-level thresholds (LCP, CLS, TBT) are more trustworthy than the score. Vendor off-switches (?perfmattersoff, ?LSCWP_CTRL=before_optm, Perfmatters Testing Mode, LiteSpeed Disable All Features) let the harness isolate the cause of a failure without rolling back. What cannot be automated: deciding whether a flagged visual change is acceptable, email delivery of form notifications, real booking or payment completion, legal correctness of consent, subjective animation quality, and confirmation from CrUX field data, which lags lab results.
critic_notes: Method: every URL listed was opened (WebFetch where DNS allowed; otherwise curl through the session proxy with the page converted to text; GitHub repos elementor/elementor @ 4.4.0 main and Really-Simple-Plugins/complianz-gdpr @ 7.5.6 were shallow-cloned read-only into the scratchpad and grepped). No site, WordPress setting or Novamira tool was touched. Open questions resolved: Complianz cookie names/prefix (cmplz_banner-status='dismissed', cmplz_consented_services, cmplz_saved_categories, cmplz_saved_services, cmplz_policy_id, cmplz_id; prefix cmplz_ or cmplz_rt_), Elementor preview iframe id (#elementor-preview-iframe inside #elementor-preview), experiment option states (default/active/inactive), LiteSpeed before_optm needs no Admin IP while NOCACHE does, Lighthouse 13 audit mapping for lighthouse.sh. Still unverified: FlyingPress `?no_optimize` (cited article 404s; no current doc found), FlyingPress option name for `wp option get`, W3TC export file format and whether import fully restores page-cache settings (Cli.php only shows `$w3tc_config->export()`), FAZ Cookie Manager and Cookie-Script cookie names, YITH/WooCommerce Bookings datepicker selectors, Elementor Pro 4.3 nested mega-menu DOM. Chrome DevTools MCP tools were not evaluated. Risk to the user: the pinned Lighthouse 12.x gives diagnostics PSI no longer shows, and LiteSpeed Guest Optimization can make PSI scores look unrelated to the settings the plugin changes; both need to be in the ledger before any before/after claim.

findings.claim: Every optimisation step must be wrapped in record-before → apply one change → purge → run gates → keep-or-undo, with the before-values captured by exact WP-CLI/plugin export commands, not by memory.
findings.detail: The existing debloat.php already stores before-values in option `elementor_lean_undo`; the harness generalises that. Before each step: `wp option get <name> --format=json` for every option the step touches (Elementor settings and experiments live in wp_options; `wp option list --search='elementor_*' --format=json` snapshots them all), `wp litespeed-option export --filename=/path/lscwp-<step>.txt` (restored with `wp litespeed-option import <file>`; file is one `option_key=option_value` per line, `;` comments), `wp w3-total-cache export <filename>` / `wp w3-total-cache import <filename>` (Cli.php also has `option get|set <name> [<value>] --type=boolean|string|integer|array|json`, note 'Options modifications do not update your .htaccess file automatically'), Perfmatters: Tools → 'Export Plugin Settings' (.json, excludes licence and Script Manager because Script Manager rules are tied to post IDs) restored with `wp perfmatters import-settings <file>`; Elementor experiments: `wp elementor experiments status <name>` before, `wp elementor experiments activate|deactivate <name>` to apply/undo. For anything not option-based (revision pruning, plugin deactivation) take `wp db export <file>` first. Then always `wp elementor flush-css [--regenerate]` and the page-cache purge (`wp litespeed-purge all`, `wp w3-total-cache flush all`) before measuring, otherwise the harness compares a stale cached page with itself.
findings.breaks_when: A step changes more than one thing (undo cannot attribute the regression), or the before-value is not recorded as the exact serialized value (e.g. Elementor `elementor_experiment-*` options store the string 'active'/'inactive'; LiteSpeed import across environments fails on host-specific values such as CDN mapping), or caches are not purged so the 'after' measurement is really the 'before' page.
findings.how_to_apply: Per step write a JSON ledger entry {step, timestamp, commands_run, before:{option:value...}, export_files:[...]} to the scratch dir and to Novamira memory key `elementor-lean-log` (already used by the plugin). Undo = replay the recorded values: `wp option update <name> '<json>' --format=json`, `wp litespeed-option import <file>`, `wp w3-total-cache import <file>`, `wp perfmatters import-settings <file>`, `wp elementor experiments deactivate <name>`. Then purge and re-run the gates to confirm the undo restored the baseline (the undo itself is a change).
findings.how_to_verify: After undo, the console diff, screenshot diff and CLS gates must be green against the step's own 'before' baseline (not the original site baseline), and `wp option get <name>` must equal the recorded before-value byte for byte.
findings.correction: Record Elementor experiment options as raw option values (`wp option get elementor_experiment-<name>` can be 'active', 'inactive' or absent/'default'), never as the CLI's binary status; note that `wp elementor flush-css` clears the Element Cache meta for all posts as well as CSS; FlyingPress settings can only be snapshotted via `wp option get` (no export/CLI exists), and its cache is purged with `wp flying-press purge-everything`. Risk stays none.

findings.claim: Use Playwright's built-in `expect(page).toHaveScreenshot()` for visual regression; its defaults already freeze CSS/Web animations and hide the caret, and the per-pixel `threshold` plus `maxDiffPixelRatio` are the two knobs that make Elementor diffs stable.
findings.detail: Playwright 1.64.1 (released 14 Oct 2026; 1.64.0 added a `type` option that can store screenshots as WebP). Documented option semantics: `animations: 'disabled'` (default) 'stops CSS animations, CSS transitions and Web Animations... finite animations are fast-forwarded to completion... infinite animations are canceled to initial state'; `caret: 'hide'` (default); `threshold` 'acceptable perceived color difference... between 0 (strict) and 1 (lax). Defaults to 0.2' (YIQ); `maxDiffPixels` and `maxDiffPixelRatio` 'Unset by default', configurable globally in `TestConfig.expect.toHaveScreenshot`; `mask: [locators]` overlays a pink #FF00FF box (change with `maskColor`); `stylePath` injects a CSS file during capture 'to hide dynamic elements'; `fullPage`, `scale: 'css'|'device'`. Baselines are updated only with `npx playwright test --update-snapshots`. Alternative engines if a Node test project is unwanted: BackstopJS (`misMatchThreshold` default 0.1 percent, `hideSelectors` sets visibility:hidden, `removeSelectors` display:none, `readySelector`, `delay`, `requireSameDimensions` default true, `backstop reference|test|approve`; latest stable v3.8.8, v5.0.2 is pre-release), odiff v4.5.0 (`odiff a.png b.png diff.png`, Node `compare()` returns {match:false, reason:'pixel-diff', diffCount, diffPercentage} or reason 'layout-diff'; benchmarks on its README show ~6x faster than pixelmatch/ImageMagick) and pixelmatch (`threshold` default 0.1, `includeAA` false; CLI exit code 0 match, 66 differ, 65 size mismatch).
findings.breaks_when: Thresholds are set too loose (a `maxDiffPixelRatio` above ~0.02 hides a missing icon font or a broken menu), or too tight (0 pixels tolerated fails on font anti-aliasing and lazy images); baselines are taken on a different OS/browser than the comparison (Playwright names snapshots per platform); `scale: 'device'` at deviceScaleFactor 3 triples the pixel count and slows diffing.
findings.how_to_apply: playwright.config.ts: `expect: { toHaveScreenshot: { threshold: 0.2, maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01, animations: 'disabled', caret: 'hide', scale: 'css' } }`, projects `{ name:'mobile', use: { ...devices['iPhone 13'] } }` (390x844, isMobile, hasTouch) and `{ name:'desktop', use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], viewport:{width:1366,height:768} } }`. Per page take two shots: above-the-fold (`fullPage:false`, strict 0.005) and `fullPage:true` (0.01) with `mask: [page.locator('.swiper-slide, .elementor-widget-video, iframe, .elementor-widget-google_maps')]` and `stylePath: 'screenshot.css'`. Name baselines per step: `expect(page).toHaveScreenshot(`${slug}-${viewport}-step${n}.png`)`, so each step is compared against the previous step's approved state.
findings.how_to_verify: Run the suite twice against the unchanged site: it must pass both times (zero flakes) before the first optimisation; then introduce a deliberate break (hide the menu button with CSS) and confirm the diff fails with the diff image showing the header. Keep the `-diff.png` and `-actual.png` artifacts for the human to approve.
findings.correction: Keep the Playwright part; fix the engine facts: BackstopJS current = 6.3.25 on npm (do not cite the GitHub Releases page), odiff 4.5.0 is installed as `odiff-bin`, pixelmatch 8.0.0. Add: generate and compare baselines inside one pinned Playwright Docker image (Playwright names snapshots per project/platform and warns rendering differs even on battery vs mains). Risk none.

findings.claim: Elementor-specific diff stabilisers: emulate prefers-reduced-motion (Elementor honours it, which removes entrance animations and motion effects), force `.elementor-invisible` visible via stylePath, mask Swiper carousels and video widgets, fix the clock for countdown/booking widgets, and block third-party hosts during screenshot runs only.
findings.detail: Elementor help ('Add entrance animations') states: 'Elementor respects the "reduced motion property" preference that a user may set. If a user has set any of the following, then motion effects will be disabled for that user'. The audited home pages carry 68 (cretaforums.gr), 33 (voreniahorizon.gr), 12 (pallada.gr) and 3 (onar-seaside-lounge.gr) `elementor-invisible` elements and 25/22/7 `_animation` data-settings; without a stabiliser these render blank or mid-animation in screenshots. Swiper markup (`swiper-slide`: pallada 10, voreniahorizon 4; `elementor-swiper`) and `elementor-widget-video` (onar 2, voreniahorizon 1) change frame to frame. Playwright gives `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` (and `colorScheme`), `page.clock.setFixedTime(new Date('2026-10-15T10:00:00'))` ('The recommended approach is to use setFixedTime'), and `page.route('**/*', route => BLOCKED_HOSTS.test(route.request().url()) ? route.abort() : route.continue())` to abort googletagmanager/facebook/maps requests so no ad, chat bubble or map tile enters the screenshot. Run the screenshot project with blocking on; run the tracking project (finding 9) with blocking off.
findings.breaks_when: reducedMotion also hides genuine animation regressions (an entrance animation that now never finishes on real devices is invisible to the harness; cover that with the console/pageerror gate and one unmasked 'allow animations' shot after `page.waitForTimeout(3000)`); blocking a host the page needs for layout (e.g. a hosted font CDN) causes a layout diff that looks like a regression; fixed clock breaks nonce/time-limited booking widgets (YITH/WooCommerce Bookings) so exclude those pages from the clock fixture.
findings.how_to_apply: In the screenshot fixture: `await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' }); await page.clock.setFixedTime(FIXED);` then `stylePath` CSS: `.elementor-invisible{visibility:visible!important;opacity:1!important;animation:none!important} .animated{animation:none!important} .swiper-wrapper{transform:none!important} video,iframe{visibility:hidden!important} *{transition:none!important;scroll-behavior:auto!important}`. Wait for `document.fonts.ready` and `networkidle` before each shot; scroll to bottom and back to top first so lazy images are decoded (`await page.mouse.wheel(0, 20000)` in a loop until scrollHeight is stable).
findings.how_to_verify: Three consecutive screenshot runs on an unchanged page produce 0 differing pixels (check Playwright's report); a run with the stylePath removed must show the animated elements as the only diff regions, proving the stabilisers target the right nodes.
findings.correction: Reduced motion in Elementor 4.x only cancels `.animated` keyframes/transitions, turns off smooth scroll and disables Swiper autoplay; it never removes `elementor-invisible`. Keep reducedMotion for the Swiper/transition benefit but treat the `.elementor-invisible` stylePath override as required for any fullPage shot, and also scroll the page once (entrance handlers fire on viewport entry) before the viewport shot. Risk low.

findings.claim: Cookie banners (Complianz, FAZ Cookie Manager, Cookie-Script are all present across the 10 sites) are handled by clicking 'accept' once in a Playwright setup project, saving `storageState`, and reusing it, rather than by vendor-specific cookie values.
findings.detail: Live home pages show three different consent stacks: `cmplz-cookiebanner`/`cmplz-accept` on onar-seaside-lounge.gr, `fazcookie` on pallada.gr, cretaforums.gr and voreniahorizon.gr, `cookie-script` on voreniahorizon.gr. Complianz stores consent partly in localStorage (banner_version data) and partly in cookies, and no official page documents the exact cookie values (complianz.io/cookies/ returns 404 today), so hard-coding values is fragile. Playwright's auth guide: 'Authenticate once in the setup project, save the authentication state, and then reuse it' via `await page.context().storageState({ path: 'playwright/.auth/consent.json' })` and `use: { storageState: 'playwright/.auth/consent.json' }` with `dependencies: ['setup']`; storageState captures cookies and localStorage. Keep two states: `consent-accepted.json` (for visual, interaction and tracking gates) and `consent-none.json` (fresh context, for the banner-visible screenshot and for Lighthouse, which always runs without consent). BackstopJS equivalent: `cookiePath` or Playwright-engine `storageState`.
findings.breaks_when: The banner plugin bumps its banner version after a settings change (Complianz does this) so the saved state is ignored and the banner reappears in every screenshot, failing all diffs at once; the accept button has no accessible name (use a vendor fallback selector list: `.cmplz-accept`, `#cookiescript_accept`, FAZ button text 'Αποδοχή'/'Accept').
findings.how_to_apply: setup.spec.ts: visit home, `await page.getByRole('button', { name: /accept|αποδοχ/i }).first().click({ timeout: 10000 }).catch(() => page.locator('.cmplz-accept, #cookiescript_accept, .cc-allow').first().click())`, wait for the banner to detach, save `storageState`. Re-run setup whenever the consent plugin is updated or its settings change (detect by diffing `wp option get` of the consent plugin options in the ledger).
findings.how_to_verify: With the saved state, the first screenshot of every page must not contain the banner (assert `page.locator('.cmplz-cookiebanner, #cookiescript_injected, [class*=fazcookie]')` hidden); with the empty state it must be visible and `facebook.com/tr` and `g/collect` must be absent (consent gating check, finding 9).

findings.claim: Console errors, uncaught exceptions and failed/4xx-5xx requests are collected on every page load and compared as a set against the step's baseline; only new entries fail the gate, because delay/defer JS breaks show up first as 'jQuery is not defined'-type errors, not as pixels.
findings.detail: Playwright: `page.on('pageerror', e => ...)`, `page.on('console', msg => msg.type() === 'error' ...)`, `page.on('requestfailed', r => r.url() + ' ' + r.failure().errorText)`. The docs warn: 'HTTP Error responses, such as 404 or 503, are still successful responses from HTTP standpoint, so request will complete with page.on("requestfinished") event and not with page.on("requestfailed")' — so also hook `page.on('response', r => r.status() >= 400 ...)`. Since v1.56 there are also `page.consoleMessages()` and `page.pageErrors()` (last 200 each) and `page.clearPageErrors()`, convenient for 'what did this click add'. Perfmatters' own troubleshooting doc says JS console errors are the clue when 'sliders, mobile menus, image galleries, popups' break after Delay/Defer, typically because jQuery or an inline dependency must be excluded too (`Excluded from Delay`, 'Include Inline Scripts'). Normalise messages before diffing (strip query strings, cache-buster `?ver=`, line:col), and allow-list known third-party noise (blocked tracker requests when consent is denied, `net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT`).
findings.breaks_when: Delay-JS implementations only execute scripts after user interaction, so a pure load test sees no error: the gate must also run after the interaction tests (scroll + tap) and re-read `page.pageErrors()`; errors inside cross-origin iframes (Maps, YouTube) are not visible to the page.
findings.how_to_apply: Fixture collects {pageErrors:[], consoleErrors:[], failed:[{url,errorText}], http4xx5xx:[{url,status}]} per URL and viewport, writes `console-<slug>-<viewport>-step<n>.json`; gate: `new = after \ before` must be empty, and `failed` for first-party URLs (same origin, uploads, fonts) must be empty. Run with the consent-accepted state and, after the load, perform `page.mouse.wheel(0,800)` + `page.tap('body')` + 3 s wait before the final read, to wake delayed scripts.
findings.how_to_verify: Inject a deliberate break on staging (Perfmatters Script Manager disable jquery-core on one page) and confirm the gate reports the new `ReferenceError` and fails; then restore and confirm green. Also check that the normal run produces an empty 'new' set on two consecutive runs.

findings.claim: Interaction smoke tests use role-based locators and assert on network/DOM outcomes: open the mobile menu, submit a form, add to cart via the official URL or Store API, open the booking calendar, open a popup (assert the `elementor/popup/show` event), and switch language (assert `html[lang]` and a 200).
findings.detail: Playwright recommends 'prioritizing user-facing attributes and explicit contracts such as page.getByRole()'. Selectors seen on the audited sites, usable as fallbacks: menu toggles `elementor-menu-toggle` (pallada.gr), `elementor-nav-menu--dropdown` (cretaforums 12, pallada 10, voreniahorizon 6, onar 4), new Mega Menu `e-n-menu-toggle` (limnoupolis 20, pallada 4); forms `elementor-widget-form` (limnoupolis 8, onar 2, voreniahorizon 1); bookings `yith-wcbk` (limnoupolis, 246 hits) and `wc-bookings-booking-form` (pallada); language switcher `wpml-ls` (voreniahorizon 12) and Polylang's `pll_the_languages()` output (limnoupolis). WooCommerce documents add-to-cart URLs: `https://example.com/?add-to-cart=PRODUCT_ID&quantity=QUANTITY` (also `VARIATION_ID`, and `/cart/?add-to-cart=...`); the Store API tutorial: `GET /wp-json/wc/store/v1/cart` returns a `Nonce` response header, then `POST /wp-json/wc/store/v1/cart/add-item?id=27&quantity=1` with that header. Elementor Pro popups fire `jQuery(document).on('elementor/popup/show', (event, id, instance) => ...)` and `elementor/popup/hide`. Elementor Pro forms submit via admin-ajax; the safest end-to-end assertion is a dedicated hidden test form whose only 'Actions after submit' is a Webhook to a request-capture endpoint you control, plus the on-page success message; never submit the live contact form (it emails the client).
findings.breaks_when: Tests add real items to a production cart or create real bookings (use a test product and empty the cart via Store API, or run on staging); the mega-menu/popup markup differs between Elementor 4.2.3 (onar) and 4.3.x (nested `e-n-menu`), so a single hard-coded selector fails on one site; element caching (`element_cache_on`, 24h) serves a stale form nonce or filter result, which only an interaction test catches.
findings.how_to_apply: Per site a `smoke.json` lists the flows: `{menu:{url:'/'}, form:{url:'/test-form/', fields:{...}, expectWebhook:true}, cart:{productId:123}, booking:{url:'/villa-x/', dateField:'input[name=from]'}, popup:{trigger:'a[href*="popup"]'}, lang:{from:'/',to:'/en/'}}`. Menu: `await page.getByRole('button',{name:/menu/i}).or(page.locator('.elementor-menu-toggle, .e-n-menu-toggle')).first().click(); await expect(page.getByRole('navigation').getByRole('link').first()).toBeVisible()`. Popup: `await page.evaluate(() => new Promise(r => jQuery(document).one('elementor/popup/show', (e,id) => r(id))))` raced with the trigger click. Booking: click the date input, `expect(page.locator('.ui-datepicker, .yith-wcbk-date-picker, .wc-bookings-date-picker')).toBeVisible()`. Cart: `page.goto('/?add-to-cart=ID&quantity=1')` then `expect(page.locator('.woocommerce-message, .wc-block-components-notice-banner')).toBeVisible()`, then empty the cart. Lang: goto `to`, `expect(page.locator('html')).toHaveAttribute('lang', /^en/)`. Run each flow once per viewport with the console gate active.
findings.how_to_verify: Each flow must pass on the untouched site first (record the selector that matched per site in the ledger); after a change, all flows green with no new console errors. Confirm the webhook endpoint received exactly one POST per form test and the client's inbox received nothing.

findings.claim: Measure CLS directly in Playwright with a buffered `layout-shift` PerformanceObserver (plus a scripted scroll pass) and fail when CLS exceeds 0.1 or rises more than 0.02 over the step baseline; this catches the lazy-load regression (0 → 0.107) that a single Lighthouse run can miss.
findings.detail: web.dev (updated 2025-02-07): `new PerformanceObserver((list) => { for (const entry of list.getEntries()) { if (!entry.hadRecentInput) {...} } }).observe({type: 'layout-shift', buffered: true})`; `hadRecentInput` is true 'within 500 milliseconds of user input' (discrete input events only, not scroll), `sources` lists up to five `LayoutShiftAttribution` nodes that moved. CLS is 'the largest burst' of shifts in a session window ('less than 1-second in between each shift and a maximum of 5 seconds for the total window duration'); good is 0.1 or less, poor above 0.25. The `web-vitals` library (v5, `web-vitals/attribution` build) exposes `onCLS(cb, {reportAllChanges:true})` with `attribution.largestShiftTarget`, `largestShiftSource`, `largestShiftValue`, `loadState`, and for LCP `target`, `url`, `resourceLoadDelay`, `elementRenderDelay`. Scrolling does not set hadRecentInput, so a scripted scroll pass reproduces real lazy-load shifts (images without dimensions, LiteSpeed/FlyingPress lazy-load placeholders, late fonts). DevTools 'Rendering > Layout Shift Regions' remains the manual tool.
findings.breaks_when: The observer is injected after the shift (must be installed via `page.addInitScript` before navigation, and `buffered: true`); the page uses `scroll-behavior: smooth` or sticky headers that animate (counted as shifts: disable via stylePath only in the visual project, never in the CLS project); fonts load from cache in the second run so FOUT shifts disappear (use a fresh context per measurement).
findings.how_to_apply: `await context.addInitScript(() => { window.__ls = []; new PerformanceObserver(l => l.getEntries().forEach(e => { if (!e.hadRecentInput) window.__ls.push({v:e.value, t:e.startTime, src:e.sources?.map(s => s.node?.outerHTML?.slice(0,120))}); })).observe({type:'layout-shift', buffered:true}); })`; after load wait 3 s, then scroll in viewport-height steps to the bottom with 500 ms pauses, then `const entries = await page.evaluate(() => window.__ls)` and compute the max 5 s/1 s session window in Node. Report the top `src` nodes. Thresholds: fail if windowed CLS > 0.1 (mobile) or > baseline + 0.02; warn above baseline + 0.01. Alternative: `page.addScriptTag({url:'https://unpkg.com/web-vitals@5/dist/web-vitals.attribution.iife.js'})` and read `webVitals.onCLS`.
findings.how_to_verify: Reproduce the known case on staging: enable LiteSpeed lazy-load images, run the gate, expect a windowed CLS around 0.1 with `img` nodes in `src`; disable it, expect CLS back near 0. Two runs on an unchanged page must agree within 0.005.
findings.correction: Same method; use web-vitals v6.x (6.2.3 today) via `https://unpkg.com/web-vitals@6/dist/web-vitals.attribution.iife.js`, and note the two web.dev pages differ in age (debug guide 2025-02-07, CLS definition 2023-04-12). Risk none.

findings.claim: Lighthouse must be run 5 times sequentially per URL and judged by the median run (FCP+TTI-closest), with the before/after 5-run ranges compared; a regression is declared only when the after-median score is at least 3 points lower and the ranges do not overlap, or when a metric median moves beyond its own threshold (LCP +200 ms, TBT +100 ms, CLS +0.02).
findings.detail: Lighthouse's variability doc: 'The median Lighthouse score of 5 runs is twice as stable as 1 run'; 'DO NOT' run multiple Lighthouse reports at the same time on one machine; use at least 2 dedicated cores (4 recommended) and 2 GB RAM, never burstable/shared-core instances; simulated throttling mitigates the most variability; isolate from third parties and random animations. `lhci collect -n 5` marks the median run with `isRepresentativeRun`; `computeMedianRun` (core/lib/median-run.js) picks the run with the smallest (medianFCP-FCP)^2 + (medianTTI-TTI)^2. Lighthouse CI assertions support `aggregationMethod: 'median-run' | 'median' | 'optimistic' | 'pessimistic'` with `minScore`, `maxNumericValue`, `maxLength`. Performance score weights: TBT 30 percent, LCP 25, CLS 25, FCP 10, SI 10, so TBT noise dominates score noise. Throttling doc: mobile preset is 150 ms RTT, 1.6 Mbps down, 750 Kbps up, 4x CPU; `benchmarkIndex` ranges (Chrome m86): high-end desktop 1500-2000, low-end desktop 1000-1500; calibrate with `--throttling.cpuSlowdownMultiplier=<n>` when outside range. The plugin's lighthouse.sh already flags TBT as unreliable when benchmarkIndex < 1000 (observed 1181-2065 on these runs, one at 142 s TBT on limnoupolis.gr, clearly a machine artefact). Current Lighthouse is v13.5.0 (18 Sep 2026, needs Node 22+); the plugin pins 12.x because 13 renamed/removed audits the jq reads.
findings.breaks_when: Runs are done concurrently or on a shared-core VM (benchmarkIndex drifts between before and after, so TBT and score shift with no site change); the 'after' run hits a cold cache or a different edge node (always warm with one plain GET first); a single run is compared to a single run (5-10 point swings are normal on CI runners per practitioners, and Lighthouse itself gives no variance number).
findings.how_to_apply: `npm i -g @lhci/cli@0.15.x` then `lhci collect --url=<url> -n 5 --settings.preset=perf --settings.formFactor=mobile --settings.onlyCategories=performance` (or keep lighthouse.sh and loop 5 times, writing `benchmarkIndex` each run); pick the median with `computeMedianRun` from `lighthouse/core/lib/median-run.js` or LHCI's `isRepresentativeRun`; store {score, lcp, cls, tbt, fcp, si, benchmarkIndex} for all 5 runs in the ledger. Gate: `regression = afterMedian.score <= beforeMedian.score - 3 && max(after.scores) < min(before.scores)` OR `afterMedian.lcp > beforeMedian.lcp + 200` OR `afterMedian.cls > beforeMedian.cls + 0.02` OR (`benchmarkIndex` within 20 percent of before AND `afterMedian.tbt > beforeMedian.tbt + 100`). Also abort the comparison and re-run if `|benchmarkIndex_after - benchmarkIndex_before| > 30 percent`. Optional `lhci assert` config: `assertions: { 'categories:performance': ['error', {minScore: 0.9, aggregationMethod: 'median-run'}], 'cumulative-layout-shift': ['error', {maxNumericValue: 0.1}], 'largest-contentful-paint': ['error', {maxNumericValue: 2500}] }`.
findings.how_to_verify: Run the 5-run block twice on an unchanged URL: the two medians must be within 2 points and the metric medians within the thresholds above (this calibrates the noise floor per site; widen thresholds only if the no-change test fails). Spot-check that `benchmarkIndex` is stable and >= 1000 on the runner.
findings.correction: Pass `-n 5` and `aggregationMethod: 'median-run'` explicitly (LHCI defaults are 3 runs and 'optimistic'); install `@lhci/cli@0.15.1`; Lighthouse 13.5.0 needs Node 22.19+ and is what PSI runs today, so compare scores across 12 vs 13 but never audit lists. Risk none.

findings.claim: Check that the Elementor editor still loads by opening `post.php?post=<ID>&action=elementor` with an admin storageState and asserting `body.elementor-editor-active`, the disappearance of `#elementor-panel-state-loading` and zero page errors; if it fails, Safe Mode isolates plugin/theme causes.
findings.detail: Elementor core builds the edit URL in `Document::get_edit_url()` with `add_query_arg(['post' => main_id, 'action' => 'elementor'], admin_url('post.php'))`. The editor wrapper template sets body classes `elementor-editor-active` (always) and `elementor-editor-content-only` (users without the `design` capability); the panel template has `id="elementor-panel-state-loading"` (spinner `eicon-loading eicon-animation-spin`), `elementor-panel-header-wrapper`, `elementor-panel-content-wrapper`, `elementor-panel-footer`, `elementor-mode-switcher`. Elementor's help centre describes the two failure modes to assert against: 'A gray page with endless loading' and 'The widget panel is grayed out or loading endlessly'. Safe Mode (Elementor > Tools, admin only, 'loads the editor without third-party plugins, theme code, or experimental features', 'Public visitors continue seeing your standard live site') is the documented next step, and 'Clear Files & Data' under Elementor > Tools (CLI: `wp elementor flush-css --regenerate`) fixes stale CSS after optimisation changes. Optimisers are a classic cause: delay/defer/minify JS applied to logged-in admins or to admin-ajax breaks the editor, which is why Perfmatters has 'disable for logged in users' and FlyingPress caches logged-in users without optimisations.
findings.breaks_when: The harness logs in on production with a real admin account (create a dedicated editor-role test user limited to one hidden test page, and never store its password in the repo); the editor takes longer than the default 30 s on slow hosts (use a 90 s timeout and treat >60 s as a warning, not a failure); Safe Mode is left enabled after debugging (it disables experiments for the admin).
findings.how_to_apply: Playwright setup project logs in via `/wp-login.php` and saves `playwright/.auth/editor.json`; test: `await page.goto('/wp-admin/post.php?post=' + TEST_PAGE_ID + '&action=elementor'); await expect(page.locator('body')).toHaveClass(/elementor-editor-active/); await expect(page.locator('#elementor-panel-state-loading')).toBeHidden({ timeout: 90000 }); await expect(page.locator('#elementor-panel-content-wrapper')).toBeVisible(); expect(await page.pageErrors()).toEqual([])`. Also assert `await page.frameLocator('iframe').locator('.elementor').first()` is visible within 90 s (preview iframe renders the document). On failure: enable Safe Mode via Tools, retry; if Safe Mode passes, the last optimisation step is the cause → undo it.
findings.how_to_verify: Green on the untouched site; then on staging enable Perfmatters Delay JS for logged-in users (or LiteSpeed 'Optimize for Guests Only' off + JS defer) and confirm the test turns red with the spinner still visible; revert and confirm green.
findings.correction: Use `#elementor-preview-iframe` for the preview assertion; Safe Mode lives at Elementor > Editor > Tools in 4.x and only isolates the canvas, not the widget panel, so treat 'still broken in Safe Mode' as inconclusive for panel failures and fall back to the optimiser off-switches (finding 11) for attribution. Risk low.

findings.claim: Verify tracking after each change by recording network requests with consent accepted: GTM container load (`googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=GTM-…`), GA4 hits to `google-analytics.com/g/collect` or `analytics.google.com/g/collect` returning 200 or 204, Meta pixel hits to `facebook.com/tr`, and the `gtm.js` event in `window.dataLayer`; compare the set and count of tag hosts with the baseline, after an interaction because delayed JS only runs on user input.
findings.detail: Google's GA4 troubleshooting page (updated 2026-10-14) says to look for requests to 'google-analytics.com/g/collect or analytics.google.com/g/collect' on each page load and for events, and that 'A 200 OK or 204 No Content status code' means success; DebugView shows events within seconds when `gtag('config','G-XXXXXX',{'debug_mode':true})` is set. The GTM snippet pushes `{'gtm.start': Date.now(), event:'gtm.js'}` to `window.dataLayer` and loads `https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=` + containerId, so `dataLayer.some(e => e.event === 'gtm.js')` proves the container booted. A firing Meta pixel 'sends network requests to facebook.com/tr'; after acceptance a consent-wired tag may stay silent, and `fbq.getState().pixels` in the console reveals duplicate inits (practitioner source). On the audited pages: gtm.js on limnoupolis, onar, pallada (2 containers on pallada), `fbq(` inline on limnoupolis, G- IDs on cretaforums (4), onar (2), voreniahorizon (4). The audit found 5 GTM tags per page on slow sites; the point of this gate is that debloating tags (delay, merge containers) must not silently drop a conversion pixel.
findings.breaks_when: The harness runs with consent denied (nothing fires by design; that is the separate consent-gating assertion); delay-JS waits for a user gesture so a load-only capture reports false 'missing' tags; ad-blocking DNS on the runner blocks facebook.com; the GA4 hit is batched and sent via `sendBeacon` on unload (wait 5 s and trigger one scroll + click before reading).
findings.how_to_apply: Tracking project (no route blocking, consent-accepted storageState): collect `page.on('request')` URLs; after load do `page.mouse.wheel(0,600)`, `page.mouse.click(10,10)`, wait 5 s; assert `requests.some(u => /googletagmanager\.com\/gtm\.js\?id=GTM-/.test(u))`, `responses.some(r => /\/g\/collect/.test(r.url()) && [200,204].includes(r.status()))`, `requests.filter(u => /facebook\.com\/tr/.test(u)).length >= 1`, and `await page.evaluate(() => window.dataLayer?.some(e => e.event === 'gtm.js'))`. Store the set of third-party hosts and per-host counts per page; gate = every host in the baseline set is still present (counts may drop when duplicates are removed deliberately, which the human approves in the ledger). Add one event test per site (e.g. click 'Book now' and expect a `g/collect` with `en=` parameter present).
findings.how_to_verify: Baseline run on the unchanged site shows all configured IDs; then in GA4 DebugView (debug_mode) see the test session's page_view; after a tag-delay change the same assertions pass only after the scripted interaction, and fail if the pixel was dropped.

findings.claim: When a gate fails, re-run the same failing check through the vendor's documented off-switch URL to attribute the breakage to the optimiser in one step, without rolling back: Perfmatters `?perfmattersoff` / `?perfmattersjsoff` / `?perfmatterscssoff`, LiteSpeed `?LSCWP_CTRL=before_optm` / `?LSCWP_CTRL=NOCACHE`, and for staged roll-outs Perfmatters Testing Mode or LiteSpeed 'Disable All Features'.
findings.detail: Perfmatters docs: append `?perfmattersoff` to turn Perfmatters off for that request; `?perfmattersjsoff` disables Delay JS, Defer JS and Minify JS; `?perfmatterscssoff` disables Unused CSS and Minify CSS. Script Manager 'Testing Mode' (Script Manager > Settings) restricts the configuration to logged-in admins: 'Only logged-in admins will see changes made in Testing Mode. The configuration won't be applied to your public site until you return and toggle Testing Mode back off', and Perfmatters recommends staging first because the Script Manager 'could break your site's appearance'. LiteSpeed Toolbox > Debug: 'View Site Before Optimization' opens the site with `?LSCWP_CTRL=before_optm` ('effectively turns off all optimizations for this one viewing'), 'View Site Before Cache' uses `?LSCWP_CTRL=NOCACHE`, and 'Disable All Features' (plus a 24-hour variant) switches off caching and optimisation site-wide; these are Admin IP Commands, so the request must come from an IP listed in 'Admin IPs' or from a logged-in admin. FlyingPress is reported to honour `?no_optimize` (its docs search returned no article today; verify on the site). Harness logic: if check(url) fails and check(url + offswitch) passes, the optimiser setting changed in this step is the cause; undo only that setting.
findings.breaks_when: The off-switch request is served from the page cache (LiteSpeed/W3TC ignore unknown query strings unless configured; use NOCACHE first or purge), the runner's IP is not in LiteSpeed Admin IPs so `LSCWP_CTRL` is ignored, or Testing Mode is forgotten and the public site never receives the change (add a ledger reminder and a final 'public parity' screenshot comparing logged-out vs admin view).
findings.how_to_apply: In the harness config per site: `offSwitches: { perfmatters: ['?perfmattersoff','?perfmattersjsoff','?perfmatterscssoff'], litespeed: ['?LSCWP_CTRL=before_optm','?LSCWP_CTRL=NOCACHE'], flyingpress: ['?no_optimize'] }`. On failure: for each switch, re-run only the failed gate (console/smoke/visual) with the suffix appended and report a table 'fails normally / passes with X off'. For Script Manager edits use Testing Mode: apply, run the smoke + console gates with the admin storageState, then toggle off and run them again logged out.
findings.how_to_verify: Confirm the switch works on the site before relying on it: with `?perfmattersjsoff` the HTML must no longer contain `pmdelayedscript` attributes; with `?LSCWP_CTRL=before_optm` the HTML must not contain `/wp-content/litespeed/` combined asset URLs, and with NOCACHE the `x-litespeed-cache` response header must be absent or 'miss'.
findings.correction: `?LSCWP_CTRL=before_optm` works from any IP without login; `?LSCWP_CTRL=NOCACHE` (and PURGE/SHOWHEADERS) work only from an IP listed in Toolbox > Debug Settings > Admin IPs, logged in or not. Drop `?no_optimize` from the FlyingPress off-switch list until verified on a site; verify FlyingPress state via the `X-Flying-Press-Cache` header instead. Risk none.

findings.claim: Choose a fixed, small page set and viewport set per site and baseline it before the first change: home, one room/product/booking page, cart or booking step, one blog/forum page, contact, and one page per language, at 390x844 (iPhone 13 descriptor) and 1366x768, both above-the-fold and full-page.
findings.detail: Playwright device descriptors (`devices['iPhone 13']`, `devices['Desktop Chrome']`) set viewport, userAgent, deviceScaleFactor, isMobile and hasTouch consistently; `isMobile` must be set after spreading a device. Above-the-fold shots judge LCP-area changes (hero, fonts, icons) strictly; full-page shots catch footer/widget breakage with a looser ratio. The audited sites have 10-295 Elementor documents each (marakaki.com 295, onar 88, limnoupolis 60), so screenshotting everything per step is too slow; the plugin should pick the page types above plus any page whose template was touched by the change (e.g. a WooCommerce page when unloading WooCommerce CSS on non-shop pages). Baselines are re-taken after each approved step (`--update-snapshots` only after human approval in the ledger), so each diff is incremental and the human reviews one change at a time.
findings.breaks_when: The set omits the page where the change bites (e.g. unloading a slider plugin's CSS site-wide while only screenshotting the home page); baselines are updated automatically on failure (then the harness proves nothing); device scale factor differs between baseline and comparison runs.
findings.how_to_apply: `pages.json` per site: `[{slug:'home',url:'/'},{slug:'room',url:'/rooms/x/'},{slug:'book',url:'/book/'},{slug:'post',url:'/blog/y/'},{slug:'contact',url:'/contact/'},{slug:'home-en',url:'/en/'}]`; `playwright.config.ts` projects `mobile` and `desktop` as in finding 2; test iterates pages × {fold, full}; snapshot path template includes site, slug, viewport and step. Approval flow: harness exits non-zero with the diff images; the human (or the agent with the user's OK) runs `npx playwright test --update-snapshots -g <slug>` and records 'approved visual change: <reason>' in the ledger.
findings.how_to_verify: Before the first change: two consecutive runs of the whole matrix pass with zero diffs (if not, add masks/stylePath rules until they do); count the run time (target under 3 minutes per site so it can run after every step).

findings.claim: Lighthouse alone cannot see post-consent or post-interaction states (tags, popups, delayed JS); use Lighthouse user flows (Puppeteer only) or `--extra-headers`/`--disable-storage-reset` for a consented run, otherwise accept that the Lighthouse gate measures the pre-consent page and rely on the Playwright gates for everything after a click.
findings.detail: Lighthouse user-flows doc: 'Analyzing a multi-step user flow is currently only available using the Lighthouse Node API along with Puppeteer' — `startFlow(page)`, `flow.navigate(url)`, `flow.startTimespan()/endTimespan()` ('layout shifts and JavaScript execution time over a timerange including interactions', no overall score, no LCP), `flow.snapshot()`, `generateReport()`. Playwright is not supported for flows. The CLI offers `--extra-headers` ('Set extra HTTP Headers to pass with request', usable for a Cookie header carrying the consent cookie) and `--disable-storage-reset` ('Disable clearing the browser cache and other storage APIs before a run'), plus `--throttling-method=devtools|provided|simulate`, `--preset=perf|desktop`, `--form-factor`, `--only-categories=performance`, `--output=json --output-path`, `--chrome-flags`, `--max-wait-for-load`, `--save-assets`. Because delayed JS executes only after a gesture, a default Lighthouse run of a delay-JS site measures a page where GTM/pixels have not run; PageSpeed Insights behaves the same, which is why the score improves, and why the harness must separately prove the tags still fire (finding 10) and that interactions still work (finding 6).
findings.breaks_when: The team reads a consented Lighthouse run as 'the PageSpeed score' (PSI never has consent, so numbers will not match), or a consent cookie passed via `--extra-headers` is also sent to third-party hosts (Lighthouse applies extra headers to every request; use only for lab diagnosis, never with real credentials).
findings.how_to_apply: Default gate: plain Lighthouse mobile, no consent (matches PSI). Optional diagnostic: `lighthouse <url> --extra-headers '{"Cookie":"cmplz_banner-status=dismissed; ..."}' --only-categories=performance --form-factor=mobile --output=json` to quantify the cost of consented tags; for interaction cost use a small Puppeteer flow script (`import {startFlow} from 'lighthouse'`): navigate, `startTimespan`, click the menu/popup trigger, `endTimespan`, save `createFlowResult()` JSON and compare TBT-equivalent 'total blocking time' and CLS in the timespan before/after a step.
findings.how_to_verify: Consented run shows the extra `g/collect`/`facebook.com/tr` requests in `network-requests`; the unconsented run does not; both runs' medians are tracked separately in the ledger and never mixed.

findings.claim: Keep measurement and change on separate, controlled machines/contexts: screenshots, console and CLS from Playwright with third parties blocked where appropriate; Lighthouse sequential on a quiet runner with benchmarkIndex logged; never from the production server itself; and run the whole chain on staging first where it exists (staging.limnoupolis.gr) since LiteSpeed/W3TC imports are environment-specific.
findings.detail: Lighthouse variability doc: 'running on inconsistent hardware will lead to inconsistent results'; avoid 'other software on the machine' and browser extensions; scale horizontally, not concurrently. Playwright's network doc: `browserContext.route()` applies to all pages of the context; disable service workers (`serviceWorkers: 'block'`) if network events appear missing. W3TC's `option set` note ('do not update your .htaccess file automatically') and LiteSpeed's import notes mean a settings file exported from staging cannot be blindly imported on production; the harness should diff `wp litespeed-option export` outputs between staging and production before promoting a change, and apply only the keys that changed in the approved step. The audit shows staging.limnoupolis.gr running Elementor 4.3.4 vs 4.3.5 on production and 37 vs 30 plugins, so a passing staging run is evidence, not proof; the production run of the gates is still required (read-only measurement plus reversible options only, per the plugin's rules).
findings.breaks_when: Staging differs in plugin set or Elementor version (as observed) so a selector or experiment behaves differently; the runner shares CPU with the Playwright suite while Lighthouse runs (run them in sequence, Playwright first); the production run is skipped because staging passed.
findings.how_to_apply: Harness order per step: (1) record before-values; (2) apply on staging; (3) run gates on staging; (4) on green, apply the same recorded key set on production; (5) run gates on production with Lighthouse last and alone; (6) keep or undo. Enforce sequential execution with a lock file; log `os.cpus().length`, load average and `benchmarkIndex` into the ledger for every Lighthouse batch.
findings.how_to_verify: Ledger shows for every kept step: staging green, production green, benchmarkIndex within 20 percent of the before-run, and identical key diffs applied on both environments (`diff <(sort before.txt) <(sort after.txt)` on the LiteSpeed exports lists exactly the intended keys).

findings.claim: Some checks cannot be automated and must be routed to a human step in the plugin: deciding whether a flagged visual difference is acceptable, confirming email delivery of form notifications, completing a real booking or payment, judging animation quality, legal correctness of consent behaviour, and confirming improvement in CrUX field data.
findings.detail: Pixel diffs and CLS attribution tell you what moved, not whether the client will accept it (e.g. a replaced hero video poster, a different font fallback for Greek glyphs); the harness should present the diff image, the `sources` nodes and the before/after metric table and wait for an explicit OK. Form actions that send email cannot be asserted end to end without mailbox access; the webhook-to-test-endpoint pattern (finding 6) proves the submission pipeline, not SMTP delivery. Live bookings (YITH, WooCommerce Bookings) and payments must not be created on production; the calendar-opens check and Store API add-to-cart/empty-cart are the automatable boundary. Lighthouse's own variability doc stresses lab results are a proxy; CrUX aggregates real-user experiences 'into page-level and origin-level distributions' and only for sufficiently popular pages, so field confirmation of a change arrives with delay and may never exist for low-traffic hotel sites. Also not automatable: whether a removed animation or script was wanted by the client (business intent), and reduced-motion emulation deliberately hides animation behaviour.
findings.breaks_when: The plugin treats a passing harness as permission to skip the human review of visual diffs, or declares success on lab numbers alone for a site whose CrUX shows a different story (e.g. a 3D hero that scores fine in the lab on a fast runner but not on real phones).
findings.how_to_apply: In the agent workflow, after each red visual gate: stop, show `-diff.png`, `-actual.png`, `-expected.png` paths and the metric table, and ask 'approve visual change / undo'. Maintain a per-site checklist of manual items (send one real form submission and confirm the email, check Greek text rendering on a physical phone, open the booking flow to the payment page on staging) that the agent prints at the end of a debloat session. Record CrUX/PSI field data at the start and re-check it later as a separate scheduled task, not as a gate.
findings.how_to_verify: The ledger contains an explicit human decision for every approved visual change and a dated manual-checklist sign-off per site; no step is marked 'kept' with a red visual gate and no decision.

findings.claim: The plugin's lighthouse.sh reads four audit ids that Lighthouse 13 (shipping in PageSpeed Insights since October 2025) no longer emits, so a 13.x run silently yields empty dom/img/third-party/lcp-lazy fields; port the jq to the insight ids before un-pinning from 12.x.
findings.detail: Lighthouse 13.0.0 (2025-10-10) 'remove audits replaced by performance insights' and PSI got it 'within a week'; 13.5.0 is dated 2026-09-17 and needs Node >=22.19. The Chrome blog table maps the removed ids: dom-size → dom-size-insight (13.0 'add numericValue'), uses-optimized-images / modern-image-formats / uses-responsive-images / efficient-animated-content → image-delivery-insight, third-party-summary → third-parties-insight, largest-contentful-paint-element → lcp-phases-insight, prioritize-lcp-image / lcp-lazy-loaded → lcp-discovery-insight, render-blocking-resources → render-blocking-insight, font-display → font-display-insight, layout-shifts → cls-culprits-insight, uses-rel-preconnect / critical-request-chains → network-dependency-tree-insight. Removed outright: offscreen-images, preload-fonts, third-party-facades, font-size, no-document-write, uses-passive-event-listeners, first-meaningful-paint. Still present and read correctly by the script: first-contentful-paint, largest-contentful-paint, cumulative-layout-shift, total-blocking-time, total-byte-weight, network-requests, unused-javascript, unused-css-rules. The blog states 'There are no changes to the performance scoring in this version', so 12.x and 13.x scores are comparable; the script's header comment wrongly lists render-blocking-resources and font-display (not read) and omits dom-size and uses-optimized-images (read).
findings.breaks_when: The harness compares a 12.x 'before' with a 13.x 'after' (or PSI) on diagnostics instead of metrics, or the runner's Node is below 22.19 so `npx lighthouse@13` fails and the loop records 'lighthouse failed' for every URL.
findings.how_to_apply: In lighthouse.sh replace `.audits["dom-size"].numericValue` with `(.audits["dom-size-insight"].numericValue // .audits["dom-size"].numericValue)`, read image savings from `image-delivery-insight` (`.details.overallSavingsBytes` or sum of items' wastedBytes), third-party transfer from `third-parties-insight`, and the lazy-LCP flag from `lcp-discovery-insight` items; fix the header comment; pin `lighthouse@13.5.0` with `node >= 22.19` or stay on 12.8.2 for all baselines of one engagement and never mix.
findings.how_to_verify: Run both versions on one URL and diff the keys: `jq '.audits|keys' lh12.json lh13.json`; the ported jq must return non-null for every field on the 13.x file, and the performance score on the two files must agree within normal run noise.

findings.claim: LiteSpeed Guest Mode / Guest Optimization makes every fresh Playwright context and every Lighthouse/PSI run measure a different page than returning visitors see, so the harness must record the Guest Mode state in the ledger and run the gates twice (first visit and second visit) on LiteSpeed sites.
findings.detail: LiteSpeed General docs: 'When Guest Mode is enabled, LSCache serves a default version of the page from cache for a visitor's first request... no cache varies are considered. Once the HTML of the page is loaded, an AJAX call is used to load the "correct" version'. Guest Optimization 'defaults to ON, but it requires Guest Mode' and applies 'the maximum level of page optimization and image optimization... even if those features are disabled otherwise... for bots, certain user agents, and a user's first visit... it will always serve a cached, highly optimized page when services like GTmetrix and PageSpeed Insights request it.' Warning in the same doc: 'There is a short delay between the default cached page being served and the correct content loading via AJAX. On some complicated sites, this can mean that the wrong language, incorrect pricing, or other problematic content may be momentarily displayed.' For the Greek/English WPML/Polylang sites this is a direct source of screenshot flakes and of 'optimisations off but PSI still high' confusion.
findings.breaks_when: Guest Mode is on and the harness treats a first-visit (guest-optimised) Lighthouse score as the effect of a setting that is actually off; or a full-page screenshot is taken before the AJAX swap and shows the wrong language; or Guest Mode is toggled mid-engagement so 'before' and 'after' are different page variants.
findings.how_to_apply: Snapshot the Guest Mode and Guest Optimization values with `wp litespeed-option export` before step 0 and refuse to compare runs whose values differ. In Playwright, for LiteSpeed sites run every page twice in the same context (`goto` → wait networkidle → `goto` again) and gate on the second load; keep one explicit 'first visit' project for the Lighthouse-equivalent view. Assert `html[lang]` after the AJAX swap on multilingual pages.
findings.how_to_verify: With Guest Mode on, the first response of a fresh context and the second differ (compare `x-litespeed-cache` and the HTML hash); with Guest Mode off they match. Lighthouse medians with Guest Optimization on vs off on an otherwise unchanged site quantify how much of the score is the guest page.

findings.claim: Perfmatters exposes its risky toggles as WP-CLI commands, so the harness can apply, attribute and undo a single Perfmatters feature per step without the UI or a full settings import.
findings.detail: perfmatters.io/docs/wp-cli (current): `wp perfmatters enable <option>` / `wp perfmatters disable <option>` with the supported list from `wp perfmatters get-options`: delay-js, defer-js, minify-js, remove-unused-css, minify-css, lazyload-images, lazyload-iframes, css-background-images, lazyload-elements, local-google-fonts, cdn-rewrite, script-manager, clean-uninstall; plus `wp perfmatters clear-used-css [--url|--network]`, clear minified JS/CSS, clear local Google Fonts, `wp perfmatters import-settings <file>`, and licence commands. This is the one-key-per-step primitive the ledger finding asks for; a JSON import restores everything at once and would mask which key mattered.
findings.breaks_when: The step toggles an option that is not in the list (e.g. individual Script Manager rules, which the export also excludes and which are tied to post IDs) — those still need the UI and Testing Mode.
findings.how_to_apply: Step = `wp perfmatters enable delay-js` → purge page cache → gates; undo = `wp perfmatters disable delay-js` → `wp perfmatters clear-used-css` when Remove Unused CSS was involved → purge → gates. Record `wp option get perfmatters_options --format=json` before and after as the authoritative diff.
findings.how_to_verify: `wp perfmatters get-options` lists the key; after enable the HTML contains `pmdelayedscript`, after disable it does not, and `?perfmattersjsoff` on the enabled page also removes it (confirms attribution path).

findings.claim: FlyingPress has no documented settings export, option CLI or per-URL off switch; its automatable surface is `wp flying-press purge-everything|purge-pages|preload-cache` and the `X-Flying-Press-Cache: HIT|MISS` header, so FlyingPress sites need `wp option get` snapshots and a header check before every measurement.
findings.detail: docs.flyingpress.com 'FlyingPress WP-CLI Commands' (May 20, 2025) lists only preload-cache, purge-pages, purge-everything and activate-license, 'non-blocking and safe to run repeatedly'. 'How to check if FlyingPress is working' documents `X-Flying-Press-Cache: HIT` ('MISS = not cached yet'), `flying-press` tags in the page source and the `wp-content/cache/flying-press/` folder. The Configuration collection has articles for 'Cache for logged-in users by role', 'Exclude pages from cache' and 'Bypass cache for cookies' but none for import/export. The `?no_optimize` parameter cited in search snippets points to an article URL that returns 404 today, so it is unverified.
findings.breaks_when: The harness measures a FlyingPress page while `X-Flying-Press-Cache: MISS` (uncached 'after' vs cached 'before'), or tries to undo a FlyingPress change by importing a file that does not exist.
findings.how_to_apply: Before/after each FlyingPress step: `wp option get` the FlyingPress options row (name to be confirmed with `wp option list --search='flying*'`), `wp flying-press purge-everything`, one warming GET, then assert the header is HIT in Playwright (`response.headers()['x-flying-press-cache']`) before screenshots and before Lighthouse. Undo = `wp option update` of the recorded JSON.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -sI the URL twice: second response carries `X-Flying-Press-Cache: HIT`; the ledger shows identical header state for before and after runs.

findings.claim: Elementor's Element Cache is post meta `_elementor_element_cache` controlled by option `elementor_element_cache_ttl` ('disable' turns it off); `wp elementor flush-css` deletes that meta for all posts, so a flush is the correct 'reset' between steps but it also means a form-nonce or filter staleness bug only reappears after the cache re-warms (TTL hours later).
findings.detail: Elementor 4.4.0 main: core/base/document.php `CACHE_META_KEY = '_elementor_element_cache'`, `'disable' !== get_option('elementor_element_cache_ttl', '')` decides activity and `get_option('elementor_element_cache_ttl')` is the expiration in hours; core/files/manager.php `clear_cache()` deletes the CSS files, `delete_post_meta_by_key(Post_CSS::META_KEY)`, `delete_post_meta_by_key(Document_Base::CACHE_META_KEY)` and the assets meta, and is also hooked to `update_option_elementor_element_cache_ttl`; modules/wp-cli/command.php `flush-css [--regenerate]` calls exactly that `clear_cache()` then optionally `generate_css()`. Interaction tests run right after a flush therefore test uncached widgets; the stale-cache case needs a second pass after the cache has been populated by a prior visit.
findings.breaks_when: The harness only ever runs its interaction gate immediately after `wp elementor flush-css`, so a cached form widget whose nonce expired (the known Element Cache failure mode) is never exercised.
findings.how_to_apply: For each page in the smoke set: load once (populates `_elementor_element_cache`), then run the form/filter interaction on the cached second load; record `wp option get elementor_element_cache_ttl` in the ledger with the other Elementor options; when a step changes that TTL note that Elementor itself flushes everything (hook on `update_option_elementor_element_cache_ttl`).
findings.how_to_verify: `wp post meta get <id> _elementor_element_cache` is empty right after `wp elementor flush-css` and non-empty after one front-end GET of that page; the interaction gate passes on both states.

title: Building lean Elementor sites from Figma / Adobe XD / references
summary: For a new site in late 2026 the lean path is Elementor Editor V4 ("Atomic"): Elementor 4.0 went live on 15 Apr 2026, new installs default to Atomic Elements, Variables, Classes and Components, and Elementor's own FAQ says atomic markup renders "without additional wrapper layers". None of the four agency sites checked read-only today has `e_atomic_elements` on, so the plugin must first flip WP Admin → Elementor → Editor → Settings → Atomic Editor before any V4 build. Design tokens map cleanly: Figma colour/type/size tokens become V4 Variables (color, font, size), components become Global Classes, tag baselines go into Design System → Defaults, and the whole set exports as a ZIP (Design System panel → ⋯ → Export) or as part of a kit, so one agency "blueprint" can seed every site. Figma access is the bottleneck: the Variables REST API is Enterprise-only, the Figma MCP is capped at 20 calls/month on Starter/View seats and 200/day on Pro Dev/Full seats, and the connector in this environment is not authenticated; the plain Files/Nodes/Styles/Images REST endpoints work with a personal access token on any plan. Converters (UiChemy 5.3.0 is the only maintained one with a V4-classes mode) are fine for structure and tokens but must be audited for inline styles, extra fonts, jsDelivr libraries and nested depth; Adobe XD is in maintenance mode with no official migration, but `.xd` is a ZIP of JSON that can be parsed for colours, text styles and artboards. Pages can be created programmatically through the documented `_elementor_data` JSON (version 0.4 wrapper; atomic elements `e-div-block`/`e-flexbox`/`e-grid`, widgets `e-heading`/`e-paragraph`/`e-button` with `{$$type,value}` settings) via `wp elementor library import`, `wp elementor kit import`, Novamira `elementor-set-content` or the official Elementor MCP (4.3.0+). To reach 95–100 on mobile, the per-page targets derived from Lighthouse's published curves are roughly LCP ≤ 1.55 s, TBT ≤ 65 ms, CLS ≤ 0.04, FCP ≤ 1.1 s, SI ≤ 2.0 s and a body DOM under 800 nodes; the plugin's current "≥85, LCP ≤2.5 s" checklist is far too lax. The local skills on this machine (adobe-xd, kallyas-to-elementor, extract-design-system, design-taste-frontend, image-to-code, design-handoff) cover migration parity and web-app aesthetics but none covers V4 tokens, Elementor JSON generation or image export rules.
critic_notes: Method: WebFetch could not resolve DNS in this session, so every source was opened with curl through the configured proxy and the article bodies extracted locally (texts saved under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/critic-build/). Elementor source was read from a sparse git checkout of elementor/elementor main (modules/atomic-widgets, image-loading-optimization, lazyload, includes/settings) in the same scratch folder. Lighthouse curve values were recomputed numerically and match the researcher's table exactly. Not checked: Snapelement/Tidweb/Hedrick/Figmentor numbers, Adobe XD sources, Google Fonts CSS Greek ranges, the Novamira check-setup output (trusted as local evidence), and whether UiChemy's 'Elementor V4 Atomic' export really produces Global Classes (still an open question). Biggest things the researcher missed: atomic e-image has no `sizes` attribute; Div Block has the same 10 px base padding as Flexbox; Lighthouse 13 removed the 800/1,400 DOM-node thresholds; Elementor's own 'Lazy Load Background Images' and 'Load Google Fonts Locally' settings; V4 animations live in `interactions[]`. No website or WordPress setting was modified.

findings.claim: Build every new site on Editor V4 atomic elements with Variables as the token layer and Global Classes as the component layer; on the agency's sites this is currently impossible because `e_atomic_elements` is off everywhere checked.
findings.detail: Elementor 4.0 announcement (15 Apr 2026): new installs start with Atomic Elements, Variables, Classes and Components enabled; existing sites must enable manually; 'each element uses just a single DIV wrapper'. V4 FAQ: 'When starting a new site, you should ideally begin with v4 Elements, build a design system using Classes and Variables, and add v3 Widgets where needed'; 'Classes and Variables are native to Atomic Elements' and do NOT apply to v3 widgets; Grid is available (free) and Atomic Loop (Pro) has its own help page as of 4.3.x. Variables are limited to font family, text colour and size (size = Pro). Read-only `novamira/elementor-check-setup` today on kand.dev6, platonos.dev6, voreniahorizon.gr and fagitiotiszois.dev6 (Elementor 4.3.3–4.3.4, Pro 4.3.1) returned `atomic.runtime_available:false` with the issue 'the `e_atomic_elements` experiment is OFF, so no `e-*` element type is registered'. Independent magnitude: Snapelement (vendor) measured CSS 342 KB→47 KB and DOM 1,847→612 nodes on the same V3→V4 homepage; Tidweb (agency) reports 15–20% fewer DOM nodes and notes DOM is rarely the main problem versus images, caching, fonts and plugin duplication.
findings.breaks_when: Custom kit/child-theme CSS written against v3 wrapper classes does not style atomic elements; third-party add-on widgets (Premium Addons, Dynamic.ooo, JetSmartFilters) stay v3 and cannot take Classes/Variables, so a page mixing both gets smaller gains and two styling systems to maintain; Elementor itself says 'a few atomic pieces are still rolling out'.
findings.how_to_apply: WP Admin → Elementor → Editor → Settings → Atomic Editor → 'Activate the new experience' (or Elementor → Settings → Features → 'Atomic Widgets' + 'Editor V4' on 4.2.x). Then in the editor: Top Bar ⋯ → Design System → Variables tab → Create a variable (Color / Font / Size); Style tab → Class field → 'Create a new class' or 'Convert to global class'; Design System → Defaults tab → set h1–h6, p, a, button, div baselines. Re-run `novamira/elementor-check-setup` and require `atomic.runtime_available:true` before the builder agent writes any `e-*` element.
findings.how_to_verify: check-setup JSON shows `atomic.runtime_available`, `global_classes_available`, `variables_available` all true; view-source of a built page shows `<div class="e-div-block …">` wrappers with no `.elementor-widget-container` inner wrappers; Lighthouse mobile 'Optimize DOM size' insight reports body nodes < 800 and max depth lower than the current 6–9 levels in audit-summary.json; compare transferred CSS bytes in DevTools Network before/after on one rebuilt page.

findings.claim: Translate the Figma/XD token sheet into one reusable Elementor Design System export (Variables + Classes ZIP) and import it on every new site before the first page is built.
findings.detail: Help centre: Design System panel → ⋯ → Export downloads a ZIP of variables and classes; Import on the target site asks to override or keep on name conflicts; limitation: whole ZIP only, no per-item selection, no prefix merging. Alternative path in Elementor → Editor → Tools → Website Templates → Export: turn off everything except 'Settings & configurations' → Edit → keep only 'Classes' and 'Variables'. Storage (Elementor GitHub main): global classes live on the active kit as post meta `_elementor_global_classes` (`items` + `order`, preview copy `_elementor_global_classes_preview`), served/updated by REST `elementor/v1/global-classes` (GET, PUT; `/usage`, `/styles`, `/post`; MAX_ITEMS 1000); variables live in a kit JSON meta record with `data` + `watermark`. Legacy v3 globals live in the kit's page settings as `system_colors`/`custom_colors` and `system_typography`/`custom_typography` (each item `_id`, `title`, value) and are emitted as CSS custom properties `--e-global-color-{id}` and `--e-global-typography-{id}-font-family|font-size|font-weight|line-height|letter-spacing…`. V4 variables can be synced one-way to v3 globals (Variables Manager → ⋯ → 'Sync to Global Colors' / 'Sync to Global Fonts'; font sync is family only). Novamira exposes `elementor-list-v3-styles`, `elementor-create-v3-color`, `elementor-create-v3-typography` for the v3 side.
findings.breaks_when: Importing with 'override' on a site that already has classes of the same name silently restyles existing pages; typography variables cover family only, so size/weight/line-height still need Classes; PlusAddons warns that hundreds of utility classes ship CSS whether used or not, so keep the set small (brand colours, 1 size scale, ~6–10 component classes).
findings.how_to_apply: 1) From the design file, write a token sheet: colours (semantic names: color-brand-primary, color-surface, color-text), font families (2 max), a size scale (clamp() strings allowed in Size variables). 2) On a clean staging site with Atomic on, create them in Design System → Variables, build classes btn-primary, btn-ghost, card, section-boxed, section-full, heading-display, then Defaults for h1–h6/p/a/button. 3) Design System → ⋯ → Export → keep `agency-base-design-system.zip` in the plugin's references. 4) New site: Design System → ⋯ → Import → choose 'keep' for conflicts; then Variables Manager → sync brand colours and fonts to Global Colors/Fonts so Pro v3 widgets (Nav Menu, Loop Grid, Woo) use the same tokens. 5) Programmatic alternative: `wp elementor kit import kit.zip --include=site-settings`.
findings.how_to_verify: After import, Design System panel lists the variables/classes; `GET /wp-json/elementor/v1/global-classes` (logged in as admin) returns the items; a Heading atomic element's Style tab shows the class in green; a v3 Heading's colour picker shows the synced globals; the rendered page CSS contains the class selectors once (not per element) and `--e-global-color-*` for v3 widgets.

findings.claim: Lighthouse 95–100 on mobile needs per-metric targets far tighter than the plugin's current checklist: roughly LCP ≤ 1.55 s, TBT ≤ 65 ms, CLS ≤ 0.04, FCP ≤ 1.1 s, Speed Index ≤ 2.0 s.
findings.detail: Official weights (Lighthouse 10+, unchanged in 13 per the LH13 post: 'There are no changes to the performance scoring in this version'): FCP 10%, SI 10%, LCP 25%, TBT 30%, CLS 25%. Scores map through a log-normal curve with two control points from Lighthouse source (mobile): LCP p10 2500 ms / median 4000; TBT 200 / 600; CLS 0.1 / 0.25; FCP 1800 / 3000; SI 3387 / 5800. Solving that curve for a 99.5 per-metric score (what rounds to 100) gives LCP ≈ 1,555 ms, TBT ≈ 66 ms, CLS ≈ 0.040, FCP ≈ 1,075 ms, SI ≈ 1,967 ms; for 95: LCP 2,188, TBT 146, CLS 0.077, FCP 1,557, SI 2,908. Chrome's doc: 'taking a score from 99 to 100 needs about the same amount of metric improvement that would take a 90 to 94' and 'top-performing sites render LCP in about 1,220ms, so that metric value is mapped to a score of 99'. The plugin's `references/checklist.md` currently targets score ≥ 85, LCP ≤ 2.5 s, CLS ≤ 0.1 — those are the 90-point thresholds, not 95–100.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break; but lab TBT on the shared runner is inflated (results.jsonl shows benchmark indexes 1181–2065 and a 142 s TBT outlier on limnoupolis.gr), so the plugin must gate on PSI/consistent-CPU runs, not on ad-hoc local Lighthouse.
findings.how_to_apply: Replace the targets in /home/user/everything-claude/plugins/elementor-lean/skills/elementor-build/references/checklist.md and the builder agent with: score ≥ 95, LCP ≤ 1.6 s, TBT ≤ 70 ms, CLS ≤ 0.04, FCP ≤ 1.1 s, SI ≤ 2.0 s, body DOM < 800 nodes, and keep ≤ 60 requests / ≤ 1.5 MB as guard rails. Make `scripts/lighthouse.sh` fail a page when any metric exceeds the 95 line and warn between 95 and 99.5.
findings.how_to_verify: Run Lighthouse 13 mobile (or PSI) three times per page; take the median; check `audits.metrics.details.items[0]` values against the table; a page passing all five 99.5 values must show a 100 score (rounding), otherwise re-check the benchmark index.

findings.claim: Create pages programmatically with Elementor's documented JSON (`_elementor_data`, data version 0.4) so the plugin can lint a page for animations, depth, fonts and image sizes before it is ever saved.
findings.detail: Template wrapper: `{title, type (page|header|footer|error-404|popup|post…), version:'0.4', page_settings:[]|{}, content:[…]}`. Legacy/v3 element: `{id (7–8 hex), elType:'container'|'widget', widgetType, isInner, settings:[]|{}, elements:[]}`. Atomic layout element: `{id, version:'0.0', elType:'e-div-block'|'e-flexbox'|'e-grid', isInner, settings, editor_settings, interactions:[], styles:[]|{}, elements}`; atomic widgets keep `elType:'widget'` with `widgetType:'e-heading'|'e-paragraph'|'e-button'…` and typed settings `{"$$type":"string","value":"h3"}`, text as `html-v3`, links as `link`/`query`. Elementor saves it with `update_metadata('post', ID, '_elementor_data', wp_slash(wp_json_encode($data)))` (core/base/document.php) plus `_elementor_edit_mode`, `_elementor_template_type`, `_elementor_version`. Import routes: `wp elementor library import <file.json|zip> [--returnType=ids|info]`, `wp elementor library import-dir <dir>`, `wp elementor kit import <zip> [--include=content,templates,site-settings] [--overrideConditions=ids] [--sourceType=local|remote|library]`; on the agency sites `novamira/elementor-set-content {post_id, content[], template_type}` validates control ids/enums server-side, auto-wraps atomic scalars into `$$type`, accepts a flat `styles:{css-prop:value}` map that becomes class `s-<id>`, invalidates CSS caches and reads the document back (`elements_written`, `not_persisted`). The official Elementor MCP (Elementor ≥ 4.3.0, WP ≥ 6.8; WP Admin → Elementor → Elementor MCP) does the same from Claude/Codex/Cursor, saves drafts only, and needs Pro 4.3.0 for Forms, Popups, Loops, Components.
findings.breaks_when: Writing `_elementor_data` directly with `json_encode` and without `wp_slash` corrupts escaped characters; writing `e-*` elements on a site where the atomic experiment is off is rejected; omitting `isInner`/`version` or using unknown control ids is silently dropped on v3 trees ('Elementor drops it on save without either of us noticing'); the official MCP and Novamira both act under the connected user's role.
findings.how_to_apply: Builder agent: generate the tree from a section spec, run a local lint (no `_animation`/`motion_fx`, depth ≤ 4, only whitelisted `widgetType`s, every `e-image` with explicit size, no `<script>` in `html`), then write via `novamira/elementor-set-content` with `template_type:'wp-page'` to a draft post, then `novamira/elementor-clear-document-cache`, screenshot at 390 px and run Lighthouse. For bulk/initial setup ship kits as ZIP and import with `wp elementor kit import site.zip --include=site-settings,templates`. Keep the JSON files in the plugin as fixtures (hero, cards, FAQ, footer) with ids as kebab-case slugs so `s-<id>` classes are readable.
findings.how_to_verify: `novamira/elementor-get-content` returns the same top-level ids; the editor opens the page without a 'data migration' notice; `wp post meta get <id> _elementor_data | jq` parses; front end renders every section; Lighthouse passes the finding-3 targets.
findings.correction: Structure is right (developers.elementor.com 'Atomic Elements' and 'Atomic Widgets': `{id, version:'0.0', elType:'e-div-block'|'e-flexbox'|'e-grid', isInner, settings, editor_settings, interactions:[], styles, elements}` and widgets `elType:'widget', widgetType:'e-heading'` with `{$$type,value}` settings). Three corrections: (1) the lint must inspect the `interactions` array, not only `_animation`/`motion_fx`: V4 entrance/scroll animations are stored there (Interactions help, Jun 19, 2026: 'Javascript functions ... entrance and scrolling animations', triggers Page load / Scroll into view / While scrolling / On hover / On click, effects Fade/Slide/Scale in Core; Pro adds Custom effects per breakpoint per the 4.0 blog). (2) The official MCP is not 'drafts only': the help page (Sep 30, 2026) says 'Save drafts or publish pages and templates directly through your connected AI tool'. (3) Require Elementor ≥ 4.3.4 before writing through MCP: 4.3.4 changelog fixes 'Element settings may lost when updating pages through MCP' and 4.3.3 fixes 'Certain MCP style values are not applied correctly in Atomic elements'. Also the 'Get started with V4' help notes a V4 element dropped on the canvas is auto-wrapped in a 3.x container (and 4.3.0 'auto-wrapping them in a Flexbox Container'), so lint the top level for stray `elType:'container'`.

findings.claim: Map each design component to the lightest atomic element, fall back to a v3 Pro widget only where no atomic equivalent exists, and push anything that is not content (scripts, legal footers, structured data) into the Hello/Inglelandi child theme.
findings.detail: Atomic elements registered in Elementor main (modules/atomic-widgets/module.php): Div_Block, Flexbox, Grid, Atomic_Heading, Atomic_Paragraph, Atomic_Button, Atomic_Image, Atomic_Svg, Atomic_Divider, Atomic_List(+Item), Atomic_Accordion, Atomic_Tabs, Atomic_Youtube, Atomic_Self_Hosted_Video, Atomic_Background_Video, Atomic_Google_Maps, Atomic_Form (Pro). V4 FAQ/PlusAddons: Div Block is 'lighter and loads faster than Flexbox'; Flexbox carries a 10 px default padding that a `div` Default Style of 0 overrides. Mapping: hero → e-div-block + e-image (static, no lazy) + e-heading + e-paragraph + e-button; feature cards → e-grid of e-div-block cards styled by one class; icons → e-svg (inline, no icon font); FAQ → Atomic Accordion; gallery → e-grid of e-image; video → Atomic_Youtube/Self_Hosted (click-to-play poster) never Background_Video above the fold; nav/mega menu, Loop Grid (pre-4.3), WooCommerce, forms (free) → v3/Pro widgets. Hedrick's 2026 mapping says nav logic, forms, sliders and interactive elements 'require manual rebuild' from converter output. Hello theme settings page (Hello 2.9+): 'Disable theme header & footer' (use Theme Builder), 'Hide page title', 'Deregister Hello reset.css' and 'Deregister Hello theme.css' only when the child theme supplies its own, 'Disable description meta tag' when an SEO plugin is active. Elementor → Settings → General: 'Disable Default Colors' / 'Disable Default Fonts'.
findings.breaks_when: Deregistering theme.css/reset.css without a child-theme replacement breaks WordPress-required styles (comments, forms, alignments); replacing a Pro Nav Menu with hand HTML loses the editor's mobile menu behaviour; Atomic_Google_Maps/YouTube still load third-party scripts on view — use a static image + link on non-contact pages.
findings.how_to_apply: Put a component→element table in the build skill: Figma 'Frame/Auto layout' → e-flexbox (only when direction/gap needed) else e-div-block; 'Grid' → e-grid; 'Text' → e-heading/e-paragraph; 'Instance:Button' → e-button + class; 'Vector/Icon' → e-svg; 'Image' → e-image with `image_size` set to a matching custom size; 'Video' → Self_Hosted/YouTube with poster; 'Navigation' → Pro Nav Menu (v3). In the child theme enqueue one `site.css` for non-Elementor markup and move every `<script>` found in HTML widgets to `wp_enqueue_script(..., strategy=>'defer')`. Toggle Hello settings: header/footer off, page title off; keep reset.css unless the child theme defines its own reset.
findings.how_to_verify: Count `widgetType` values in the saved JSON: zero add-on widgets on brochure pages; view-source shows `<svg>` inline instead of `fa-*` classes; no `<script>` inside `.elementor-widget-html`; Lighthouse 'Avoid non-composited animations' and '3rd parties' insights are empty on the home page.
findings.correction: Element list confirmed in `modules/atomic-widgets/module.php` (Div_Block, Flexbox, Grid, Heading, Paragraph, Button, Image, Svg, Divider, List, Accordion, Tabs, Youtube, Self_Hosted_Video, Background_Video, Google_Maps, Atomic_Form; plus Carousel_Promotion and Collection_Loop_Promotion placeholders for Pro). Correction: Div Block is not padding-free or materially 'lighter' than Flexbox. `div-block.php` `define_base_styles()` is `display:block; padding:10px; min-width:30px` and `flexbox.php` is `display:flex; padding:10px` — same single `<div>`, same base padding.
