findings.how_to_apply: For new builds either theme is fine; keep Inglelandi if it ships no front-end CSS/JS beyond Hello's (verify by diffing the theme's enqueued assets). Do not schedule theme migrations as a performance task; spend the time on findings 1-8.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse network-requests filtered to /wp-content/themes/: total bytes < 20 KB and no JS; if Inglelandi exceeds that, dequeue the extra assets rather than switch theme.

findings.claim: DOM size, 'Optimized Markup' and Elementor 4's single-div atomic elements are worth little for the mobile score on these sites (pallada has 2024 DOM nodes and scores 86; limnoupolis has 703 and scores 27) and carry custom-CSS breakage risk on existing sites.
findings.detail: Local: dom-size pallada 2024, cretaforums 1224, kand 1152 (scores 86/74/68) vs limnoupolis 703, onar 561, vorenia 704 (27/44/50): no correlation. onar is the only site with optimized_markup OFF (and Elementor 4.2.3) and has the most CSS requests (56), but its LCP problem is the video + banner, not DOM. Official: Elementor 4.0 blog (2026-04-15) 'each element uses just a single DIV wrapper'; new installs get Atomic features by default, 'For existing websites, updating to 4.0 will not change the current setup'. 365i (Jan 2026, on 3.35 beta): V4 single-div wrappers 'reducing DOM nodes by 15-20% in testing' and 'Custom CSS targeting V3 classes like .elementor-widget-container will break in V4'. Crocoblock: Optimized DOM Output 'works great with the new sites... most probably will cause problems if switched on the existing site'. ShortPixel: Optimized Markup 'Test if you rely on custom CSS or third-party plugins'. Plus Addons (Sept 2026): Default Styles 'padding default on div overrides the container's usual 10px default padding'.
findings.breaks_when: Site has custom CSS or addon CSS selecting .elementor-widget-container / .elementor-column-wrap / .elementor-inner; Dynamic.ooo or Premium Addons widgets styled by those wrappers; mixing V3 widgets with V4 atomic elements and then applying 4.3 Default Styles for div.
findings.how_to_apply: New builds: start on Elementor 4.x with Atomic Editor on (default on new installs), Optimized Markup (e_optimized_markup) Active, Flexbox containers, max nesting 3-4 (audit shows nesting 6-9 today). Existing sites: leave Optimized Markup as is unless the custom CSS is grepped for the legacy wrapper classes first; do not migrate V3 pages to atomic just for speed.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse 'dom-size' < 800 body nodes on new builds (Lighthouse warning threshold cited by 365i); after enabling Optimized Markup on an existing site, visual diff of 5 templates and grep theme/child CSS and Elementor Custom CSS for 'elementor-widget-container' = 0 matches.

findings.claim: Element Caching is not a scoring lever on these sites (it is disabled on the fastest one) and is a known breaker of dynamic widgets; keep it off on sites with JetSmartFilters, bookings, WooCommerce or Polylang dynamic strings and use full-page cache for TTFB instead.
findings.detail: audit-summary: pallada element_cache 'disabled' (score 86); onar/limnoupolis 'default'; others 24h. Element caching only helps the uncached render path (TTFB on a cache miss); with a page-cache HIT the HTML is never regenerated. Elementor help (Last Update Sept 15, 2026): 'Element Caching cannot be used on elements that contain dynamic tags or any other type of dynamic information, such as shortcodes'; 'the feature is inactive by default'; Container, Grid Container, Off Canvas, Section, Column, Inner Section 'are automatically cached and their status cannot be changed'; per-element override in Advanced > Cache Settings; expiration under Elementor > Editor > Settings > Performance > Element Cache Expiration; disable via Performance > Element Cache = Disable. FacetWP (2026-03-23): 'Elementor's Element Caching feature is incompatible with FacetWP' and marks its widgets dynamic to force Inactive. The observed experiment list shows it under e_element_cache; Elementor's performance-features page (updated 2026-06-19) still labels it experimental in the Features tab.
findings.breaks_when: Filters (JetSmartFilters/FacetWP), YITH/Woo Bookings forms, logged-in or language-specific content, shortcode widgets, Loop Grids with dynamic tags: visitors see stale or another language's HTML; forms render with an expired nonce.
findings.how_to_apply: Leave Element Cache 'Disable' (Elementor > Editor > Settings > Performance) on dynamic sites; if used on brochure sites, set Cache Settings = Inactive on every widget with a dynamic tag/shortcode and set Element Cache Expiration to 24 h. Spend the TTFB effort on page cache hit ratio (finding 5).
findings.how_to_verify: Measure server-response-time on a cold URL with and without the feature (expect < 100 ms difference when object cache is on); test a filter, a booking form submission and a language switch in a private window after toggling.

findings.claim: Hero images belong in an Image widget (HTML with fetchpriority high), not in a container background: a CSS background is discovered late, is not responsive and cannot carry fetchpriority, which matches why the fast sites' LCP shows zero Load Delay.
findings.detail: web.dev optimize-lcp: resources discoverable by the preload scanner start earliest; 'The LCP element requires a CSS background image' is listed among late-discovery cases, fix is or an ; 'setting a high priority on more than one or two images makes priority setting unhelpful'. corewebvitals.io (reviewed March 2026): Elementor 'adds hero images as a background image by default'; background images are 'not immediately discovered... linked in stylesheets', 'missing newer properties like native lazy loading, fetchpriority and async decoding' and 'will always load a full desktop sized image, even for small mobile devices'; gives a 2-minute CSS pattern (.relative container, .heroimg with position:absolute; object-fit:cover). wptraining.at: 'An image used as a container background loads later than a real image widget.' Smolik: 'If the hero is a CSS background, the browser may discover the resource later... I convert the visual implementation'. Local: pallada's HTML carries fetchpriority="high" on 3 images, platonos 2, limnoupolis 1 (on the wrong, lazy image); vorenia's 1 unsized image. Elementor's 'Lazy Load Background Images' Performance feature lazy-loads 'all background images except the first one' (official), which is fine for below-fold only.
findings.breaks_when: The object-fit override collides with Elementor's helper divs on legacy Sections (.elementor-container/.elementor-column need position:static per the snippet); designers lose Background Position/parallax controls; more than one image gets fetchpriority high so none wins.
findings.how_to_apply: Build rule: hero Container has no background image; first child is an Image widget (full size srcset, Loading Eager) with CSS class heroimg and the container class relative; custom CSS from corewebvitals.io (.relative{position:relative} .heroimg{position:absolute;inset:0;object-fit:cover;z-index:-1}). Mobile: use Elementor responsive image size (Image Size per device) so the phone gets ~800px. Keep 'Lazy Load Background Images' Active for decorative below-fold backgrounds. If a background must stay, add Perfmatters > Preloading > Fetch Priority / Preload Critical Images for that URL.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse LCP phases: Load Delay ~0 ms (image discovered in HTML); 'prioritize-lcp-image' passes; hero has fetchpriority="high", srcset with a ~800w candidate chosen on mobile (DevTools Network shows the small file); visual check that cover/focal point matches design on 390px and 1440px.
findings.correction: Keep 'hero as '. Replace the per-widget Loading control with: enable Image Loading Optimization, confirm the hero gets fetchpriority="high" in view-source, and if it does not, add it via Perfmatters > Preloading > Fetch Priority. Add 'data-dce-background-image-url' (Dynamic.ooo) and 'lmn-hero-bg'-style container backgrounds to the audit's late-discovery patterns.

findings.claim: Sliders, background slideshows and swiper in the first viewport cost 100-600 ms of mobile main-thread on the agency's sites and appear in no 95-100 case; a static first slide on mobile is the documented pattern.
findings.detail: Local bootup-time: vorenia swiper.min.js 589 ms + background-slideshow/background-video chunks; pallada swiper 142 ms + background-slideshow.min.js 88 ms (8 slideshows site-wide, 2 bgvideo markers on the home page); limnoupolis lightbox chunk 27 KB. AcceleraWP: replaced Slider Revolution with a lighter slider plus lazy-loaded hidden slides to go green. wptraining.at lists 'sliders and carousels, animated counters, motion effects on scroll, embedded videos and external scripts' as the INP/TBT suspects. Smolik: 'Carousels, filters and effects' are where handlers get expensive. OMM step 14: use fewer widgets/columns; FlyingPress 'Lazy render elements' for below-fold sections. Elementor 3.24 made slider/lightbox CSS conditional, so the remaining cost is JS, not CSS.
findings.breaks_when: Hiding the slider with Elementor responsive visibility leaves swiper.min.js and all slide images in the mobile HTML (display:none images still download); replacing a slideshow with a static image changes the client's approved design.
findings.how_to_apply: Hero: no Slides/Carousel/Background Slideshow on mobile; if desktop needs it, render a separate mobile Container with one Image widget and make the desktop slider Container output nothing on mobile (Elementor Pro Display Conditions or a device-aware shortcode), not CSS hiding. Below the fold: Loop Carousel with lazy load ON, and FlyingPress 'Lazy render elements' / Perfmatters equivalent. Audit should flag swiper, background-slideshow, lightbox chunks in the mobile waterfall.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse mobile bootup-time: no swiper/background-slideshow/background-video entries; network-requests: slide images 2-8 absent on mobile; TBT down by the removed bootup ms; desktop slider still works.
findings.correction: Remove 'Elementor Pro Display Conditions' as the device-gating tool; use a third-party condition with a Device rule (Dynamic.ooo visibility is already installed on onar/pallada/marakaki, unverified here) or a server-side check, and verify by grepping the mobile HTML for swiper/background-slideshow chunks, not just by viewport.

findings.claim: Every published 95-100 result warns that single PSI runs fluctuate by several points; acceptance must be the median of repeated mobile runs plus CrUX, and a true 100 needs lab LCP around 1.2 s, which none of the agency's sites currently has.
findings.detail: Justin Ferriman: 'PageSpeed Insights fluctuates at any given time the test is run. GapScout's mobile score usually lands between 94-99.' Stricker: 'the PageSpeed Score of Google fluctuates a lot'. Substack: 'scores on this site can vary quite a bit each time you run it, so they're not a scientific evaluation'. ThemeZhub: LCP 'Under 1.2 seconds (Excellent / 100 score)'. wptraining.at: 'Google judges on field data from real visitors, not on the test result of a single run'. Local runs are Lighthouse 12.8.2, mobile, throttlingMethod 'simulate', single run per URL (benchmarkIndex 1181-2065, i.e. the runner's CPU varied ~75% between runs, which alone shifts TBT/score). Best local LCP today is 2.2 s (platonos).
findings.breaks_when: not known to break
findings.how_to_apply: In the audit skill's lighthouse.sh: run each URL 3-5 times (--throttling-method=simulate, mobile), report median score and median LCP/TBT/CLS plus benchmarkIndex; fail the gate if benchmarkIndex < 1000 (noisy runner). Define 'done' as median >= 95 AND LCP <= 1.5 s AND CLS <= 0.05 AND third-party blocking 0 ms, then confirm with PSI field data after 28 days.
findings.how_to_verify: Five consecutive PSI mobile runs within +/-3 points; PSI 'Core Web Vitals Assessment: Passed' for the origin once CrUX refreshes.
findings.correction: Acceptance = median of 3-5 runs on Lighthouse 13.x (same major as PSI), report benchmarkIndex, then CrUX. Label the 1.2 s LCP target as derived from the scoring curve, not from a documented case.

findings.claim: Elementor 4.x version hygiene matters for 'without breaking anything': update Core and Pro together to >= 4.3.2, and treat the new 4.3 atomic Background Video element as a hero-video temptation to keep off mobile; no published case has yet measured a 95-100 site on 4.x.
findings.detail: Plus Addons (2026-09-29, citing the official changelog): 4.3.0 on 22 Sept 2026 added Elementor MCP, Background Video (atomic container element with Autoplay/Mute/Loop), Atomic Accordion, Default Styles; 4.3.2 (24 Sept) 'fixes page styles after regeneration' and 'Improved update stability between Elementor Core and Pro'; sites 'running mismatched Core and Pro versions' broke. Elementor 4.0 blog: atomic features default on new installs only; existing sites unchanged. The audit shows onar on Core 4.2.3 while the fleet's Pro runs up to 4.3.1 and most Core at 4.3.3-4.3.5. All 95-100 write-ups found (WP Rocket on Pro 3.21.1, Ferriman 2023, Stricker 2022/2024, Substack Feb 2025, ThemeZhub May 2026 unspecified version) predate or do not state 4.x; Elementor's performance-features page (updated 2026-06-19) still lists the same levers (Inline Font Icons, Element Caching, Optimized Gutenberg Loading, Lazy Load Background Images), so the practices carry over but the numbers are unconfirmed on 4.x.
findings.breaks_when: Core updated without Pro (or vice versa) across a 4.x minor; 'Regenerate Files & Data' run on 4.3.0/4.3.1 (style regeneration bug fixed in 4.3.2); a V4 Default Style for div changes container padding site-wide.
findings.how_to_apply: Debloat skill pre-flight: refuse to toggle experiments or regenerate CSS unless Core and Pro are the same minor and >= 4.3.2; update onar from 4.2.3 before any optimisation work. Build skill: do not use the atomic Background Video element in the hero for mobile; prefer the Video widget with image overlay or desktop-only output. Record Elementor Core/Pro version in every Lighthouse baseline so gains are attributable.
findings.how_to_verify: wp-admin > Elementor > System Info shows matching Core/Pro versions >= 4.3.2; after update, Elementor > Tools > Regenerate Files & Data then visual diff of 3 templates; Lighthouse baseline re-run.
findings.correction: Pre-flight: Core and Pro on the latest patch of the same minor (today Core 4.3.5 + Pro 4.3.2), never a Core major ahead of Pro; onar (Core 4.2.3) must be updated first. The atomic Background Video element has no documented mobile-off control, so it is a stronger mobile risk than the legacy container video.

findings.claim: The plugin's Lighthouse verify scripts must target Lighthouse 13 audit ids: PSI dropped third-party-summary, dom-size, font-display, lcp-lazy-loaded, prioritize-lcp-image and render-blocking-resources in favour of *-insight audits, while the local runs are still Lighthouse 12.8.2.
findings.detail: Chrome blog 'Lighthouse 13.0' (published Oct 10 2025): 'in Lighthouse 13 we are removing the old audits from both the report and the underlying JSON'; 'There are no changes to the performance scoring in this version'. Replacement table on the page: cls-culprits-insight, document-latency-insight, dom-size-insight (replaces dom-size), duplicated-javascript-insight, font-display-insight (font-display), image-delivery-insight, interaction-to-next-paint-insight, lcp-discovery-insight (replaces prioritize-lcp-image AND lcp-lazy-loaded), lcp-phases-insight, legacy-javascript-insight, modern-http-insight, network-dependency-tree-insight, render-blocking-insight (render-blocking-resources), third-parties-insight (third-party-summary), use-cache-insight, viewport-insight. Also removed with no replacement: offscreen-images, third-party-facades, preload-fonts, font-size, and the older FMP-style metric. Available in PSI 'within the next week' of Oct 10 2025 and Chrome 143 stable. All 17 researcher findings' how_to_verify steps use the old ids.
findings.breaks_when: not known to break; but a verify script keyed on the old ids silently returns null on PSI/Lighthouse 13 and passes a gate it should fail.
findings.how_to_apply: Pin lighthouse@13.x in the plugin's lighthouse.sh (npm i -g lighthouse@13) so local and PSI JSON match; map: third-party-summary -> third-parties-insight; lcp-lazy-loaded/prioritize-lcp-image -> lcp-discovery-insight; LCP phases -> lcp-phases-insight; render-blocking-resources -> render-blocking-insight; dom-size -> dom-size-insight; font-display -> font-display-insight; keep largest-contentful-paint-element, total-blocking-time, cumulative-layout-shift, network-requests, bootup-time only if still present in the 13.x JSON (check once).
findings.how_to_verify: Run lighthouse@13 against pallada.gr and assert audits['third-parties-insight'] and audits['lcp-discovery-insight'] exist while audits['third-party-summary'] is undefined; compare the score with a PSI mobile run of the same URL (expect within normal +/-3 noise).

findings.claim: The observed flag e_optimized_css_files is Elementor's alpha 'Optimized CSS Files' experiment (default inactive): it only de-duplicates and filters Elementor's CSS-purge triggers so sites behind page caching/CDN stop serving 404 stylesheets after plugin updates; it is not a CSS-size optimisation.
findings.detail: From elementor/elementor main branch, core/experiments/manager.php: name 'e_optimized_css_files', title 'Optimized CSS Files', tag 'Performance', description 'Keeps external CSS files available and consistent for sites behind page caching or a CDN.', release_status ALPHA, default INACTIVE. core/files/manager.php: register_site_changed_hooks() purges all generated CSS (uploads/elementor/css/*) on activated_plugin, deactivated_plugin, switch_theme, upgrader_process_complete and update_option_elementor_element_cache_ttl; with the experiment active, repeated purges in one request are collapsed and purges are skipped for non-genuine updates ('update checks, translation updates, and bulk-update submissions with an empty item queue'); when inactive 'behaviour is unchanged: always purge'. Core 4.3.0 changelog also lists 'Fix: Page-specific CSS may be missing on the first visit after automatic CSS cleanup' and 4.3.2 'Fix: Page styles may not load correctly after being regenerated', i.e. this area is actively changing. Consequence for the agency: every plugin/translation update on a LiteSpeed/FlyingPress/W3TC site deletes post-*.css while cached HTML still references the old hashed file -> unstyled pages until the page cache is purged. This answers the researcher's open question 2.
findings.breaks_when: Alpha code: skipping a purge that was genuinely needed would leave stale CSS after a real update; the experiment is new (since 3.33.0) and has no help-center page; toggling it also regenerates nothing by itself.
findings.how_to_apply: Do not recommend enabling it for speed. Instead, in the debloat skill: after any plugin/theme/Elementor update or Element Cache TTL change, run Elementor > Tools > Regenerate Files & Data and purge the page cache (LiteSpeed/FlyingPress/W3TC) in that order. Optionally trial 'Optimized CSS Files' on staging.limnoupolis only, with a 1-week visual check, before touching production.
findings.how_to_verify: After a plugin update on a cached site, curl the cached home HTML, extract the /uploads/elementor/css/post-*.css URLs and confirm each returns 200; repeat with the experiment on vs off on staging.

findings.claim: On onar and vorenia the mobile MP4 download is Elementor's own container background video with 'Play On Mobile' switched on (chunks/background-video.min.js is in both waterfalls), so the fix is a per-container toggle plus a fallback image, not removing a Dynamic.ooo/Premium Addons widget.
findings.detail: Official 'Add & edit a background video in Elementor' (Last Update Oct 26 2025) lists Play Once, 'Play On Mobile: Toggle to Yes if you want ... the video to run on smaller screens' (the sentence is garbled on the page), Privacy Mode and 'Background Fallback: Select an image that will be used if the video is unavailable'. Lighthouse mobile JSON: onar loads /uploads/2026/10/onar-seaside-lounge.mp4 (352 KB, Media) and vorenia /uploads/2026/09/Main-Video-Final.mp4 (256 KB) immediately after elementor/assets/js/chunks/background-video.min.js (ver 4.2.3 / 4.3.4). Both files were uploaded in Sept/Oct 2026, i.e. the videos are a recent design change that coincides with the slow LCP (onar 16.4 s, vorenia 9.0 s). pallada also loads background-video.min.js but no MP4, consistent with Play On Mobile = No.
findings.breaks_when: Client wants motion on phones; the fallback image is missing so mobile shows a flat colour; the hero is the new 4.3 atomic Background Video element, which documents no mobile-off switch (then rebuild the hero with a legacy container or an image).
findings.how_to_apply: Edit the hero container > Style > Background > Video: Play On Mobile = No, set Background Fallback to the optimised hero JPG/WebP (~800 px wide for mobile), keep Autoplay muted on desktop. Audit rule: flag any mobile waterfall containing background-video.min.js followed by a Media request.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse mobile network-requests contains no .mp4/.webm; LCP element becomes the hero fallback image or h1; onar LCP from 16.4 s and vorenia from 9.0 s should fall by several seconds in the same run; desktop still plays the video.
tools: Elementor container Background Video (Play On Mobile)

findings.claim: voreniahorizon.gr requests all four of its Google-font files from a different origin (villavorenia.gr) and receives 0 KB, so its brand fonts are almost certainly failing CORS and rendering in fallback; the site needs Elementor's Replace URL + Regenerate Files.
findings.detail: Lighthouse mobile network-requests for voreniahorizon.gr: https://villavorenia.gr/wp-content/uploads/elementor/google-fonts/fonts/intertight-701d4a64.woff2, ebgaramond-ef73a8c5.woff2, intertight-c382e7f8.woff2, lexenddeca-fcf1177e.woff2, each resourceType Font with transferSize 0, and third-party-summary lists entity 'villavorenia.gr' 0 KB. Elementor's local Google Fonts feature writes absolute URLs into the generated CSS (help page: fonts stored under /wp-content/uploads/elementor/ and 'updates your site's CSS to point to the local files'), so a domain move without regenerating leaves the old host in the font-face rules. Fonts are CORS-restricted cross-origin, which explains 0 bytes. Separately, the audit-summary lists vorenia fonts as EB Garamond/Inter Tight/Lexend Deca families that then never render as designed.
findings.breaks_when: villavorenia.gr sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin for voreniahorizon.gr (then fonts load but still cost a second connection); the site intentionally serves assets from villavorenia.gr as a CDN alias (unlikely for uploads).
findings.how_to_apply: Elementor > Tools > Replace URL (villavorenia.gr -> voreniahorizon.gr), then Tools > Regenerate Files & Data, purge FlyingPress cache; if the Performance-tab 'Load Google Fonts Locally' is off after the 4.x update (default Disabled since 3.32.1), re-enable it so fonts are re-downloaded to the new host.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse network-requests: every Font request has host voreniahorizon.gr and transferSize > 0; DevTools Console shows no CORS font error; a Greek heading renders in the brand serif (screenshot); font-display insight passes.

title: Per-site triage: decision procedure after elementor-audit, Lighthouse 13.x reading, per-stack lever matrix, auto-action audit, stopping rules, Googlebot guard
summary: The triage must start from what the Lighthouse JSON actually says, and on these 10 sites it says something the draft skill does not expect: on pallada.gr, cretaforums.gr and onar-seaside-lounge.gr the LCP element is the cookie-consent banner text (FAZ Cookie Manager / Complianz), not the hero, so hero levers cannot move LCP there; on pallada.gr 1.1 s of LCP is a 302 redirect from / to /en/ added in .htaccess on 2026-10-11; and the 'WP Rocket 3.23' signal on pallada.gr is a leftover .htaccess block, the active stack being W3TC 2.10.7 + Perfmatters 2.6.9. I ran Lighthouse 13.5.0 locally (pallada.gr) and diffed it against the 12.8.2 runs: every *-insight id already exists in 12.8.2, 13.x only deletes 24 legacy audits (third-party-summary, largest-contentful-paint-element, dom-size, font-display, render-blocking-resources, uses-optimized-images, etc.), so one jq (saved at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/lh13/triage.jq, tested on both versions) serves both; the Chrome blog's names lcp-phases-insight / interaction-to-next-paint-insight / use-cache-insight are NOT the shipped ids (lcp-breakdown-insight / inp-breakdown-insight / cache-insight). The decision tree is: consolidate duplicate optimisers and turn LiteSpeed Guest Mode off before measuring; write WooCommerce/booking exclusion lists; then cache (no HIT footprint or TTFB > 600 ms) -> classify the LCP element (consent banner / lazy img / CSS background / text with render delay / video-canvas) -> third parties > 250 ms main-thread (consent gating, then delay specified) -> fonts and icon fonts -> render-blocking and first-screen animations -> RUCSS opt-in -> delay-all last. Per stack: LiteSpeed 7.9.1 has every global lever as a wp litespeed-option key but no per-page unloading (its metabox only has Disable Cache / Disable Image Lazyload / Viewport Images) so Perfmatters is the complement; the 'FlyingPress' on cretaforums/voreniahorizon is a CretaForce fork (header 4.22.1, Author CretaForce, own update URI) whose RUCSS is a local HTML-selector engine, not the cloud engine the official docs describe; W3TC free is page cache only. Of the draft auto-actions, element_cache_on should be removed (Elementor: breaks dynamic tags/shortcodes, TTFB-only benefit), optimized_markup_on gated on a grep for .elementor-button-wrapper in custom CSS/JS, litespeed_optimize split into one-key-per-action with wp litespeed-option get before-values and no localize of gtm/gtag. Stop tuning and ask for a design change when lcp_type is video/canvas or the network chain contains three.js/.glb, when first-party bootup stays > 2 s after defer, or when the marketer refuses consent gating / delay of a 5-tag GTM. Google states Google Search does not interact with the page and declines permission prompts, so anything delayed-until-interaction never runs for Googlebot: exclude content-producing scripts from delay and verify with URL Inspection's rendered HTML.
critic_notes: Method: re-ran the audit-key diff and every claimed JSON path on the local 12.8.2 and 13.5.0 files; opened the cited LiteSpeed (general, pageopt, metabox, thirdparty, cli; base.cls.php; readme 7.9.1), Perfmatters (changelog, delay, RUCSS, script manager, WP-CLI, defer), Elementor (element caching, performance features, optimized DOM, 3.25 and 4.0 developer updates, V4 FAQ, explore V4, wordpress.org readme 4.3.5), Chrome/Lighthouse (13.0 blog and release notes, scoring, LCP-breakdown, third-parties, default-config v13.5.0, bootup-time.js, readme, throttling.md), Google Search (lazy-loading, fix-search-javascript), WP Rocket (delay, RUCSS), FlyingPress (docs + changelog), W3TC readme and DevTools DocumentLatency.ts; probed the live sites with curl; read the FlyingPress fork files and pallada's .htaccess read-only through Novamira. WebFetch could not resolve most hosts, so pages were fetched with curl through the proxy; GitHub API (gh) was not authorised for GoogleChrome/lighthouse, so PR #16729's file list was not re-opened (the release-notes entry and the local key diff were used instead). Not verified: Perfmatters lazy-load 'exclude leading images' option text (doc URL returned no body), PSI's current cpuSlowdownMultiplier (only DebugBear's 1.2x statement), the exact V4 per-document stylesheet markup, and the fork's full CSS.php beyond the first 7000 bytes (the selector-collection functions were seen by name only). Nothing on any site was modified; only read-file/check-setup abilities were used.
open_questions: Perfmatters' database option key for before-value capture (believed to be `perfmatters_options`) was not stated on any page opened; the documented interfaces are `wp perfmatters get-options`, `wp perfmatters enable|disable <option>` and `wp perfmatters import-settings <file>` - use export/import JSON for undo until the key is confirmed.

Neither WP Rocket's delay-JS articles (1349, 1560) nor Perfmatters' delay doc say anything about Googlebot; the guard rests on Google's own statements. Whether either plugin skips delay for known crawler user agents is unverified.
Elementor Video widget: the inventory claims `lazy_load` only produces a facade when an Image Overlay is set; the widget doc was not opened, so video_lazy is kept as 'reported fix' rather than auto.

LiteSpeed default values could not be read from source (data/const.default.ini returned 404 and the GitHub API listing failed); defaults quoted (Guest Mode OFF, Guest Optimization ON, Load JS Deferred OFF, Lazy Load Images OFF, Optimize for Guest Only ON) come from the docs pages.

Official FlyingPress 5.6 behaviour (cloud RUCSS, 'Load unused CSS' modes) could not be fully read because docs.flyingpress.com articles are partly JS-rendered; the matrix describes the CretaForce fork from its source, which is what the agency actually runs.

PSI confirmation was impossible today (HTTP 429, project quota 0/day): PSI's current Lighthouse version (13.5 per the task) and Lightrider cpuSlowdownMultiplier 1.2 were not re-verified; the Chrome blog only confirms 13.0 reached PSI around Oct 2025. Whether `--throttling.cpuSlowdownMultiplier=1.2` reproduces PSI locally is unverified.

platonos.dev6 LCP element is a `p` (2.2 s) - not checked whether it is a consent banner or page copy; the consent-banner regex in triage.jq should be validated against each CMP's markup (FAZ `.faz-notice`, Complianz `#cmplz-message*`, Cookie-Script class names unknown).

Google's docs do not address opacity:0 (`elementor-invisible`) content; indexing of animated-in text is assumed fine because it is in the rendered DOM, but the URL Inspection screenshot check is the only way to see what Googlebot renders when frontend JS is delayed.

e_opt_in_v4 status per site is not in audit-summary.json (audit.php reads features but the summary omitted it); branch (i) needs that field before it can fire, and the exact set of CSS Elementor V4 emits (local/global per-document stylesheets) is known only from the Perfmatters 2.6.9 changelog wording.
WP Rocket 3.23 is installed on none of the 10 sites (pallada's header is a ghost .htaccess block), so the WP Rocket column of the matrix is docs-only and untested here.

Elementor 4.3.x changelog was not opened: the list of wrappers Optimized Markup removes beyond `.elementor-button-wrapper` (3.25 named Button/PayPal/Stripe and promised more) must be read from the installed version's changelog before the grep gate is complete.
Lighthouse's exact 'serverResponseIsFast' threshold was inferred (575 ms passed, 600 ms used as the branch threshold); the document-latency insight doc page was not opened.

findings.claim: One jq can read Lighthouse 12.8.2 and 13.5.0 because every performance insight id already exists in 12.8.2; 13.x only deletes 24 legacy audits, and the shipped ids differ from the names in Chrome's 13.0 blog (lcp-breakdown-insight, inp-breakdown-insight, cache-insight; not lcp-phases-insight, interaction-to-next-paint-insight, use-cache-insight).
findings.detail: Verified by running `npx -y lighthouse@13 https://pallada.gr/ --only-categories=performance --form-factor=mobile --output=json` in the container (lighthouseVersion 13.5.0, saved at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/lh13/pallada13.json) and diffing `.audits|keys` against the 12.8.2 runs. Only in 12.8.2 (gone in 13): critical-request-chains, dom-size, duplicated-javascript, efficient-animated-content, first-meaningful-paint, font-display, largest-contentful-paint-element, lcp-lazy-loaded, legacy-javascript, modern-image-formats, no-document-write, offscreen-images, prioritize-lcp-image, render-blocking-resources, third-party-facades, third-party-summary, uses-http2, uses-long-cache-ttl, uses-optimized-images, uses-passive-event-listeners, uses-rel-preconnect, uses-responsive-images, uses-text-compression, viewport. Nothing is only-in-13. Still present in 13.5 (default-config.js v13.5.0): unused-css-rules, unused-javascript, bootup-time, long-tasks, mainthread-work-breakdown, total-byte-weight, network-requests, server-response-time (hidden), unsized-images, bf-cache. ID -> JSON path map (identical in 12.8.2 and 13.5.0): LCP element = .audits["lcp-breakdown-insight"].details.items[] | select(.type=="node") -> {selector,snippet,nodeLabel}; LCP phases = same audit .details.items[] | select(.type=="table") | .items[] -> {subpart: timeToFirstByte|resourceLoadDelay|resourceLoadDuration|elementRenderDelay, duration} (only timeToFirstByte+elementRenderDelay appear for text LCP, matching Chrome's LCP-breakdown doc: load phases are 0 when no resource is loaded); LCP discovery = .audits["lcp-discovery-insight"].details.items[] | select(.type=="checklist") | .items -> {priorityHinted,requestDiscoverable,eagerlyLoaded}.value, scoreDisplayMode=="notApplicable" when LCP is text; render-blocking = .audits["render-blocking-insight"] .metricSavings.FCP/.LCP and .details.items[] {url,totalBytes,wastedMs}; third parties = .audits["third-parties-insight"].details.items[] {entity,transferSize,mainThreadTime, subItems.items[] {url,mainThreadTime,transferSize}} - NO blockingTime field in either version; DOM = .audits["dom-size-insight"].numericValue (added in 13.0.0; in 12.8.2 use .details.items[0].value.value or .audits["dom-size"].numericValue); fonts = .audits["font-display-insight"] .metricSavings.FCP and .details.items[] {url,wastedMs}; TTFB/redirect = .audits["document-latency-insight"].details.debugData {serverResponseTime,redirectDuration} and .details.items {noRedirects,serverResponseIsFast,usesCompression}.value, metricSavings {FCP,LCP}; images = .audits["image-delivery-insight"].details.debugData.wastedBytes and .details.items[] {url,totalBytes,wastedBytes,node (13.0+)}; legacy JS = .audits["legacy-javascript-insight"].details.items[] {url,wastedBytes}; duplicated JS = .audits["duplicated-javascript-insight"].details.items[] {source,wastedBytes}; unused = .audits["unused-css-rules"|"unused-javascript"].details.overallSavingsBytes; CLS culprits = .audits["cls-culprits-insight"].details.items[0].items[] {node.selector, score} (first row is node.type=="text" 'Total'); network tree = .audits["network-dependency-tree-insight"].details.items[0].value.chains (recursive navStartToEndTime); forced reflow = .audits["forced-reflow-insight"].details.items[0].items[] {source,reflowTime}; long tasks = .audits["long-tasks"].details.items[] {url,startTime,duration}; bootup = .audits["bootup-time"].details.items[] {url,total,scripting,scriptParseCompile}; main-thread groups = .audits["mainthread-work-breakdown"].details.items[] {group,duration}. Third-party blocking time replacement: join bootup-time items to network-requests items on url and group by .entity (network-requests items carry an `entity` key in both versions). The tested jq program is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/lh13/triage.jq (gotcha fixed there: `{k: empty}` collapses the whole object in jq, so notApplicable insights must be wrapped `[...]|.[0]`). The current lighthouse.sh fields third_party_kb (third-party-summary), lcp_lazy (largest-contentful-paint-element), dom (dom-size), img_kb (uses-optimized-images) and font_display_fail (font-display) read null on 13.x and must move to the ids above. PSI returns the same tree under lighthouseResult.audits[...] with lighthouseResult.lighthouseVersion.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break the site; the plugin breaks (null fields) if it keeps reading third-party-summary, largest-contentful-paint-element, dom-size, font-display or render-blocking-resources on 13.x, or if it uses the blog's audit names.
findings.how_to_apply: In skills/elementor-audit/scripts/lighthouse.sh drop the 12-pin, run `npx lighthouse@13` and replace the jq with `jq -c -f triage.jq "$out/$name.json"` (copy triage.jq next to the script). Keep `--only-categories=performance --form-factor=mobile`; pass the FINAL url (see redirect finding). For PSI, read .lighthouseResult.audits with the same program after `jq .lighthouseResult`.
findings.how_to_verify: `jq -c -f triage.jq` on one 12.8.2 file and one 13.x file both print lh, lcp_type, lcp_phases_ms, bootup_by_entity etc. (done: limnoupolis 12.8.2 -> lcp_type img, lcp_lazy true, phases TTFB 1057/loadDelay 548/loadDuration 573/renderDelay 177; pallada 13.5.0 -> lcp_type consent-banner-text, redirect_ms 1107). `jq '.audits|keys' | grep -c insight` prints 17 on both.

findings.claim: Triage decision tree (text form): gates first, then levers in the order cache -> LCP-element class -> third parties -> fonts/icons -> render-blocking + first-screen animations -> RUCSS opt-in -> delay-all last; each branch has a threshold, an owner, a gate and an approval class.
findings.detail: INPUT = audit.php JSON (plugins.by_role, elementor.features, elementor.settings, usage.flags, kit_fonts, db) + median of 3 triage.jq lines on the FINAL url of home, one inner page and the booking/checkout page. GATES (before any change or measurement): G0 two owners for one job -> plugins.by_role.cache has 2 entries, or optimizer present AND the cache plugin's page-optimisation keys are on (LiteSpeed optm-js_defer/optm-css_min/media-lazy, FlyingPress js_defer/js_delay/css_rucss, W3TC minify) -> STOP, propose single owner per job (page cache: the cache plugin; assets/JS: Perfmatters when present), needs human OK (deactivation). Also flag ghost rules: `# BEGIN WP Rocket` in .htaccess with no WP Rocket plugin (pallada.gr) -> human OK to remove. G1 LiteSpeed `guest`=true -> set false (auto, before-value), `wp litespeed-purge all`, then measure (otherwise PSI sees a page users never get). G2 redirect_ms>0 -> measure the final url and report the redirect as its own lever (pallada.gr: / -> /en/ 302 in .htaccess, 1107 ms = metricSavings FCP/LCP 1100), human OK (SEO/i18n decision). G3 WooCommerce / WC Bookings / YITH Booking / JetSmartFilters / forum active -> write the exclusion list first: cache bypass for cart, checkout, my-account, booking/checkout steps and ?-filtered URLs; delay/defer exclusions for jquery.min.js, booking calendar JS, filters; RUCSS page exclusion for checkout. Only then touch cache/defer/delay. LEVERS (one setting at a time, measure after each): L1 CACHE - trigger: no HIT footprint (see cache-detection finding) or ttfb_ms>600 (Lighthouse's 'Server responds quickly' passed at 575 ms, dev sites showed 2.2-4.2 s) -> enable page cache in the existing cache plugin (LiteSpeed `cache`=true on LiteSpeed hosts), auto, gate = HIT footprint on 2nd request + ttfb_ms. Expected gain: whole TTFB phase (0.5-3.5 s LCP here). Risk low; breaks when logged-in/cart pages are cached (G3). L2 LCP ELEMENT CLASS (lcp_type from triage.jq): consent-banner-text (pallada, cretaforums, onar) -> banner lever: exclude the CMP script from delay/defer so it paints early and small, or configure the banner to render after first paint / smaller font; the hero must paint before the banner. Human OK (legal). Gain high on onar (elementRenderDelay 6060 ms of 16.4 s LCP). img AND (lcp_lazy OR !priorityHinted) -> Elementor Settings > Performance > Optimized Image Loading = Enable (adds fetchpriority=high on LCP, lazy below fold) or widget Image > Lazy Load = No; one owner for lazy-load (not LiteSpeed media-lazy). Auto + visual check. limnoupolis hero img has loading="lazy", priorityHinted false, resourceLoadDelay 4270 ms in the LH-element audit. css-background-image (lcp-discovery requestDiscoverable=false; staging.limnoupolis resourceLoadDelay 1290, marakaki swiper slide) -> preload the hero image (FlyingPress img_preload / Perfmatters preload / LiteSpeed VPI) or convert the first slide to an ; visual check. video or canvas, or longest network chain contains .glb|three|webgl|.mp4 (limnoupolis chain / -> GLTFLoader.js -> buoy.glb = 7797 ms) -> HERO BRIEF to the designer; stop tuning LCP/TBT on that page. text with elementRenderDelay>500 ms (voreniahorizon h1 2693 ms, cretaforums 1393) -> fonts_no_swap + Google Fonts CSS in render_blocking_top + first-screen `_animation` (elementor-invisible until JS) -> levers L4/L5. L3 THIRD PARTIES - trigger: third_party_main_thread_ms>250 or bootup_by_entity[GTM|Facebook]>250 (limnoupolis: GTM 1618 ms + Facebook 915 ms bootup, 1625 ms blocking in 12.8.2 third-party-summary; pallada with FAZ consent gating: 0 entities, 0 ms) -> (a) consent gating through the existing CMP (human OK: marketer), (b) 'delay specified scripts' list = /gtm.js,/gtag/js,gtag(,fbevents.js,fbq( (Perfmatters) or googletagmanager.com, google-analytics.com, fbevents.js (FlyingPress default js_delay_selected) or LiteSpeed JS Delayed Includes; never localize gtm/gtag; one GTM container. Gate: third_party_entities drops to 0 before interaction and the marketer confirms tags still fire on interaction. L4 FONTS/ICONS - trigger: kit_fonts>2 families, fonts_in_widgets>2, fonts_no_swap non-empty, fonts.googleapis in render_blocking_top, fa4_shim yes, e_font_icon_svg off, CDN icon font (materialdesignicons on staging: 780 ms) -> reduce to 2 families/2-3 weights with Greek+Latin subsets, woff2, font-display swap (LiteSpeed optm-css_font_display, FlyingPress fonts_display_swap, Perfmatters local-google-fonts), Inline Font Icons = Active, FA4 shim off when no `fa fa-` icons. Auto for shim/swap, visual check for family changes. L5 RENDER-BLOCKING + ANIMATIONS - trigger: render_blocking_fcp_ms>300 (limnoupolis 950: jQuery-UI CDN css 885 ms, booking-calendar css, woocommerce.css on home) -> defer JS by ONE plugin; unload page-irrelevant CSS per page with Perfmatters Script Manager (Testing Mode first); animations>0 and lcp_type text with render delay -> remove `_animation`/`motion_fx` on first-screen elements (backup _elementor_data, visual check). L6 UNUSED CSS - trigger: unused_css_kb>50 after L5 -> RUCSS opt-in only (staging first), with Elementor safelist; if e_opt_in_v4 active, only with Perfmatters >=2.6.9 (built-in exclusions for V4 per-document stylesheets) or skip. L7 DELAY ALL - last, staging only, needs Googlebot check (URL Inspection) and human OK. STOP: all five metrics within targets, or remaining loss attributable to design (video/canvas hero, >2 s first-party bootup after defer, 5-tag GTM without gating) -> report instead of tuning.
findings.breaks_when: Running levers out of order: delay/RUCSS before exclusion lists breaks booking calendars and checkout; lazy-load by two owners raised CLS 0 -> 0.107 on staging; measuring with Guest Mode on or on the redirecting url produces numbers that do not reproduce in PSI.
findings.how_to_apply: Encode G0-G3 then L1-L7 in skills/elementor-debloat/SKILL.md as the fixed order; each lever = one setting, one measurement, keep/undo; store before-values; the agent (agents/elementor-debloater.md) asks for human OK at G0, G2, L2-banner, L2-hero-brief, L3(a), L6, L7.
findings.how_to_verify: After each lever re-run triage.jq (3 runs, median) and compare only the metric the lever targets (L1 ttfb_ms/timeToFirstByte, L2 lcp_type+lcp_phases_ms, L3 third_party_main_thread_ms+bootup_by_entity, L4 fonts_no_swap+render_blocking_top, L5 render_blocking_fcp_ms+elementRenderDelay, L6 unused_css_kb); screenshot before/after; click the booking/checkout flow after G3-dependent levers.
findings.correction: Order, gates and thresholds hold. Two corrections: (1) the 'first-party JS bootup > 2 s after defer' escalation inside L2/STOP is computed from bootup-time `total`, which includes style/layout work attributed to the script URL; Lighthouse's bootup-time numericValue sums only scripting + scriptParseCompile for URLs >= 50 ms (cretaforums: numericValue 2804 ms vs sum of total 9172 ms) - use scripting+scriptParseCompile for the JS threshold or rename the metric 'main-thread by URL'. (2) G1 should read 'if guest is true'; LiteSpeed's Guest Mode defaults OFF (Guest Optimization defaults ON but is ignored without Guest Mode), so on most sites G1 is a no-op check, not a change. The 600 ms TTFB trigger matches the DevTools document-latency constant TOO_SLOW_THRESHOLD_MS = 600 (limnoupolis passed at 575 ms).

findings.claim: On 3 of the 9 measured sites the LCP element is the cookie-consent banner text, so hero-image levers cannot move LCP there; the plugin must classify the LCP node before choosing a lever.
findings.detail: 12.8.2 largest-contentful-paint-element / 13.5.0 lcp-breakdown-insight node: pallada.gr `div.faz-notice > div.faz-notice-group > div.faz-notice-des > p` (LCP 2.5-2.6 s, phases TTFB + elementRenderDelay 478-504 ms only); cretaforums.gr same FAZ selector (LCP 4.4 s, render delay 1393 ms); onar-seaside-lounge.gr `#cmplz-message-2-optin` (Complianz; LCP 16.4 s, elementRenderDelay 6060 ms in triage.jq / 15356 ms in the 12.8.2 element audit). A text LCP has no resourceLoad phases (Chrome LCP-breakdown doc: 'If the LCP element doesn't require a resource load ... this time is 0'), so the whole loss is TTFB + render delay, i.e. render-blocking CSS/JS, fonts and the CMP's own JS. platonos (LCP 'p', 2.2 s) was not checked for banner identity.
findings.breaks_when: Breaks nothing by itself; mis-triage wastes the budget on hero images while LCP stays on the banner. Delaying the CMP script to 'fix' it would break consent (legal) and can make the banner paint even later.
findings.how_to_apply: In triage.jq lcp_type = consent-banner-text when the selector matches /cmplz|faz-notice|cookie|consent|cky-|moove|gdpr|cookie-script/i. Branch: (1) keep the CMP out of delay/defer exclusions so it paints with the first frame; (2) ask the client to use the CMP's smaller/bottom-bar layout or a later render so the hero h1/img becomes LCP; (3) fix render delay (fonts, render-blocking CSS) which the banner shares with the hero. Human OK required (legal/marketing).
findings.how_to_verify: After the change triage.jq lcp_selector is the hero (h1.elementor-heading-title or img) and lcp_phases_ms.elementRenderDelay < 500; screenshot shows the banner still appears; PSI mobile LCP element in 'LCP breakdown' is no longer the banner.

findings.claim: Branch (a) cache-first needs a per-stack HIT footprint and must run on the final URL: pallada.gr loses 1107 ms to a 302 / -> /en/ added in .htaccess, and its 'x-powered-by: WP Rocket/3.23.2.1' header is a leftover .htaccess block with no WP Rocket plugin installed.
findings.detail: Observed with read-only curl -I and Novamira read-file: limnoupolis.gr/staging/onar send `x-litespeed-cache: hit` and the HTML ends with `<!-- Page cached by LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1 on ... -->`; cretaforums.gr/voreniahorizon.gr HTML ends with `<!-- cached by FlyingPress on 2026-10-15 ... -->` (CF fork, lowercase 'cached'); pallada.gr/en/, kand, marakaki HTML ends with `Performance optimized by W3 Total Cache ... Served from: <host> @ <time> by W3 Total Cache`; the three dev sites with no cache send nothing and had TTFB 2264-4246 ms in Lighthouse. pallada.gr .htaccess (/home/palladag/public_html/.htaccess) contains `# BEGIN Pallada language redirect ... RewriteRule ^$ https://pallada.gr/en/ [R=302,L]` (comment dated 2026-10-11) followed by `# BEGIN WP Rocket ... Header set X-Powered-By "WP Rocket/3.23.2.1" ... # END WP Rocket` and then `# BEGIN W3TC Page Cache core`; wp-content/advanced-cache.php is W3 Total Cache's drop-in; Novamira agent-context lists W3 Total Cache 2.10.7 and Perfmatters 2.6.9 active, no WP Rocket. Lighthouse 13.5.0 document-latency-insight on https://pallada.gr/ reports `Had redirects (1 redirects, +1107 ms)`, metricSavings FCP 1100 / LCP 1100, serverResponseTime 226 ms (12.8.2 run: 1187 ms redirect, TTFB phase 2817 ms).
findings.breaks_when: Removing the WP Rocket block also removes its Expires/deflate rules (W3TC Browser Cache can replace them) - test static asset caching after; removing the language redirect is an i18n/SEO decision (Polylang default language), not a performance one.
findings.how_to_apply: audit.php: add a cache-footprint probe (fetch home twice, check x-litespeed-cache, 'cached by FlyingPress', 'by W3 Total Cache', 'Performance optimized by WP Rocket' or `x-powered-by: WP Rocket` AND verify the plugin is active; flag `# BEGIN WP Rocket` in .htaccess when inactive). lighthouse.sh: follow redirects first (`curl -sIL -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}'`) and measure that url; print redirect_ms from document-latency-insight as its own finding. Threshold: ttfb_ms > 600 or no footprint -> L1.
findings.how_to_verify: Second request shows the footprint; triage.jq ttfb_ms < 600 and redirect_ms == 0 on the measured url; for pallada compare LCP on https://pallada.gr/en/ (no redirect) with https://pallada.gr/ (1.1 s redirect).

findings.claim: Branch (c): consent gating is the only lever that removed third-party main-thread time to zero on these sites; without it a 5-tag GTM + Facebook pixel costs 1.6-2.9 s of main thread, so 'delay specified scripts' is the second step and needs the marketer's OK.
findings.detail: limnoupolis.gr (Cookie-Script banner, tags not gated): 12.8.2 third-party-summary GTM mainThreadTime 1618 ms / blockingTime 1105 ms, Facebook 915 / 520 ms; third-parties-insight shows one GTM container plus four gtag/AW loaders (G-N4ZCDFPJ4S, AW-11212507349 x2, AW-10939197448), 870 KB. staging.limnoupolis: 2865 ms third-party main thread. pallada.gr (FAZ Cookie Manager gates GTM): third-parties-insight items = [] in both 12.8.2 and 13.5.0, 61/62 requests all first-party. Perfmatters docs: 'Only delay specified scripts' list for GTM = /gtm.js, /gtag/js, gtag(, /gtm-, /gtm. ; Facebook = fbevents.js, fbq(, /busting/facebook-tracking/; optional timeout 15 s (filter perfmatters_delay_js_timeout); turn off JS combine in LiteSpeed/WP Rocket when delaying. FlyingPress CF default js_delay_method 'selected' with js_delay_selected incl. googletagmanager.com, google-analytics.com, fbevents.js, grecaptcha.execute, 10 s timeout (filter flying_press_js_delay_timeout). LiteSpeed: Load JS Deferred = Delayed (`optm-js_defer` 2) runs ALL JS after user activity; JS Delayed Includes (`optm-js_delay_inc`) forces specific scripts; 'Localize Resources' is for google/facebook JS but the inventory says not to localize gtm/gtag (consent + versioning).
findings.breaks_when: Delaying gtm/gtag drops pageview/conversion hits from visitors who bounce without interacting (Perfmatters names this as the reason for the timeout); delaying the CMP itself breaks consent; LiteSpeed 'Delayed' mode also delays Elementor frontend JS (menus, sliders) unless excluded in JS Deferred/Delayed Excludes.
findings.how_to_apply: Trigger: triage.jq third_party_main_thread_ms > 250 or bootup_by_entity entity in {Google Tag Manager, Facebook, Google/Doubleclick Ads} > 250 ms. Step 1 (human OK, marketer): gate GTM behind the CMP (Consent Mode) and merge the 4 gtag loaders into the one GTM container. Step 2: Perfmatters `wp perfmatters enable delay-js` + Delay behavior 'Only delay specified scripts' with the list above; or FlyingPress CF keep js_delay_method=selected; or LiteSpeed `wp litespeed-option set optm-js_delay_inc $'gtm.js\ngtag/js\nfbevents.js'` (Deferred mode does not delay inline JS per docs). Never put gtm/gtag in LiteSpeed Localization Files.
findings.how_to_verify: triage.jq third_party_entities == 0 and bootup_by_entity has no GTM/Facebook before interaction; after a scroll in DevTools the gtm.js request appears (Perfmatters: type="pmdelayedscript" tags present in HTML - 35 on pallada, 53 on marakaki today); GTM Preview shows tags firing on interaction; marketer confirms GA4 realtime.

findings.claim: Per-stack lever matrix: LiteSpeed 7.9.1 exposes every global lever as a `wp litespeed-option` key but has no per-page asset unloading; the CretaForce 'FlyingPress' fork stores everything in option FLYING_PRESS_CONFIG with a local RUCSS engine; W3TC free is page cache only, so Perfmatters owns assets; WP Rocket 3.23 (docs only, not installed anywhere) owns defer/delay/RUCSS via its File Optimization tab.
findings.detail:
MATRIX (lever | LiteSpeed 7.9.1 | FlyingPress-CF 4.22.1 | W3TC 2.10.7 + Perfmatters 2.6.9 | WP Rocket 3.23 docs)
- Page cache | `cache`=true, `cache-mobile`, `cache-priv`, `wp litespeed-purge all` | cache_lifespan, cache_mobile (filter flying_press_cache_mobile), cache_bypass_urls, cache_bypass_cookies | W3TC Page Cache (footer comment 'Served from ... by W3 Total Cache'); Perfmatters none | WP Rocket cache
- Separate mobile cache (needed for Perfmatters device-based disables) | `cache-mobile` | cache_mobile | W3TC 'Cache mobile' | Mobile Cache
- Minify CSS/JS | `optm-css_min`, `optm-js_min` (combine `optm-css_comb`/`optm-js_comb` - keep OFF when delaying) | css_minify, js_minify | `wp perfmatters enable minify-css|minify-js` | File Optimization
- Defer JS | `optm-js_defer`=1 Deferred, excludes `optm-js_defer_exc` | js_defer, js_defer_excludes (fork also moves type=module scripts to </body>) | `wp perfmatters enable defer-js` (+ 'Include Inline Scripts', 'Include jQuery' off by default) | 'Load JavaScript deferred' (data-rocket-defer)
- Delay JS until interaction | `optm-js_defer`=2 Delayed (all JS) + `optm-js_delay_inc` includes; no 'delay specified only' mode | js_delay, js_delay_method selected|all, js_delay_selected, js_delay_all_excludes, timeout 10 s | 'Only delay specified scripts' / 'Delay all scripts', Excluded from Delay, Quick exclusions, 15 s timeout, per-page meta opt-out | 'Delay JavaScript execution' (type="text/rocketlazyloadscript"), One-click exclusions, nowprocket attribute, Safe Mode
- Remove unused CSS | `optm-ucss` (+`optm-ucss_inline`, `optm-ucss_whitelist`) and `optm-css_async`/CCSS - BOTH need QUIC.cloud (fee) | css_rucss, css_rucss_method async|interaction|remove, css_rucss_include_selectors (selectors only), css_rucss_exclude_stylesheets - LOCAL engine, see RUCSS finding | `wp perfmatters enable remove-unused-css`, Used CSS method Inline|File, Stylesheet behavior Delay|Async|Remove, Excluded Selectors, `wp perfmatters clear-used-css` | 'Remove Unused CSS' (SaaS; auto-disabled when Perfmatters RUCSS is on; needs WP-Rocket-SaaS UA allow-listed)
- Fonts | `optm-css_font_display` (Font Display Optimization), `optm-ggfonts_async`, `optm-ggfonts_rm` | fonts_optimize_google_fonts (self-host incl. @import), fonts_display_swap, fonts_preload_urls, bloat_remove_google_fonts | `wp perfmatters enable local-google-fonts` + Display Swap | Google Fonts optimization
- Image lazy-load / LCP priority | `media-lazy` (disables WP core lazy; needs `media-add_missing_sizes`; VPI `media-vpi` needs QUIC.cloud) + metabox 'Disable Image Lazyload' per post | img_lazyload, img_lazyload_exclude_count=2, img_preload (fetchpriority=high on preload), img_width_height, img_responsive | `wp perfmatters enable lazyload-images` (+ exclude leading images) | LazyLoad, Image Dimensions
- iframe/video facade | `media-iframe_lazy` | iframe_lazyload, iframe_youtube_placeholder | `lazyload-iframes` (YouTube preview) | LazyLoad iframes/videos
- Per-page unload of plugin CSS/JS | NOT AVAILABLE (metabox = Disable Cache, Disable Image Lazyload, Viewport Images, VPI Mobile; 'URI Excludes' only disables optimisation) -> recommend Perfmatters Script Manager | NOT AVAILABLE (global excludes only) -> Perfmatters | Script Manager: Everywhere / Current URL / Regex / post type, Testing Mode, MU mode, `wp perfmatters enable script-manager` | NOT AVAILABLE -> Perfmatters
- Bloat (emoji, dashicons, cart fragments, heartbeat, revisions) | `optm-emoji_rm`, `db_optm-revisions_max/age` | bloat_disable_emojis, bloat_disable_dashicons, bloat_disable_woo_cart_fragments, bloat_heartbeat_*, bloat_post_revisions_limit | Perfmatters General toggles | Heartbeat, Database
- Guest Mode | `guest`, `guest_optm` (turn OFF before measuring) | n/a | n/a | n/a
UNAVAILABLE -> RECOMMEND: LiteSpeed-only site (limnoupolis) -> per-page unloading impossible, UCSS/CCSS/VPI cost QUIC.cloud credits -> propose Perfmatters for Script Manager/RUCSS and keep LiteSpeed for cache+fonts+defer only; FlyingPress-CF sites -> no script manager, RUCSS is heuristic -> Perfmatters if per-page unloading is needed; W3TC sites -> W3TC does page cache only, Perfmatters already present on pallada/marakaki (kand has none -> add Perfmatters or FlyingPress). LiteSpeed's own Elementor page (July 27 2026): Optimized Image Loading Disable, Optimized Gutenberg Loading Enable, Inline Font Icons Active, Lazy Load Background Images Inactive when LiteSpeed does the optimisation.
findings.breaks_when: Two plugins doing the same job (e.g. LiteSpeed defer + Perfmatters defer, LiteSpeed media-lazy + Elementor Optimized Image Loading, W3TC minify + Perfmatters minify) - Perfmatters docs say to turn off combine in LiteSpeed/WP Rocket, WP Rocket disables its RUCSS when Perfmatters RUCSS is on, LiteSpeed says disable its Page Optimization when Autoptimize-type plugins run.
findings.how_to_apply: Store the matrix in skills/elementor-debloat/references/fixes.md; debloat.php chooses the owner column from audit.plugins.by_role and refuses a lever whose owner is not installed, printing the recommendation instead. Before-values: LiteSpeed `wp litespeed-option get <key>` or get_option('litespeed.conf.<key>'); FlyingPress-CF get_option('FLYING_PRESS_CONFIG')[key]; Perfmatters `wp perfmatters get-options` + export JSON (`wp perfmatters import-settings <file>` restores).
findings.how_to_verify: `wp litespeed-option all` / `wp perfmatters get-options` / get_option('FLYING_PRESS_CONFIG') show exactly one owner ON per row; HTML footprints: LiteSpeed `data-lazyloaded`/`litespeed` attrs, Perfmatters `pmdelayedscript`, FlyingPress `flying-press-used-css`/`data-src`, WP Rocket `rocketlazyloadscript` appear from one plugin only.
findings.correction: 'W3TC free is page cache only' is wrong: W3TC 2.10.7's readme lists Minify CSS/JS/HTML, Browser Cache, Lazy Load images, Defer non-critical CSS/JS and an Image Converter (WebP/AVIF) in the free tier, with Delay Scripts, Fragment Cache and Lazy Load Google Maps as Pro. So on W3TC+Perfmatters sites the G0 duplicate-owner check must cover W3TC Minify, Lazy Load and Defer against Perfmatters, not just page cache. Everything else in the matrix checks out; two small notes: LiteSpeed's Guest Mode row should say Guest Mode default OFF / Guest Optimization default ON, and the 'Perfmatters lazyload-images + exclude leading images' cell could not be verified (the Perfmatters lazy-load doc URL returned no content).

findings.claim: The 'FlyingPress 4.22.1' on cretaforums.gr/voreniahorizon.gr is a CretaForce fork with its own versioning and update server, and its Remove Unused CSS is a local HTML-selector engine (not the cloud engine in the official docs) - so the inventory's '4.16.x fork' claim is wrong on the number but right in substance, and RUCSS there needs a selector safelist and a visual gate.
findings.detail: wp-content/plugins/flying-press/flying-press.php header: `Plugin Name: FlyingPress`, `Plugin URI: https://www.cretaforce.gr`, `Update URI: https://downloads.cretaforce.gr/wordpress/flying-press/`, `Version: 4.22.1`, `Author: CretaForce`; readme.txt changelog '4.22.1 - 21 September, 2026', '4.21.1 ... Updated the plugin logo to FlyingPress CF', '4.20.1 - Improved LCP image prioritization by detecting one likely large above-fold image and excluding it from lazy loading', '4.20.0 - Added fetchpriority="high" to image preload tags'. Official FlyingPress is at 5.6 (June 24 2026 release post on flyingpress.com). src/Optimizer/CSS.php: `RUCSS_JSON_FORMAT = 'flying-press-local-rucss'`; remove_unused_css() skips logged-in users, collects tags/classes/ids/attributes present in the HTML (DOMDocument) plus class names found by regex `classList.add|classList.toggle|addClass|toggleClass` in page scripts, drops every CSS block whose selectors are not present, inlines the kept CSS as `<style class='flying-press-used-css' original-href=...>` and then applies css_rucss_method: 'async' (media=print + onload swap), 'interaction' (href -> data-href), 'remove' (tag deleted). @font-face and @keyframes are stripped from parsing (kept). Classes Elementor adds at runtime without a literal classList call (e.g. states set via jQuery toggleClass with variables, swiper, sticky, animated/elementor-invisible, e-con states) are not detected unless listed in css_rucss_include_selectors. Options live in get_option('FLYING_PRESS_CONFIG'); defaults in Config.php: css_rucss true, css_rucss_method 'async', js_defer true, js_delay true (selected), js_lazy_render true, img_lazyload true (exclude_count 2), img_preload true, fonts_optimize_google_fonts true, fonts_display_swap true, bloat_disable_emojis/dashicons/oembeds/rss true.
findings.breaks_when: RUCSS strips rules for classes toggled at runtime (sticky header active state, mobile menu open, slider nav, entrance animations' .animated keyframe classes) - symptom is unstyled elements after interaction; 'remove' method removes the fallback entirely; js_lazy_render wraps below-fold content in `<div data-flying-press-lazy-render style="height:1000px"><noscript>` which Googlebot sees only as noscript content.
findings.how_to_apply: Treat it as its own stack 'flyingpress-cf' in audit.php (match Author: CretaForce / Update URI). Before enabling or keeping css_rucss: set css_rucss_method='async' (never 'remove'), add Elementor safelist to css_rucss_include_selectors (elementor-sticky--active, elementor-active, e-n-menu-, swiper-, animated, elementor-invisible, elementor-menu-toggle, elementor-nav-menu--dropdown, wc-, woocommerce-), exclude checkout/booking pages, and run the visual gate (header scrolled, menu open, slider swiped). Capture before-value with get_option('FLYING_PRESS_CONFIG').
findings.how_to_verify: HTML contains `<style class='flying-press-used-css'` and triage.jq render_blocking_fcp_ms drops; screenshots at scroll 0 / after scroll / menu open match the pre-change screenshots; Lighthouse unused_css_kb falls; no console 404 for data-href stylesheets.
findings.correction: Substance confirmed; one number is stale: official FlyingPress is at 5.6.5 (20 August 2026) per flyingpress.com/changelog, not '5.6 (June 24 2026)'. Also note that the fork's default delay list includes 'cookie-law-info' (a CMP script) and js_lazy_render defaults to true - both must be reviewed before relying on the defaults.

findings.claim: Branch (g): LiteSpeed Guest Mode + Guest Optimization serve bots and first visits a maximally optimised page that real repeat visitors do not get, so the plugin must set `guest`=false before any measurement and only re-evaluate it at the end.
findings.detail: LiteSpeed docs (General Settings tab): Guest Mode 'serves a default version of the page from cache for a visitor's first request ... no cache varies ... an AJAX call is used to load the correct version'; warning about momentarily wrong language/pricing (relevant on Polylang/WPML + WooCommerce sites); Guest Optimization (default ON, needs Guest Mode) 'the maximum level of page optimization and image optimization is enacted on this default page even if those features are disabled otherwise ... enabled for bots, certain user agents, and a user's first visit ... will always serve a cached, highly optimized page when services like GTmetrix and PageSpeed Insights request it'. Option keys (base.cls.php): `guest`, `guest_optm`, `guest_uas`, `guest_ips`; related `optm-guest_only` (optimise non-logged-in only, default ON) and `optm-gm_js_exc`. UCSS Inline is 'not automatically enabled for Guest Mode pages'.
findings.breaks_when: Nothing breaks when turned off; leaving it on makes PSI/Lighthouse numbers unreproducible and hides regressions (optimisations the agent 'adds' were already applied to bots).
findings.how_to_apply: debloat.php action `ls_guest_off`: before-value `get_option('litespeed.conf.guest')`, then `wp litespeed-option set guest false` (and `guest_optm false`), `wp litespeed-purge all`; measure. Document that Guest Mode may be re-enabled only as a last, separately measured step with the client told about the first-visit flash risk.
findings.how_to_verify: `wp litespeed-option get guest` prints false; first and second curl of the home page return the same HTML (no guest-mode AJAX swap); Lighthouse numbers match PSI within the CPU-multiplier difference.

findings.claim: Branch (h): on WooCommerce/booking sites the exclusion lists must exist before cache, defer, delay or RUCSS are touched - Perfmatters auto-excludes cart/checkout/account, LiteSpeed and the CF fork do not know your booking URLs, and limnoupolis' home page already pays 258 ms each for booking-calendar and WooCommerce CSS that only Perfmatters could unload per page.
findings.detail: Perfmatters docs: 'we automatically exclude specific URLs from optimizations when running WooCommerce (cart, checkout, account) for compatibility reasons' and per-post opt-outs for Delay/Defer/Unused CSS; Script Manager disables by Everywhere / Current URL / Regex / post type with Testing Mode. LiteSpeed third-party page lists WooCommerce as confirmed compatible but the per-page metabox only offers Disable Cache / Disable Image Lazyload / VPI; cache exclusions are global (`cache-exc` URIs). FlyingPress-CF: cache_bypass_urls, cache_bypass_cookies, js_defer_excludes, js_delay_all_excludes, css_rucss_exclude_stylesheets (global). Lighthouse limnoupolis render-blocking-insight: wp-simple-booking-calendar-premium style-front-end.min.css 258 ms, woocommerce.css 12.5 KB 258 ms, jquery-ui.min.css from cdnjs 885 ms on the HOME page. pallada.gr runs WooCommerce 11.2.1 + WooCommerce Bookings 3.11.0 + Product Add-Ons + Stripe + Nexi XPay; marakaki/kand/pallada run JetSmartFilters (AJAX filtering).
findings.breaks_when: Page-caching a booking step or cart with a cached nonce/fragment, delaying jquery.min.js or the calendar JS (date picker never initialises until mouse move), RUCSS stripping datepicker/jQuery-UI classes, lazy-rendering the booking form (CF fork js_lazy_render) - all break the money path silently.
findings.how_to_apply: G3 in the tree: generate exclusion lists from audit.php (plugins.by_role booking|filters|woocommerce) -> cache bypass: /cart/, /checkout/, /my-account/, booking confirmation/payment URLs, any URL with jsf= or ?filter; defer/delay excludes: jquery.min.js, jquery-ui, wp-simple-booking-calendar, wc-bookings, yith-wcbk, jet-smart-filters, stripe, nexi; RUCSS: exclude checkout/booking pages (Perfmatters page meta 'Unused CSS' unchecked). Per-page unloading of WooCommerce/booking CSS on brochure pages only with Perfmatters Script Manager in Testing Mode first.
findings.how_to_verify: Click-through on mobile emulation after each lever: open date picker, pick dates, add to cart, reach payment step; no 'is not defined' console errors; cache footprint absent on cart/checkout responses; JetSmartFilters results update without reload.

findings.claim: Branch (i): when Elementor's Editor V4 opt-in (e_opt_in_v4 / atomic elements) is active, RUCSS/UCSS must stay opt-in and gated: V4 emits per-document local and global stylesheets that Perfmatters only learned to exclude in 2.6.9 (2026-10-06), Elementor still positions V4 for staging, and the CF fork's local RUCSS has no such exclusion.
findings.detail: Perfmatters changelog 2.6.9 - 10.06.2026: 'Added built-in Remove Unused CSS exclusions for Elementor's new local and global per-document stylesheets' and 'Updated delay JS quick exclusions for Elementor to include hooks.min.js and i18n.min.js to fix a dependency error'. Elementor help 'Explore the V4 features' (June 11 2025): after opting in, V4 elements sit next to 3.x widgets; every element has a local class, classes managed in the Class Manager. Elementor's experiments page for V4 states staging-only testing (via search summary; the help page itself did not state it). Elementor 3.25 developers update: Pro modules now load per-widget CSS ('Modules with multiple widgets will load only the style belonging to that widget'), which already reduces unused CSS without RUCSS. Confidence is medium because I could not open a page naming the experiment id e_opt_in_v4 or describing V4's CSS output in detail.
findings.breaks_when: RUCSS removes V4 local/global class rules (styles vanish on atomic elements), especially with the CF fork's 'remove' method or any RUCSS older than Perfmatters 2.6.9; delay-all without hooks.min.js/i18n.min.js exclusions throws dependency errors.
findings.how_to_apply: audit.php already reads experiments; add `v4_active = features.e_opt_in_v4 == on OR usage.widgets has e-* atomic types`. If true: skip L6 unless Perfmatters >= 2.6.9 is the RUCSS owner; never enable LiteSpeed UCSS or CF-fork css_rucss automatically; Perfmatters delay quick exclusion 'Elementor' must be ticked. Report V4 as 'staging-only per Elementor' when found on production.
findings.how_to_verify: After RUCSS: screenshots of V4 pages at 3 breakpoints identical; `<style>` for e-* local classes still present in HTML; no console dependency errors with delay on.
findings.correction: The gating advice stands, but 'Elementor still positions V4 for staging' is stale: Elementor's V4 FAQ says 'Atomic features are stable, safe for production, and are already used in real production environments', and the 4.0 developers update (4.0 launched April 2026) makes the Atomic Editor 'the default experience for all new websites' while existing sites keep v3 until they opt in. So the plugin should NOT report V4 on production as 'staging-only'; it should still gate RUCSS because the Perfmatters exclusion is 10 days old and the CF fork has none. Detection: Novamira elementor-check-setup on cretaforums (Elementor 4.3.4) reports the atomic runtime loaded but `e_atomic_elements` OFF, so v4_active must test e_atomic_elements (and the presence of e-* element types), not only e_opt_in_v4.

findings.claim: Draft auto-actions audit: remove element_cache_on, gate optimized_markup_on on a custom-code grep, split litespeed_optimize into one-key actions with wp litespeed-option before-values and no gtm/gtag localisation, keep video_lazy only as a reported fix, keep revisions_prune behind confirm and run it last.
findings.detail: element_cache_on (sets elementor_element_cache_ttl=24): Elementor help (Sep 15 2026) 'Element Caching cannot be used on elements that contain dynamic tags or any other type of dynamic information, such as shortcodes ... inactive by default ... only activate caching on static elements'; it reduces server render time/TTFB only, which a page cache already removes for the measured (cached) page -> not a PageSpeed lever on cached sites; pallada (bookings, Dynamic.ooo, JetSmartFilters) has it disabled deliberately. REMOVE. optimized_markup_on: developers.elementor.com 3.25 - the experiment removes `.elementor-button-wrapper` on Button, PayPal Button, Stripe Button and 'future releases will remove additional HTML elements'; breaks only custom CSS/JS querying removed wrappers; Elementor help 'Optimized DOM Output and custom code' lists earlier removed wrappers (.elementor-section-wrap, .elementor-image, .elementor-text-editor, now core since 3.19). CHANGE: before enabling, grep `_elementor_data` custom_css, kit custom CSS, theme CSS and HTML widgets for `elementor-button-wrapper` (and for selectors removed in the running 4.3.x version, list to be read from the changelog of that version); if hits -> report instead of enabling; always screenshot pages with custom_css>0 (onar has it off, 251 HTML widgets on limnoupolis). litespeed_optimize (one shot: ggfonts_async + css_min + js_min + localize + js_defer): REPLACE with five actions, each `get_option('litespeed.conf.<key>')` before, `wp litespeed-purge all` after, measured separately: ls_font_display (`optm-css_font_display`=swap) -> ls_css_min (`optm-css_min`) -> ls_js_min (`optm-js_min`) -> ls_js_defer (`optm-js_defer`=1 Deferred; add Elementor/jQuery exclusions to `optm-js_defer_exc` on failure) -> ls_ggfonts_async (`optm-ggfonts_async`) only if fonts.googleapis.com is still requested after the font lever (self-hosted fonts make it a no-op). Never `optm-localize` with gtm/gtag in Localization Files (docs describe it as copying Google/Facebook JS locally, which freezes tag versions and bypasses consent). Keep `media-lazy` OFF (CLS 0 -> 0.107 on staging; docs: it also needs `media-add_missing_sizes`). video_lazy: keep as a reported fix with before-backup; it is a scoring lever only when the widget shows a thumbnail instead of loading the player (inventory: requires an image overlay; not verified in Elementor docs). revisions_prune: not a scoring lever (DB size), keep behind $revision_confirm, run after all front-end levers. fa4_shim_off and expired_transients: keep as is. New automatic actions: ls_guest_off (see Guest Mode finding), redirect_report (document-latency redirectDuration>0), owner_conflict_report (two optimisers).
findings.breaks_when: element cache on dynamic widgets shows stale prices/availability; optimized markup breaks custom CSS targeting removed wrappers; one-shot litespeed_optimize makes a regression unattributable and localised gtm.js goes stale; LiteSpeed lazy-load without sizes causes CLS.
findings.how_to_apply: Edit skills/elementor-debloat/scripts/debloat.php: delete case 'element_cache_on'; in 'optimized_markup_on' add `$hits = $wpdb->get_var("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {$wpdb->postmeta} WHERE meta_key='_elementor_data' AND meta_value LIKE '%elementor-button-wrapper%'")` + theme/kit CSS grep and skip when >0; replace 'litespeed_optimize' with ls_font_display, ls_css_min, ls_js_min, ls_js_defer, ls_ggfonts_async each doing one $set_option('litespeed.conf.<key>') and do_action('litespeed_purge_all'); add ls_guest_off. Update the table in SKILL.md and fixes.md accordingly.
findings.how_to_verify: Each action's report line shows before -> after value; Lighthouse (triage.jq) run between actions attributes the delta; `wp litespeed-option get optm-localize` stays false; pages with custom_css screenshot-identical after optimized markup; no `data-lazyloaded` attributes on LiteSpeed sites.

findings.claim: Stopping rules: report 'what is left' per metric with its culprit from the insights, and declare 95 unreachable without a design change when the LCP is a canvas/video or the critical chain contains three.js/.glb, when first-party JS bootup stays above ~2 s after defer, or when third-party main thread stays >250 ms because the marketer refuses gating/delay.
findings.detail: Targets (inventory): LCP <= 1.55 s, TBT <= 65 ms, CLS <= 0.04, FCP <= 1.1 s, SI <= 2.0 s; weights FCP 10 / SI 10 / LCP 25 / TBT 30 / CLS 25 (Chrome scoring page, unchanged in 13 per the 13.0 blog: 'no changes to the performance scoring'). RESIDUAL REPORT after each step (from triage.jq): LCP -> lcp_type + lcp_selector + dominant phase (ttfb / resourceLoadDelay / resourceLoadDuration / elementRenderDelay) + lcp_discovery flags; TBT -> bootup_by_entity top 3 + long_tasks count + mainthread-work-breakdown groups (pallada 13.5: scriptEvaluation 1484 ms, styleLayout 1048 ms, jquery.min.js 916 ms scripting); CLS -> cls_culprits (limnoupolis hero section 0.103); FCP -> render_blocking_top + fonts_no_swap + redirect_ms; SI -> longest_chain_ms + image_waste_kb + lcp phases. ESCALATE TO DESIGN when: (1) lcp_type in {video, canvas} or longest chain includes /three|\.glb|webgl|\.mp4/ (limnoupolis: / -> GLTFLoader.js -> buoy.glb, 7797 ms; TBT 142 s in a GPU-less lab) ; (2) first-party bootup_by_entity > 2000 ms after defer+delay-specified (cretaforums 8531 ms, voreniahorizon 8664 ms, pallada 3673-4121 ms, onar 3918 ms - these are Elementor+addons+theme JS, not third parties); (3) third_party_main_thread_ms > 250 after the marketer declined consent gating or delay; (4) LCP is the consent banner and the client declines a banner change; (5) animations on the first screen (voreniahorizon 160, pallada 90) that the designer wants to keep while elementRenderDelay > 500 ms. MEASUREMENT CAVEATS to print with every verdict: local CLI used cpuSlowdownMultiplier 4 (both 12.8.2 and 13.5.0 runs) vs PSI's 1.2, so local TBT/SI are pessimistic; benchmarkIndex 1181-2090 here; PSI API returned 429 'Queries per day ... quota_limit_value 0' today, so a PSI confirmation needs a key with quota; declare a 95 verdict only from PSI or from a local run with `--throttling.cpuSlowdownMultiplier=1.2` (flag name not re-verified).
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break; the failure mode is endless tuning: no lever below the design level can take limnoupolis (3D hero), onar (16 s LCP from a late-painted banner + 38 motion effects) or cretaforums (8.5 s first-party JS) to 95.
findings.how_to_apply: Add a 'Residual' block to the debloater's report template: for each metric above target print value, target, culprit (fields above) and the next lever or 'DESIGN CHANGE REQUIRED: <reason>'. Add the escalation rules as explicit checks in SKILL.md; stop the loop when two consecutive levers improve the target metric by < 5 % or when an escalation rule fires.
findings.how_to_verify: The report for limnoupolis.gr names the .glb chain and stops; for pallada.gr it names the banner + redirect and jquery.min.js bootup; PSI mobile on the final url agrees with the local verdict within one score band.
findings.correction: (1) The 'first-party JS bootup > 2 s' rule and the quoted figures (cretaforums 8531, voreniahorizon 8664, pallada 3673-4121, onar 3918) are sums of bootup-time `total`, which Lighthouse computes per URL including style/layout work; the audit's own numericValue sums only scripting + scriptParseCompile for URLs >= 50 ms (cretaforums 2804 ms). Either define the rule on scripting+scriptParseCompile (then cretaforums is ~2.8 s, still over) or call the metric 'main-thread by URL' and set the threshold accordingly. (2) The PSI CPU multiplier: `--throttling.cpuSlowdownMultiplier` is the correct flag (Lighthouse readme and docs/throttling.md), but '1.2' for PSI is a DebugBear statement (PSI moved 4x -> 1.2x in Dec 2024), not confirmed by any Google page I opened; treat as plausible and read lighthouseResult.configSettings.throttling.cpuSlowdownMultiplier from a real PSI response once quota is available. (3) Since Lighthouse 13 shipped to PSI in Oct 2025, a 12-pinned local run no longer matches PSI's audit set.

findings.claim: Googlebot guard: Google states that Google Search does not interact with the page and declines permission prompts, so scripts delayed until interaction never execute for Googlebot - the plugin must exclude every content-producing script from delay and verify with URL Inspection's rendered HTML; neither the WP Rocket nor the Perfmatters pages opened make any statement about crawlers.
findings.detail: Google 'Fix lazy-loaded content' (last updated 2025-12-10): lazy-loading must not 'rely on user actions, such as scrolling or clicking, to load content, which is important as Google Search does not interact with your page'; test by checking the rendered HTML in the URL Inspection Tool (src present on /
