findings.breaks_when: Delay-all or an over-broad specified list delays a script that injects indexable content -> that content is missing from the rendered HTML and drops out of the index; lazy-render placeholders hide below-fold content behind noscript.
findings.how_to_apply: Default to 'delay specified scripts' (tags, pixels, chat, maps) and never delay-all without the check; exclude Elementor frontend/webpack/hooks/i18n (Perfmatters 'Elementor' quick exclusion), JetSmartFilters, loop/load-more, reviews, forum JS; keep FlyingPress-CF js_lazy_render off on content pages. Verification step in the debloat loop after any delay change: Search Console > URL Inspection > Test live URL > View tested page > HTML (grep for a sentence from each JS-produced block) and Screenshot; also run `npx lighthouse` 'Screenshot thumbnails' / final-screenshot to see whether elementor-invisible sections are blank.
findings.how_to_verify: Rendered HTML in URL Inspection contains the loop/filter/forum text; src present for lazy images; screenshot not blank in the hero; GA4/GTM still fire on interaction; no 'Page partially loaded' resource errors for delayed scripts in the 'More info' tab.

findings.claim: Branches (d) and (e): the font-display and render-blocking insights name the exact files to fix (Modak/Poppins .woff without swap, an 18-variant Open Sans Google Fonts CSS costing 841 ms, materialdesignicons CDN 780 ms), and text-LCP sites lose their LCP mostly in elementRenderDelay, which tracks first-screen entrance animations and blocking fonts/CSS.
findings.detail: limnoupolis font-display-insight: Modak-Regular.woff 170 ms, Poppins-Regular.woff (metricSavings FCP 150); render-blocking-insight: fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Open+Sans:100..900italic&display=swap 841 ms, cdnjs jquery-ui.min.css 885 ms; staging: cdn.jsdelivr.net materialdesignicons.min.css 780 ms (render_blocking_fcp_ms 3850). onar: font-display 200 ms, render-blocking 1850 ms. Text-LCP render delays: voreniahorizon h1 2693 ms (160 entrance animations, 12 motion fx), cretaforums 1393 ms (76 animations), pallada 478-504 ms (90 animations). audit-summary fonts: limnoupolis 3 kit families + 4 in widgets, marakaki 3 + 6, onar 3 + 2. Perfmatters delay doc: Elementor needs exclusions 'if you're using a lot of animations' (frontend.min.js, webpack.runtime, elements-handlers etc.), i.e. animated first-screen elements depend on JS to become visible. LiteSpeed Elementor page recommends Inline Font Icons: Active (e_font_icon_svg) and Font Display Optimization = swap applies to all @font-face before caching CSS.
findings.breaks_when: Cutting families/weights changes typography (visual OK needed); Greek text falls back to a system font if the kept font lacks the Greek subset (keep Greek+Latin subsets when self-hosting); removing animations is a design decision; FA4 shim off removes `fa fa-` icons if still used (script already checks).
findings.how_to_apply: Order inside L4/L5: (1) convert custom .woff/.ttf to .woff2 with Greek subset, font-display swap (LiteSpeed `optm-css_font_display`=swap, CF fonts_display_swap, Perfmatters Display Swap) - auto; (2) cut kit to 2 families x 2-3 weights, exact weights only (visual); (3) self-host Google Fonts (Perfmatters local-google-fonts, CF fonts_optimize_google_fonts) or LiteSpeed `optm-ggfonts_async` if still remote; (4) e_font_icon_svg Active, `elementor_load_fa4_shim` off, drop CDN icon fonts (materialdesignicons) in favour of inline SVG; (5) when lcp_type is text and elementRenderDelay > 500: remove `_animation`/`motion_fx_*` from elements whose boundingRect top < 800 px in the LCP viewport (backup `_elementor_data`), visual check.
findings.how_to_verify: triage.jq fonts_no_swap == [] and font_display_fcp_ms null/0; render_blocking_top has no fonts.googleapis/cdnjs/jsdelivr entries; network-requests Font count <= 6; lcp_phases_ms.elementRenderDelay < 500 on text-LCP pages; Greek headings render in the intended font (screenshot of a Greek page).

findings.claim: Image lazy-load must have exactly one owner per site and it should not be LiteSpeed's `media-lazy`: the hero on limnoupolis is lazy-loaded with no fetchpriority (4.3 s load delay), onar already carries LiteSpeed `data-lazyloaded` attributes next to Perfmatters, and LiteSpeed's docs tie its lazy-load to QUIC.cloud VPI and Add Missing Sizes to avoid exactly the CLS seen on staging.
findings.detail: limnoupolis LCP img snippet ``, lcp-discovery priorityHinted false / eagerlyLoaded false, 12.8.2 element audit Load Delay 4270 ms (55 % of LCP). onar-seaside-lounge.gr HTML today contains 11 `data-lazyloaded` attributes (LiteSpeed lazy-load active) while Perfmatters 2.6.x is also installed. LiteSpeed docs: Lazy Load Images 'When you turn this option ON, the WordPress core Lazy Load feature is automatically disabled'; Add Missing Sizes 'works only when Lazy Load Images is ON'; Viewport Images (VPI) excludes above-fold images from lazy-load but 'uses the QUIC.cloud Page Optimization service ... a fee may apply'; 'Preload Featured Image' was removed in favour of VPI. Elementor's own Performance tab has 'Optimized Image Loading: applying fetchpriority="high" on LCP images and loading="lazy" on images below the fold' (LiteSpeed's Elementor page says to disable it when LiteSpeed does lazy-load - so pick one). FlyingPress-CF: img_lazyload with img_lazyload_exclude_count=2 and img_preload adding fetchpriority=high (changelog 4.20.0/4.20.1). Inventory: LiteSpeed lazy-load raised CLS 0 -> 0.107 on staging.
findings.breaks_when: Two lazy-loaders stack (double placeholders, broken srcset), LiteSpeed lazy-load without VPI lazy-loads the hero and without Add Missing Sizes shifts layout; disabling Elementor's Optimized Image Loading while no other owner adds fetchpriority leaves the LCP undiscoverable.
findings.how_to_apply: Owner rule in L2-img: LiteSpeed-only sites -> `media-lazy` false, Elementor Optimized Image Loading = Enable (owner Elementor); FlyingPress-CF sites -> img_lazyload true + img_preload true, Elementor Optimized Image Loading = Disable; W3TC+Perfmatters sites -> Perfmatters lazyload-images with the first 2 images excluded, Elementor's off. Widget-level fallback: Image widget > Lazy Load = No on the hero. Record before-values (`litespeed.conf.media-lazy`, FLYING_PRESS_CONFIG.img_lazyload, Perfmatters lazyload-images, elementor_optimized_image_loading).
findings.how_to_verify: triage.jq lcp_lazy false, lcp_discovery.priorityHinted true, resourceLoadDelay < 300 ms; cls <= 0.04 on 3 runs; HTML has lazy attributes from one source only (`data-lazyloaded` xor `loading="lazy"` from Elementor/Perfmatters).

findings.claim: Lighthouse 13's third-parties-insight has no blockingTime, so TBT attribution per vendor must come from joining bootup-time (per-URL total/scripting) with network-requests.entity; the join works identically on 12.8.2 and 13.5.0 and exposes that most TBT on these sites is first-party Elementor/theme/addon JS.
findings.detail: third-parties-insight headings in both versions: entity, transferSize, mainThreadTime (subItems: url, mainThreadTime, transferSize). network-requests items carry `entity` (e.g. 'Google Tag Manager', 'Facebook', or the first-party domain). bootup-time items: url, total, scripting, scriptParseCompile; long-tasks items: url, startTime, duration; mainthread-work-breakdown items: group, duration. triage.jq `bootup_by_entity` output: limnoupolis first-party 165,909 ms (three.js), GTM 1618, Facebook 915; staging first-party 3824, GTM 1953, Facebook 855; pallada 13.5 first-party 3673 (jquery.min.js scripting 916 ms, faz-cookie-manager script 194 ms long task), unattributable 573; cretaforums first-party 8531; voreniahorizon 8664; onar 3918 + GTM 599; marakaki 1480. The 12.8.2 third-party-summary blockingTime for limnoupolis (GTM 1105, Facebook 520) is no longer available in 13.x; long-tasks per URL is the closest blocking-time proxy.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break; mis-attribution happens if the join uses subdomain-only matching (use the `entity` field, not the host).
findings.how_to_apply: Use the `$bt` block of triage.jq (first(select(.url==$b.url)).entity; 'Unattributable' kept separately). Decision thresholds: third-party entity > 250 ms -> L3; first-party > 2000 ms after defer -> escalate (design/addons); long_tasks > 10 with first-party urls -> list the top 3 urls (Elementor frontend, addon packs, theme) as unload candidates for Perfmatters Script Manager.
findings.how_to_verify: Sum of bootup_by_entity main_thread_ms equals .audits["bootup-time"].numericValue within rounding; third-party sum matches third-parties-insight mainThreadTime sum on the same run.
findings.correction: Headings and the join are right, but the verification rule 'Sum of bootup_by_entity main_thread_ms equals bootup-time numericValue within rounding' is false: triage.jq sums `total`, while bootup-time.numericValue sums scripting + scriptParseCompile and only for URLs whose total >= 50 ms (cretaforums: items total 9172 ms vs numericValue 2804 ms). Fix: either sum scripting+scriptParseCompile per entity (then the check holds, minus sub-threshold URLs) or keep `total` and verify against the sum of items instead. The first-party figures quoted (8531/8664/3673/3918) are therefore 'main thread attributed to URL', not JS execution time; TBT also depends on long-task structure, so 'long-tasks' per URL remains the better blocking proxy as the finding says.

findings.claim: On 12.8.2 runs the legacy largest-contentful-paint-element phase table is unreliable for text LCP (negative Render Delay, inflated TTFB), so even 12.8.2 files must be read through lcp-breakdown-insight, never the legacy audit.
findings.detail: pallada 12.8.2: legacy phases TTFB 2817 / Load Delay 0 / Load Time 0 / Render Delay -344 ms, while lcp-breakdown-insight gives timeToFirstByte 2817 + elementRenderDelay 504 (LCP 2473). platonos: legacy Render Delay -734 vs insight 433. onar: legacy Render Delay 15356 vs insight 6060 (LCP 16375). cretaforums: 3621 vs 1393. The insight values are the ones that sum to the LCP and that PSI shows; the legacy table mixes the redirect into TTFB and can go negative. For image LCP (limnoupolis) the two also disagree: legacy Load Delay 4270 / Load Time 1840 vs insight resourceLoadDelay 548 / resourceLoadDuration 573 - the insight is computed from the trace engine and matches Chrome's LCP-breakdown doc.
findings.breaks_when: not known to break
findings.how_to_apply: In triage.jq and lighthouse.sh never read .audits["largest-contentful-paint-element"].details.items[1]; use lcp-breakdown-insight for phases on both 12.x and 13.x and drop the legacy fallback entirely.
findings.how_to_verify: For each local 12.8.2 file, sum of lcp_phases_ms equals .audits["largest-contentful-paint"].numericValue within 1 ms; the legacy table does not.

findings.claim: The CretaForce FlyingPress fork's DEFAULT delay list contains a cookie-consent script ('cookie-law-info') and js_lazy_render defaults to true, so on fresh FlyingPress-CF installs the plugin must audit and prune the delay list and switch lazy render off before the Googlebot/consent rules can hold.
findings.detail: Config.php $initial_config on cretaforums: js_delay true, js_delay_method 'selected', js_delay_selected = googletagmanager.com, google-analytics.com, googleoptimize.com, adsbygoogle.js, xfbml.customerchat.js, fbevents.js, widget.manychat.com, cookie-law-info, grecaptcha.execute, static.hotjar.com, hs-scripts.com, embed.tawk.to, disqus.com/embed.js, client.crisp.chat, matomo.js, usefathom.com, code.tidio.co, metomic.io, js.driftt.com, cdn.onesignal.com, clarity.ms; js_lazy_render true; img_lazyload true with exclude_count 2; img_preload true; self_host_third_party_css_js true; cache_mobile is forced from the filter flying_press_cache_mobile (default false), so Perfmatters device-based toggles need that filter, not a setting.
findings.breaks_when: Delaying the CMP (CookieYes/cookie-law-info or any CMP matched by a list entry) delays consent itself and can make the banner paint even later or the LCP shift; js_lazy_render hides below-fold HTML behind a placeholder for crawlers.
findings.how_to_apply: audit.php for stack 'flyingpress-cf': read get_option('FLYING_PRESS_CONFIG'); flag any js_delay_selected entry matching the CMP regex (cmplz|faz|cookie|consent|cky|moove|gdpr) and js_lazy_render=true on content pages; report before-values. Debloat: remove CMP entries from js_delay_selected, set js_lazy_render false unless the client accepts the SEO risk; keep cache_mobile via add_filter('flying_press_cache_mobile','__return_true') when device-specific optimisations are used.
findings.how_to_verify: After the change the HTML has no data-flying-press-lazy-render wrappers (0 today on cretaforums/voreniahorizon) and the CMP script tag has a normal src; banner appears on first paint in a mobile-emulated screenshot.

findings.claim: Lighthouse's 'server responds quickly' and the L1 TTFB trigger share one constant: the DevTools document-latency insight fails at serverResponseTime >= 600 ms (TOO_SLOW_THRESHOLD_MS = 600, 'we want devs to shoot for 100ms'), so the plugin's threshold should be read as the insight's own pass/fail rather than a hand-picked 600.
findings.detail: devtools-frontend front_end/models/trace/insights/DocumentLatency.ts: '// We set our failure threshold to 600ms to avoid those false positives but we want devs to shoot for 100ms.' const TOO_SLOW_THRESHOLD_MS = 600; failedRedirects string 'Had redirects ({PH1} redirects, +{PH2})'. In the local files .details.items.serverResponseIsFast.value is true at 575 ms (limnoupolis) and 226 ms (pallada13).
findings.breaks_when: not known to break
findings.how_to_apply: In triage.jq expose ttfb_fast = .audits["document-latency-insight"].details.items.serverResponseIsFast.value and redirect flag noRedirects; make L1 fire on ttfb_fast == false OR no cache footprint; keep 600 only as documentation of the constant.
findings.how_to_verify: ttfb_fast flips to true after enabling the page cache on a dev site whose TTFB was 2.2-4.2 s; the insight's 'Server responds quickly' row turns green in the HTML report.

findings.claim: Elementor's current Features-tab inventory (help page June 19 2026) lists only 'Optimized Control Loading' and 'Element Caching' as experiments and Inline Font Icons / Additional Custom Breakpoints as stable; Optimized Markup is not on the page, so the plugin must enumerate experiments from the live site (elementor_experiment-* options or the Experiments manager) instead of a hard-coded list, and must read atomic state from e_atomic_elements.
findings.detail: what-are-performance-experiments (Last Update June 19 2026): 'Experimental features found in the Features tab: Optimized Control Loading ... Element Caching'; 'Stable features found in the Features tab: Inline font Icons ... Additional Custom Breakpoints'; 'Stable features found in the Performance tab: Optimized Image Loading, Optimized Gutenberg Loading, Lazy Load Background Images'. audit-summary nevertheless reports optimized_markup on/off per site, so the option key still exists in 4.2-4.3. Novamira elementor-check-setup on cretaforums (Elementor 4.3.4 / Pro 4.3.1) returns atomic.runtime_available false with the note 'the v4 atomic runtime is loaded but the `e_atomic_elements` experiment is OFF, so no `e-*` element type is registered'. Elementor's wordpress.org readme shows 4.3.5 (2026-10-13) as stable and 4.3.0 (2026-09-22) adding Elementor MCP, Background Video, Accordion, Default Styles - all V4-side features.
findings.breaks_when: not known to break; a hard-coded experiment list silently misses features that were promoted to core or renamed between 4.2.3 and 4.3.5.
findings.how_to_apply: audit.php: read all options LIKE 'elementor_experiment-%' plus elementor_element_cache_ttl, elementor_optimized_image_loading, elementor_optimized_gutenberg_loading, elementor_lazy_load_background_images, and set v4_active = experiment e_atomic_elements == active (or e_opt_in_v4 == active); print 'unknown experiment' for keys not in the plugin's reference so the knowledge base can be updated per version.
findings.how_to_verify: On cretaforums the audit prints e_atomic_elements inactive and v4_active=false; on a fresh 4.x install it prints active (atomic default on new sites per the V4 FAQ).

findings.claim: Lighthouse 13 has been PSI's engine since mid-October 2025, so the 12-pinned lighthouse.sh produces audit sets PSI no longer shows and must be unpinned now; locally only lighthouse@13 reproduces PSI's insight ids.
findings.detail: Chrome blog (Oct 10 2025): 'Lighthouse 13 is available immediately on the command line through npm, in Chrome Canary, and will be available in PageSpeed Insights within the next week. It will land in Chrome stable in Chrome 143.' lighthouse.sh header comment still says 'pinned to Lighthouse 12 - 13.x removed/renamed third-party-summary, render-blocking-resources, largest-contentful-paint-element and font-display'. The local results.jsonl fields dom, img_kb, third_party_kb, lcp_lazy and font_display_fail come from removed audits (img_kb is already 0 on every row because uses-optimized-images rarely fires).
findings.breaks_when: not known to break the site; a 12-only script cannot be cross-checked against PSI once quota returns.
findings.how_to_apply: Replace `npx lighthouse` with `npx -y lighthouse@13` in lighthouse.sh and swap the inline jq for triage.jq; delete the pin comment.
findings.how_to_verify: `jq .lighthouseVersion` on a new run prints 13.x; PSI's lighthouseResult.lighthouseVersion (once quota allows) also prints 13.x and the same audit keys.

title: Replacing JS heroes on mobile without breaking page cache: responsive visibility, device-vary, facades (Elementor 4.3.5 / Pro 4.3.x)
summary: The single safe, cache-neutral way to serve phones a static hero while desktops keep a three.js canvas, an autoplay MP4 or a Lottie is a client-side facade: one responsive tree, a first-paint Image-widget poster (eager, width/height, no entrance animation) and a tiny inline module loader that imports the heavy asset only when `matchMedia('(min-width:1025px)')` (optionally `(hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)`) is true. Elementor's own 'Hide on Mobile' is confirmed in the deployed 4.3.5 frontend.min.css to be nothing but `display:none`; an empirical Chromium 141 test under Lighthouse-style emulation shows eager and fetchpriority=high images, autoplay `
critic_notes: Method: WebFetch could not resolve DNS in this sandbox, so every doc page was fetched with curl through the proxy and text-extracted; raw source files were pulled from GitHub/SVN at the exact tags named (Elementor 4.3.5, Lighthouse main = 13.5.0 and v12.8.2, LSCWP master = readme Stable tag 7.9.1, DVE trunk = 6.0.6, WordPress master, Chromium main). I re-ran the researcher's Playwright test independently with the system Playwright (Chromium 141.0.7390.37) and extended it with a second page (critic/site/t2.html) to test <source media>, <picture> and preload media; results are in this session only and not written outside the scratchpad (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/critic/). Live-site checks were read-only GETs of voreniahorizon.gr and pallada.gr (pallada answered 302 at the root, so its hidden-tree counts were not re-verified). Local Lighthouse JSONs (12.8.2) were read to confirm the MP4 bytes, LCP nodes and TBT figures quoted. Not checked: Elementor Pro Lottie internals (closed source), Elementor Pro plan tiers for Display Conditions, the agency's FlyingPress fork options, Cloudflare plan limits beyond the docs page, and how WP Rocket/Perfmatters/FlyingPress treat `<script type=\"importmap\">`. Elementor 4.x applicability: all code citations are 4.3.5 (the deployed version); the v4 Atomic 'Display: None' is documented as the same per-breakpoint CSS mechanism but I did not inspect atomic-element CSS output. Skipped: re-parsing container order on the three video sites and rerunning Lighthouse. Risk for the plugin: the draft's fixes.md line 7 and every recipe step that says 'Image widget > Lazy Load' must be rewritten before the knowledge base ships, or the debloat agent will hunt for a control that does not exist.
open_questions: FlyingPress-CF fork: does it expose 'Separate Mobile Cache and Optimizations' (official doc May 21, 2025) or the older `flying_press_cache_mobile` filter, and does FlyingCDN honour the vary? Not verifiable from docs; check the fork's settings/source read-only before any UA-based rendering on cretaforums.gr/voreniahorizon.gr.

Elementor Pro 4.3.x Lottie internals (private source): whether 'Lazy Load' defers the .json fetch when the widget is display:none on mobile, and whether the lottie library is enqueued regardless. Inferred from docs only.

Elementor v4 atomic elements: 'Display: None' per breakpoint is documented as the hide mechanism; its generated CSS was not inspected in source (behaviour inferred from the v3 rules and the help article).
Image widget 'Image Resolution' responsiveness per device in 4.3 (would allow a smaller mobile poster in one tree) was not verified.
Field INP/LCP (CrUX) for the 10 sites was not fetched (no API key in this session); the INP justification rests on web.dev guidance and lab TBT.

Whether Playwright's `hasTouch` and Lighthouse's `Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled` produce identical hover/pointer media results in every Chromium version (confirmed for Chromium 141 via Playwright; Lighthouse 13.5 bundles Chrome 136-era UA).
Cloudflare in front of limnoupolis.gr (cf-nel headers): whether any 'Cache Everything' rule caches HTML; if so, UA-based rendering would break even with LiteSpeed 'Cache Mobile' ON.

Tablet policy: with 'Play On Mobile' OFF tablets (768-1024px) still autoplay the MP4; decide per client whether the facade gate should be min-width 1025px (recommended) and whether to also hide the video container on tablets via custom CSS.

Mobile layout-viewport quirk seen in the test (innerWidth 808 at 412px device width when an 800px-wide eager image overflowed): Elementor pages with fixed-width content wider than 412px may evaluate `innerWidth` differently from media queries under emulation; use matchMedia, not innerWidth, in loaders.

findings.claim: In Elementor 4.3.5 'Hide On Mobile' is CSS-only (`display:none` at max-width 767px); eager images, fetchpriority=high images, autoplay <video src> and inline scripts inside the hidden tree still download/execute on phones.
findings.detail: Deployed frontend.min.css?ver=4.3.5 contains exactly `@media (max-width:767px){.elementor .elementor-hidden-mobile,.elementor .elementor-hidden-phone{display:none}}` plus `@media (min-width:768px) and (max-width:1024px){.elementor .elementor-hidden-tablet{display:none}}` and `@media (min-width:1025px) and (max-width:99999px){.elementor .elementor-hidden-desktop{display:none}}`; mobile_extra/laptop/widescreen rules are compiled as `(min-width:-1)` (inactive unless custom breakpoints are on). Elementor's help article confirms v3 Advanced > Responsive 'Hide On Desktop/Tablet/Mobile' toggles and v4 Atomic Editor Style > Layout > Display: None (also CSS). Empirical test (Playwright, Chromium 141, Lighthouse-style context 412x823, DPR 1.75, isMobile+touch, Moto G Power UA) on a page with a `.hidden-mobile{display:none}` tree: requested = eager img, fetchpriority=high img, `<video autoplay muted playsinline src>` (networkState 3 after load), inline `<script>` ran (fetch ping sent), module script ran; NOT requested = `loading=lazy` img and a CSS background-image. web.dev confirms: 'Chrome, Safari, and Firefox don't load images using display: none; styling, either on the image element or on a parent element' only for loading=lazy images.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break (it is a diagnosis). It misleads when a builder hides a desktop hero with the toggle and assumes phones no longer download it.
findings.how_to_apply: Audit rule: in the public HTML count `elementor-hidden-mobile` nodes and list every without loading=lazy, every
findings.how_to_verify: Run `scripts/lighthouse.sh` mobile and compare `network-requests` against the hidden tree's assets; or reproduce with the Playwright script at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/pwtest/run.js (serves pwtest/site/t.html and prints the request list per emulation).

findings.claim: Elementor 'Optimized Image Loading' hands fetchpriority=high and eager loading to the first tags in HTML order via a regex over the output buffer, with no knowledge of hidden containers, so a desktop-only hero image hidden on mobile steals the high-priority slot on phones.
findings.detail: modules/image-loading-optimization/module.php @4.3.5: `wp_lazy_loading_enabled` is forced false, core fetchpriority logic is stopped (`wp_high_priority_element_flag(false)`), then `filter_images()` runs `preg_replace_callback('/<img\s[^>]+>/', ...)` on the buffered page; `$omit_threshold = 3` (first three images with width/height are not lazy-loaded), `maybe_add_fetchpriority_high_attr` gives fetchpriority=high to the first non-lazy image with width*height >= 50000 (filter `elementor/image-loading-optimization/min_priority_img_pixels`); option `elementor_optimized_image_loading` (Elementor > Settings > Performance). Combined with finding 1 the hidden desktop hero image downloads at high priority on phones while the visible mobile image gets normal priority or even loading=lazy if it is the 4th image.
findings.breaks_when: Two heroes (desktop/mobile) exist: the mobile one can end up lazy (if 4th+ image) and the desktop one fetchpriority=high. Also breaks when a logo/icon above the hero consumes one of the three eager slots.
findings.how_to_apply: Keep one hero tree so the poster is the first large . If a logo precedes it, that is fine (logo < 50000 px² does not take the high slot). Do not add `loading=lazy` on the poster (Image widget > Lazy Load: No). If a third-party lazy-loader (LiteSpeed/Perfmatters) is active, exclude the poster by class ('Lazy Load Image Class Name Excludes' / Perfmatters exclusion).
findings.how_to_verify: In the mobile Lighthouse JSON, `largest-contentful-paint` element snippet must contain `fetchpriority="high"` and no `loading="lazy"`; Lighthouse 13 `lcp-discovery-insight` must pass (it replaced `prioritize-lcp-image` and `lcp-lazy-loaded`, which still exist in 12.8.2).
findings.correction: The effect (first eligible in source order wins fetchpriority=high, hidden-on-mobile or not) is correct, but three details are wrong or missing. (a) Mechanism: the output-buffer regex only covers the HEADER: `add_action('get_header', set_buffer)` + `add_filter('the_content', flush_header_buffer, 0)`; Elementor page content is handled through core's `wp_content_img_tag` filter (Elementor's `the_content` priority is 9 (`THE_CONTENT_FILTER_PRIORITY = 9`), core `wp_filter_content_tags` runs at 12), with a shared media counter across both. (b) Only images carrying BOTH width and height attributes are touched (`if ( ! isset( $attr['width'], $attr['height'] ) ) return`); images without dimensions get neither lazy nor priority and do not consume a slot. (c) Pre-existing attributes are honoured: an `` or `` written in an HTML widget keeps them (lines 221-249 copy core's handling) - that is the real lever. (d) 'Image widget > Lazy Load: No' does NOT exist: includes/widgets/image.php @4.3.5 has no lazy/loading/fetchpriority control (controls are Image, Caption, Link, Lightbox, Alignment, Width, Max Width, Height, Object Fit/Position, Opacity, Hover, Border Radius, Caption styles). The plugin draft already carries this error at /home/user/everything-claude/plugins/elementor-lean/skills/elementor-debloat/references/fixes.md line 7 ('Widget → Image → Lazy Load: No').

findings.claim: Container Background Video with 'Play On Mobile' OFF is already a cache-safe mobile facade: 4.3.5 adds `elementor-hidden-mobile` to the video container and the JS handler never sets `
findings.detail: includes/elements/container.php @4.3.5 lines 215-217: `if ( ! $settings['background_play_on_mobile'] ) { $this->add_render_attribute( 'background-video-container', 'class', 'elementor-hidden-mobile' ); }`; the `<video class="elementor-background-video-hosted" autoplay muted playsinline loop>` is printed WITHOUT src. assets/dev/js/frontend/handlers/background-video.js line 272: `if ( ! elementSettings.background_play_on_mobile && 'mobile' === elementorFrontend.getCurrentDeviceMode() ) { return; }` before `activate()` sets `.attr('src', videoLink)`. frontend.js line 120: `getCurrentDeviceMode()` reads `getComputedStyle(#elementor-device-mode, ':after').content`, i.e. the CSS breakpoint, not the UA, so one cached HTML works for all devices. The fallback (includes/controls/groups/background.php line 606-618, control `video_fallback`, label 'Background Fallback') renders `{{SELECTOR}} background: url("{{URL}}") 50% 50%; background-size: cover;` — a CSS background that is only discovered after the Elementor post CSS loads and is also applied on desktop behind the video. Observed: onar-seaside-lounge.gr, voreniahorizon.gr and kand.dev6 all have `"background_play_on_mobile":"yes"`; mobile Lighthouse fetched 352 KB, 256 KB and 80 KB of MP4; onar's fallback is a 553 KB JPEG (largest request), voreniahorizon has no fallback at all. Tablets (768-1024px) still play the video.
findings.breaks_when: Design expects motion on phones (client decision). Custom Elementor breakpoints can change what 'mobile' means. If the mobile LCP becomes the CSS fallback background it is discovered late (post CSS) and, if the hero is the 3rd+ top-level container, suppressed by Lazy Load Background Images (see finding 10).
findings.how_to_apply: Recipe B (Background Video): (1) Edit hero container > Style > Background > Video: switch 'Play On Mobile' OFF; set 'Background Fallback' to a compressed poster (<=120 KB WebP). (2) Add an Image widget with the same poster as the FIRST child of the hero (Lazy Load: No, width/height set, no entrance animation), positioned behind the content via a CSS class (e.g. `.hero-poster{position:absolute;inset:0}` with `object-fit:cover`), so phones have an LCP candidate that Optimized Image Loading marks fetchpriority=high; the extra ~100 KB on desktop doubles as the pre-roll frame. (3) Remove entrance animations/motion effects from hero heading and buttons. (4) No cache-plugin change is required. Harness gates: mobile Lighthouse `network-requests` contains no `.mp4`/youtube/vimeo; LCP element is the poster ; CLS unchanged.
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse (412px): `network-requests` has no video request; `largest-contentful-paint` element selector points to the poster img; desktop Lighthouse still lists the MP4 (206 response). Manually: Chrome DevTools device toolbar at 412px, Network filter 'media' empty; at 1025px+ the video plays.
findings.correction: Mechanism confirmed; two fixes to the recipe. (1) Step 2 'Image widget ... Lazy Load: No' is impossible (no such control, see finding 2); the poster must instead be the first `` with width+height in the page (so Optimized Image Loading gives it fetchpriority=high), or be written in an HTML widget as ``, which Elementor's module preserves. (2) Device mode comes from CSS `#elementor-device-mode:after{content}`: frontend.min.css 4.3.5 compiles `@media (max-width:767px){...content:"mobile"}`, `(max-width:1024px) -> "tablet"`, `(min-width:1025px) -> "desktop"`, so 'mobile' is exactly the <=767px band - tablets 768-1024 and phones in landscape >767px still download and play the video. Also the frontend.js handler only runs after frontend.min.js executes, so on desktop the video starts late; the CSS fallback/poster is what paints first on every device.

findings.claim: Recipe A (three.js/WebGL hero): keep one tree, make the poster an eager Image widget, and load the canvas from an HTML-widget `<script type="module">` only when `matchMedia('(min-width:1025px)')` matches; gating on prefers-reduced-motion or Save-Data alone does nothing for Lighthouse mobile because both are false under its emulation.
findings.detail: includes/widgets/html.php @4.3.5 `render()` is `$this->print_unescaped_setting('html')`, so the widget's markup/script is emitted inline at its DOM position and runs during parse, before elementor frontend.min.js (loaded in the footer without defer on limnoupolis), so the loader must not depend on `elementorFrontend`. Empirical Lighthouse-style emulation results (Chromium 141): `(min-width:1025px)` false, `(max-width:767px)` true, `(hover: hover)` false, `(pointer: fine)` false, `(pointer: coarse)` true, `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` false, `navigator.connection.saveData` false; desktop emulation inverts the first four. Lighthouse 13.5.0 constants: 412x823, deviceScaleFactor 1.75, UA 'Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 11; moto g power (2022)) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/136.0.0.0 Mobile Safari/537.36', touch emulation enabled (`Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled {enabled: mobile}` in core/lib/emulation.js). three.js manual: load as ES modules via an import map `{"imports":{"three":"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@<version>/build/three.module.js","three/addons/":"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@<version>/examples/jsm/"}}` with a pinned version, or self-host. limnoupolis.gr already self-hosts under /wp-content/uploads/lmn-3d/vendor/three/ and uses dynamic `import()` behind an IntersectionObserver with a reduced-motion branch, but has no viewport/pointer gate, so the mobile Lighthouse run still fetched three.module.min.js (171 KB br, 671 KB raw), GLTFLoader, meshopt decoder and ball.glb/buoy.glb (112/127 KB, `model/gltf-binary`, no content-encoding, already meshopt-compressed); lab TBT 142,018 ms with 155 s 'Other' main-thread time attributed to the inline script, versus 1,796 ms on staging.limnoupolis.gr which has no 3D hero.
findings.breaks_when: Delay-JS plugins rewrite the inline loader (see finding 9) and the canvas never appears on desktop; a desktop user resizes below 1025px (no canvas, poster stays — acceptable); the import map is printed after the module script (import maps must precede any module); CDN import without a pinned version.
findings.how_to_apply:
Elementor UI: hero container (1st top-level container) > child 1 = Image widget poster (exact mobile render width, WebP, width/height attributes, Lazy Load: No, Motion Effects/Entrance Animation: none); child 2 = HTML widget: `
`. hero-3d.js (child theme or uploads) does the `import('three')`/GLTF work and fades the canvas over the poster; print the import map from the child theme with `add_action('wp_head', fn() => print '', 1)` or use absolute self-hosted paths. Cache settings: none (single HTML for all devices). Delay-JS: Perfmatters 'Excluded from Delay' keyword `hero-3d`; FlyingPress exclusion keyword `hero-3d`; WP Rocket `nowprocket` attribute; LiteSpeed skips non-`text/javascript` types automatically, `data-no-optimize="1"` is belt-and-braces. Harness gates: mobile run has zero requests matching `three|\.glb|\.gltf|draco|meshopt`; LCP element is the poster ; TBT < 200 ms; desktop run shows the canvas assets.
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse JSON: filter `network-requests` for three/.glb (must be empty), `largest-contentful-paint` element = `img.hero-poster`, `total-blocking-time` numericValue; desktop Lighthouse or Chrome at 1350px: canvas assets requested after the hero intersects. Re-run the Playwright script in the scratchpad to confirm matchMedia values if the Lighthouse version changes.

findings.claim: Recipe C (Lottie): the Pro Lottie widget offers 'Lazy Load' and a 'Trigger' control (Viewport / On Click / On Hover / Scroll / None) but no device gate, so a hero Lottie must become a static poster on all devices or be loaded through the same HTML-widget facade; 'Hide on Mobile' on the widget is CSS only.
findings.detail: Elementor help (Lottie widget): 'toggle Lazy Load on. This means the animation will only load when it becomes visible'; Trigger choices: Viewport (with percentage slider), On Click, On Hover (Hover Area: Animation/Column/Section/Container, On Hover Out), Scroll, None; Source: External URL or Media File (.json). Elementor Pro source is not public, so whether the JSON is fetched when the widget is display:none on mobile could not be verified (inferred from finding 1: Lazy Load uses visibility, so a display:none widget probably never intersects and the JSON may not load, but the lottie library itself still loads).
findings.breaks_when: A Lottie is the only visual in the hero on mobile (poster replaces it); 'On Click'/'On Hover' triggers on a decorative hero animation confuse users.
findings.how_to_apply: Hero: replace the Lottie with an Image widget poster (SVG/WebP) for all devices; if the client insists on desktop motion, use the Recipe A HTML widget and `import()` lottie-web/dotLottie from the child theme behind the same `(min-width:1025px)` gate, rendering into a div over the poster. Below the fold: keep the Pro Lottie widget with Lazy Load ON and Trigger = Viewport (or On Click for heavy files). Build checklist: no Lottie above the fold; every Lottie has Lazy Load ON.
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse `network-requests`: no `.json` animation files and no `lottie` script before LCP; LCP element is the poster. Desktop: Lottie assets appear only after the trigger.

findings.claim: Dynamic.ooo 'Dynamic Visibility > Device and Browser' removes the element from the HTML server-side using `wp_is_mobile()`; Elementor Pro Display Conditions have no device condition and Elementor warns they do not work with caching, so neither is usable without a UA-varying page cache.
findings.detail: Dynamic Visibility 6.0.6 trunk `includes/extensions/dynamic-visibility/triggers/device.php`: description 'Not really responsive, remove the element from the code based on the user's device. This trigger uses native WP device detection...' and `if ( wp_is_mobile() )` in `check_conditions()`; help article (March 19, 2025): only 'Desktop & TV' vs 'Mobile & Tablet'; 'Keep HTML' is off by default ('The module strips the HTML tag element from the page content by default'). WordPress 7.x `wp_is_mobile()` (wp-includes/vars.php) returns true for `Sec-CH-UA-Mobile: ?1` or UA containing Mobile|Android|Silk/|Kindle|BlackBerry|Opera Mini|Opera Mobi, so Lighthouse mobile is detected as mobile. Elementor help 'Show and hide elements on a page (Display Conditions)': available conditions are Page parent, Author, In Categories, In Tags, Date Modified, Date of Publish, Login Status, Role, Registration Date, Day of the week, Time of day, Current date, Of Tags, Of Categories, From URL — no device/UA; plus the warning 'Because display conditions are dynamic, they do not work well in conjunction with caching. If you use display conditions, we recommend you disable advanced caching or any caching plugins.' Elementor's hide-per-device article adds that Display Conditions are 'not screen breakpoints'. Display Conditions require Advanced/Expert/Agency Pro plans (Elementor blog).
findings.breaks_when: Any full-page cache without a mobile vary (LiteSpeed 'Cache Mobile' OFF is the inventory baseline, FlyingPress mobile cache off, W3TC groups disabled, Cloudflare 'Cache Everything' without device key): the first visitor's device decides which HTML everyone gets — desktop users lose the hero or phones get the heavy one. Also breaks for Android tablets (treated as mobile) while iPads with desktop UA get the desktop hero.
findings.how_to_apply: Only consider Dynamic Visibility device rules when finding 7's cache vary is in place and verified; otherwise use the facade (findings 3-5). Never use Elementor Pro Display Conditions for device decisions. If used: Element > Advanced > Dynamic Visibility > Enable, Triggers: Device and Browser, Responsive = Mobile & Tablet, Display Mode = Hide, Keep HTML OFF.
findings.how_to_verify: curl the page twice with the cache warm: once with the Lighthouse mobile UA and once with a desktop UA, diff the HTML for the hero node; both must be correct on repeated hits (`x-litespeed-cache: hit`). Lighthouse mobile should then show no hero assets.

findings.claim: UA-based mobile rendering needs an explicit cache vary in every layer: LiteSpeed 'Cache Mobile' + 'List of Mobile User Agents', WP Rocket's default mobile cache (phones only), FlyingPress 'Separate Mobile Cache and Optimizations', W3TC 'Manage User Agent Groups' (all default groups disabled), Cloudflare custom cache key 'Cache by device type'; each doubles cache size and warm-up, multiplied again by Polylang/WPML language URLs.
findings.detail: LiteSpeed docs: 'Cache Mobile' default OFF, 'enables separate cached versions of pages for mobile and desktop views... If your site has mobile-specific content, such as widgets that appear only on mobile or desktop'; 'List of Mobile View User Agents must not be empty when Cache Mobile is set to ON'; default list `Mobile|Android|Silk/|Kindle|BlackBerry|Opera Mini|Opera Mobi` (pipe-separated, escape spaces with backslash); warning 'Enabling this option will create additional cache varies. If you have crawling enabled, cache varies cause multiple crawlers to be created'; also listed as needed for CCSS/UCSS/Guest Mode. The Lighthouse 13.5 UA contains both 'Android' and 'Mobile', so it hits the default list. WP Rocket (doc updated Aug 26, 2026): mobile cache on by default, 'WP Rocket will create a separate set of cache files for mobile devices' (`index-mobile.html_gzip`), 'By default, the Mobile Cache feature works on phones only... the default cache (for desktop) will be served to tablet devices', 'Mobile phones get detected by the HTTP user agent', and with Varnish/NGINX/Cloudflare Cache Everything in front you get 'Wrong display for mobile, tablet or desktop'; APO needs 'caching by device type'. FlyingPress (May 21, 2025): 'FlyingPress caches mobile and desktop pages separately... Cache size will double... Avoid using this unless your site behavior or layout truly differs by device' — not verified for the agency's CF fork. W3TC ConfigKeys.php: `mobile.rgroups` defaults `tablets`, `phones`, `search_engines` each `'enabled' => false`, matched as `preg_match('~<group>~i', HTTP_USER_AGENT)` (Mobile_UserAgent.php); UI path Performance > Cache Groups > Manage User Agent Groups. Cloudflare Cache Rules: 'You can switch on or off Cache deception armor, Cache by device type, and Sort query string' in the custom Cache Key; header-based keys (user-agent) and the 'User > Device type' section are Enterprise; Cloudflare does not vary HTML by UA on its own.
findings.breaks_when: Any layer is left non-varying (LiteSpeed Cache Mobile OFF but Dynamic Visibility device rule on; Cloudflare Cache Everything in front of a varying origin; FlyingPress fork without the option); LiteSpeed crawler/QUIC.cloud CCSS/UCSS budgets double; tablets fall on the 'wrong' side (WP Rocket treats tablets as desktop, wp_is_mobile treats Android tablets as mobile).
findings.how_to_apply: Prefer the facade (no vary). If a site must vary: LiteSpeed Cache > Cache > Cache tab: 'Cache Mobile' ON and keep/verify 'List of Mobile User Agents' contains `Mobile|Android|...`; purge all; expect two crawler passes. WP Rocket: leave Mobile cache enabled (default). FlyingPress: enable 'Separate Mobile Cache and Optimizations' (verify the CF fork exposes it). W3TC: Performance > Cache Groups > enable the 'phones' group with Theme pass-through. Cloudflare: do not 'Cache Everything' for HTML, or add a Cache Rule with 'Cache by device type' ON. Polylang/WPML: no extra setting, but budget 2x cache per language.
findings.how_to_verify: With cache warm, `curl -sI -A '<Lighthouse mobile UA>' URL` and with a desktop UA; both must return cache hits (`x-litespeed-cache: hit`, `x-flying-press-cache`, W3TC footer comment) AND different hero markup; run the mobile Lighthouse against production (not a bypass URL).

findings.claim: Lighthouse mobile emulation is what the harness must satisfy: Lighthouse 13.5.0 uses 412x823 @1.75 DPR, UA 'Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 11; moto g power (2022)) ... Chrome/136.0.0.0 Mobile Safari/537.36', touch enabled, slow-4G throttling; matchMedia width/pointer gates fire correctly, reduced-motion/Save-Data do not; PSI runs the same Lighthouse and reports CrUX field data separately.
findings.detail: core/config/constants.js: `MOTOGPOWER_EMULATION_METRICS = {mobile:true,width:412,height:823,deviceScaleFactor:1.75}`, `MOTOG4_USERAGENT = 'Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 11; moto g power (2022)) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/136.0.0.0 Mobile Safari/537.36'`, `formFactor:'mobile', throttling: mobileSlow4G`; emulation.js sends `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` and `Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled {enabled: mobile}` and userAgentMetadata `{platform:'Android', model:'moto g power (2022)', mobile:true}` (so `Sec-CH-UA-Mobile: ?1` is sent and wp_is_mobile() is true). The local runs used Lighthouse 12.8.2 with the same UA/viewport. PSI doc: lab data via Lighthouse ('mid-tier device (Moto G4)' per its FAQ, which lags the code), field data = CrUX 28-day FCP/LCP/CLS/INP/TTFB. Lighthouse 13 removed `lcp-lazy-loaded`, `prioritize-lcp-image` and `largest-contentful-paint-element` (404 in main; present in v12.8.2) in favour of `lcp-discovery-insight` (declares `replacesAudits: ['prioritize-lcp-image','lcp-lazy-loaded']`) and `lcp-breakdown-insight`; `long-tasks`, `bootup-time`, `mainthread-work-breakdown`, `total-blocking-time`, `third-parties-insight`, `inp-breakdown-insight` exist.
findings.breaks_when: The harness greps 12.x audit ids on a 13.x report (fields read empty, as scripts/lighthouse.sh already warns); a UA-based cache vary uses a list that does not contain 'Android' or 'Mobile'; the loader is gated only on reduced-motion/Save-Data (Lighthouse still loads the canvas).
findings.how_to_apply: Harness: pin Lighthouse (12.8.2 today) or port the jq to `lcp-discovery-insight`/`lcp-breakdown-insight`; gates = LCP element snippet is the poster , no hero-asset URLs in `network-requests`, `lcp-discovery-insight` score 1. For real-phone checks, read PSI's CrUX panel (origin-level if the URL lacks data) rather than relying on the lab TBT, which is inflated on slow runners (benchmarkIndex < 2000 in the local runs).
findings.how_to_verify: `jq '.lighthouseVersion, .configSettings.screenEmulation, .environment.networkUserAgent' run.json`; confirm the matchMedia matrix with the Playwright script (hover/pointer/min-width false, coarse true under mobile emulation).

findings.claim: Delay-JS features will delay the inline facade loader unless excluded; the exclusion mechanisms differ: WP Rocket `nowprocket` attribute, LiteSpeed `data-no-optimize`/`data-cfasync="false"`/non-`text/javascript` type (module scripts are skipped) and `data-no-defer`, Perfmatters and FlyingPress only by keyword lists (no attribute documented).
findings.detail: WP Rocket doc: exclude 'Programmatically by adding the nowprocket attribute to inline scripts or scripts in external files'; delayed scripts get `type="text/rocketlazyloadscript"`. LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1 src/optimize.cls.php `_parse_js()`: skips tags with `data-optimized`, non-empty `data-no-optimize`, `data-cfasync="false"`, or `type` other than `text/javascript` (so `<script type="module">` is never minified/deferred/delayed by LSCWP); `_js_inline_defer()` bypasses on `data-no-defer`, honours 'JS Deferred/Delayed Excludes' (`cfg_js_defer_exc`), and in Delayed mode (`cfg_js_defer === 2`) rewrites inline scripts to `type="litespeed/javascript"`; the docs warn 'JS Delayed Includes' does not work for inline JS when Load JS Deferred = Deferred. Perfmatters docs: 'Delay all scripts... will attempt to delay all JavaScript, including inline'; exclude via 'Excluded from Delay' with 'a unique string from that script', filters `perfmatters_delayed_scripts` and `perfmatters_delay_js`; no exclusion attribute is documented (`data-perfmatters` not found). FlyingPress 'Delay All JavaScript' (June 25, 2025): three strategies (Defer loading / Load when idle / Load after interaction), 'All scripts are delayed unless excluded', exclusion checks 'the full <script> tag—src, id, and inline content', partial case-insensitive keywords, no wildcards; 'Load after interaction' is 'not suitable if your site has sliders, animations, menus... in the above-the-fold area'. Observed markers: pallada.gr 35 and marakaki.com 53 `pmdelayedscript` tags (Perfmatters delay active), cretaforums.gr/voreniahorizon.gr `flying-press` rewrites.
findings.breaks_when: Loader is delayed: desktop never shows the canvas until interaction (acceptable visually but a silent regression) or, worse, a delayed poster-swapping script leaves a blank hero. Also when a cache plugin combines/minifies the inline module (LiteSpeed skips modules; others may not).
findings.how_to_apply: Give the loader a stable unique token (`hero-3d`) in its id and body and add: WP Rocket -> `nowprocket` attribute; Perfmatters -> JavaScript > Delay JavaScript > 'Excluded from Delay': `hero-3d`; FlyingPress -> JavaScript > Delay > exclusions: `hero-3d`; LiteSpeed -> `type="module"` plus `data-no-optimize="1"` and, if Load JS Deferred = Delayed, add `hero-3d` to Page Optimization > Tuning > 'JS Deferred/Delayed Excludes'. Keep heavy code in the imported file, not inline (Perfmatters notes large inline JS raises LCP).
findings.how_to_verify: View source of the cached page: the loader `<script>` must keep `type="module"` (no `text/rocketlazyloadscript`, `pmdelayedscript`, `litespeed/javascript`, `flying-press` type rewrite); desktop Lighthouse/DevTools shows the hero module request without any interaction.

findings.claim: Elementor 'Lazy Load Background Images' suppresses CSS backgrounds of the 4th+ top-level container, and of the 3rd+ when the viewport is at most 1024px tall (Lighthouse mobile is 823px), so a poster set as a container background must be in the first two top-level containers or carry `e-no-lazyload`; the three video heroes audited are all container #1, so this is a build rule rather than a current bug.
findings.detail: modules/lazyload/module.php @4.3.5 prints in wp_head: `.e-con.e-parent:nth-of-type(n+4):not(.e-lazyloaded):not(.e-no-lazyload), ... * { background-image: none !important; }`, `@media screen and (max-height: 1024px) { ... :nth-of-type(n+3) ... }`, `@media screen and (max-height: 640px) { ... :nth-of-type(n+2) ... }`; a footer IntersectionObserver adds `e-lazyloaded`; option `elementor_lazy_load_background_images` (default '1', Elementor > Settings > Performance). nth-of-type counts siblings inside the same `.elementor` wrapper, so header-template containers do not count against the page hero. Observed e-parent order: voreniahorizon 16d563b, onar 06d62a4, kand 4eb0a77 are each index 1 of their page wrapper. All 10 pages carry the rule (`nth-of-type(n+4)` present), marakaki has it off.
findings.breaks_when: A builder puts a 'spacer' or announcement container above the hero so the hero becomes the 3rd container: on Lighthouse mobile its background poster disappears until the observer fires, LCP shifts to text or a later image.
findings.how_to_apply: Build rule: hero = first top-level container; use an Image widget (not a container background) for the poster; if a CSS-background poster is unavoidable add CSS class `e-no-lazyload` (Container > Advanced > CSS Classes) or filter the option. Debloat rule: when LCP is a CSS background in a 3rd+ container, add `e-no-lazyload` or move the container up.
findings.how_to_verify: In the mobile Lighthouse screenshot/filmstrip the hero background is painted at FCP; `lcp-breakdown-insight` shows no 'resource load delay' from the post CSS; DOM check: hero container has no `e-lazyloaded` class dependency (it is `:nth-of-type(1)`).

findings.claim: Entrance animations and consent banners, not the hero image, were the LCP element on two of the slow sites: voreniahorizon's h1 carries `elementor-invisible` (`visibility:hidden`) with `_animation: fadeIn` and reaches LCP at 8.95 s; onar's LCP (16.4 s) is the Complianz cookie banner; limnoupolis's LCP is a `loading="lazy"` image below the hero.
findings.detail:
frontend.min.css 4.3.5: `.elementor-invisible{visibility:hidden}`; voreniahorizon hero markup `

); limnoupolis LCP node `` at 7.7 s (`lcp-lazy-loaded` score 0). Audit summary: voreniahorizon has 160 entrance animations and 12 motion effects, onar 12 + 38.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break; removing an animation only changes the look. If the consent banner stays the LCP, the hero fix will not move LCP much until the banner is made small/late or exempted.
findings.how_to_apply: Debloat: for every widget in the first top-level container set Advanced > Motion Effects > Entrance Animation: None (and Scrolling/Mouse effects off); set the poster Image widget Lazy Load: No; configure Complianz/FAZ/Cookie-Script banner as a compact bottom bar without a large image/paragraph so it is not the largest paint (keep legal text, shrink layout). Build checklist: zero entrance animations above the fold.
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse `largest-contentful-paint` element selector must be the poster `img` (not `h1.elementor-invisible`, not `#cmplz-...`); LCP <= 2.5 s; `audits.largest-contentful-paint-element.details.items[0].items[0].node.snippet` must not contain `loading="lazy"` or `elementor-invisible`.

findings.claim: Duplicate desktop/mobile sections are rare and small on the agency's home pages (pallada 6 hidden-mobile trees / 6.9 KB, voreniahorizon 3 / 6.7 KB, marakaki 3 / 6.7 KB, cretaforums 1, onar 1, others 0; no inside any), so the lean rule is preventive: one responsive container per section, mobile differences via responsive controls, never two trees.
findings.detail: curl of the 10 home pages with the Lighthouse mobile UA and a parser that measures each `elementor-hidden-*` element: pallada.gr 9 hidden-mobile / 4 hidden-tablet / 5 hidden-desktop class occurrences (6 hidden-mobile trees, 6,914 bytes; 4 hidden-desktop trees, 4,676 bytes; 0 images); www.marakaki.com 4/5/4 (3 trees 6,702 B / 3 trees 3,559 B); voreniahorizon.gr 5/4/5 (3 trees 6,719 B / 4 trees 7,082 B); cretaforums.gr 1/1/1 (3,307 B); onar-seaside-lounge.gr 1/1/0 (693 B — the video container itself); limnoupolis, staging, kand, platonos, fagitiotiszois 0. Each hidden tree still ships its CSS rules in the post CSS and any eager images would download (finding 1). Elementor's per-device controls (responsive values on padding, alignment, image size, background) and the hide toggles are documented in the help article; v4 atomic Display: None is the same CSS mechanism.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break. The rule costs effort when a layout genuinely differs (e.g. a mobile carousel vs desktop grid); then the mobile-only variant must not contain eager images or scripts, or must be built with the facade pattern.
findings.how_to_apply: Build checklist: one hero/one section tree; use Container > Style responsive values and Image widget responsive controls for device differences; if a second tree is unavoidable, give every image inside it `loading="lazy"` (Image widget Lazy Load: Yes) because Chrome skips lazy images in display:none trees, and keep scripts out of it. Audit script: flag any `elementor-hidden-mobile` tree containing `<img` without `loading="lazy"`, `<video`, `<iframe` or `<script`.
findings.how_to_verify: `grep -o 'elementor-hidden-mobile' page.html | wc -l` and the parser in the scratchpad (bytes/images per hidden tree) before/after; mobile Lighthouse `network-requests` shows no asset that belongs to a hidden tree.
findings.correction: Counts spot-checked: voreniahorizon.gr today has 5 `elementor-hidden-mobile` class occurrences (matches). pallada.gr root returned a 302 to my curl so its figures were not re-verified. Fix the how_to_apply: 'Image widget Lazy Load: Yes' is not a control in Elementor 4.3.5; to make images in an unavoidable second tree lazy, rely on Optimized Image Loading (images after the 3rd dimensioned one are lazy automatically) or write the markup in an HTML widget with `loading="lazy"`, or use `<picture><source media>` so phones never fetch the desktop asset at all (see additions).

findings.claim: Removing the JS hero on mobile is also the main INP lever: web.dev attributes high INP to long tasks (>50 ms) and recurring main-thread work such as timers and JavaScript-driven animations, which is exactly what a three.js rAF render loop, autoplay video resize handlers and Swiper autoplay add; the lab proxy on limnoupolis is TBT 142 s vs 1.8 s without the 3D hero.
findings.detail: web.dev INP: good <= 200 ms, poor > 500 ms; 'An input delay occurs until event handlers start running, possibly caused by factors such as long tasks on the main thread'. web.dev optimize-input-delay: 'Avoid recurring timers that kick off excessive main thread work' (setInterval/recursive setTimeout), 'Avoid long tasks', third-party timers you do not control. web.dev optimize-long-tasks: 'Any task that takes longer than 50 milliseconds is a long task'; tasks are queued by 'JavaScript-driven animations, and background activity such as analytics collection'. Local lab: limnoupolis mobile TBT 142,018 ms, main-thread 'Other' 155 s and 'Script Evaluation' 6.9 s, long tasks attributed to the inline page script and elementor frontend.min.js (10 s, 9.9 s, ...), while staging.limnoupolis.gr (same stack, no three.js) has TBT 1,796 ms; software WebGL in headless Chromium inflates the absolute number, so treat it as directional. Field INP (CrUX) was not opened.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break. Claims about field INP stay unproven until CrUX shows the 28-day p75 after the change.
findings.how_to_apply: Justify the hero change in the client report with the web.dev definitions and the TBT/long-task delta; after deploy, record PSI's CrUX INP p75 (mobile) for the URL/origin monthly. In the facade, also stop Swiper autoplay on mobile and keep the three.js loop paused when off-screen or `document.hidden` (limnoupolis already does the latter).
findings.how_to_verify: Lab: `total-blocking-time`, `long-tasks` and `mainthread-work-breakdown` in the mobile run before/after; `inp-breakdown-insight` (Lighthouse 13) when a flow interaction is scripted. Field: PSI CrUX panel INP p75 <= 200 ms for mobile over 28 days.

findings.claim: Do-not-do list for hero handling on Elementor 4.3 sites (each item is a verified failure mode in this research).
findings.detail: 1) 'Hide On Mobile' / Display: None alone for a heavy hero (CSS only; eager images, fetchpriority=high images, autoplay video and scripts still load — Playwright test, frontend.min.css 4.3.5). 2) Two hero trees (desktop + mobile) — doubles HTML/CSS and the desktop image takes the fetchpriority slot (module.php). 3) Dynamic.ooo device trigger or any wp_is_mobile()-based rendering with LiteSpeed 'Cache Mobile' OFF, FlyingPress separate mobile cache OFF, W3TC groups disabled, or Cloudflare 'Cache Everything' in front — first visitor's device poisons the shared HTML. 4) LiteSpeed 'Cache Mobile' ON without checking the UA list matches Lighthouse ('Android'/'Mobile' are in the default list; a trimmed list breaks lab tests) or with a crawler budget that cannot warm two varies. 5) Elementor Pro Display Conditions for device — no device condition; Elementor warns they do not work with caching. 6) Gating the facade loader only on `prefers-reduced-motion` or Save-Data (both false under Lighthouse mobile; use min-width/pointer). 7) `loading="lazy"` on the poster (limnoupolis LCP was a lazy image; lazy + display:none means the mobile hero never loads if hidden). 8) Entrance animations/motion effects on hero heading or poster (`elementor-invisible` -> visibility:hidden; voreniahorizon LCP 8.95 s). 9) Poster as a container CSS background in the 3rd+ top-level container (Lazy Load Background Images hides it under 1024px-tall viewports). 10) Autoplay `<video src>` or inline three.js/Lottie init inside a hidden container (downloads/executes anyway). 11) LiteSpeed/other image lazy-load applied to the hero (CLS 0 -> 0.107 on staging per the audit). 12) 'Load after interaction' delay strategies on sites with above-the-fold sliders/animations without excluding the hero loader (FlyingPress's own warning).
findings.breaks_when: Each item describes when a site breaks: wrong hero for a device class (3,4,5), missing hero on desktop (6,12), slow/blank LCP on mobile (1,2,7,8,9,10,11).
findings.how_to_apply: Put the list verbatim in skills/elementor-debloat/references/fixes.md ('Do not') and skills/elementor-build/references/checklist.md; make the audit script flag 1, 2, 7, 8, 9, 10 from the public HTML and 3/4 from plugin settings (read-only).
findings.how_to_verify: Per item: HTML grep for `elementor-hidden-mobile` trees with media/scripts; grep `elementor-invisible` inside the first `.e-parent`; grep `loading="lazy"` on the first large ; LiteSpeed option `cache-mobile` and `cache-mobile_rules` values; curl with mobile vs desktop UA for divergent markup on a non-varying cache.
findings.correction: Items 1-6, 8-12 verified. Item 7 and the companion fix text must not reference 'Image widget Lazy Load' (no such control in 4.3.5; Elementor decides via Optimized Image Loading, honouring attributes you set yourself in HTML-widget markup). Add item 13: 'Video widget (hosted) with Autoplay on, relying on Play On Mobile OFF or Lazy Load to spare phones' - Play On Mobile only toggles `playsinline`, Lazy Load is not offered for hosted videos, and Preload is hidden once Autoplay is on, so the MP4 always downloads. Add to the allowed list: `<video><source media="(min-width:1025px)">`, `<picture><source media>` and `<link rel=preload media>` (cache-safe facades, see additions).

findings.claim: `<video><source src=... media="(min-width:1025px)">` is a zero-JS, cache-safe mobile video facade: Chromium 141 (and current Firefox/Safari) evaluate the `media` attribute during source selection, so a desktop-only source is never requested on a 412px viewport while the poster paints.
findings.detail: Blink html_media_element.cc on main: 'If candidate has a media attribute whose value does not match the environment ... jump down to the failed with elements step' guarded by `kVideoSourceMediaQuerySupport`, declared `BASE_FEATURE(kVideoSourceMediaQuerySupport, base::FEATURE_ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT)`. MDN browser-compat-data source.json: `media` supported Chrome 3+, Safari 3.1+, Firefox 15+ with note 'In Firefox 53-119, media is supported only in <source> within <picture>' (i.e. video support again from 120). HTML spec note: 'The media attribute is only evaluated once during the resource selection algorithm for media elements' (no re-evaluation on resize). My Playwright test (Chromium 141.0.7390.37, Lighthouse mobile emulation): `<video autoplay muted playsinline><source src=desktop.mp4 media="(min-width:1025px)"><source src=mobile.mp4 media="(max-width:767px)">` requested only mobile.mp4 (currentSrc = mobile); `<video poster=p.png><source src=desktop-only.mp4 media="(min-width:1025px)">` requested only the poster (currentSrc empty, no video bytes); desktop emulation requested desktop.mp4 and desktop-only.mp4. Older web posts claiming Chrome dropped support at v34 are obsolete.
findings.breaks_when: A browser without the feature falls back to the first `<source>` without media match semantics (put the lightest/mobile source first as a safety order, or give the desktop source the media query and no mobile source at all). Desktop window resized below 1025px after load keeps whichever source was chosen (spec: evaluated once). Elementor's own container Background Video cannot emit `<source>` (it prints a src-less `<video>` and sets src via JS), so this needs an HTML widget or a child-theme filter on `elementor/frontend/the_content`.
findings.how_to_apply: HTML widget as first child of the hero container: `` with CSS `.hero-video{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover}`. Omit any mobile source if phones should get a still image; add `` only if the client wants a small mobile clip. No cache-plugin setting changes; single HTML for all devices. Keep the poster first so Optimized Image Loading leaves it eager and high-priority.
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse `network-requests`: no `.mp4`; desktop run: the MP4 appears with 206. DevTools device toolbar at 412px: Network 'Media' filter empty; `document.querySelector('.hero-video').currentSrc === ''`. Re-run /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/critic/run2.js with t2.html (serves critic/site on 127.0.0.1:8766) after any Chromium/Lighthouse upgrade.

findings.claim: `<picture><source media>` and `<link rel="preload" as="image" media>` give device-specific hero images without any cache vary: under Lighthouse mobile emulation only the matching source/preload is fetched, and Elementor's Optimized Image Loading keeps `fetchpriority`/`loading` attributes you write yourself.
findings.detail: Playwright test (Chromium 141, mobile emulation): `` requested only m.png (currentSrc = m.png); desktop requested only d.png. `` was not requested on mobile; the `(max-width:767px)` preload was. Elementor module.php 4.3.5: when an `` already has `loading` or `fetchpriority="high"` the module keeps it (lines 221-249, 'Logic to handle a loading attribute that is already provided'), and it ignores images without both width and height. Elementor's Image widget cannot output ``; HTML widget content runs through `the_content` (Elementor priority 9) and core `wp_filter_content_tags` (12), so the module still sees it.
findings.breaks_when: Forgetting width/height on the `` (then no fetchpriority and possible CLS); giving the mobile `` a `sizes`/`srcset` mismatch; a delay/lazy plugin (LiteSpeed Lazy Load Images, Perfmatters lazy) rewriting the `` to data-src - exclude by class (`hero-poster`).
findings.how_to_apply: HTML widget first in the hero: ``; optional child-theme `wp_head`: `` and the desktop twin with `(min-width:768px)`. Exclusions: LiteSpeed Page Optimization > Media > 'Lazy Load Image Class Name Excludes': `hero-poster`; Perfmatters Lazy Loading exclusions: `hero-poster`.
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse: `network-requests` contains hero-mobile-828.webp and not hero-1600.webp; LCP element snippet is `img.hero-poster` with `fetchpriority="high"` and no `loading="lazy"`; `lcp-discovery-insight` (LH 13) passes. Desktop run shows the 1600 file.

findings.claim: Elementor 4.3.5's Image widget has no 'Lazy Load' control; eager/lazy and fetchpriority are decided only by the global 'Optimized Image Loading' option (first three dimensioned images eager, first >=50,000 px² one high) or by attributes you write in HTML-widget markup - every 'Image widget > Lazy Load: No/Yes' instruction in the findings and in the plugin draft is unactionable.
findings.detail: includes/widgets/image.php @4.3.5 contains no control named lazy/loading/fetchpriority; its labels are Image, Choose Image, Caption, Custom Caption, Link, Lightbox, Alignment, Width, Max Width, Height, Object Fit, Object Position, Opacity, Hover, Transition Duration, Hover Animation, Border Radius, Caption, Text Color, Background Color, Spacing. The only lazy-load controls in free 4.3.5 are the Video widget `lazy_load` (YouTube, or image-overlay embeds that are not hosted) and the global options `elementor_optimized_image_loading` and `elementor_lazy_load_background_images` (Elementor > Settings > Performance). The draft's /home/user/everything-claude/plugins/elementor-lean/skills/elementor-debloat/references/fixes.md line 7 says 'Widget → Image → Lazy Load: No'.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break; it misleads the debloat agent into looking for a control that is absent, and an operator may instead disable Optimized Image Loading globally, which removes fetchpriority=high from every page.
findings.how_to_apply: Rewrite the rule as: (a) keep Optimized Image Loading ON; (b) make the poster the first `` with width and height after the header (logo included in the count of three; the first image >= 50,000 px² takes fetchpriority=high); (c) when order cannot be guaranteed, output the poster from an HTML widget with explicit `fetchpriority="high" loading="eager" width height`; (d) when a hero image must be lazy (e.g. inside an unavoidable hidden-on-mobile tree), write `loading="lazy"` in HTML-widget markup. Audit script: read the LCP element snippet rather than widget settings.
findings.how_to_verify: Elementor editor: Image widget Content/Style/Advanced tabs show no Lazy Load switch (screenshot). Public HTML: the poster `` has `fetchpriority="high"` and no `loading="lazy"`; mobile Lighthouse LCP element = poster.

findings.claim: The Elementor Video widget (hosted MP4) cannot be made mobile-safe from its own controls: with Autoplay on, 'Play On Mobile' only adds `playsinline`, 'Lazy Load' is unavailable for hosted sources, and 'Preload' is hidden, so the file downloads on every device; use the `<source media>` HTML-widget pattern or a click-to-play Image Overlay instead.
findings.detail: video.php @4.3.5: `play_on_mobile` (condition `autoplay=yes`) is consumed in `get_hosted_params()` as `$video_params['playsinline'] = ''` only; `autoplay`, `loop`, `controls` are added whenever set; `preload` (Metadata/Auto/None, default metadata) has condition `video_type=hosted` AND `autoplay=''`; `lazy_load` condition is `video_type===youtube` OR (`show_image_overlay===yes` AND `video_type!==hosted`); `poster` is honoured as the `poster` attribute. Elementor help 'Video widget' describes Play On Mobile as 'You can also enable the autoplay for mobile devices' and Lazy Load as loading 'the extra video stuff only once someone hits the play button' (embeds).
findings.breaks_when: A hero built with the Video widget and Autoplay is expected to stop downloading on phones by toggling Play On Mobile off - it does not (Chrome Android autoplays muted video inline anyway). Replacing with Image Overlay changes UX to click-to-play.
findings.how_to_apply: Hero: do not use the Video widget with Autoplay; use the HTML-widget `
findings.how_to_verify: Mobile Lighthouse `network-requests`: no `.mp4`/`.webm` before interaction; `<video>` in HTML has `preload="none"` and `poster`; desktop shows the clip after intersect/interaction.

findings.claim: Perfmatters' documented `perfmatters_delayed_scripts` example ('exclude a script from being delayed on a desktop device') and any `wp_is_mobile()`-based PHP filter are the same cache trap as Dynamic Visibility: the first visitor's UA decides which delayed-script markup is cached for everyone unless a mobile cache vary exists.
findings.detail: perfmatters.io/docs/delay-javascript: 'You can use the perfmatters_delayed_scripts filter to manipulate your delayed scripts. For example, you could exclude a script from being delayed on a desktop device.' The delay rewrite (`pmdelayedscript` type) happens in PHP at render time, so a device branch is baked into the cached HTML. Perfmatters offers only keyword exclusions and filters - no attribute - so device-specific delay decisions must be made client-side (matchMedia in the loader) instead.
findings.breaks_when: LiteSpeed 'Cache Mobile' OFF (inventory baseline) or FlyingPress separate mobile cache OFF while a Perfmatters/LiteSpeed/FlyingPress filter branches on `wp_is_mobile()`: desktop users get the mobile variant or vice versa after the first hit.
findings.how_to_apply: Audit rule: grep the child theme / mu-plugins / Code Snippets for `wp_is_mobile(`, `perfmatters_delayed_scripts`, `litespeed_optm_js_defer_exc`, `flying_press_` filters with device branches; flag any when the page cache has no mobile vary. Prefer the matchMedia gate in the facade loader (finding 4) - it is evaluated in the browser, so one cached HTML serves all devices.
findings.how_to_verify: curl the home page twice with the Lighthouse mobile UA and a desktop UA after the cache is warm (`x-litespeed-cache: hit`): the `<script` tags carrying `pmdelayedscript` / `litespeed/javascript` must be identical in both responses.

title: WooCommerce 11 / YITH Booking / WC Bookings / JetSmartFilters / payment gateways / WPML-Polylang: front-end footprint, cache rules and Delay-JS exclusions (Elementor Pro 4.3 stack)
summary: On the agency's e-shop and booking sites the WooCommerce layer itself is small (about 25 KB gzip of core CSS/JS on a brochure page) but it drags two uncacheable requests onto every page view: WooCommerce's cart-fragments XHR (?wc-ajax=get_refreshed_fragments, 1.5-1.7 s in the Lighthouse runs) and Elementor Pro's own admin-ajax call for the Menu Cart (1.9-2.0 s), plus Order Attribution's sourcebuster (6 KB) that is on by default and loads site-wide. WooCommerce 11.2 core is already conditional for select2, product-gallery scripts, password meter and block styles, and since 7.8 only enqueues wc-cart-fragments when a Cart widget renders, so the plugin must not fight core: the forcing agent on these sites is Elementor Pro's Menu Cart (confirmed on kand.dev6 where the child theme dequeues all WooCommerce scripts yet cart-fragments still loads). The real weight is in the add-ons: on limnoupolis.gr a YITH Booking Premium 2.1.8 from November 2019 (current is 5.37.0, 7 Oct 2026) loads 9 stylesheets + 6 scripts + jQuery UI datepicker + a cdnjs jQuery UI theme on every page including cart and account, and the legacy PayPal Express Checkout plugin (closed on wordpress.org 9 July 2024) still loads a script site-wide; on pallada.gr Nexi XPay loads a 14 KB "Pagodil" sticker script on the home page and Polylang 302-redirects / to /en/ with no-store for every visitor, costing 1.2 s before the first byte. WooCommerce Bookings (pallada) and JetSmartFilters 3.8.6 (kand) are properly conditional (bookable product: 51 KB booking form JS + 18 KB moment + jQuery UI; archive: 34 KB public.js + jQuery UI datepicker) and their AJAX endpoints (/?wc-ajax=wc_bookings_find_booked_day_blocks with nonces in booking_form_params; admin-ajax with jsf query params) define exact Delay-JS and cache exclusions. Cart, checkout and My Account are uncached by LiteSpeed, FlyingPress and WP Rocket by design and checkout carries gateway iframes/reCAPTCHA, so the plugin should measure them for regressions but not chase 95 there; home, shop archive (with and without ?jsf=), single product, bookable product and each language root are the pages where 95+ is realistic. Everything below cites pages that were actually opened; Elementor Pro's PHP is closed source, so its cart-fragment behaviour is inferred from public HTML and JS and marked as such.
critic_notes: Method: WebFetch could not resolve external hosts in this sandbox, so every doc was fetched with curl through the proxy and converted to text (files under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-everything-claude/bcd5434c-e674-5a25-baaa-faec7a068a29/scratchpad/critic/). WooCommerce 11.2.0 sources (class-wc-frontend-scripts.php, OrderAttributionController.php, class-wc-widget-cart.php), WP Rocket dynamic-lists.json and LiteSpeed esi.nonces.txt were read raw from GitHub. Elementor Pro 4.3.1 module.php and widgets/menu-cart.php were read read-only from kand.dev6 via Novamira novamira/read-file (no writes performed anywhere). Live checks today: kand.dev6 home handle list and pallada.gr '/' headers with three Accept-Language values. Not verified: per-handle byte sizes measured by the researcher, the limnoupolis plugin inventory, the exact WPML 5.1 hreflang option label, Everypay/Viva/Stripe plugin pages, and Elementor Pro's elements-handlers JS (the PHP side was enough). Lighthouse admin-ajax/wc-ajax timings were re-read from the local runs/*.json: they are post-LCP XHRs, so cart-fragments removal is a server/INP win more than a PageSpeed-score win. Skipped: checking kand-core.php itself again (prior read trusted) and FlyingPress 'Disable WooCommerce assets' handle list (not documented beyond the v4.3 announcement). Risk to flag: several 'must shorten TTL for nonces' recommendations rest on a plausible but undocumented failure mode; the only documented cache failure for WC Bookings is cache lifetime exceeding the 2-day wp_woocommerce_session_ cookie.
open_questions: Elementor Pro 4.3 PHP is closed source: the claim that the Menu Cart widget enqueues wc-cart-fragments (and whether the Site Settings 'Mini Cart template' toggle changes that) is inferred from kand.dev6's HTML plus the public elements-handlers.min.js; confirm on staging by removing the Menu Cart widget from the header template and checking whether cart-fragments.min.js disappears, and identify the admin-ajax POST seen in Lighthouse (likely action=elementor_menu_cart_fragments) with DevTools.

YITH Booking 2.1.8 (Nov 2019) on limnoupolis.gr: the exact nonce/stale-availability failure after 12-24 h on a LiteSpeed-cached bookable product was not reproduced (no booking was placed); the 'Update non-available dates on loading (AJAX)' option documented for current versions may not exist in 2.1.8; the exact admin-ajax action names of 2.1.8 (only the JS event names yith_wcbk_booking_form_update / yith_wcbk_form_update_response were observed) need confirming from the plugin's class.yith-wcbk-ajax.php via Novamira read-file.

Elementor Pro 4.3 Cart/Checkout widgets (shortcode-based) vs WooCommerce Cart/Checkout blocks: the handle sets differ (classic wc-cart/wc-checkout/selectWoo/password meter vs ~15 wc-blocks-* bundles on kand) but gzip sizes and Lighthouse scores were not compared on the same site; needs a controlled staging test before recommending one over the other.

WooCommerce Brands (merged into core) registers 'brands-styles' from wp_enqueue_scripts in class-wc-brands.php; it was not observed on any crawled page, but the enqueue condition in 11.2 was not read in full — verify on a site that uses brands.

The Interactivity API runtime (wp-interactivity) and wc-blocks-style were absent on all crawled pages; which WooCommerce 11.2 blocks (Product Collection, Mini-Cart block, Product Filters) pull them in on an Elementor Pro site and their gzip cost was not measured.

WooCommerce Bookings slot/availability AJAX handlers' nonce lifetime vs WP Rocket cache lifespan on pallada.gr: the 'nonce after 12-24 h' failure was reasoned from booking_form_params nonces + public cache headers, not reproduced; also check whether WP Rocket's lifespan is already set below 12 h there.

Checkout footprint of Attica Bank (webexpert), Everypay 3.10 and Nexi XPay with a non-empty cart (iframes, 3DS scripts, reCAPTCHA origin on pallada — which plugin injects it) was not measured because checkout redirects to cart without items; needs a Playwright-seeded cart.
voreniahorizon.gr emits no hreflang tags although WPML with two languages is active — confirm which WPML SEO option is off and whether the site is intentionally single-indexed.

JetSmartFilters compatibility statements from Crocoblock predate Elementor 4.x (Loop Grid provider since JSF 3.2.0; element-cache warning is generic to JetEngine listings) — an explicit test of JSF 3.8.6 + Elementor 4.3 Element Cache on a Loop Grid is still needed.

pallada.gr runs two page caches (WP Rocket 3.23.2.1 header + W3 Total Cache page-cache footer) and marakaki.com W3TC + Perfmatters; which layer is authoritative and whether both minify was not determined (read-only audit).
