findings.claim: WooCommerce 11.2 loads about 25 KB gzip of CSS/JS on every non-shop page (3 stylesheets, woocommerce.js + blockUI + js-cookie, optionally wc-add-to-cart) and these are the only core assets that are unconditional; select2, gallery scripts, password meter, wc-blocks-style and cart-fragments are already conditional in 11.2 and must not be re-dequeued blindly.
findings.detail: Measured on limnoupolis.gr (WooCommerce 11.2.1), gzip transfer / raw: woocommerce-general (woocommerce.css) 12.2 KB / 92.7 KB; woocommerce-layout 3.5 / 20.2 KB; woocommerce-smallscreen 1.4 / 8.7 KB; wc-jquery-blockui 3.5 / 9.6 KB; woocommerce (woocommerce.min.js) 1.5 / 4.3 KB; wc-js-cookie 0.8 / 1.7 KB; wc-add-to-cart 1.4 / 4.4 KB (only when WooCommerce > Settings > Products > 'Enable AJAX add to cart buttons on archives' = option woocommerce_enable_ajax_add_to_cart is yes; source class-wc-settings-products.php). Per class-wc-frontend-scripts.php at tag 11.2.0: 'woocommerce' script is enqueued always (deps wc-jquery-blockui, wc-js-cookie); styles woocommerce-layout/smallscreen/general come from get_styles() through filter woocommerce_enqueue_styles plus inline 'woocommerce-inline'; selectWoo + select2.css only on is_cart()||is_checkout()||is_account_page(); wc-zoom/wc-flexslider/wc-photoswipe-ui-default/wc-single-product only on product pages and only with theme support wc-product-gallery-zoom/-slider/-lightbox (Hello Elementor/Inglelandi declares all three, confirmed in the parent theme functions.php); wc-password-strength-meter only on account/lost-password or checkout with registration; wc-cart-fragments is registered but NOT enqueued by this file. Block styles: BlockTypesController::enqueue_block_style_for_classic_themes attaches each woocommerce/* block style to render_block_* so wc-blocks-style loads only when a block renders — zero occurrences of wc-blocks-style or wp-interactivity on any of the 7 crawled page types across 5 sites. Observed page-type matrix (handles): home/shop/archive = the 3 CSS + woocommerce/blockui/js-cookie (+wc-add-to-cart); single product adds wc-zoom, wc-flexslider, wc-photoswipe(+ui-default), wc-single-product, wc-add-to-cart-variation, underscore, wp-util; cart adds wc-cart, wc-country-select, wc-address-i18n, selectWoo, select2.css, zxcvbn-async + password-strength-meter; my-account adds wc-account-i18n, selectWoo, password meter. Perfmatters 'Disable Scripts' dequeues wc_price_slider, wc-single-product, wc-add-to-cart, wc-checkout, wc-add-to-cart-variation, wc-cart, wc-chosen, woocommerce, prettyPhoto(-init), jquery-blockui, jquery-placeholder, fancybox, jqueryui and the styles woocommerce-general/layout/smallscreen/woocommerce_frontend_styles/fancybox/chosen/prettyPhoto/woocommerce-inline everywhere except product, cart and checkout pages (Perfmatters doc). FlyingPress has 'Disable WooCommerce assets' in Bloat (v4.3 announcement). LiteSpeed Cache has no asset-unloading feature. The kand.dev6 child theme (inc/kand-core.php, read via Novamira) does the same with wp_dequeue_style/script at priority 99 when !is_woocommerce() && !is_cart() && !is_checkout() && !is_account_page() and it works on the live page (home shows no woocommerce.js/css).
findings.breaks_when: A brochure page contains a WooCommerce shortcode, Elementor Pro Products/Add-to-Cart widget or an Elementor popup with a product form: wc-add-to-cart and the WooCommerce notice/button CSS are then needed (Perfmatters' rule keeps them only on product/cart/checkout). Removing woocommerce-inline breaks button alignment on pages that print WooCommerce markup. Dequeuing selectWoo on account/checkout breaks country selects.
findings.how_to_apply: Prefer the official switch first: WooCommerce > Settings > Products > untick 'Enable AJAX add to cart buttons on archives' only if the shop does not use ajax add-to-cart buttons on archives (removes wc-add-to-cart site-wide). Then one of: Perfmatters > General > WooCommerce > 'Disable Scripts' ON; or FlyingPress > Bloat > 'Disable WooCommerce assets' ON; or (sites without either, e.g. LiteSpeed-only) a theme snippet identical to kand-core.php: add_action('wp_enqueue_scripts', function(){ if (is_woocommerce()||is_cart()||is_checkout()||is_account_page()) return; foreach(['woocommerce-general','woocommerce-layout','woocommerce-smallscreen'] as $h) wp_dequeue_style($h); foreach(['woocommerce','wc-add-to-cart'] as $h) wp_dequeue_script($h); }, 99). Do NOT add select2/selectWoo, wc-zoom, photoswipe, wc-blocks-style to a global dequeue list — core already scopes them. For the gallery libraries, if the design does not use zoom/slider, add_filter('woocommerce_single_product_flexslider_enabled','__return_false') and add_filter('woocommerce_single_product_zoom_enabled','__return_false') (both exist in class-wc-frontend-scripts.php and are used by kand-core.php).
findings.how_to_verify: curl -sL <home> | grep -oE 'id="(woocommerce-general|woocommerce-layout|woocommerce-smallscreen|woocommerce-js|wc-add-to-cart-js|wc-jquery-blockui-js|wc-js-cookie-js)"' must be empty on brochure pages and present on /shop/, /product/*, /cart/. Click-test: add to cart from an archive, open a product page gallery, change country on checkout, run Lighthouse mobile on home before/after (expect 20-25 KB less transfer and 1 fewer render-blocking stylesheet chain).
findings.correction: Perfmatters 'Disable Scripts' keeps WooCommerce assets on cart, checkout, account, single product, product category and shop pages (not just product/cart/checkout) and always dequeues the styles woocommerce-general/layout/smallscreen/woocommerce_frontend_styles/fancybox/chosen/prettyPhoto/woocommerce-inline/wc-block-style/wc-block-vendors-style. wc-add-to-cart is enqueued on every front-end page (not only archives) when 'Enable AJAX add to cart buttons on archives' is on. Risk stays low.

findings.claim: WooCommerce Order Attribution (on by default) enqueues sourcebuster.min.js + order-attribution.min.js (~6 KB gzip) on every front-end page of every WooCommerce site; the only way to remove the scripts is to disable the feature, because the wc_order_attribution_allow_tracking filter only flips a JS flag.
findings.detail: Observed on limnoupolis.gr, staging, kand.dev6, pallada.gr and marakaki.com home pages: sourcebuster-js (4.9 KB gz / 15.0 KB raw) and wc-order-attribution (1.1 KB gz / 2.5 KB raw) plus an inline wc_order_attribution object with ajaxurl admin-ajax.php and allowTracking:true. Source (OrderAttributionController.php, tag 11.2.0): on_init() bails only if feature 'order_attribution' is disabled, then add_action('wp_enqueue_scripts', enqueue_scripts_and_styles) unconditionally; apply_filters('wc_order_attribution_allow_tracking', true) is passed to the script as params.allowTracking, the scripts are still enqueued. Cookie lifetime filter wc_order_attribution_cookie_lifetime_months (default 0.00001 = session), session length wc_order_attribution_session_length_minutes (30), base64 option wc_order_attribution_use_base64_cookies (WooCommerce 9.0, for WAF false positives). Official doc: enable/disable at WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Features > Order Attribution; cookies expire with the session; data is only stored when an order is placed.
findings.breaks_when: The client's marketer uses the Orders > Attribution report (Origin column / Analytics). Disabling the feature stops attribution for orders placed while off (doc). Delaying (rather than disabling) is safe but the first-click attribution may be lost when the visitor leaves without interacting.
findings.how_to_apply: Agree with the client whether the attribution report is used. If not: WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Features > untick 'Order Attribution'. If yes but speed matters: keep it and add 'sourcebuster' and 'order-attribution' to the Delay-JS list (Perfmatters 'Delay JavaScript' box, LiteSpeed 'JS Delayed Includes', FlyingPress delay keywords, WP Rocket already covers inline js-extra by its built-in delay_js_exclusions only for exclusion — add the two file names to Delay JS). Do not use add_filter('wc_order_attribution_allow_tracking','__return_false') expecting the scripts to disappear.
findings.how_to_verify: grep -c 'sourcebuster' on the home HTML goes to 0 after disabling; place a test order and check WooCommerce > Orders > order edit > 'Order attribution' box shows 'Unknown' (expected when disabled). Lighthouse: 2 fewer requests, ~6 KB less JS.

findings.claim: Elementor Pro 4.3's Menu Cart widget forces wc-cart-fragments onto every page (WooCommerce core stopped doing that in 7.8) and adds its own admin-ajax call, producing two uncacheable requests per page view that cost 1.5-2.0 s each in the Lighthouse runs; the safe fix is Perfmatters 'Disable Cart Fragmentation' or FlyingPress 'Disable WooCommerce cart fragments', or delaying cart-fragments.min.js.
findings.detail: Evidence: kand.dev6 home page has NO WooCommerce widget and its child theme dequeues 'woocommerce' and 'wc-add-to-cart', yet the HTML contains wc-cart-fragments-js + wc_cart_fragments_params and the only WooCommerce UI is <div class="elementor-menu-cart--cart-type-side-cart"> (Elementor Pro 4.3.1). WooCommerce developer blog (16 Jun 2023): 'Beginning with WooCommerce 7.8 ... the script will now only be enqueued if the Cart Widget is rendered in a view' or when a third party registers it as a dependency/enqueues it; 11.2.0 class-wc-widget-cart.php is the only core enqueue (widget(), skipped on cart/checkout via filter woocommerce_widget_cart_is_hidden). Elementor Pro's elements-handlers.min.js (4.3.1, public) binds 'wc_fragments_refreshed removed_from_cart added_to_cart' and POSTs action 'elementor_menu_cart_fragments' with _nonce from ElementorProFrontendConfig.woocommerce.menu_cart.fragments_nonce to elementorProFrontend.config.ajaxurl — so Pro both depends on WooCommerce's fragments script and adds a second admin-ajax round trip. Lighthouse network logs: limnoupolis.gr /?wc-ajax=get_refreshed_fragments 1508 ms + admin-ajax.php POST 1968 ms; kand 1706 ms + 1959 ms; staging.limnoupolis get_refreshed_fragments timed out at 5001 ms (status -1). Elementor help: Menu Cart 'Automatically Update Cart' = refresh via Ajax; 'Automatically Open Cart' requires WooCommerce > Settings > Products AJAX add to cart; the Elementor Mini Cart template auto-enables under Elementor > Settings > Integrations > WooCommerce once the widget is used. Perfmatters 'Disable Cart Fragmentation' loads the script only when the woocommerce_cart_hash cookie exists (changelog 2.1.1); FlyingPress Bloat has 'Disable WooCommerce cart fragments' (v4.3). LiteSpeed has no toggle; its docs only offer 'Vary for Mini Cart' (OFF by default, creates a cache vary when the cart is not empty) and private ESI for the cart. Pro's PHP is closed source, so 'Pro enqueues wc-cart-fragments' is inferred from the HTML/JS, not read from code.
findings.breaks_when: Menu Cart item count/total shown from the page cache is stale for a visitor who already has items until the fragments script runs; with Perfmatters' cookie check the first add-to-cart on a brochure page updates only after the next page load; Pro's side cart 'Automatically Open Cart' after add-to-cart needs the fragments events, so with delay-until-interaction it still works (the click is the interaction) but with a hard dequeue it does not. YITH/WC Bookings add-to-cart flows and Polylang language-suffixed fragment names (observed fragment_name wc_fragments_..._lmn1_en on limnoupolis) are unaffected by the Perfmatters cookie approach.
findings.how_to_apply: Perfmatters > General > WooCommerce > 'Disable Cart Fragmentation' ON (recommended; keeps the cart working once the woocommerce_cart_hash cookie exists). FlyingPress > Bloat > 'Disable WooCommerce cart fragments' ON. LiteSpeed-only sites: add 'cart-fragments.min.js' to Page Optimization > Tuning > 'JS Delayed Includes' (Load JS Deferred must be 'Delayed'), or use a snippet add_action('wp_enqueue_scripts', function(){ if (!isset($_COOKIE['woocommerce_cart_hash'])) wp_dequeue_script('wc-cart-fragments'); }, 999). Alternative that removes the whole mechanism: replace the Pro Menu Cart with the WooCommerce Mini-Cart block (does not use the fragments API per the WooCommerce dev blog) — design change, test first. Never dequeue on cart/checkout/account (core already does not load it there).
findings.how_to_verify: Open a brochure page in a fresh private window: Network tab must show no ?wc-ajax=get_refreshed_fragments and no admin-ajax POST action=elementor_menu_cart_fragments. Add a product to cart, return to home: counter must show the item (cookie now present). Lighthouse mobile: 2 fewer requests and lower TBT/'network dependency tree'. Record before/after on kand.dev6 (home) and limnoupolis.gr (home).
findings.correction: Elementor Pro 4.3.1 Menu Cart render() always enqueues wc-cart-fragments and the widget's own JS POSTs action=elementor_menu_cart_fragments to admin-ajax.php; neither the 'Automatically Update Cart' nor 'Automatically Open Cart' switch disables this (they are CSS/UX toggles). Score gain is low (requests are post-LCP XHRs); gain is server load, TTFB under traffic and INP. Fixes as stated (Perfmatters cookie-gated disable, FlyingPress toggle, delay cart-fragments.min.js); note that delaying cart-fragments also delays Pro's refresh because Pro's handler listens to wc_fragments_refreshed.

findings.claim: On limnoupolis.gr the booking stack loads on every page: YITH Booking Premium 2.1.8 (released 5 Nov 2019, 'WC tested up to 3.8.x'; current premium is 5.37.0 of 7 Oct 2026) adds 9 stylesheets + 6 scripts (~20 KB gzip) plus jQuery UI datepicker and a cdnjs jQuery UI theme, and WP Simple Booking Calendar, Product Input Fields and dashicons add ~8 KB more — all of it also on cart and My Account.
findings.detail: Plugin header read via Novamira (read-only): Version 2.1.8, YITH_WCBK_VERSION '2.1.8', 'WC tested up to: 3.8.x'. YITH changelog: 2.1.8 released 5 November 2019; latest 5.37.0 7 October 2026 (adds WooCommerce 11.2 support). Home page handles and gzip sizes: yith-wcbk-search-form-css 2.2 KB, yith-wcbk-frontend-style 2.2, yith-wcbk-booking-form 2.1, yith-wcbk-simple-style 1.9, yith-wcbk-datepicker 1.6, people-selector 0.9, popup 0.8, date-range-picker 0.6, fields 0.3; scripts booking_form.min.js 2.2, datepicker.min.js 1.7, people-selector 1.4, yith-wcbk-dates 0.3, monthpicker 0.3, confirm-button 0.2; plus wp-includes jquery-ui core (6.3 KB) + datepicker (10.4 KB) and jquery-ui-datepicker-css from //cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/jqueryui/1.11.4/themes/smoothness/jquery-ui.min.css (6 KB, third-party origin, extra connection); wp-simple-booking-calendar-premium style 3.8 KB + script 3.1 KB (admin-ajax action wpsbc_change with search_form_nonce); product-input-fields alg-datepicker 0.4 KB; dashicons.min.css enqueued for guests. The same list appears on /cart/, /my-account/, /shopping/ and the bookable product /tickets/fixed-date/ (where YITH additionally loads fields.min.js, DOMPurify and TipTip). YITH FAQ: with a cache plugin use Booking Forms > 'Update non-available dates on loading (AJAX)' so non-available dates are fetched via Ajax instead of baked into the cached page (option may not exist in 2.1.8). YITH loads Google Maps only when the Google Maps module is enabled under YITH > Add-ons > Modules and an API key is set in YITH > Booking > Settings > General settings (no Maps request observed). Booking form JS events observed on the product page: yith_wcbk_booking_form_update, yith_wcbk_form_update_response, yith_wcbk_booking_form_loaded; requests go to admin-ajax.php (ajax_url in yith params) and WooCommerce's /?wc-ajax=%%endpoint%% for add-to-cart.
findings.breaks_when: YITH search forms (shortcode/widget) are placed on non-product pages (the home uses one: booking-search-form.css is needed there); unloading jQuery UI datepicker where a search form or Product Input Fields date field exists breaks the picker; delaying booking_form.min.js on the product page breaks price updates until interaction (acceptable) but delaying jQuery itself breaks the form init. Updating YITH from 2.1.8 to 5.x is a major upgrade (new settings, data migration) and needs staging first.
findings.how_to_apply: 1) Plan a YITH Booking update 2.1.8 -> 5.37.0 on staging (prerequisite for any supported fix; 2.1.8 predates WooCommerce 4). 2) Per-page unload with Perfmatters Script Manager or FlyingPress/LiteSpeed cannot target YITH handles natively on this LiteSpeed-only site, so use a snippet: add_action('wp_enqueue_scripts', function(){ if (is_product() || is_cart() || is_checkout() || is_page([<search-results page id>])) return; if (is_front_page()) { /* keep yith-wcbk-search-form-css, yith-wcbk-datepicker-*, jquery-ui-datepicker for the search form */ return; } foreach(['yith-wcbk-fields','yith-wcbk-people-selector','yith-wcbk-date-range-picker','yith-wcbk-booking-form','yith-wcbk-frontend-style','yith-wcbk-popup','yith-wcbk-search-form','yith-wcbk-datepicker','yith-wcbk-simple-style','wpsbc-style','dashicons'] as $h) wp_dequeue_style($h); foreach(['yith-wcbk-dates','yith-wcbk-datepicker','yith-wcbk-monthpicker','yith-wcbk-people-selector','yith-wcbk-booking-form','yith-wcbk-confirm-button','wpsbc-script','alg-datepicker','jquery-ui-datepicker'] as $h) wp_dequeue_script($h); }, 999). 3) Self-host the jQuery UI theme CSS instead of cdnjs (copy smoothness/jquery-ui.min.css to the child theme and wp_deregister_style('jquery-ui-datepicker') + register local) to drop the third-party origin. 4) In YITH > Booking > Settings > Booking Forms enable 'Update non-available dates on loading (AJAX)' once on 5.x. 5) Delay-JS: on bookable product pages exclude jquery, jquery-ui-core, jquery-ui-datepicker, yith-wcbk-*, booking_form.min.js, fields.min.js; on other pages they can be delayed or removed.
findings.how_to_verify: Before/after on home, /cart/, /my-account/: count of yith-wcbk-* link/script tags (grep -c 'yith-wcbk') and total gzip weight; Lighthouse 'render-blocking resources' loses the cdnjs stylesheet. Functional: on /tickets/fixed-date/ pick a date, change people, see price update and add to cart; on home submit the booking search form; on cart change quantities. Repeat after the YITH update on staging.

findings.claim: WooCommerce Bookings (pallada.gr) is correctly conditional — nothing on the home page, ~90 KB gzip on a bookable product (wc-bookings-booking-form 50.8 KB, moment 18.4 KB, jQuery UI datepicker 10.4 KB + core 6.3 KB, jquery-ui-styles.css 8 KB, frontend.css 2.2 KB) and two stylesheets on checkout — and its calendar depends on jQuery + nonces embedded in the cached page, so Delay-JS must exclude it and page-cache TTL must stay below the 24 h nonce life.
findings.detail: pallada.gr/en/product/olive-oil-tour-tasting-chania/ (WooCommerce Bookings, served by WP Rocket 3.23.2.1 cache: cache-control public, max-age=0, x-powered-by: WP Rocket/3.23.2.1) loads jquery-ui-style-css (woocommerce-bookings/dist/jquery-ui-styles.css 8.0 KB gz / 47.7 KB), wc-bookings-styles-css (dist/frontend.css 2.2 KB / 12.0 KB), jquery-ui-core-js, jquery-ui-datepicker-js, wc-bookings-booking-form-js (dist/frontend.js 50.8 KB gz / 245.3 KB raw), moment-js (wp-includes moment.min.js 18.4 KB gz / 58.8 KB). Inline data: wc_bookings_date_picker_args.ajax_url = '/en/?wc-ajax=wc_bookings_find_booked_day_blocks' (language-prefixed by Polylang), booking_form_params = {cache_ajax_requests:'false', nonce:{get_end_time_html:'7af3ec2d85', show_available_month_blocks:'bd954acf92'}, ajax_url: admin-ajax.php}, wc_bookings_booking_form_<id> with duration/resource settings. /en/checkout/ loads only jquery-ui-styles.css + frontend.css from Bookings (plus Product Add-Ons css/js); /en/ home loads nothing from Bookings; simple products load nothing. WooCommerce docs: the calendar's availability comes from the /?wc-ajax XHR 'wc_bookings_find_booked_day_blocks' made when the calendar loads; 'Why is the calendar not displaying' — typically caching plugins or Cloudflare (disable Rocket Loader), and caches whose expiry exceeds the wp_woocommerce_session_ cookie can make the calendar load indefinitely with a 403 in the console; the fix is to exclude WooCommerce cookies from caching. Changelog 3.12.0 (2026-10-14): requires WordPress 7.0 and WooCommerce 11.1, 'Improved booking calendar loading performance', and an older entry added filter disable_find_booked_day_blocks_nonce_check for the get_end_time_html handler (so nonce checks exist on these AJAX handlers). WordPress nonces are valid 12-24 h; a page cached for a week (LiteSpeed Default Public Cache TTL 604800) or WP Rocket's default lifespan carries stale nonces into booking_form_params.
findings.breaks_when: Delay-JS or 'load after interaction' applied to jquery, jquery-ui-datepicker, moment or wc-bookings-booking-form on a bookable product: the calendar does not render until the user moves/clicks and may initialise in the wrong order; Remove-Unused-CSS/UCSS drops .ui-datepicker and .wc-bookings-* classes that only appear after the XHR (calendar shows unstyled); page cache TTL > 12 h serves nonces that fail on get_end_time_html / show_available_month_blocks (time-slot lists stop loading until the page is purged); Cloudflare Rocket Loader on the product page; FlyingPress/WP Rocket serving cached product pages to visitors with wp_woocommerce_session_ is fine for display but combine with 'Bypass Cache for Cookies: woocommerce_items_in_cart' only if the calendar misbehaves (it lowers hit ratio).
findings.how_to_apply: Delay-JS exclusions (all plugins, as partial strings): 'woocommerce-bookings', 'moment.min.js', 'jquery-ui', 'jquery.min.js', 'jquery-migrate', 'wc_bookings_' (inline). WP Rocket: File Optimization > Delay JavaScript execution > Excluded JavaScript Files add those; Remove Unused CSS > CSS safelist add .ui-datepicker, .wc-bookings-booking-form, .wc-bookings-date-picker, .block-picker, .fully_booked, .partial_booked. Cache TTL: WP Rocket Cache > Cache Lifespan <= 10 hours; LiteSpeed Cache > Cache > TTL > Default Public Cache TTL 36000 (10 h) or add the bookable product URIs to Cache > Excludes > Do Not Cache URIs; LiteSpeed Enterprise with ESI: Cache > ESI > 'Enable ESI' ON and add nonce actions 'get_end_time_html' and 'show_available_month_blocks' (and 'woocommerce-login', already predefined) to 'ESI Nonces' so they expire independently (predefined list in lscache_wp data/esi.nonces.txt does not include WC Bookings or YITH). Never add 'wc-ajax' or 'admin-ajax.php' URLs to any cache. Keep Polylang's language prefix: the plugin's cache exclusion patterns must match /en/?wc-ajax=... as well as /?wc-ajax=....
findings.how_to_verify: Open the bookable product in a private window 13+ hours after the last purge (or set the TTL to 1 h and wait): the month calendar must load (Network: 200 for ?wc-ajax=wc_bookings_find_booked_day_blocks), pick a day, the time-slot/end-time list must appear (admin-ajax action get_end_time_html returns 200 not 403/-1), add to cart succeeds. Lighthouse on the product page: wc-bookings frontend.js and moment in 'reduce unused JavaScript' is expected; target is TBT and LCP, not removal. Record with Playwright: click the first available day and assert '.wc-bookings-booking-form .wc-bookings-booking-cost' becomes visible.
findings.correction: Keep the Delay-JS exclusions. Replace 'TTL must stay below the 24 h nonce life' with: WooCommerce documents the breakage as cache lifetime > wp_woocommerce_session_ (2 days) causing 403/endless loading; nonce-based failure on get_end_time_html/show_available_month_blocks is plausible but undocumented. Recommended: TTL <= 10 h on bookable product URLs as a precaution, verify by testing a page cached > 12 h.

findings.claim: JetSmartFilters 3.8.6 (kand.dev6) loads only on filtered archive pages (public.js 34 KB gzip / 197 KB raw + jet-plugins.js 2 KB + jQuery UI core/datepicker 17 KB, inline CSS) and filters via admin-ajax with 'jsf' query strings; Crocoblock itself says use 'Page Reload' with Loop Grid or any server cache, exclude /wp-content/plugins/jet-smart-filters/ and admin-ajax.php from Delay-JS, and never collapse the jsf/tax/meta/sort/pagenum parameters in the page cache.
findings.detail: kand.dev6.inglelandi.com/product-category/rings/ (JetSmartFilters 3.8.6, Elementor Pro 4.3.1 archive template): jet-plugins-js 2.2 KB gz, jet-smart-filters-js (assets/js/public.js) 34.2 KB gz / 197.2 KB raw, jquery-ui-core 6.3 KB, jquery-ui-datepicker 10.4 KB (enqueued although no date filter is visible), styles inlined as #jet-smart-filters-inline-css. Inline JetSmartFilterSettings: ajaxurl admin-ajax.php, provider selectors for epro-archive-products, epro-archive, epro-loop-builder, epro-products, epro-posts, epro-portfolio, jet-engine, jet-woo-products-grid, woocommerce-archive/shortcode; misc.url_type 'plain' with valid_url_params ['jsf','tax','meta','date','sort','alphabet','_s','_sm','pagenum','plain_query','jet-smart-filters','jet_paged','search','_tax_query_','_meta_q...']; providers on the page use apply type 'ajax' with jsf_signature/jsf_query_signature tokens. Home, product and cart pages load no JSF assets. Crocoblock KB 'AJAX, Mixed, Page Reload': AJAX = no URL change, 'when LiteSpeed Cache / WP Rocket / any server-side cache is used, AJAX works in preview but shows cached results on live' and 'If one uses static caching (LiteSpeed, WP Rocket), Do not cache URLs with GET parameters should be activated'; with the Elementor Pro Loop Grid provider the Custom Search URL is not passed correctly with AJAX; Mixed = URL changes + AJAX; Page Reload recommended for Loop Grid and cache. Providers overview: Elementor Pro Loop Grid provider since JSF 3.2.0, loop must have 'Is Filterable' enabled. Crocoblock WP Rocket review (updated 03/06/2026): if filters stop after enabling WP Rocket exclude /wp-content/plugins/jet-smart-filters/ and admin-ajax.php from Delay JS; element cache can leave JetEngine listings empty/stale. Cache plugins: LiteSpeed caches each query-string URL separately by default and 'Drop Query String' (Cache > Cache tab) must not list jsf/tax/meta/sort/pagenum; FlyingPress by default does NOT cache URLs with query parameters (bypass) and 'Separate Cache for Query Parameters' can list parameters that change content; WP Rocket's built-in cache_ignored_parameters list is tracking params only (utm_*, fbclid, gclid, ...), jsf is not ignored. Compatibility with Elementor 4.3 Element Cache and Pro Loop Grid 4.3 specifically is not documented by Crocoblock; the 3.2.0 Loop Grid provider note and the generic element-cache warning are the closest statements.
findings.breaks_when: Delay-JS delays public.js/jet-plugins.js or admin-ajax: filters render but do nothing until interaction and the first click is lost; Elementor Element Cache on the Loop Grid/Archive Products widget serves the unfiltered grid; LiteSpeed 'Drop Query String' containing jsf (or FlyingPress ignoring it) serves the unfiltered archive for filtered URLs; UCSS removes .jet-filter/.jet-checkboxes-list classes that appear only after AJAX; 'Mixed' apply type plus a cache that bypasses all query strings means every filtered page is a cache MISS (slow TTFB, not wrong).
findings.how_to_apply: Smart Filters > Settings (per filter widget) > Apply type: 'Page Reload' for Loop Grid providers and on cached sites; otherwise 'Mixed'. Elementor: on the filtered Loop Grid/Archive Products widget set Advanced > 'Element caching' to Inactive (do not rely on the global 24 h default). Delay-JS exclusions: '/wp-content/plugins/jet-smart-filters/', 'admin-ajax.php', 'JetSmartFilterSettings', 'jquery.min.js', 'jquery-ui'. LiteSpeed: Cache > Cache > Drop Query String — keep only tracking params (utm_*, fbclid, gclid), never jsf/tax/meta/sort/pagenum; FlyingPress: Caching > 'Separate Cache for Query Parameters' add jsf, tax, meta, sort, pagenum, jet_paged, _s if filtered pages should be cached, else leave bypass; W3TC/WP Rocket: keep query-string pages uncached (default) and rely on the 'Page Reload' type. Unload jquery-ui-datepicker on archives without a date filter with Perfmatters Script Manager (handle jquery-ui-datepicker) only after checking no JSF Date filter exists.
findings.how_to_verify: On /product-category/rings/ apply a material filter: results change, URL updates (Mixed/Reload), reload keeps the state; compare cached vs uncached (?nocache=1) output; with Delay-JS on, the very first click must work. Lighthouse on the archive before/after: public.js stays (expected), jquery-ui-datepicker disappears if removed; 'reduce unused JavaScript' drops ~17 KB.

findings.claim: Payment gateways actually present on the 10 sites are redirect/iframe-style Greek and Italian gateways plus one abandoned plugin: limnoupolis.gr runs Attica Bank (webexpert), Everypay 3.10, Mastercard Simplify and the legacy WooCommerce PayPal Checkout (PPEC) that was closed on wordpress.org on 9 July 2024 yet still loads a script on every page; pallada.gr runs Nexi XPay 8.4.0 which loads a 14 KB 'Pagodil' sticker script site-wide; marakaki.com runs Klarna Payments (checkout only). Stripe and PayPal Payments are not installed anywhere.
findings.detail: limnoupolis.gr plugin directory (Novamira list-directory, read-only): webexpert-woocommerce-atticabank-payment-gateway, everypay-payment-gateway, woocommerce-simplify-payment-gateway-plugin-master, woocommerce-gateway-paypal-express-checkout; checkout HTML shows payment_method_attica_gateway and ppec. PPEC: wordpress.org says 'This plugin has been closed as of July 9, 2024 ... Reason: Author Request', version 2.1.3, tested up to WP 5.8.18; it enqueues wc-gateway-ppec-order-review.js (0.4 KB gz) on home, shop, product, cart and account pages. Everypay Payment Gateway 3.10 ('Last updated 4 months ago', tested up to 7.0.7, '3ds2 iframe') — no site-wide assets observed. pallada.gr: cartasi-x-pay (Nexi XPay 8.4.0, tested up to 7.0.7, '3D Secure 2', 'Compatibility with WooCommerce Block Checkout') enqueues xpay-checkout-js (xpay.js 0.7 KB gz), pagodil-script-js (pagodil-sticker.min.js 14.2 KB gz / 71.4 KB raw), xpay-checkout-css and wc-gateway-xpay-blocks-integration-style-css on the HOME page and shop; checkout also loads www.google.com/recaptcha/api (whitelisted by FAZ cookie manager). marakaki.com /checkout/ loads klarna-payments-for-woocommerce assets; none on home. Generic rules for the gateways the agency may add: WooCommerce Stripe 11.1.0 ('Last updated 3 days ago', tested up to 7.1.3): Payment Request Buttons fully replaced by Express Checkout in 10.0.0; express buttons are configured per location (checkout page, individual product pages, cart page) at WooCommerce > Settings > Payments > Stripe > Payment Methods > Express checkouts (Amazon Pay, Apple Pay/Google Pay, Link) — untick product and cart locations to keep Stripe's SDK off those pages. WooCommerce PayPal Payments 4.1.3 (2026-09-09): legacy-UI doc 'Smart Button Locations — Select the pages where you want the PayPal buttons to be shown'; defaults Checkout, single product, Cart; 'Mini Cart buttons are disabled by default. Enabling this section results in the PayPal scripts loading on (almost) every page of the website'; 4.1.2 'Scope reCAPTCHA assets and markup to active PayPal payment locations', 4.1.1 fixed Pay upon Invoice enqueued outside checkout with Block Mini Cart; new-UI Styling > Location checkboxes Cart / Classic Checkout / Express Checkout / Mini Cart / Product Page. Viva.com Smart Checkout for WooCommerce 1.1.0 is redirect-based ('Move the Smart Checkout redirect into a separate, cache-friendly script'), so no site-wide JS. WP Rocket's built-in defer_js_external_exclusions already contains www.paypal.com/sdk/js.
findings.breaks_when: Removing or delaying xpay.js/pagodil-sticker only on checkout breaks the Nexi 3DS/redirect flow; delaying js.stripe.com, www.paypal.com/sdk/js, Klarna or recaptcha/api on checkout breaks card fields, express buttons and 3-D Secure iframes (they must run before the customer clicks Place order); deleting PPEC without configuring a replacement removes PayPal as a payment method.
findings.how_to_apply: limnoupolis: deactivate and delete woocommerce-gateway-paypal-express-checkout (closed plugin; replace with WooCommerce PayPal Payments if PayPal is still wanted, with Smart Button Locations = Checkout only and Mini Cart unticked); remove woocommerce-simplify-* if unused. pallada: Perfmatters Script Manager (or a snippet wp_dequeue_script('pagodil-script'); wp_dequeue_script('xpay-checkout-js'); wp_dequeue_style('xpay-checkout-css'); wp_dequeue_style('wc-gateway-xpay-blocks-integration-style') when !is_checkout() && !is_product()) — check XPay settings for a Pagodil (instalment sticker) toggle first and turn it off if Pagodil is not offered. Stripe (if added): WooCommerce > Settings > Payments > Stripe > Payment Methods > Express checkouts > Customize > untick 'Individual product pages' and 'The cart page'. PayPal Payments (if added): Smart Button Locations = Checkout only; leave Mini Cart off. Delay-JS: NEVER on checkout for js.stripe.com, paypal.com/sdk/js, recaptcha/api, klarna, xpay.js, 'wc-checkout', 'wc-cart'; SAFE to delay or unload gateway scripts on non-checkout pages; Perfmatters already skips cart/checkout/account URLs from its optimizations. WP Rocket: tick the WooCommerce/payment one-click exclusions and add '/cartasi-x-pay/', 'klarna', 'js.stripe.com', 'paypal.com/sdk' to Excluded JavaScript Files.
findings.how_to_verify: grep the home HTML for 'cartasi-x-pay' (pallada) and 'paypal-express-checkout' (limnoupolis): expect 0 after the change, >0 on checkout (pallada). Complete a 1 EUR test order per gateway in sandbox/test mode including a 3DS challenge; confirm no console errors from delayed scripts on /checkout/. Lighthouse home: pallada minus ~15 KB JS and one fewer stylesheet.

findings.claim: Polylang's browser-language detection on pallada.gr makes '/' a 302 to '/en/' with 'cache-control: no-cache, no-store' for every visitor (even Accept-Language: el and no header), adding 1.18 s before the first byte of the real home page in Lighthouse; turning detection off and hiding the default-language code (or excluding '/' from cache and letting the cookie do the rest) removes it.
findings.detail: curl https://pallada.gr/ with Accept-Language en-US, el-GR and none: all return HTTP/2 302 Location https://pallada.gr/en/ with cache-control no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, max-age=0. Lighthouse run for pallada.gr: requestedUrl https://pallada.gr/ -> finalDisplayUrl https://pallada.gr/en/; the 302 took 1183 ms, the /en/ document 1869 ms. /en/ is served by WP Rocket 3.23.2.1 (x-powered-by header; cache-control public, max-age=0) AND W3 Total Cache ('Performance optimized by W3 Total Cache ... Page Caching using' footer comment) — two page caches stacked on the same site (the audit summary recorded only W3TC). Polylang doc 'Detect the browser preferred language': first visit to the homepage is redirected to the homepage in the browser's language, default language if none matches, a cookie is set so returning visitors go to their last browsed language; 'If you don't want any redirection to occur, you must deactivate the browser preferred language detection and hide the default language code in URLs'. Cookie name pll_language (constant PLL_COOKIE; false disables cookies but breaks the login translation). pallada sets the cookie client-side: inline script pll_cookie_script-js-after writes document.cookie = 'pll_language=en; expires=+1 year; path=/; secure; SameSite=Lax' (Perfmatters wraps it as type=pmdelayedscript, harmless). WP Rocket doc (updated 13 March 2026): with Polylang browser detection 'the first visit for each user will be uncached so that the language can be accurately detected'; for a home-to-default-language redirect 'exclude the homepage from the cache. In WP Rocket, go to Advanced Rules > Never Cache URL(s) and enter: /'. hreflang: pallada emits el/en alternates; limnoupolis.gr also runs polylang + polylang-wc (plugin list) and its cart fragment name is language-suffixed (wc_fragments_..._lmn1_en).
findings.breaks_when: Greek-browser visitors who expect to land on Greek at '/' will get the default language instead once detection is off (set the default language to the majority audience first); if detection stays on and '/' is cached by W3TC/LiteSpeed/Cloudflare, every visitor gets the cached redirect (wrong language); removing one of the two page caches must be done on staging (W3TC minify/object cache may also be in use).
findings.how_to_apply: Polylang > Settings > 'Detect browser language' deactivate, and Settings > 'URL modifications' > tick 'Hide URL language information for default language' and set the default language = main audience (then '/' is the Greek or English home with 200 and cacheable; language switcher still works via cookie/URL). If the client insists on detection: WP Rocket > Advanced Rules > Never Cache URL(s): '/' (and LiteSpeed: Cache > Excludes > Do Not Cache URIs: '^/$'), accept the uncached first hit. Remove the duplicate cache layer on pallada (keep WP Rocket, deactivate W3 Total Cache page cache, or vice versa) so only one plugin rewrites HTML. Keep '/el/' and '/en/' as separate cached URLs (directory mode works with every cache plugin; LiteSpeed also stores one copy per language URL).
findings.how_to_verify: curl -sI https://pallada.gr/ returns 200 (or a cacheable 301 to the default language if that design is chosen) with no 'no-store'; Lighthouse requestedUrl == finalUrl and TTFB on '/' drops by ~1.1 s; switch language in the header and reload: pll_language cookie value changes and pages stay in the chosen language; only one cache signature remains in headers/HTML (either x-powered-by: WP Rocket or the W3TC footer comment).
findings.correction: The cause is Polylang's default-language home redirect ('/' -> '/en/' because the default language code is not hidden), not (only) browser detection — a Greek Accept-Language also lands on /en/. Fix: Polylang > Settings > URL modifications > 'Hide URL language information for default language' (and set the default language to the main audience), plus switch off 'Detect browser language' if a cacheable 200 on '/' is wanted. If the redirect is kept, WP Rocket 'Never Cache URL(s): /' works but WP Rocket warns it can conflict with other cache layers (W3TC on pallada).

findings.claim: WPML's front-end footprint on voreniahorizon.gr and marakaki.com is tiny (language-cookie.js ~0 KB, one or two switcher stylesheets, a dropdown script, plus WCML multi-currency and cart scripts on marakaki) and cache plugins already store one copy per language URL; the real WPML risks are the 'Store a language cookie ... for AJAX' option (default on since 4.5, breaks or is broken by caches), the one-time JS browser redirect (off by default) and voreniahorizon emitting no hreflang tags at all.
findings.detail: voreniahorizon.gr home (FlyingPress 4.22.x cache HIT, WPML sitepress 5.1): wpml-cookie-js -> sitepress-multilingual-cms/res/js/cookies/language-cookie.js (0 KB transfer in Lighthouse), inline var wpml_cookies, wpml-legacy-horizontal-list-0-css and wpml-menu-item-0-css (both minified by FlyingPress), flag SVG; hreflang/alternate link count = 0. marakaki.com home (W3 Total Cache + Perfmatters): wpml-cookie-js (minified by Perfmatters), wpml-legacy-dropdown-click-0-js + -css, wcml-dropdown-0-css, wcml-mc-scripts (woocommerce-multilingual/res/js/wcml-multi-currency.min.js) and cart-widget (woocommerce-multilingual/res/js/cart_widget.min.js); 2 hreflang occurrences. WPML doc: 'Store a language cookie to support language filtering for AJAX' (WPML > Languages, Language filtering for AJAX operations) sets the cookie with JavaScript for logged-out users so it works on cached pages; 'If you use WPML 4.5 or later, this setting is enabled by default. If you notice it interferes with your caching plugin, you can disable it'. WPML 'Automatic Redirect Based on Browser Language': default is to not redirect; options 'Only redirect visitors if translations exist' / 'Always redirect'; WPML redirects only once (so visitors can switch) and warns that Google follows JS redirects. LiteSpeed third-party doc: WPML — 'Separate cache copies are stored for each page for each language'. WP Rocket doc (13 Mar 2026): detects WPML config, caches/purges/preloads per language, and for WooCommerce Multilingual uses mandatory cookies (wcml_client_currency_language etc.; with Multicurrency 'Client Location' the cookie wcml_client_country must be set before caching starts). Elementor duplication: each language home loads its own 4 elementor-post-N.css files (translated header/footer/kit/page IDs) — one set per rendered page, not double; fonts are not duplicated unless the translated kit differs (not observed).
findings.breaks_when: Disabling the AJAX language cookie on a WooCommerce + WCML site makes AJAX responses (cart fragments, Elementor Pro forms, JetSmartFilters) fall back to the default language; enabling 'Always redirect' adds a JS redirect on the first visit of every language page and can hurt indexing; adding WCML cookies to 'Bypass Cache for Cookies' lowers hit ratio to near zero on multi-currency stores.
findings.how_to_apply: Keep WPML > Languages > 'Store a language cookie to support language filtering for AJAX' ON on WooCommerce sites (marakaki) and test cart fragments in the second language; it may be turned OFF on brochure sites without AJAX content (voreniahorizon) — the 0 KB script is not worth chasing, prefer leaving it. WPML > Settings > 'Browser language redirect' = 'Do not redirect' (default) unless the client asks. Fix SEO on voreniahorizon: WPML > Languages > 'SEO Options' > enable 'Display alternative languages in the HEAD section' (verify the exact label in 5.1) so hreflang alternates are output. Cache: no per-language exclusion needed with directory URLs on LiteSpeed/WP Rocket/FlyingPress; with Cloudflare APO or a CDN, bypass cache on cookie wp-wpml_current_language only if language is negotiated by cookie rather than URL. Delay-JS: language-cookie.js and the legacy dropdown script are safe to delay; keep 'wpml_cookies' out of 'delay inline' lists only if AJAX content must be language-correct on first interaction.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -s https://voreniahorizon.gr/ | grep -c hreflang > 0 after the SEO change; in the second language add to cart (marakaki) and confirm the Menu Cart/mini cart fragments come back in that language; Lighthouse per language root (/, /en/) scores within 2 points of each other; FlyingPress/WP Rocket cache directory shows both language folders.

findings.claim: Exact Delay-JS / defer exclusion strings per optimizer for this stack: jQuery and jQuery UI, WooCommerce frontend scripts on shop pages, booking form scripts, JetSmartFilters, gateway SDKs and reCAPTCHA must never be delayed; sourcebuster/order-attribution, cart-fragments, pixels and cookie banners are safe to delay; the matching syntax differs (WP Rocket regex per line, LiteSpeed partial strings without wildcards or data-no-defer="1", Perfmatters file/inline substrings, FlyingPress case-insensitive keywords).
findings.detail: WP Rocket (doc 1560, last updated 10 Jan 2025): use One-click exclusions boxes, else 'Excluded JavaScript Files'; its core auto-exclusion list (dynamic-lists.json delay_js_exclusions, 75 entries) contains generic items like 'js-extra', 'gforms_recaptcha_', 'wpformsRecaptchaCallback', 'var gtm4wp', 'consent.cookiebot.com/uc.js' but nothing for WooCommerce, Stripe, PayPal, Bookings or Jet; defer_js_external_exclusions includes 'www.paypal.com/sdk/js'; doc 1837 (18 Sep 2024) gives the jQuery pattern \/jquery(-migrate)?-?([0-9.]+)?(.min|.slim|.slim.min)?.js(\?(.*))?( |'|"|>|$). LiteSpeed (pageopt doc): Page Optimization > JS Settings > 'Load JS Deferred' = OFF | Deferred | Delayed ('Delayed runs the JS only after detecting user activity'); Tuning > 'JS Deferred/Delayed Excludes' — 'full URI or partial strings to match; do not use wildcards'; 'JS Delayed Includes' for opt-in delay; HTML attribute data-no-defer="1" and filter litespeed_optm_gm_js_exc for Guest Mode. Perfmatters (delay-javascript doc): Delay Behavior 'Only Delay Specified Scripts' (list) or 'Delay All Scripts' with 'Excluded from Delay' (source URL or unique inline string, one per line), optional 'Delay Timeout' 15 s (filter perfmatters_delay_js_timeout); documented Elementor exclusions jquery.min.js, jquery-migrate.min.js, jquery.smartmenus.min.js, jquery.sticky.min.js, /elementor/assets/js/frontend.min.js, /elementor-pro/assets/js/frontend.min.js; 'we automatically exclude specific URLs from optimizations when running WooCommerce (cart, checkout, account)'; examples to delay: fbevents.js, fbq(, /gtm.js, /gtag/js, gtag(. FlyingPress (Delay All JavaScript doc): modes Defer vs 'Load after interaction' ('not suitable if your site has sliders, animations, menus ... above-the-fold'); exclusions are partial, case-insensitive keywords matched against the whole script tag (src, id, inline), wildcards unsupported; '/wp-content/plugins/' excludes all plugin scripts. Crocoblock asks for '/wp-content/plugins/jet-smart-filters/' and 'admin-ajax.php'. WooCommerce Bookings doc blames Cloudflare Rocket Loader for calendars not rendering. Verdict table (handle -> loads where -> gzip KB -> safe removal -> Delay-JS): woocommerce-general/layout/smallscreen -> all pages -> 12.2/3.5/1.4 -> Perfmatters Disable Scripts, FP Disable WooCommerce assets, snippet -> n/a CSS (never UCSS-strip on shop pages); woocommerce + wc-jquery-blockui + wc-js-cookie -> all -> 1.5/3.5/0.8 -> same -> never on shop/product/cart/checkout, safe on brochure; wc-add-to-cart -> all when ajax archives on -> 1.4 -> WC setting -> never on archives/product; sourcebuster-js + wc-order-attribution -> all -> 4.9+1.1 -> WC Features toggle -> safe; wc-cart-fragments -> all pages with Pro Menu Cart -> 1.0 + 2 uncached XHR -> Perfmatters/FP toggles -> safe (after test); selectWoo/select2 -> cart/checkout/account -> n/a -> leave -> never; wc-zoom/flexslider/photoswipe/single-product -> product -> n/a -> theme filters -> after test; wc-cart/wc-checkout/wc-country-select/wc-address-i18n/password meter -> cart/checkout/account -> n/a -> leave -> never; yith-wcbk-* (6 js, 9 css) -> all (2.1.8) -> ~20 total -> snippet per page -> never on bookable product, safe elsewhere; wc-bookings-booking-form + moment + jquery-ui-datepicker -> bookable product (+2 css on checkout) -> 50.8/18.4/10.4 -> none -> never; jet-smart-filters public.js + jet-plugins + jquery-ui -> filtered archives -> 34.2/2.2/16.7 -> none (datepicker only if no date filter) -> never; xpay.js + pagodil-sticker -> all (pallada) -> 0.7/14.2 -> Script Manager/snippet off checkout -> never on checkout, remove elsewhere; wc-gateway-ppec-order-review -> all (limnoupolis) -> 0.4 -> delete plugin -> n/a; wpml-cookie + switcher assets -> all -> ~0-2 -> leave -> safe; pll_cookie_script inline -> all -> 0 -> leave -> safe; faz/complianz cookie banner js -> all -> 33-36 -> leave -> after test (consent must still block pixels); fbevents/gtm/pixelyoursite -> all -> 114+159+63 (fb) -> move into GTM -> safe.
findings.breaks_when: Any 'delay all' mode on cart/checkout/account/bookable-product/filtered-archive pages without these exclusions: add-to-cart buttons, country selects, booking calendars, filters and 3DS iframes stop working until interaction or entirely; LiteSpeed users enter wildcards (ignored) or FlyingPress users enter generic keywords like 'js' (excludes everything); mixing two optimizers (pallada: WP Rocket + W3TC; marakaki: W3TC + Perfmatters) applies delay/minify twice.
findings.how_to_apply: Put this list in fixes.md and in the audit script as the canonical exclusion set, mapped per plugin: NEVER-DELAY (all plugins): jquery.min.js, jquery-migrate.min.js, /jquery/ui/, /woocommerce/assets/js/frontend/ (except cart-fragments and order-attribution), woocommerce_params, wc_add_to_cart_params, selectWoo, /woocommerce-bookings/, moment.min.js, wc_bookings_, booking_form_params, /yith-woocommerce-booking-premium/ (on product pages), yith_wcbk, /jet-smart-filters/, JetSmartFilterSettings, admin-ajax.php, js.stripe.com, paypal.com/sdk/js, recaptcha/api, /cartasi-x-pay/ (checkout), klarna, /elementor/assets/js/frontend.min.js, /elementor-pro/assets/js/frontend.min.js, jquery.smartmenus.min.js, jquery.sticky.min.js. SAFE-TO-DELAY: sourcebuster, order-attribution, cart-fragments.min.js, fbevents.js, fbq(, /gtm.js, /gtag/js, gtag(, pixelyoursite, language-cookie.js, pll_cookie_script. WP Rocket: File Optimization > Delay JavaScript execution > tick WooCommerce/Elementor/payment one-click boxes, paste the NEVER list (one per line, regex allowed). LiteSpeed: Page Optimization > JS Settings > Load JS Deferred = Delayed only after pasting the NEVER list in Tuning > JS Deferred/Delayed Excludes as plain substrings. Perfmatters: Assets > JavaScript > Delay JavaScript = 'Only Delay Specified Scripts' with the SAFE list (lowest risk), or 'Delay All Scripts' + NEVER list in 'Excluded from Delay' + 'Delay Timeout' ON. FlyingPress: JavaScript > Delay all JavaScript = Defer (not 'Load after interaction') on e-shops; exclusions as keywords from the NEVER list.
findings.how_to_verify: Automated: for each page type run Playwright with a cold profile and assert, without any prior interaction, that (a) a product archive add-to-cart click adds an item, (b) the bookable product calendar renders (.ui-datepicker visible) within 5 s, (c) a JetSmartFilters checkbox click changes the results, (d) the checkout payment method iframes/buttons are present; collect console errors ('jQuery is not defined', 'wc_add_to_cart_params is not defined'). Then Lighthouse mobile on home/archive/product: TBT and 'minimize main-thread work' should drop; if LCP rises, a critical script was delayed.
findings.correction: FlyingPress JavaScript > Delay All JavaScript offers Defer loading / Load when idle / Load after interaction; use 'Defer loading' (or 'Load when idle' on brochure sites) on e-shops. LiteSpeed 'JS Delayed Includes' cannot delay inline JS unless Load JS Deferred = Delayed. Everything else as stated.

findings.claim: Cart, checkout and My Account are uncached by every cache plugin in the stack and WooCommerce redirects an empty-cart checkout to the cart, so the plugin's measurement set must seed a cart via Playwright before measuring checkout, must treat cart/checkout/account as 'no regression' pages (TTFB-bound, gateway iframes, reCAPTCHA, password meter), and should chase 95+ only on home, shop archive (plain and with ?jsf=/filter_ params), single product, bookable product (calendar rendered) and each language root.
findings.detail: Observed headers: limnoupolis /cart/ and /my-account/ 'cache-control: no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0, private' + 'x-litespeed-cache-control: no-cache'; /checkout/ first response 'no-cache, no-store' then redirected to /cart/ (identical HTML — empty cart redirect), kand /cart/ and /checkout/ 'no-cache ... private' (block cart: ~15 wc-blocks-*/wc-cart-checkout-* scripts incl. wc-cart-checkout-vendors-frontend.js, wc-blocks-components, wc-settings, wc-cart-block-frontend) while limnoupolis cart is the classic shortcode cart (wc-cart, wc-country-select, wc-address-i18n, selectWoo, zxcvbn-async + password-strength-meter + wc-password-strength-meter). LiteSpeed doc: 'By default, the My Account, Checkout, and Cart pages are excluded from caching' and 'We highly recommend that you enable ESI when using WooCommerce'; FlyingPress doc: 'Cart, Checkout, and My Account pages are automatically excluded from caching' and cached pages are still served to visitors with items in cart unless 'Bypass Cache for Cookies: woocommerce_items_in_cart' is added; Perfmatters: cart/checkout/account URLs are excluded from its optimizations and the meta box is hidden there. Checkout third parties: pallada /en/checkout/ includes www.google.com/recaptcha/api (FAZ consent whitelist) and Nexi XPay; marakaki Klarna; limnoupolis Attica Bank + PPEC. Bookable product: the calendar only appears after the wc_bookings_find_booked_day_blocks XHR (WC Bookings) or YITH's form init, so Lighthouse's static load misses interaction cost (INP) — a Playwright step that clicks the first available day is needed. Multilingual: pallada's measured 'home' is really /en/ after a 1.2 s redirect, so each language root must be measured directly (/, /en/, /el/). Pro Cart/Checkout widgets (shortcode-based) vs Cart/Checkout blocks change the handle set (classic: wc-cart/wc-checkout + selectWoo + password meter; blocks: wc-blocks bundle) but a controlled size comparison was not done.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break (measurement policy). Misreading: a 'checkout' Lighthouse run without a cart cookie measures the cart page; a bookable product measured without opening the calendar underestimates TBT/INP; comparing / with /en/ across sites compares a redirect with a page.
findings.how_to_apply: In the audit script define the URL set per e-shop/booking site: 1) home (each language root, direct URL, expect 95+), 2) shop archive /shop/ or /product-category/<largest>/ (expect 95+), 3) same archive with a filter applied (JSF: ?jsf=... in 'plain' URL type or the Mixed URL; WooCommerce layered nav ?filter_<attr>=...) (expect 90+, cache MISS allowed), 4) single simple product (expect 95+), 5) bookable product with Playwright: wait for '.wc-bookings-booking-form' or '.yith-wcbk-booking-form', click the first enabled day, measure INP/TBT and record the XHR latency of wc_bookings_find_booked_day_blocks or YITH's admin-ajax (expect 85-90+, do not chase), 6) cart with 1 item (seed via Playwright add-to-cart, then measure; expect 80-90, TTFB-bound), 7) checkout with 1 item (expect 70-85 because of gateway SDK/iframes/reCAPTCHA; only fail the audit on regressions or console errors), 8) My Account logged-out (expect 85-90; password meter zxcvbn is WooCommerce core). Record for each: cache status header (x-litespeed-cache, x-flying-press-cache, x-powered-by WP Rocket, W3TC comment), TTFB, number of /wc-ajax and admin-ajax requests, and the handle list (script id attributes) so the debloat skill can diff before/after.
findings.how_to_verify: The script's output for limnoupolis.gr must show checkout measured with a non-empty cart (payment_method_* radios present in the captured HTML) and the bookable product run must contain a wc-ajax/admin-ajax availability request; the per-page-type ceilings above are met on the fast reference sites (pallada /en/ already at 86 with WP Rocket) before any fixes are declared done.

findings.claim: LiteSpeed Cache's WooCommerce-specific levers for these sites are few and specific: cart/checkout/account are excluded automatically, ESI (Enterprise only) is the recommended way to keep pages public with a private cart block and independently-expiring nonces, 'Vary for Mini Cart' should stay OFF with Elementor's JS-updated Menu Cart, 'Drop Query String' must only hold tracking parameters, and the default one-week public TTL must be shortened on sites whose cached product pages embed booking nonces.
findings.detail: LiteSpeed docs (cache page dated 29 Sept 2026): Cache > Cache tab > 'Drop Query String' (default empty; 'compatible only with LiteSpeed Enterprise v5.2.3 and later', OpenLiteSpeed needs manual rewrite rules); TTL tab 'Default Public Cache TTL' 604800 (1 week), 'Default Private Cache TTL' 1800, 'Default Front Page TTL' also used by WooCommerce for the Shop page; ESI tab: 'OpenLiteSpeed does not support ESI', 'the WooCommerce shopping cart is treated as a private ESI block', 'ESI Nonces: List nonces one per line to convert them automatically to ESI blocks. Wildcards are supported. Nonces often expire before the site TTL ...'; the predefined nonce list (data/esi.nonces.txt) covers wp_rest, woocommerce-login, elementor-pro-frontend, elementor-conversion-center-click, legacy PPEC nonces (_wc_ppec_* private), WP Menu Cart, Gravity/WS Forms — not YITH Booking, WC Bookings, JetSmartFilters or WP Simple Booking Calendar nonces; WooCommerce tab (only with WooCommerce active): 'We highly recommend that you enable ESI when using WooCommerce', 'By default, the My Account, Checkout, and Cart pages are excluded from caching', 'Product Update Interval' (purge product/categories on stock changes), 'Vary for Mini Cart' OFF ('Most themes use JavaScript to update the mini cart, so caching is not an issue'); Cache Mobile OFF by default (needed only for UA-specific markup). Third-party page: WooCommerce 'respects WooCommerce's own cacheability rules', 'If using Recently Viewed Products widget, Set Enable ESI to ON', WPML separate copies per language, YITH Wishlist needs 'CacheEngine on esi combine'. limnoupolis.gr (LiteSpeed 7.9.1, x-litespeed-cache: hit on home/shop/product) embeds YITH, WPSBC (search_form_nonce), Product Input Fields (nonce) and WooCommerce (fragments_nonce) nonces in cached product HTML; the staging test showed a 5 s timeout on get_refreshed_fragments.
findings.breaks_when: ESI enabled on OpenLiteSpeed or a host without 'esi on' (settings silently do nothing); 'Vary for Mini Cart' ON doubles the cache footprint and busts hit ratio for every visitor with items; 'Drop Query String' containing jsf/filter_/orderby/pagenum serves the wrong archive; a long TTL with nonces in the page makes booking forms fail after 12-24 h (YITH add-to-booking / WC Bookings slot lookups return nonce errors) — exact failure mode on YITH 2.1.8 not reproduced here.
findings.how_to_apply: LiteSpeed Cache > Cache > [1] Cache: 'Cache Mobile' OFF (responsive Elementor), 'Drop Query String' = utm_source utm_medium utm_campaign utm_term utm_content fbclid gclid _ga (one per line) and nothing used by JSF/WooCommerce; [2] TTL: 'Default Public Cache TTL' 36000 (10 h) on booking sites until ESI nonces are confirmed, 'Default Front Page TTL' 36000; [6] WooCommerce: 'Vary for Mini Cart' OFF, 'Product Update Interval' = 'Purge product on changes to the quantity or stock status. Purge categories only when stock status changes' (default); [7] ESI (Enterprise/QUIC.cloud only): 'Enable ESI' ON, 'Cache Admin Bar' ON, 'ESI Nonces' add: search_form_nonce, get_end_time_html, show_available_month_blocks, yith_wcbk*, alg_wc_pif* — then test; keep the LiteSpeed Elementor recommendations (Elementor Performance tab settings) from the third-party page. Never add wc-ajax or admin-ajax to 'Do Not Cache URIs' as a fix (they are not cached anyway); if the YITH form must stay fresh, exclude only the bookable product URIs under Cache > Excludes > 'Do Not Cache URIs' as a last resort.
findings.how_to_verify: Response headers: x-litespeed-cache: hit on home/shop/product, x-litespeed-cache-control: no-cache on cart/checkout/account; with ESI on, the page source contains <esi:include> for the mini cart/nonces and the admin bar renders for logged-in users on a cached page; after TTL/2 + 1 h (e.g. 6 h) pick dates on a bookable product and complete add-to-cart without a 'link expired / nonce' error; LiteSpeed > Toolbox > Debug log shows no 'drop query' for jsf URLs.

findings.claim: Removing WooCommerce assets site-wide is already implemented safely in the agency's own kand.dev6 child theme (inc/kand-core.php) and that code — not a plugin — should be the reference snippet the debloat skill ships: it dequeues WooCommerce CSS/JS outside WooCommerce/cart/checkout/account pages, moves all scripts to the footer for guests, drops jquery-migrate, disables the product gallery slider/zoom via core filters and keeps cart fragments for the header count.
findings.detail: Read via Novamira (read-only) from /wp-content/themes/Inglelandi-child/inc/kand-core.php: (1) add_action('wp_enqueue_scripts', ..., 99) dequeues styles woocommerce-general, woocommerce-layout, woocommerce-smallscreen and scripts woocommerce, wc-add-to-cart when !is_woocommerce() && !is_cart() && !is_checkout() && !is_account_page(), with the comment 'cart fragments stay for the header count'; (2) kand_skip_front_tweaks() guards admin, ajax, cron, customizer, REST, Elementor preview; (3) all registered scripts get group=1 (footer) for logged-out visitors at PHP_INT_MAX; (4) wp_default_scripts removes jquery-migrate from jquery deps for guests; (5) add_filter('woocommerce_single_product_flexslider_enabled','__return_false') and ('woocommerce_single_product_zoom_enabled','__return_false') (the kand product page still loads wc-zoom/wc-flexslider files because the theme support is declared — the filters only disable init, so the plugin should also remove_theme_support('wc-product-gallery-zoom'/'wc-product-gallery-slider') in after_setup_theme at priority 11 to drop the files); (6) output-buffer tweaks: fetchpriority=high on the gallery image, sizes="auto, ..." on lazy images, Adobe Fonts stylesheet made non-blocking. Live effect verified: kand home has none of the WooCommerce CSS/JS handles while /product-category/rings/ and /product/* have them. Equivalent plugin toggles: Perfmatters > General > WooCommerce 'Disable Scripts' (same handle list plus prettyPhoto/fancybox/chosen legacy handles); FlyingPress Bloat 'Disable WooCommerce assets'.
findings.breaks_when: A non-WooCommerce page embeds an Elementor Pro Products/Add To Cart widget, a [products] shortcode or a YITH search form that relies on woocommerce.css; moving every script to the footer breaks inline scripts in Elementor HTML widgets that expect jQuery in <head> (the snippet exempts logged-in users for that reason); removing theme support for the gallery slider changes the product page layout (stacked images) — a design decision, as on kand.
findings.how_to_apply: Ship kand-core.php's WooCommerce block as the canonical snippet in skills/elementor-debloat/references/fixes.md (mu-plugin or child theme), adding remove_theme_support('wc-product-gallery-zoom'); remove_theme_support('wc-product-gallery-slider'); remove_theme_support('wc-product-gallery-lightbox') at after_setup_theme priority 11 when the design does not use them, and extend the is_* guard with is_page() checks for pages that embed WooCommerce widgets (detect via the audit: Elementor documents containing widgetType woocommerce-*). On sites with Perfmatters prefer its toggle; on FlyingPress sites the Bloat toggle; on LiteSpeed-only sites the snippet.
findings.how_to_verify: Diff script/style id attributes on home vs /shop/ (expect WooCommerce handles only on shop); click-test add-to-cart on an archive, variation select on a product, gallery lightbox; console must show no 'jQuery is not defined' for guests; Lighthouse home: fewer render-blocking stylesheets and ~25 KB less transfer.
findings.correction: The kand-core.php block is a valid reference but incomplete: on kand home wc-cart-fragments + wc-js-cookie (Elementor Pro Menu Cart), woocommerce-inline CSS and the Order Attribution pair still load. Ship it together with (a) a cookie-gated wc-cart-fragments dequeue at priority 999 (or the Perfmatters/FlyingPress toggle), (b) the Order Attribution feature decision, and (c) remove_theme_support('wc-product-gallery-zoom'/'-slider'/'-lightbox') at after_setup_theme 11 when the design does not use them.

findings.claim: Elementor Pro 4.3.1's Menu Cart widget re-enqueues wc-cart-fragments in render() on every page where the widget appears (header template = every page), independent of any widget setting, so the only ways to remove it are the cookie-gated dequeue (Perfmatters / snippet), the FlyingPress toggle, delaying cart-fragments.min.js, or replacing the widget with the WooCommerce Mini-Cart block.
findings.detail: elementor-pro/modules/woocommerce/widgets/menu-cart.php (version 4.3.1 installed on kand.dev6, read via Novamira read-file, read-only) lines 2267-2275: protected function render() { $settings = $this->get_settings_for_display(); if ( ! wp_script_is( 'wc-cart-fragments' ) ) { wp_enqueue_script( 'wc-cart-fragments' ); } $this->maybe_use_mini_cart_template(); Module::render_menu_cart( $settings ); }. The 'Automatically Update Cart' control (lines 730-745) only sets CSS variables through selectors_dictionary ('--elementor-remove-from-cart-button'), and 'Automatically Open Cart' (716-728) is a frontend_available flag; neither gates the enqueue. module.php lines 1418-1419 register wp_ajax_elementor_menu_cart_fragments / nopriv, verified with a nonce for MENU_CART_FRAGMENTS_ACTION ('elementor-menu-cart-fragments') created in localized_settings_frontend(); module.php line 1421 adds e_cart_count_fragments to woocommerce_add_to_cart_fragments. wc-cart-fragments deps in WooCommerce 11.2.0 are jquery + wc-js-cookie, which is why wc-js-cookie survives on the kand home even after the child theme dequeues 'woocommerce'. Elementor Pro changelog: 3.9.0 (2022-12-06) 'Fix: Cart is not updated when cache enabled in Menu Cart widget (#19312)' — the origin of the admin-ajax refresh. A snippet-level dequeue must run after render(), i.e. on wp_print_scripts / wp_enqueue_scripts at priority >= 999 or in wp_footer before scripts print, because the widget enqueues during the_content/template rendering, not at wp_enqueue_scripts 10.
findings.breaks_when: Visitors with items in cart see a stale counter on cached pages if the script is removed unconditionally; with the woocommerce_cart_hash cookie gate the first add-to-cart from a brochure page still updates (the add-to-cart response carries fragments) but the Pro side cart will not auto-open until the next page load; dequeueing at priority 10 does nothing because the widget enqueues later.
findings.how_to_apply: Perfmatters > General > WooCommerce > 'Disable Cart Fragmentation' ON (cookie-gated), or FlyingPress > Bloat > 'Disable WooCommerce cart fragments', or snippet: add_action('wp_print_scripts', function(){ if ( is_admin() || is_cart() || is_checkout() ) return; if ( empty($_COOKIE['woocommerce_cart_hash']) && empty($_COOKIE['woocommerce_items_in_cart']) ) { wp_dequeue_script('wc-cart-fragments'); } }, 999). Do not expect Elementor's 'Automatically Update Cart' switch to help. Structural alternative: WooCommerce Mini-Cart block (no fragments API per the WooCommerce dev blog).
findings.how_to_verify: Fresh private window on a brochure page: script id="wc-cart-fragments-js" absent, no ?wc-ajax=get_refreshed_fragments and no admin-ajax POST action=elementor_menu_cart_fragments in the Network tab; add a product, revisit home: cookie present, script present, counter correct.

findings.claim: WooCommerce's 'Default customer location = Geolocate (with page caching support)' enqueues wc-geolocation.js on every non-cart/checkout/account page for non-bot user agents and triggers an extra client-side request/redirect; set it to 'Shop base address' or 'No location by default' on cached brochure-heavy sites.
findings.detail: class-wc-frontend-scripts.php 11.2.0 lines 544-553: if DefaultCustomerAddress::GEOLOCATION_AJAX === get_option('woocommerce_default_customer_address') && !(is_cart()||is_account_page()||is_checkout()||is_customize_preview()) and the UA does not contain bot/spider/crawl, self::enqueue_script('wc-geolocation'). The script (assets/js/frontend/geolocation.min.js, registered at line 300) exists precisely to work around page caches by resolving the location client-side, which means an extra request after load on every cached page. Setting is WooCommerce > Settings > General > 'Default customer location'. Not observed on the 5 crawled sites (none printed wc-geolocation-js), so this is a guard rule for the audit script rather than a current defect.
findings.breaks_when: Stores that show geolocated taxes/prices (tax based on customer location, country-specific pricing) lose the automatic pre-selection until the customer enters an address at checkout.
findings.how_to_apply: WooCommerce > Settings > General > Default customer location: 'Shop base address' (or 'No location by default'). Audit check: grep -c 'wc-geolocation-js' on the home HTML must be 0.
findings.how_to_verify: Home HTML has no id="wc-geolocation-js"; checkout still pre-fills country from the shop base; taxes display as before for Greek customers.

findings.claim: WP Rocket ships default protections this stack can rely on and should not duplicate: '/woocommerce-bookings/dist/frontend.js' is excluded from JS minify/combine, 'www.paypal.com/sdk/js' from defer, 'osm.klarnaservices.com/lib.js' from external minify, and the inline objects var wc_cart_fragments_params / var woocommerce_params / wc_add_to_cart_params / elementorFrontendConfig / jetMenuPublicSettings / JetTricksSettings are excluded from inline-JS moving — but none of these are in delay_js_exclusions, so the Delay-JS exclusion list from the finding still has to be entered manually.
findings.detail: wp-rocket trunk dynamic-lists.json (opened 2026-10-16): exclude_js_files (17 entries) includes '/woocommerce-bookings/dist/frontend.js', '/jet-menu/assets/public/js/jet-menu-public-scripts.js'; defer_js_external_exclusions (37) includes 'www.paypal.com/sdk/js'; defer_js_inline_exclusions (10) includes 'bookingInProgress'; js_minify_external (132) includes 'osm.klarnaservices.com/lib.js'; js_excluded_inline (315) includes 'var wc_cart_fragments_params', 'var woocommerce_params', 'wc_add_to_cart_params', 'wc_product_block_data', 'woocommerce_price_slider_params', 'elementorFrontendConfig', 'jetMenuPublicSettings', 'JetTricksSettings'; delay_js_exclusions (75) has only generic items (jetpack, booking-suedtirol, st-booking-widget, gforms_recaptcha_ ...), no WooCommerce/Stripe/PayPal/Jet/Bookings; cache_ignored_parameters (100) are tracking params only; lazy_rendering_exclusions includes 'elementor-location-footer', 'elementor-location-floating_buttons', 'class="sticky-add-to-cart-wrapper'. rucss_inline_content_exclusions includes '.jet-listing-dynamic-post-'.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break; informational for the fixes.md mapping.
findings.how_to_apply: In fixes.md mark these as 'already covered by WP Rocket defaults (dynamic-lists.json)' and list only what must be typed into File Optimization > Delay JavaScript execution > Excluded JavaScript Files: jQuery regex from doc 1837, /woocommerce/assets/js/frontend/ (minus cart-fragments/order-attribution), /woocommerce-bookings/, moment.min.js, /jet-smart-filters/, admin-ajax.php, js.stripe.com, paypal.com/sdk/js, recaptcha/api, /cartasi-x-pay/, klarna, yith-wcbk on product pages.
findings.how_to_verify: After enabling Delay JS in WP Rocket, the view-source of a bookable product shows wc-bookings frontend.js and moment without the type="rocketlazyloadscript" rewrite; the calendar renders without interaction.

findings.claim: LiteSpeed's recommended Elementor baseline (Elementor > Settings > Performance: keep CSS Print Method unchanged, Optimized Image Loading OFF) and the 'Set TTL to 24 hours or less' pattern it documents for plugins with nonces in cached HTML (Contact Form 7) give an official precedent for shortening TTL on booking pages; WPML gets one cached copy per language automatically.
findings.detail: docs.litespeedtech.com third-party page (opened 2026-10-16): 'Contact Form 7 — Purge cache after creating/editing a form. Set TTL to 24 hours (86400 seconds) or less' (the nonce-in-page problem LiteSpeed itself solves by TTL), 'WPML — Separate cache copies are stored for each page for each language', 'WooCommerce — If using Recently Viewed Products widget, Set Enable ESI to ON in Cache > ESI. The plugin respects WooCommerce's own cacheability rules', 'YITH Wishlist — Define CacheEngine on esi combine ... in Apache config', and the Elementor section: 'In the Elementor Settings, navigate to the Performance tab... CSS Print Method: we recommend not changing this if the frontend is working as expected. Optimized Image Loading: Disable' so that LiteSpeed's own lazy-load/placeholders do not double up with Elementor's. The page says the Elementor navigation 'was verified accurate as of this writing' — the settings names correspond to Elementor 3.x; in Elementor 4.x the Performance tab still exists but verify the labels.
findings.breaks_when: Turning Elementor's Optimized Image Loading off while LiteSpeed lazy-load is also off removes lazy loading entirely (LCP unaffected, total bytes up); on this agency's staging LiteSpeed lazy-load raised CLS to 0.107, so prefer Elementor's native loading=lazy + explicit dimensions over LiteSpeed's lazy-load.
findings.how_to_apply: On LiteSpeed sites pick ONE lazy-load owner: either Elementor Performance > Optimized Image Loading ON with LiteSpeed Page Optimization > Media > Lazy Load Images OFF (recommended given the CLS regression), or the LiteSpeed-documented inverse. Set Cache > TTL > Default Public Cache TTL to 86400 or less on sites that embed form/booking nonces (CF7 precedent), 36000 on booking product URLs as a precaution.
findings.how_to_verify: Lighthouse mobile CLS stays at 0 on home after the change; images below the fold carry loading="lazy" from one source only (no data-lazyloaded attribute from LiteSpeed when Elementor owns it).

findings.claim: WooCommerce's own cookie doc sets the correct cache-bypass list for the booking sites: wp_woocommerce_session_ lives 2 days, woocommerce_cart_hash and woocommerce_items_in_cart are session cookies, so any 'bypass cache for cookies' rule should name woocommerce_items_in_cart (not the session cookie) or the hit ratio collapses.
findings.detail: woocommerce.com/document/woocommerce-cookies/: 'woocommerce_cart_hash — session — Helps WooCommerce determine when cart contents/data changes', 'woocommerce_items_in_cart — session — same', 'wp_woocommerce_session_ — 2 days — Contains a unique code for each customer so that it knows where to find the cart data in the database'. The Bookings troubleshooting doc asks hosts to 'exclude all WooCommerce cookies from being cached', which if implemented as 'bypass when wp_woocommerce_session_ exists' makes every visitor who ever viewed a bookable product (Bookings creates a session) uncached for 2 days. FlyingPress documents the narrower rule 'Bypass Cache for Cookies: woocommerce_items_in_cart'. Perfmatters' cart-fragments gate uses woocommerce_cart_hash.
findings.breaks_when: Bypassing on wp_woocommerce_session_ : hit ratio near zero on booking/e-shop sites (TTFB regression for everyone); bypassing on woocommerce_items_in_cart only affects shoppers with items.
findings.how_to_apply: FlyingPress > Caching > Bypass Cache for Cookies: woocommerce_items_in_cart only if the mini cart misbehaves; LiteSpeed: leave 'Do Not Cache Cookies' empty (WooCommerce integration already handles cart/checkout); WP Rocket: nothing (mandatory/dynamic cookies handled). Never add wp_woocommerce_session_ as a bypass cookie.
findings.how_to_verify: After viewing a bookable product in a private window, reload the home page: x-litespeed-cache / x-flying-press-cache header must still say hit.

title: WordPress 7.x core performance features and PHP 8.4 interactions with Elementor 4.3 and the cache plugins (speculative loading, core image loading, script strategies, bfcache/headers, PHP 8.4, Site Health + Performance Lab)
summary: WordPress 7.1.3 core already does three things on every one of the 10 sites that nobody configured: it prints a conservative-prefetch speculation rule (confirmed in all 10 home pages, including the two FlyingPress sites, which means FlyingPress 'Preload links' is off there), it defers every WooCommerce 11.2 frontend script via the 6.3 strategy API, and it would apply sizes="auto" plus iframe lazy-loading — except that Elementor 4.3.5's default-on 'Optimized Image Loading' sets wp_lazy_loading_enabled to false globally and re-implements only the part with regex, so the 7 sites with the module on have 13–85 lazy images and zero sizes="auto" (verified in core wp_filter_content_tags order: auto-sizes runs before the wp_content_img_tag filter Elementor hooks). None of these core features is visible to Lighthouse/PSI (the 6.8 performance post says so for speculative loading; bf-cache passed on all 10 local LH 12.8.2 runs), so they are field-only wins; the PSI score levers remain the ones from the other dimensions. The headers are clean for bfcache: no Cache-Control: no-store on any 200 HTML; the only no-store is pallada.gr's uncached WPML language 302, and the only Set-Cookie on a home page is Polylang's pll_language on the uncached dev site platonos. WooCommerce 11.2 itself strips no-store for logged-out visitors on cart/checkout/account, so the one remaining recipe item is W3TC's HTML cache-control policy (never pick no_cache/no_store) and a Permissions-Policy: unload=() header. For PHP 8.4, WordPress 7.0/7.1 are fully compatible, Elementor Pro fixed its 8.4 deprecations in 3.32.0 and 3.34.0 (both before the 4.x line), and the read-only check on cretaforums (PHP 8.4.26) shows the practical state: WP_DEBUG false gives error_reporting 4983 (no E_DEPRECATED), so deprecations cost nothing unless someone turns WP_DEBUG on in production; the plugin should read PHP_VERSION, WP_DEBUG, WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY and the debug.log size before any step. The Performance Lab plugins Optimization Detective 1.0.0-beta7 + Image Prioritizer 1.0.0-beta4 are the only measured way to preload an Elementor CSS-background hero (they handle background-image via inline style and via stylesheet), but they need the REST API open to anonymous visitors, a mobile+desktop sample of 3 visits per breakpoint, and should run with Elementor's image module OFF so one engine decides loading/fetchpriority. Core Site Health exposes reusable read-only thresholds: page cache 600 ms median of loopback requests, autoloaded options 800,000 bytes, object-cache suggestion at 500 alloptions / 100 KB / 1,000 posts, plus OPcache info since 7.0.
critic_notes: Method: WebFetch had no DNS in this sandbox, so every cited page was downloaded with curl through the proxy and converted to text; WordPress 7.1.3 core files were read from the GitHub wordpress-develop 7.1.3 tag, WooCommerce 11.2.1 files from the woocommerce monorepo tag, Elementor 4.3.5 and W3TC 2.10.7 from the wordpress.org zips, OD/IP classes from WordPress/performance trunk (not the beta tag, so group logic is 'trunk as of today'). Not re-checked: the researcher's live curl header tables, Novamira runtime values, saved-HTML counts, Elementor Pro source (no Pro zip available), Dynamic.ooo/JetSmartFilters/YITH PHP 8.4 statements, Image Placeholders version. Overall the dimension holds; corrections are precision fixes (LiteSpeed emoji toggle, Vary Cookies vs Vary Groups, Speed Brain origin safety, OIL also hooks wp_content_img_tag and its own min-pixels filter name, OD viewport-group geometry, jquery-migrate snippet guard, filter-over-constant precedence). Skipped: no new web searches beyond the cited pages; no browser-level verification of prefetch cookie behaviour. Risk for the user: Elementor Pro's script registration remains unverified, so the defer recipe must be confirmed on a rendered page before being promised.
open_questions: GA4 (gtag.js), Google Tag Manager and the Meta pixel: whether they already wait for prerenderingchange before firing page_view/PageView could not be confirmed from an opened vendor page (the GA4 page_view doc fetched has no prerender section; Chrome's doc only says 'not all analytics providers may do this by default'). Needed before recommending mode=prerender anywhere.

Whether PageSpeed Insights skips the bf-cache audit in Lighthouse 13 was not confirmed from an opened page; the local runs were Lighthouse 12.8.2 (bf-cache passed on all 10) and the Chrome Lighthouse overview page merely lists the audit.
