PHP 8.4 statements for Dynamic.ooo Pro (changelog URL returned 403), JetSmartFilters 3.8.x (Crocoblock changelog page 404) and YITH Booking (page shows WP 7.1 / Woo 11.2 compatibility only) were not found; staging test with WP_DEBUG_LOG on PHP 8.4 is the fallback.

pallada.gr: the x-powered-by: WP Rocket/3.23.2.1 header together with a W3TC footer comment and an uncached no-store 302 at '/' needs a server-side look (leftover WP Rocket .htaccess rules vs. a second active cache plugin) – read-only Novamira access to pallada was not used.

Whether FlyingPress / LiteSpeed 'Delay JS' and 'JS Combine' leave <script type="speculationrules"> and Optimization Detective's inline detection module untouched – confirmed only for Perfmatters Delay JS (marakaki.com) by inspection.

Trac #65624 (7.1 host override for eagerness/mode) returned 403; the constant/env-var behaviour was verified from the 7.1.3 source instead, and the 'auto-moderate when object+page cache detected' default did not ship in 7.1.3 (default remains prefetch/conservative).

The WordPress 7.0 and 7.1 field guides contain no dedicated performance section; frontend 7.x changes (fetchpriority low/auto in 7.0, speculative-loading constants and client-side media processing in 7.1) were taken from the 7.1.3 source and its @since tags, not from a dev note.

Elementor header/footer template images rendered by Elementor Pro theme locations: whether core's threshold-of-3 counting treats them as content (via the_content-like filters) or as template images was not verified; check the hero attributes after turning Optimized Image Loading off.

findings.claim: Core speculative loading fires on all 10 sites as prefetch/conservative and is correctly excluded for query-string, wp-*.php, wp-admin, wp-content and rel=nofollow links; leave it on, and raise eagerness only via the 7.1 constant or filter, never to prerender on the Polylang/WPML and Woo sites without the exclusions below.
findings.detail: All 10 saved home pages contain exactly one <script type="speculationrules"> block: {"prefetch":[{"source":"document","where":{"and":[{"href_matches":"/*"},{"not":{"href_matches":["/wp-*.php","/wp-admin/*","/wp-content/uploads/*","/wp-content/*","/wp-content/plugins/*","/wp-content/themes/<theme>/*","/*\\?(.+)"]}},{"not":{"selector_matches":"a[rel~=\"nofollow\"]"}},{"not":{"selector_matches":".no-prefetch, .no-prefetch a"}}]},"eagerness":"conservative"}]}. In wp-includes/speculative-loading.php (7.1.3): default null when is_user_logged_in() or no pretty permalinks; wp_get_speculation_rules_default_configuration() returns prefetch/conservative unless WP_SPECULATIVE_LOADING_DEFAULT_MODE / WP_SPECULATIVE_LOADING_DEFAULT_EAGERNESS are set as env var or constant (constant wins; @since 7.1.0); 'immediate' is refused for document rules; filters wp_speculation_rules_configuration (array|null), wp_speculation_rules_href_exclude_paths ($paths, $mode), action wp_load_speculation_rules (WP_Speculation_Rules::add_rule). Both constants are undefined on cretaforums and limnoupolis (read-only check). WooCommerce 11.2.1 add-to-cart loop buttons carry rel=nofollow (includes/wc-template-functions.php:1468) and ?add-to-cart= URLs are query strings, so both are excluded by default; wp-login.php?action=logout is excluded by /wp-*.php. YITH/Bookings 'book now' are POST forms, unaffected. Chrome eagerness (prerender-pages doc): conservative = pointer/touch down; moderate = 200 ms hover on desktop, viewport heuristics on mobile since Aug 2025 (500 ms after scroll stops); eager = 10 ms hover / 50 ms in viewport (Chrome 143+); limit of 2 concurrent speculations for eager/moderate/conservative (FIFO). The 6.8 dev note reports ~1.9% higher LCP pass rate at the median for sites that enabled the plugin. Prerender is only enabled when the user's 'Preload pages' setting is on and not on low-memory/save-data devices.
findings.breaks_when: Switching to prerender (or moderate eagerness) on the Polylang sites: platonos' HTML response sets Set-Cookie: pll_language=en on every page, so a prerendered language-switcher link flips the visitor's language cookie without a navigation; pallada.gr's root 302 (WPML language redirect, Cache-Control: no-store) would be fetched on every speculation. Prerender also runs GTM/GA4/Meta tags before activation unless they handle document.prerendering (Chrome: 'not all analytics providers may do this by default'). Hosts with per-request PHP work on uncached pages see extra load from moderate/eager prefetches that never navigate.
findings.how_to_apply: Existing sites: keep core default; add to a mu-plugin add_filter('wp_speculation_rules_href_exclude_paths', fn($p,$mode)=>array_merge($p,['/cart/*','/checkout/*','/my-account/*','/καλάθι/*','/ολοκλήρωση-αγοράς/*']),10,2) using the real Woo page slugs; for hotel brochure sites set define('WP_SPECULATIVE_LOADING_DEFAULT_EAGERNESS','moderate') in wp-config.php (7.1+) and keep mode prefetch. Do not add a second rule source (see finding 2). New lean builds: same defaults; add class no-prefetch to language switchers and any GET action links.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -s URL | grep -o '<script type="speculationrules">[^<]*' shows exactly one block with the expected eagerness; in Chrome DevTools > Application > Speculative loads, mousedown on an internal link shows a prefetch with status 'Ready'; chrome://network-internals is not needed. Confirm the Woo cart/checkout URLs are listed under not.href_matches. Lighthouse/PSI will show no change (expected).

findings.claim: Only one speculation-rule source must exist per site: FlyingPress 'Preload links on hover' replaces core's rule, Perfmatters 2.4.3+ exposes core's mode/eagerness and deprecated its instant.page script, Cloudflare Speed Brain adds a Speculation-Rules HTTP header, and LiteSpeed 7.9 / W3TC 2.10 add none.
findings.detail: FlyingPress docs: 'We use browser-native speculation rules to prefetch the next page as soon as the user hovers over a link' (moderate), skips .php, admin/login, query strings, Woo cart/checkout/logout, and 'disables WordPress's default speculation rules (added in newer versions) to prevent conflicts'. Both FlyingPress sites (cretaforums.gr, voreniahorizon.gr) still print core's conservative rule, so the FlyingPress option is currently off there. Perfmatters changelog: 2.4.3 (2025-04-15) 'Added new preload options to control Speculative Loading mode and eagerness settings for sites running WordPress 6.8+' and 'Deprecated Instant Page option throughout the plugin for sites running WordPress 6.8+'; 2.4.4 added a mode to disable it entirely; 2.4.6 'disable speculative loading on WooCommerce cart and checkout URLs'; 2.6.8 (2026-09-09) moved Instant Page/Preconnect/DNS Prefetch into the main queue. Cloudflare Speed Brain (Free/Pro, enabled by default on new zones per the doc) adds a 'Speculation-Rules' response header pointing to a conservative prefetch config; none of the 4 Cloudflare-fronted sites (limnoupolis, cretaforums, marakaki, voreniahorizon) returned that header today, so Speed Brain is off. LiteSpeed Cache 7.9 Page Optimization docs list only DNS Prefetch / DNS Prefetch Control / Preconnect (no page prefetch/instant click). W3TC 2.10.7 source contains no 'speculationrules' and its 'Preload Requests' feature is resource preload. Perfmatters Delay JS on marakaki.com left the speculationrules block intact (53 type="pmdelayedscript" tags, rule unchanged).
findings.breaks_when: Two engines (core + FlyingPress, or core + Cloudflare Speed Brain) both emit rules: duplicate prefetches of the same URL count against Chrome's limit of 2 concurrent speculations and double the server hits on uncached pages; FlyingPress + core together can also disagree on exclusions (FlyingPress excludes cart/checkout by slug, core by query string only).
findings.how_to_apply: Existing sites: keep core's rule; leave FlyingPress > Preload links OFF (or, if the team prefers FlyingPress's hover prefetch, accept that it removes core's rule and verify its Woo exclusions); in Perfmatters set Preloading > Speculative Loading to the desired eagerness instead of editing wp-config; Instant Page stays off; in Cloudflare Speed > Optimization keep Speed Brain off while the WordPress rule exists. New builds: same; document the single chosen source in the handover checklist.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -sI URL | grep -i speculation-rules must be empty; curl -s URL | grep -c 'type="speculationrules"' must be 1; DevTools > Application > Speculative loads > Rules shows one rule set and its source (document vs header).
findings.correction: Sources and versions confirmed (FlyingPress doc: 'disables WordPress's default speculation rules (added in newer versions) to prevent conflicts', excludes query strings and Woo cart/checkout/logout; Perfmatters 2.4.3 04.15.2025 mode/eagerness options + Instant Page deprecated, 2.4.4 05.08.2025 disable mode, 2.4.6 06.17.2025 Woo cart/checkout exclusion, 2.6.8 09.09.2026 queue move; W3TC 2.10.7 zip contains no 'speculationrules'; LiteSpeed Page Optimization lists only DNS Prefetch / DNS Prefetch Control / DNS Preconnect). The breaks_when is wrong for Cloudflare: Speed Brain prefetches 'will never reach origin servers. Prefetch requests only serve content that is stored in Cloudflare's Cache' and answer 503 when not cached, so there is no doubled origin load; the real cost on these sites (HTML is cf-cache-status DYNAMIC) is that every Speed Brain prefetch fails with 503 while still occupying one of Chrome's 2 speculation slots. Cloudflare also states 'If origin server responses include the Speculation-Rules header, it will not be overridden' (irrelevant to WP, which uses an inline script, so core + Speed Brain would coexist). Speed Brain is 'Enabled by default' on Free/Pro/Business, not Enterprise. Also: Perfmatters' setting works through the core filter, which overrides the 7.1 wp-config constant, so pick one place.

findings.claim: Elementor 4.3.5's default-on 'Optimized Image Loading' (option elementor_optimized_image_loading, std '1') discards core's image heuristics: it sets wp_lazy_loading_enabled to false for every tag (so iframes never get loading=lazy), disables core fetchpriority via wp_high_priority_element_flag(false), re-implements only with a regex buffer, and loses sizes="auto" on every image it lazy-loads; turning it off and using core + two filters is the cleaner base.
findings.detail: modules/image-loading-optimization/module.php (4.3.5): add_filter('wp_lazy_loading_enabled','__return_false'); add_action('init',[stop_core_fetchpriority_high_logic]) → wp_high_priority_element_flag(false); ob_start on get_header and flush at the_content priority 0; preg_replace_callback('/<img\s[^>]+>/') prepending loading=/fetchpriority= via str_replace('<img', ...); copies of core's logic with private $omit_threshold = 3 and $min_priority_img_pixels = 50000 (filterable by wp_min_priority_img_pixels only); no auto-sizes code. Core 7.1.3 wp_filter_content_tags() runs wp_img_tag_add_loading_optimization_attrs → wp_img_tag_add_auto_sizes → apply_filters('wp_content_img_tag') in that order, so Elementor's filter adds loading="lazy" after core's auto-sizes step has already bailed ('Bail early if the image is not lazy-loaded'). Evidence: limnoupolis 27 lazy images with srcset+sizes and 0 sizes="auto"; pallada 41/0; platonos 12/0 (saved HTML). The few sizes="auto" that do appear (cretaforums 53, kand 24, voreniahorizon 4, all with OIL ON per read-only get_option on cretaforums) come from callers that pass loading=lazy explicitly into wp_get_attachment_image(), where core adds 'auto, ' itself (media.php lines ~1257-1267). Core defaults: wp_omit_loading_attr_threshold 3, wp_min_priority_img_pixels 50000, 7.0 added support for fetchpriority=low/auto so such images are neither lazied nor counted (@since 7.0.0 in wp_get_loading_optimization_attributes). Elementor's companion option elementor_lazy_load_background_images (std '1') hides CSS backgrounds of .e-con.e-parent:nth-of-type(n+4) (n+3 at max-height 1024px, n+2 at max-height 640px) until .e-lazyloaded, i.e. on a phone only the first top-level container keeps its background before JS runs. Elementor's 'Optimized Gutenberg Loading' (elementor_optimized_gutenberg_loading, std '1') dequeues wp-block-library, wp-block-library-theme, wc-block-style, wc-blocks-style only when get_post() is Elementor-built and has no blocks (modules/gutenberg/module.php) – wp-block-library was indeed absent on all 10 home pages, but archive/shop/search pages still load it.
findings.breaks_when: After turning Optimized Image Loading off, the hero can receive loading="lazy" if it is the 4th+ image in document order (header logos, menu icons and Elementor Pro header template images count toward core's threshold of 3) – check the hero attributes; a hero placed in the 2nd top-level container on mobile is hidden by the lazy-background CSS until JS runs regardless of this setting (add class e-no-lazyload or move it first). Sites whose Image widgets set the widget-level 'Lazy Load' to No rely on Elementor's handling.
findings.how_to_apply: Existing sites (staging first): Elementor > Settings > Performance > Optimized Image Loading = Inactive (option elementor_optimized_image_loading = '0'); then in an mu-plugin add_filter('wp_omit_loading_attr_threshold', fn()=>1) when the hero is the first image, and add_filter('wp_min_priority_img_pixels', fn()=>20000) if the mobile hero is small; keep Optimized Gutenberg Loading on. New builds: same, plus hero in the first container with the Image widget's own Lazy Load = No. Keep Lazy Load Background Images on only when the hero is in container 1.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -s URL | grep -o '<img[^>]*>' | head -5: hero shows fetchpriority="high" and no loading="lazy"; grep -c 'sizes="auto' rises from 0 to the number of lazy responsive images; grep -c 'loading="lazy"' on <iframe> embeds becomes >0 where embeds exist; Lighthouse LCP and 'LCP request discovery' insight unchanged or better; screenshot the first screen on a 360x640 emulated phone to confirm the hero background renders.
findings.correction: All mechanics confirmed in elementor.4.3.5/modules/image-loading-optimization/module.php, with one precision: the module is not only a header buffer. It (a) ob_start()s on get_header and flushes at the_content priority 0 (header markup only), and (b) also hooks add_filter('wp_content_img_tag', [$this,'loading_optimization_image']) for content images, running after core's wp_img_tag_add_auto_sizes() step (media.php 2058-2072 order: loading attrs → auto sizes → wp_content_img_tag). Footer images are untouched by the buffer. No 'sizes'/'auto' code exists in the module (grep: zero matches). Everything else stands: wp_lazy_loading_enabled → __return_false (all tags, so iframes lose loading=lazy), wp_high_priority_element_flag(false) on init, private $omit_threshold = 3, $min_priority_img_pixels = 50000 filterable only via 'elementor/image-loading-optimization/min_priority_img_pixels' (not wp_min_priority_img_pixels as the finding's text implies — correct that name), width/height required, attributes prepended via str_replace('<img', ...). Lazyload module CSS confirmed: .e-con.e-parent:nth-of-type(n+4) (n+3 at max-height 1024px, n+2 at max-height 640px) :not(.e-lazyloaded):not(.e-no-lazyload) and descendants get background-image: none !important; option elementor_lazy_load_background_images std '1'. Gutenberg module dequeues wp-block-library, wp-block-library-theme, wc-block-style, wc-blocks-style at wp_enqueue_scripts 999 only when has_blocks($post) is false.

findings.claim: Core's script strategy API is already used by WooCommerce 11.2 (every frontend script registered with strategy=>'defer') and by core only for comment-reply (async, fetchpriority low) and wp-embed (defer); Elementor 4.3.5 declares defer only for its assets-manager module script, and adding defer to elementor-frontend via wp_script_add_data is silently downgraded to blocking whenever any dependent (Elementor Pro frontend, add-on widget scripts, inline 'after' scripts) is not itself deferred.
findings.detail: WooCommerce includes/class-wc-frontend-scripts.php register_script()/enqueue_script() default $in_footer = array('strategy' => 'defer') – matches the observed defer on wc-add-to-cart-js, wc-js-cookie-js, woocommerce-js, wc-cart-fragments-js (limnoupolis, pallada, kand, staging) and 8 other 'strategy' => 'defer'/'async' declarations (Jetpack assets, Blocks GoogleAnalytics). Core script-loader.php: comment-reply add_data strategy async + fetchpriority low; wp-embed strategy defer; no other core handle. Elementor: grep of 4.3.5 finds 'strategy' => 'defer' only in modules/assets-manager/module.php (experiment e_assets_manager); elementor-webpack-runtime, elementor-frontend-modules (deps elementor-webpack-runtime, jquery) and elementor-frontend are blocking footer scripts (includes/frontend.php 360-460). WP_Scripts::filter_eligible_strategies() (class-wp-scripts.php) returns array() – i.e. blocking – when a non-alias handle has no intended strategy, when it has an inline script in the 'after' position, or recursively when any enqueued dependent is blocking; so a mu-plugin wp_script_add_data('elementor-frontend','strategy','defer') only takes effect if elementor-pro-frontend and every add-on handle that lists elementor-frontend as a dependency also get defer and none has after-inline code. frontend.js reveals .elementor-invisible elements (entrance animations) via waypoints when it runs. Cache plugins defer at the HTML level after WordPress: Perfmatters docs 'There is a check to see if the script already has a defer attribute, so you don't need to worry about it getting multiple attributes applied' and 'Include jQuery' is optional with a warning; LiteSpeed 'Load JS Deferred' has Deferred vs Delayed modes; W3TC has Minify embed types (blocking/extsrc/asyncsrc) and a separate 'Defer Scripts' feature (2.10.3 fix). Observed: marakaki.com serves elementor-frontend-modules and elementor-frontend with type="pmdelayedscript" (Perfmatters Delay JS) and has 10 .elementor-invisible elements; onar-seaside-lounge serves them combined by LiteSpeed (data-optimized="1").
findings.breaks_when: Delaying (not deferring) elementor-frontend until user interaction leaves every .elementor-invisible element (entrance animations) and Swiper/Pro widgets uninitialised on first paint on a bounce – marakaki.com shows this pattern; deferring jQuery breaks inline jQuery(document).ready snippets printed by HTML widgets or add-ons (251 HTML widgets on limnoupolis); an mu-plugin defer for elementor-frontend that is downgraded gives no gain and no error.
findings.how_to_apply: Existing sites: prefer the cache plugin's defer (LiteSpeed Page Optimization > JS Settings > Load JS Deferred = Deferred; Perfmatters Assets > Defer JavaScript with 'Include jQuery' off; W3TC Minify > JS embed type non-blocking) and exclude elementor-frontend, elementor-frontend-modules, elementor-pro-frontend and jquery from Delay JS; remove entrance animations above the fold instead of delaying the engine. mu-plugin route only on new lean builds without add-ons: foreach (['elementor-webpack-runtime','elementor-frontend-modules','elementor-frontend','elementor-pro-frontend'] as $h) wp_script_add_data($h,'strategy','defer') at wp_enqueue_scripts priority 1000, then confirm the rendered tag actually has defer.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -s URL | grep -o '<script[^>]*elementor-frontend[^>]*>' must show ' defer' (not type="pmdelayedscript"); DevTools Console shows no 'elementorFrontend is not defined'; load the page on a throttled phone without touching it and screenshot after 3 s: all elements visible, sliders initialised; Lighthouse 'Total Blocking Time' and 'render-blocking resources' before/after.

findings.claim: Several core assets still load for logged-out visitors on these sites and are safe to remove: the wp-emoji detection script (4 sites), dashicons CSS (2 sites), jquery-migrate (all 10), the 11.3 KB global-styles inline CSS (all 10), wp-embed (all 10) and wp-polyfill (2 sites); wp-block-library and the Interactivity API runtime are already absent on the home pages.
findings.detail: WordPress 7.1.3 default-filters.php still hooks print_emoji_detection_script at wp_head 7 and wp_enqueue_emoji_styles at wp_enqueue_scripts; the inline window._wpemojiSettings script is present on limnoupolis.gr, staging.limnoupolis.gr, fagitiotiszois and platonos (6 'wp-emoji' matches each) and absent where Perfmatters/FlyingPress disable emojis. dashicons-css link present logged-out on limnoupolis.gr (8 matches) and staging (4). jquery-migrate loaded on all 10 (2 matches each). style#global-styles-inline-css is 11,306 bytes on each of limnoupolis, pallada, marakaki, cretaforums (classic-theme theme.json presets; Elementor's Gutenberg module does not touch it). wp-embed.min.js (core adds strategy defer) on all 10. wp-includes/js/dist/hooks.min.js + i18n.min.js on all 10; marakaki additionally api-fetch, url, private-apis and wp-polyfill (2 sites: pallada, marakaki). wp-interactivity: 0 on all 10 (loads only with interactive blocks). wp-block-library: 0 on all 10 home pages (Elementor Optimized Gutenberg Loading on Elementor-built singular pages only). Perfmatters changelog shows built-in toggles for emojis (emoji_svg_url filter), dashicons (front-end when logged out) and Script Manager; LiteSpeed has no emoji/dashicons toggle in its Page Optimization docs.
findings.breaks_when: Removing dashicons breaks admin-bar icons for logged-in editors unless the removal is wrapped in !is_user_logged_in() (Perfmatters ships a Script Manager rule for exactly this); dequeuing global-styles removes theme.json color/spacing CSS variables that Elementor Global Colors never use but a block in a footer widget might; removing jquery-migrate exposes deprecated-jQuery warnings in old add-on scripts (console only, rarely functional); wp-polyfill is a dependency of some plugin script and will be re-enqueued if that script loads.
findings.how_to_apply: mu-plugin for existing sites: remove_action('wp_head','print_emoji_detection_script',7); remove_action('wp_enqueue_scripts','wp_enqueue_emoji_styles'); remove_action('wp_head','wp_oembed_add_host_js'); add_action('wp_enqueue_scripts', function(){ if(!is_user_logged_in()){ wp_dequeue_style('dashicons'); wp_dequeue_style('global-styles'); } }, 100); add_filter('wp_default_scripts', fn($s)=>($s->registered['jquery']->deps = array_diff($s->registered['jquery']->deps,['jquery-migrate'])) ? $s : $s); or the equivalent Perfmatters toggles (Disable Emojis, Disable Dashicons, Remove jQuery Migrate, Disable Embeds). New builds: same mu-plugin from day one.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -s URL | grep -c 'wp-emoji\|dashicons-css\|jquery-migrate\|global-styles-inline-css\|wp-embed.min.js' returns 0 logged out; log in and check the admin bar icons still render; Lighthouse request count and 'unused CSS' drop by the removed files; console has no new errors on the pages with sliders/forms.
findings.correction: Core hooks confirmed (default-filters.php 7.1.3: print_emoji_detection_script at wp_head 7, wp_enqueue_emoji_styles at wp_enqueue_scripts, wp_oembed_add_host_js at wp_head; script-loader: jquery deps = jquery-core + jquery-migrate 3.4.1). Two fixes: (1) the detail 'LiteSpeed has no emoji/dashicons toggle' is wrong — LiteSpeed Cache Page Optimization has a 'Remove WordPress Emoji' option ('removes the extra JavaScript file used to add emoji support in older browsers'); it has no dashicons toggle. (2) The jquery-migrate snippet: 'wp_default_scripts' is an action receiving the WP_Scripts object; the add_filter form works because actions and filters share one hook table, but wrap it in !is_admin() so wp-admin keeps Migrate, e.g. add_action('wp_default_scripts', function($s){ if(!is_admin() && isset($s->registered['jquery'])) $s->registered['jquery']->deps = array_diff($s->registered['jquery']->deps, ['jquery-migrate']); });. Perfmatters changelog confirms Disable Dashicons (front-end, logged out) with a built-in Script Manager rule, emoji_svg_url filter and Instant Page/Preconnect handling.

findings.claim: bfcache is not blocked on any of the 10 home pages today (no Cache-Control: no-store on 200 HTML, Lighthouse bf-cache audit passes on all 10), WooCommerce 11.2 removes no-store for logged-out visitors on cart/checkout/account, and the only recipe items are W3TC's HTML cache-control policy choice, a Permissions-Policy: unload=() header, and pallada's uncached no-store language redirect.
findings.detail: Header table (curl, mobile UA, 2026-10-16): limnoupolis.gr – LiteSpeed (x-litespeed-cache: hit), behind Cloudflare (cf-cache-status DYNAMIC), no Cache-Control on HTML, no Set-Cookie, PHP/8.3.35 header; /shop/ returns 301 with Set-Cookie: _fbp (server-side Meta pixel cookie) and x-litespeed-cache-control: no-cache. staging.limnoupolis.gr – LiteSpeed hit, no Cache-Control, no cookie. cretaforums.gr – FlyingPress HIT (x-flying-press-cache: HIT, x-flying-press-source: Web Server), Cloudflare, cache-control: no-cache, must-revalidate + expires now, no cookie. fagitiotiszois.dev6 – no cache plugin, nginx, no Cache-Control, no cookie. kand.dev6 – W3TC 'Page Caching using Disk: Enhanced' footer, no Cache-Control header, no cookie. www.marakaki.com – W3TC footer + Perfmatters, cache-control: private, must-revalidate + pragma: public (= W3TC Browser Cache HTML policy 'cache_noproxy'), Cloudflare, no cookie. onar-seaside-lounge.gr – LiteSpeed hit, no Cache-Control, no cookie. pallada.gr – '/' answers 302 to /en/ with cache-control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, max-age=0 (WPML language redirect, uncached PHP on every root hit); /en/ 200 has cache-control: public, max-age=0,public, expires now and x-powered-by: WP Rocket/3.23.2.1 while the HTML footer says 'Performance optimized by W3 Total Cache' (leftover WP Rocket .htaccess rules or two cache layers – unresolved). platonos.dev6 – no cache plugin, Set-Cookie: pll_language=en on the home page (Polylang). voreniahorizon.gr – FlyingPress HIT, cache-control: no-cache, must-revalidate, Cloudflare, no cookie. Local Lighthouse 12.8.2 runs: audit bf-cache score 1 on all 10; the no-unload-listeners audit is not present in those runs. WooCommerce 11.2.1 includes/class-wc-cache-helper.php prevent_caching(): nocache headers only on cart/checkout/my-account pages and 'If the user is not logged in, remove the no-store directive so that bfcache is not blocked for visitors' (references core Trac #63636). W3TC 2.10.7 BrowserCache_Environment.php HTML policies: cache_public_maxage (default), cache_validation ('public, must-revalidate, proxy-revalidate'), cache_noproxy ('private, must-revalidate'), cache_maxage, no_cache ('private, no-cache'), no_store ('no-store' + Pragma no-store). Chrome CCNS doc (updated 2025-09-09): no-store was the largest bfcache blocker, ~17% of mobile and 7% of desktop history navigations; since 2025 Chrome enters bfcache for no-store pages unless cookies change, with a 3-minute instead of 10-minute timeout; other browsers still block. web.dev (updated 2026-07-02): never use unload; desktop Chrome/Firefox make pages ineligible with an unload listener, mobile Chrome/Safari still cache them; recommends Permissions-Policy: unload=() to stop third parties adding one; CrUX counts bfcache restores as separate page visits – the article gives no LCP delta figure. Performance Lab's 'Instant Back/Forward' plugin (slug nocache-bfcache v1.3.3, 2026-09-12) strips no-store for logged-in users.
findings.breaks_when: Choosing W3TC Browser Cache > HTML&XML policy 'don't cache' or 'don't store' blocks bfcache in non-Chrome browsers and weakens it in Chrome; adding Permissions-Policy: unload=() breaks a script that genuinely relies on unload (none observed; Lighthouse 13 has no unload audit in the 12.8.2 runs, so test in DevTools). A page that sets cookies on every response (Polylang pll_language, PixelYourSite _fbp) is normally bypassed by LiteSpeed/FlyingPress page cache – fix at the plugin, not with headers.
findings.how_to_apply: Recipe: LiteSpeed – nothing (no Cache-Control on HTML is fine; Browser Cache applies to static files only). FlyingPress – nothing ('no-cache, must-revalidate' is bfcache-safe). W3TC – Browser Cache > HTML&XML > Cache Control policy = 'cache with validation' or 'cache without proxy' (current on marakaki), never 'don't cache'/'don't store'. All: add Header always set Permissions-Policy "unload=()" at the server (Plesk Apache & nginx additional directives). pallada.gr: switch WPML to serve the root in the default language without a redirect, or make the redirect cacheable, so the first request does not hit PHP with no-store. Logged-in editors: install Instant Back/Forward (nocache-bfcache) only if staff speed matters.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -sI URL (and a product page) shows no 'no-store' and no Set-Cookie on 200 HTML; DevTools > Application > Back/forward cache > 'Test back/forward cache' reports 'Successfully served from back/forward cache'; performance.getEntriesByType('navigation')[0].notRestoredReasons is null after a back navigation (Chrome 123+); Lighthouse bf-cache audit stays green.

findings.claim: PHP 8.4 is fully supported by WordPress 7.0/7.1 and by Elementor Pro since 3.32.0/3.34.0; on the agency sites deprecation notices cost nothing today because WP_DEBUG is false (error_reporting 4983 excludes E_DEPRECATED), but WP_DEBUG=true in production would log every notice on every uncached request and, with the default WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY=true, print them into HTML; the plugin should check PHP version, debug constants and debug.log size before any optimisation step.
findings.detail: make.wordpress.org PHP compatibility table: WordPress 7.1 and 7.0 are 'Y' for PHP 8.4 (and 8.5); 6.7 added beta support for 8.4; in May 2026 the 'beta support' label was retired; 7.0 dropped PHP 7.2/7.3. Elementor requirements page: 'PHP 7.4 or Greater … we highly recommend using PHP 8.x', WP memory 256 MB min (768 MB best); no explicit 8.4 statement. Elementor Pro changelog: 3.32.0 (2025-09-15) 'Fix: PHP 8.4 deprecation notices when running with WP_DEBUG enabled'; 3.34.0 (2025-12-22) 'Fix: PHP 8.4 deprecation notices related to deprecated E_STRICT constant'. Elementor 4.3.5 readme: Requires PHP 7.4, Requires at least 6.8, Tested up to 7.1. WooCommerce 11.2.1: Requires PHP 7.4, Requires at least 7.0. W3TC 2.10.7: Requires PHP 7.4, changelog has no 8.4 entry ('We recommend using PHP 8'). LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1 (2026-09-01): Requires PHP 7.4, no 8.4 entry. Premium Addons 4.11.113 (2026-10-15): tested 7.1.3, no PHP statement. Dynamic Visibility (Dynamic.ooo free) 6.0.6: Requires PHP 7.1; Dynamic.ooo Pro changelog returned 403; JetSmartFilters and YITH Booking: no PHP 8.4 statement found (YITH page: 'Compatible up to WordPress 7.1.x and WooCommerce 11.2.x'). Perfmatters 2.3.7 (2025-01-01): 'Updated CSS parsing library … Improves support for PHP 8.4'. Read-only runtime check: cretaforums.gr PHP 8.4.26, WP_DEBUG false, WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY true (core default from default-constants.php), WP_DEBUG_LOG false, display_errors 0, log_errors 1, error_reporting 4983, no debug.log, opcache.enable 1, validate_timestamps 1, revalidate_freq 2, memory 512, max_accelerated_files 130987, jit disable, no persistent object cache; limnoupolis.gr PHP 8.3.35, same debug state, opcache memory 256, jit tracing. wp_debug_mode() (load.php 7.1.3): WP_DEBUG false → error_reporting(E_CORE_ERROR|E_CORE_WARNING|E_COMPILE_ERROR|E_ERROR|E_WARNING|E_PARSE|E_USER_ERROR|E_USER_WARNING|E_RECOVERABLE_ERROR) = 4983, so E_DEPRECATED/E_NOTICE are suppressed; WP_DEBUG true → E_ALL and display_errors per WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY; display_errors is forced to 0 for REST, XML-RPC, wp_doing_ajax() and wp_is_json_request() requests regardless, so admin-ajax JSON survives but custom plugin endpoints and the Elementor editor iframe do not. developer.wordpress.org debug page: WP_DEBUG_LOG writes to wp-content/debug.log, 'useful … to view notices generated off-screen (e.g. during an AJAX request)'. php.net: opcache.jit default changed in PHP 8.4 (was 'tracing'); opcache.revalidate_freq only applies when validate_timestamps is on.
findings.breaks_when: WP_DEBUG true on production with PHP 8.4 and the unpatched add-ons: hundreds of 'Implicitly marking parameter as nullable is deprecated' / E_STRICT lines per uncached request written to the PHP error log (disk I/O on Plesk shared hosts) and, with WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY left at its default true, printed above <!DOCTYPE> which breaks the Elementor editor loading screen and any plugin endpoint that is not REST/admin-ajax; a debug.log of several hundred MB slows every PHP write. Setting validate_timestamps=0 without a deploy hook means plugin updates are not picked up until OPcache reset.
findings.how_to_apply: Pre-check in the plugin (read-only): PHP_VERSION, WP_DEBUG, WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY, WP_DEBUG_LOG, ini_get('display_errors'), error_reporting(), filesize(WP_CONTENT_DIR.'/debug.log'), and each active plugin's 'Requires PHP' header; stop and report if display_errors is on or debug.log > 50 MB. Production wp-config.php: define('WP_DEBUG', false); define('WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY', false); @ini_set('display_errors', 0); when diagnosing use define('WP_DEBUG', true); define('WP_DEBUG_LOG', true); define('WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY', false). php.ini (Plesk PHP settings): display_errors = Off, log_errors = On, error_reporting = E_ALL & ~E_DEPRECATED & ~E_NOTICE, opcache.enable = 1, opcache.memory_consumption = 256 (512 on the Woo sites), opcache.interned_strings_buffer = 32, opcache.max_accelerated_files = 100000+, opcache.validate_timestamps = 1 with opcache.revalidate_freq = 60 on shared hosts (0 + reset on deploy only where the agency controls deploys); leave opcache.jit as the host set it. Keep PHP 8.3 on sites running Dynamic.ooo Pro/JetSmartFilters/YITH until their changelogs state 8.4, or test on staging with WP_DEBUG_LOG and grep the log for 'Deprecated'.
findings.how_to_verify: Read-only PHP: return [PHP_VERSION, WP_DEBUG, WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY, ini_get('display_errors'), error_reporting(), @filesize(WP_CONTENT_DIR.'/debug.log')]; curl -s URL | head -c 300 must start with <!DOCTYPE (no PHP notice text); on staging with WP_DEBUG_LOG on, load home, a product, a booking page and open the Elementor editor, then grep -c 'PHP Deprecated' wp-content/debug.log per plugin path; Site Health > Info > Server shows OPcache enabled (7.0+) and Site Health status has no 'PHP version' critical issue.

findings.claim: Core Site Health already implements the read-only checks the plugin needs: page cache (median of loopback requests < 600 ms + known cache headers or advanced-cache.php), persistent object cache suggestion (alloptions > 500 entries or > 100,000 bytes, or > 1,000 posts/options/terms/comments/users), autoloaded options > 800,000 bytes, and OPcache status in Info > Server since 7.0; none of the two sites checked runs a persistent object cache.
findings.detail: wp-admin/includes/class-wp-site-health.php (7.1.3): get_test_page_cache() → get_page_cache_detail() compares median response time against get_good_response_time_threshold() = apply_filters('site_status_good_response_time_threshold', 600) ms and reports 'A page cache plugin was detected' when advanced_cache_present or when any of get_page_cache_headers() is present: cache-control, expires, age, last-modified, etag, x-cache-enabled, x-cache-disabled, x-cache, x-litespeed-cache, x-srcache-store-status, x-srcache-fetch-status, x-cache-status (callbacks treat 'hit' values as a hit). should_suggest_persistent_object_cache(): filter site_status_should_suggest_persistent_object_cache short-circuit, thresholds via site_status_persistent_object_cache_thresholds: alloptions_count 500, alloptions_bytes 100000, comments_count 1000, options_count 1000, posts_count 1000, terms_count 1000, users_count 1000. get_test_autoloaded_options(): limit apply_filters('site_status_autoloaded_options_size_limit', 800000) bytes with description/action filters. 7.0 field guide: 'Site Health: OPCache added to Site Health > Info > Server (Trac #63697)'. Observed: wp_using_ext_object_cache() false on limnoupolis.gr and null on cretaforums.gr (no object-cache.php drop-in) although limnoupolis runs WooCommerce + 30 plugins; audit summary autoload sizes 43–720 KB (pallada.gr 720 KB, limnoupolis 461 KB, marakaki 495 KB, onar 549 KB) – pallada is within 10% of the 800 KB warning. LiteSpeed Cache docs list its own object cache (Redis/Memcached) module; W3TC has Object Cache too; FlyingPress has none. FlyingPress sends x-flying-press-cache which core does not recognise, but its cache-control/expires headers satisfy the header check.
findings.breaks_when: The page-cache test issues 3 loopback GETs to the home URL with a cache-busting query arg; on sites where loopbacks are blocked (Plesk firewall, basic auth on dev6 hosts) it returns 'Server response time could not be determined' and the plugin must fall back to curl -w %{time_starttransfer}. Enabling a persistent object cache (Redis/Memcached) on a shared Plesk host without a running service produces fatal connection errors; WPML/Polylang and Woo session data need the cache flushed on deploy.
findings.how_to_apply: Plugin audit step (read-only, WP-CLI or Novamira execute-php reading only): $h = WP_Site_Health::get_instance(); $h->get_test_page_cache(); $h->get_test_persistent_object_cache(); $h->get_test_autoloaded_options(); $h->get_autoloaded_options_size(); or REST GET /wp-json/wp-site-health/v1/tests/page-cache with an app-password that has view_site_health_checks. Fix path: autoload > 600 KB → list the biggest options (SELECT option_name, LENGTH(option_value) FROM wp_options WHERE autoload IN ('yes','on') ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20) and set autoload off for logs/caches of removed plugins; object cache → LiteSpeed Cache > Cache > Object (Redis) on LiteSpeed hosts or W3TC Object Cache (Redis) where a Redis socket exists; never two object caches. New builds: enable the object cache before importing content; keep autoload under 400 KB.
findings.how_to_verify: Site Health > Status shows 'Page cache is detected and the server response time is good' and no 'autoloaded options' or 'persistent object cache' recommendation; wp_using_ext_object_cache() true after enabling; TTFB of an uncached page (append ?nocache=1) measured 5 times with curl -w '%{time_starttransfer}' drops after the object cache; Lighthouse 'Server response time' audit on an uncached URL.

findings.claim: Optimization Detective 1.0.0-beta7 + Image Prioritizer 1.0.0-beta4 (2026-08-26, require WP 6.9, tested 7.1.3) are the only measured way to preload an Elementor CSS-background hero: they collect real LCP element data per breakpoint and emit breakpoint-specific <link rel=preload fetchpriority=high> (plus Link headers) for background-image set by inline style or by a stylesheet, but they need the REST API open to anonymous visitors, 3 mobile + 3 desktop visits per URL, and should be run with Elementor's Optimized Image Loading off.
findings.detail: Image Prioritizer readme: preload links 'for image URLs of LCP elements: an IMG (imagesrcset/imagesizes), the first SOURCE with type in a PICTURE, an element with a CSS background-image inline style attribute, an element with a CSS background-image applied with a stylesheet (when the image is from an allowed origin), a VIDEO poster'; 'Ensure fetchpriority=high is only added to an IMG when it is the LCP element across all responsive breakpoints'; fetchpriority=low for occluded initial-viewport images (carousel slides); lazy loading of IMG/VIDEO and inline-style backgrounds outside every breakpoint's viewport; sizes=auto after lazy; 'optimizations are not applied for admins by default'; 'wait for URL Metrics to be gathered for both mobile and desktop visits'. Optimization Detective readme/docs: REST API must be accessible to unauthenticated visitors; no Safari metrics (no LCP API); filters od_breakpoint_max_widths (default 480, 600, 782), od_url_metrics_breakpoint_sample_size (default 3), od_url_metric_storage_lock_ttl (60 s, 0 for admins), od_url_metric_freshness_ttl (1 week, invalidated by ETag of post changes), od_can_optimize_response (also disabled by ?optimization_detective_disabled); od_start_template_optimization fires after the whole template is in the output buffer and the docs show header('Cache-Control: private') there as a way to keep uncached until metrics exist; changelog: 'Eliminate the detection time window which prevented URL Metrics from being gathered when page caching is present' and 'Send post ID … to schedule page cache validation'; garbage-collects od_url_metrics posts after 3 months. Performance Lab FAQ: beta-testing plugin, 'utilizing it comes with inherent risks'. Interaction with Elementor: OIL prepends loading/fetchpriority by regex before OD's buffer; IP then rewrites the same attributes from URL metrics, so two engines decide (turn OIL off, finding 3); Elementor's lazy-background CSS hides backgrounds of the 2nd+ top-level container on ≤640 px tall viewports until JS adds .e-lazyloaded, so OD's web-vitals sees the hero as LCP only when it is in container 1 or has e-no-lazyload; LiteSpeed VPI (QUIC.cloud, paid) and Perfmatters/FlyingPress 'preload critical images' do the same job with fixed counts – pick one; Perfmatters 'Disable REST API' for logged-out users would stop metric collection; Delay-JS tools must not delay OD's inline detection module. Elementor 4.3.5 ships a modules/performance-lab/module.php that only swaps background URLs to WebP when the legacy Performance Lab 'webp-uploads' module is active (option site-health/webp-support), unrelated to OD. A third-party 'Elementor LCP Background Image Preloader' add-on exists but is stale (0.1.0, tested 6.6) and is superseded by IP's stylesheet support.
findings.breaks_when: Sites that block or restrict the anonymous REST API (security plugins, Perfmatters REST toggle, basic-auth dev6 hosts) collect no metrics and nothing is optimised; pages whose LCP differs per language/variation share one URL metric set per URL only (WPML directories are separate URLs – fine); a hero rotating via Elementor background slideshow (pallada 8, voreniahorizon 2) gives inconsistent LCP URLs and therefore preloads one slide; Safari visitors never contribute; beta code – a fatal in an output-buffer callback blanks the page (OD had such a fix in 1.0.0-beta: od_get_current_url_metrics_etag with null posts).
findings.how_to_apply: Staging trial per site: install Performance Lab 4.2.0, activate Optimization Detective + Image Prioritizer (+ Embed Optimizer where YouTube embeds sit above the fold), set Elementor > Settings > Performance > Optimized Image Loading = Inactive, verify GET /wp-json/ returns 200 anonymously, visit each key URL 3× from a phone-sized and 3× from a desktop browser (not logged in), then purge the page cache once. Keep LiteSpeed VPI / Perfmatters 'Preload critical images' off on those sites. Add class e-no-lazyload to the hero container if it is not the first. New lean builds: start with OD+IP from day one, hero in container 1, no slideshow.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -s URL | grep -o '<link rel="preload"[^>]*fetchpriority="high"[^>]*>' shows a preload with media= per breakpoint pointing at the hero background URL and the response has a matching Link: header; <meta name="generator" content="optimization-detective …"> lists no disabled reasons; wp post list --post_type=od_url_metrics --format=count grows per URL; Lighthouse mobile: LCP element unchanged, 'LCP request discovery' insight passes, LCP time drops; CLS unchanged.
findings.correction: Versions/dates/requirements confirmed via api.wordpress.org (IP 1.0.0-beta4, OD 1.0.0-beta7, both 2026-08-26, requires 6.9, tested 7.1.3, PHP 7.4); readme confirms preload LINK elements and Link headers for IMG, first typed SOURCE, inline-style background-image, stylesheet background-image from an allowed origin, VIDEO poster; fetchpriority=low for occluded images; admins not optimised; REST API must be open; no Safari metrics. Precision on visits: default od_breakpoint_max_widths (480, 600, 782) create FOUR viewport groups (≤480, 481–600, 601–782, ≥783). Breakpoint-specific preload links are emitted for whichever groups are populated (get_groups_by_lcp_element), while fetchpriority=high on an IMG via get_common_lcp_element() requires the narrowest AND widest groups populated (source: 'Ensure both the narrowest (first) and widest (last) viewport groups are populated'). So the '3 mobile + 3 desktop' recipe is right only if the 'mobile' visits are ≤480 CSS px wide (a 600-px tablet lands in a middle group) and desktop ≥783 px. IP's own sizes computation was removed ('use Enhanced Responsive Images instead'), which does not help classic themes. 'Only measured way' is an opinion, not refuted. OD hooks doc confirms od_breakpoint_max_widths, od_url_metrics_breakpoint_sample_size 3, od_url_metric_storage_lock_ttl 60 s (0 for authorized users), od_url_metric_freshness_ttl 1 week, od_can_optimize_response, optimization_detective_disabled query arg, and the header('Cache-Control: private') example in od_start_template_optimization; GC TTL changed to 3 months in beta4.

findings.claim: Performance Lab status on 2026-08-26: Speculative Loading (6.8), auto-sizes (6.7), fetchpriority (6.3) and Performant Translations (6.5) are in core; still plugins are Modern Image Formats 2.7.1 (AVIF by default when the server supports it), Image Placeholders 1.3.0, Enhanced Responsive Images 1.8.0 (block themes only), View Transitions 1.2.1, Instant Back/Forward 1.3.3, Embed Optimizer beta6, OD beta7, IP beta4; core 7.1 itself still outputs the uploaded format unless image_editor_output_format is filtered.
findings.detail: api.wordpress.org: performance-lab 4.2.0 (requires 6.9, tested 7.1.3) lists Embed Optimizer, Enhanced Responsive Images, Image Placeholders, Image Prioritizer, Instant Back/Forward, Modern Image Formats, Optimization Detective, Performant Translations, Speculative Loading, View Transitions (experimental). speculation-rules 1.7.0: 'This core Speculative Loading functionality was merged into WordPress 6.8 … this plugin defaults to prerendering with moderate eagerness … provides a user interface … on the Settings > Reading admin screen' and warns when a persistent object cache is absent for logged-in use. auto-sizes 1.8.0 (Enhanced Responsive Images): 'Implementation of … sizes="auto" … merged into WordPress 6.7'; remaining feature improves sizes accuracy 'using layout information available in block themes. This enhancement is not available to classic themes' (Inglelandi/Hello are classic → no benefit). webp-uploads 2.7.1 (Modern Image Formats): 'By default, AVIF images will be generated if supported on the hosting server, otherwise WebP'; only new uploads; 'Output fallback images' checkbox; 2.7.0 also converts Cover/Group block backgrounds. Core 7.1.3 media.php: wp_get_image_editor_output_format() default array maps only HEIC/HEIF → JPEG; filter image_editor_output_format($output_format, $filename, $mime_type); AVIF/WebP upload support depends on wp_image_editor_supports(['mime_type'=>'image/avif'|'image/webp']); default quality 82 (WebP 86) via wp_editor_set_quality; big_image_size_threshold default 2560. 7.1 additions: client-side media processing (wp_is_client_side_media_processing_enabled() true only over HTTPS/localhost, filter wp_client_side_media_processing_enabled; cross-origin isolation headers are set only on load-post.php, load-post-new.php, load-site-editor.php and load-widgets.php, so no frontend COOP/COEP impact) and a per-user Media Library infinite scroll default. The 7.0 and 7.1 field guides contain no frontend performance section beyond these; 7.0 removed the script type attribute for all themes and deprecated html5 script theme support (Trac #64442); 7.0 added fetchpriority=low/auto handling in wp_get_loading_optimization_attributes. On limnoupolis two converters (TinyPNG + Converter for Media) duplicate what one of the above does.
findings.breaks_when: Modern Image Formats with 'Output fallback images' unchecked produces only AVIF/WebP sub-sizes; AVIF decode is slow on old Android devices and Imagick AVIF encoding is slow on shared Plesk hosts (uploads time out); a second converter (TinyPNG, Converter for Media, ShortPixel) rewriting the same URLs produces double conversions and broken srcset; Elementor background images (CSS) are not covered by srcset-based converters – Elementor's own performance-lab module only swaps them when the legacy Performance Lab WebP module function exists.
findings.how_to_apply: Existing sites: keep exactly one converter; if choosing core, add_filter('image_editor_output_format', fn($f)=>$f+['image/jpeg'=>'image/webp','image/png'=>'image/webp']) in an mu-plugin and regenerate (wp media regenerate --only-missing) – WebP, not AVIF, on these hosts unless wp_image_editor_supports AVIF and a test upload of a 4000 px JPEG finishes in < 10 s. Do not install Enhanced Responsive Images on the classic themes. Speculative Loading plugin only if the client wants a UI; otherwise finding 1. New lean builds: Modern Image Formats (WebP, fallback on) or the core filter, no third-party converter; big_image_size_threshold left at 2560.
findings.how_to_verify: wp eval 'var_dump(wp_image_editor_supports(["mime_type"=>"image/avif"]), wp_image_editor_supports(["mime_type"=>"image/webp"]));' (read-only); upload a test image and check wp-content/uploads for .webp sub-sizes; curl -s URL | grep -o 'srcset="[^"]*' | head shows .webp; Lighthouse 'Serve images in next-gen formats'/'Improve image delivery' insight passes; no 404s in DevTools Network for image URLs.

findings.claim: Speculative loading, bfcache and the core image/script features are invisible to Lighthouse and PageSpeed Insights, so they must be sold and verified as field (CrUX) wins, not score levers.
findings.detail: WordPress 6.8 performance post: 'the performance metrics do not benefit from the new speculative loading feature, since it only helps with performance when navigating from one URL of the site to another URL of the site. Because the benchmarks rely on individual requests to specific URLs though, speculative loading does not trigger.' Chrome: prerendered pages' timing is exposed via activationStart; CrUX records navigation types including bfcache restores (web.dev). All 10 local Lighthouse 12.8.2 runs score 'bf-cache' = 1 (binary pass) – it is a diagnostic, not weighted. The lab scores (27–86) on these sites are driven by the hero media, fonts, GTM tags and animations documented in the other dimensions; nothing in this dimension moves the mobile score by more than the removed request bytes (finding 5) and the LCP preload (finding 9).
findings.breaks_when: not known to break
findings.how_to_apply: In the plugin's report, put core features under a 'field / repeat-visit' heading with CrUX (PSI 'Discover what your real users are experiencing') as the metric, and keep PSI-score promises to the hero/font/JS fixes. Record the CrUX p75 LCP and 'navigation types' before and 28 days after enabling moderate eagerness or OD+IP.
findings.how_to_verify: PSI 'Discover what your real users are experiencing' p75 LCP/INP/CLS for the origin after 28 days; CrUX API navigation_types.fractions.back_forward_cache grows after bfcache fixes; performance.getEntriesByType('navigation')[0].activationStart > 0 on a prerendered second page.

findings.claim: On the two cache-less dev6 sites and the LiteSpeed sites the per-response cookies observed (Polylang pll_language, server-side Meta _fbp) are the mechanism that makes page caches bypass or fragment pages; fix them at the plugin level before measuring anything.
findings.detail: platonos.dev6 (no cache plugin) answers the home page with Set-Cookie: pll_language=en; expires 1 year; SameSite=Lax – Polylang sets its language cookie on every uncached frontend response. limnoupolis.gr/shop/ (LiteSpeed) answers 301 with Set-Cookie: _fbp=fb.1… from PHP (server-side Facebook pixel cookie, e.g. PixelYourSite – Novamira lists pixelyoursite-pro abilities on marakaki) and x-litespeed-cache-control: no-cache. LiteSpeed docs: a page is confirmed uncached when X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: no-cache is present, and pages are cached per the configured Vary/cookie rules; WooCommerce 11.2.1 sets woocommerce_items_in_cart via wc_setcookie only when the cart is non-empty (class-wc-cart-session.php maybe_set_cart_cookies) – cached HTML for visitors without a cart is unaffected. Core 7.1.3 speculative loading excludes nothing cookie-related, so a prefetch of a cookie-setting page also sets the cookie.
findings.breaks_when: Polylang 'Detect browser language' + cookie set on every page and LiteSpeed 'Cache Logged-in'/vary misconfigured: visitors get the wrong-language cached page or every page is a cache miss; a server-side pixel that sets _fbp on redirects turns those redirects into PHP hits for every visitor.
findings.how_to_apply: Polylang: Languages > Settings > 'Detect browser language' off on sites whose root should be cached, or let the cache plugin vary by pll_language (LiteSpeed Cache > Cache > Vary Group / FlyingPress language cookie exclusion); PixelYourSite/Meta: disable 'server-side _fbp cookie' or move the pixel into GTM so no Set-Cookie leaves PHP; keep the Woo cart cookie as is.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -sI URL shows no Set-Cookie on home, category and product pages for a cookie-less client; x-litespeed-cache: hit / x-flying-press-cache: HIT on the second request; a Greek-browser and an English-browser request to the root both receive the intended language (curl -H 'Accept-Language: el').
findings.correction: Mechanism confirmed but the LiteSpeed setting name is wrong: 'Vary Groups' is role-based ('combine cache varies with user roles'); the option for a plugin cookie that changes page content is LiteSpeed Cache > Cache > Vary > 'Vary Cookies' ('Use this option if a third-party plugin uses cookies to change page content. Enter one cookie per line'). Note also LiteSpeed's warning for 'Do Not Cache Cookies': excluding a cookie that appears on every page 'effectively exclude[s] your entire site from caching' — never put pll_language there. Polylang offers a documented hard switch: define('PLL_COOKIE', false) in wp-config.php makes Polylang 'not set any cookie' (caveat: 'the login page will not translate'); use it on sites with per-language URL structures where the cookie only serves browser-language redirects. WooCommerce 11.2.1 class-wc-cart-session.php confirmed: maybe_set_cart_cookies() sets woocommerce_items_in_cart only when !$this->cart->is_empty(). LiteSpeed docs confirm 'X-LiteSpeed-Cache-Control: no-cache' marks an uncached page.

findings.claim: A plugin filter on wp_speculation_rules_configuration (Perfmatters 2.4.3+, FlyingPress) overrides the WordPress 7.1 WP_SPECULATIVE_LOADING_DEFAULT_MODE/_EAGERNESS constants, so the plugin must read the rendered rule, not wp-config, to know the effective eagerness.
findings.detail: wp-includes/speculative-loading.php (7.1.3): wp_get_speculation_rules_configuration() builds array('mode'=>'auto','eagerness'=>'auto') (or null when logged in / no pretty permalinks), runs apply_filters('wp_speculation_rules_configuration', $config), and only THEN replaces 'auto' values with wp_get_speculation_rules_default_configuration(), which is where the 7.1 constants/env vars are read (constant beats env var). Any filter returning explicit values therefore wins over the constant with no warning. Perfmatters' Preloading > Speculative Loading setting uses this filter path (changelog 2.4.3 04.15.2025 'control Speculative Loading mode and eagerness settings for sites running WordPress 6.8+'); the Speculative Loading plugin 1.7.0 does the same via Settings > Reading and defaults to prerender/moderate.
findings.breaks_when: Not known to break; the failure mode is a silent mismatch between what wp-config says and what the browser receives (a team member sets the constant to moderate, Perfmatters keeps conservative, nobody notices).
findings.how_to_apply: In the plugin's audit, treat the <script type="speculationrules"> JSON in the rendered HTML as the source of truth and report which layer produced it: check defined('WP_SPECULATIVE_LOADING_DEFAULT_EAGERNESS'), has_filter('wp_speculation_rules_configuration') (read-only via execute-php) and the Perfmatters option perfmatters_options['preload']['speculative_loading_*'] / FlyingPress 'Preload links' option. Document one owner per site: constant on plain sites, Perfmatters setting on Perfmatters sites, FlyingPress on FlyingPress sites.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -s URL | grep -o '"eagerness":"[a-z]*"' equals the intended value; after changing the constant on a Perfmatters site the value must NOT change (proves the filter owns it); after changing the Perfmatters setting it must.

findings.claim: Cloudflare Speed Brain is harmless to origin load but useless on these sites while HTML is cf-cache-status DYNAMIC: its prefetches are served only from Cloudflare's edge cache and return 503 otherwise, each failed prefetch still consuming one of Chrome's two speculation slots.
findings.detail: Cloudflare doc (last updated Aug 14, 2026): requirements 'The web page requested by the prefetch is eligible for cache' and 'does not invoke a Worker'; safeguards 'Prefetch requests will never reach origin servers. Prefetch requests only serve content that is stored in Cloudflare's Cache. If the content is not in Cache, the prefetch request will not continue to origin servers'; 'Prefetches that are not successful will respond with a 503 status code'; Speculation-Rules header, conservative prefetch; enabled by default on Free/Pro/Business, not Enterprise; origin Speculation-Rules headers are not overridden. Chrome limits (prerender-pages doc): 2 concurrent speculations for conservative/moderate/eager, FIFO. The researcher found no Speculation-Rules header on the 4 Cloudflare-fronted sites today, so Speed Brain is currently off there.
findings.breaks_when: Speed Brain on + HTML not cached at the edge (default for WordPress without Cache Rules/APO): every mousedown prefetch 503s; with core's rule also present, the duplicate URL can push a useful speculation out of the 2-slot FIFO. No origin impact, so the earlier 'double server hits' concern does not apply to Speed Brain.
findings.how_to_apply: Keep Speed Brain off (Cloudflare dashboard > Speed > Optimization > Content) unless the site caches HTML at the edge for anonymous visitors (Cache Rule 'Eligible for cache' on text/html with cookie bypass for wordpress_logged_in_*, woocommerce_*, pll_language); if it is turned on, disable core's rule with add_filter('wp_speculation_rules_configuration','__return_null') so one engine remains.
findings.how_to_verify: curl -sI URL | grep -i '^speculation-rules' empty when off; when on, DevTools > Network with mousedown on a link shows the prefetch request with sec-purpose: prefetch and status 200 (edge hit) rather than 503; DevTools > Application > Speculative loads shows a single rule source.

title: Elementor Pro Theme Builder templates and popups as a per-page tax: audit, lazy-load and conditions (Elementor 4.3.5 / Pro 4.3.1-4.3.2, WordPress 7.1.3, measured 2026-10-16)
summary:
On the 10 audited home pages the Theme Builder layer costs 4-8 extra post-N.css files (page + kit + header + footer + every popup + every container/section template inserted via the Template widget), 7-25 header widgets, a 35-100 KB raw footer, and one hidden popup document per matching popup. Elementor Pro renders every popup whose conditions match as a server-side `
` with its own post-N.css file; Pro 4.3.1's JS (`showPopup`) simply returns if the popup document is not already in the page, so there is no on-demand fetch and every trigger type (page load, scroll, click, exit intent, Open By Selector, form action) implies the full popup HTML is downloaded on every page it matches. Lazy `` inside the hidden popup do not download in Chrome/Safari/Firefox (display:none), but non-lazy ones (the site-logo widget, 2396x825 PNG on onar) and the popup's CSS file do, and a Pro Form inside a popup pulls widget-form CSS and the form bundle onto every page. Loop items are the exception: Pro 4.3.1 prints each loop template's CSS inline once (`
critic_notes: critic did not finish; findings unreviewed
open_questions: Whether a @font-face used only inside a display:none popup is downloaded: expected no (fonts load on first rendered glyph) but not tested; Chrome DevTools MCP could not launch in this container (no Chrome binary, running as root), so the lazy-image-in-popup behaviour relies on web.dev (2024-08-13) and phpied (2024-01-01) rather than a live test on onar.

Pro 4.3 inlining of popup CSS: confirmed as a separate post-N.css file under the default `elementor_css_print_method=external` (onar Pro 4.2.x link tag, kand Pro 4.3.1 rules inside the W3TC bundle); under `internal` everything is inlined (cretaforums). Not checked on Pro 4.3.2 specifically.

Priority/specificity when several headers' conditions match the same page (e.g. a Checkout header via Singular > Pages plus an Entire Site header): not found in the help pages opened; the recommendation uses explicit Exclude rows instead.
Byte-for-byte comparison of a mobile-menu popup vs an Off-Canvas widget on the same site was not measured (no site changes allowed).

Dangling `template_id`s (717953, 725023…) referenced by marakaki's home-template documents 38085/40768: origin (kit import / WPML duplication) and what the Loop Grid renders for a missing template were not investigated.
JetPopup Ajax caveats come from GitHub issue titles seen in search results; the issue pages returned 403 and the versions affected are unknown.
How the `elementor_pro_theme_builder_conditions` option behaves when Element Caching and LiteSpeed ESI are both on (stale header after a conditions change) was reasoned, not reproduced.
The `_elementor_popup_display_settings` meta and `elementor_pro_theme_builder_conditions` option were verified on Pro 4.3.1 (marakaki) only; the other sites run Pro 4.2.x-4.3.1.

Skipped: a Pro 4.3.2 source check (closed source), live Lighthouse re-runs, and any staging experiment. Risk to the user: the 'safe to trash' rule must honour translation groups and Template/Loop/DCE references, or a language's header, a listing or a PDF template disappears.

findings.claim: Pro popups are rendered server-side on every page their conditions match and Pro 4.3.1 has no on-demand fetch: `showPopup()` returns silently if the popup document is not already in the DOM, so every trigger type implies the full popup HTML, its post-N.css and its widget assets are downloaded on every matching page.
findings.detail: Confirmed in live HTML (2026-10-16): kand.dev6 home renders `<div data-elementor-type="popup" data-elementor-id="506" class="elementor elementor-506 elementor-location-popup" data-elementor-settings="{"a11y_navigation":"yes","triggers":[],"timing":[]}">` (Newsletter popup, Pro Form, 3.9 KB raw / 1.1 KB gzip, triggers [] = manual-only) and onar-seaside-lounge.gr renders popup 6302 'Mobile-Menu' (12.2 KB raw / 2.5 KB gzip, nav-menu + site-logo + 2 imgs, entrance_animation slideInDown). The dialog wrapper `.elementor-popup-modal` is created by JS, so the audit must grep `data-elementor-type="popup"` / `elementor-location-popup`, not `elementor-popup-modal`. In Pro 4.3.1 elements-handlers.min.js (served by pallada.gr): `showPopup(t,n){const s=elementorFrontend.documentsManager.documents[t.id];if(!s)return;...s.showModal(null,n)}` and `closePopup` likewise; no ajax/fetch/wp-json call exists in the popup module. `ElementorProFrontendConfig.popup.hasPopUps` only gates pageViews/sessions storage (`shouldSetViewsAndSessions()`), it does not lazy-load anything; marakaki has hasPopUps:true yet renders 0 popups on home because its 4 popups are scoped to WooCommerce product/product_archive or have no conditions. Elementor's own marketing claim that popups 'only load when needed' is not what the code does. Popup CSS is a separate file: onar loads `id='elementor-post-6302-css'` (post-6302.css, 3,032 bytes, 5 font-family rules) and kand's W3TC bundle 83f37.css contains 31 `.elementor-506` rules. Audit rule: popups_per_page (count of `data-elementor-type="popup"`), KB per popup (raw and gzip of the wrapper), widgets per popup, imgs without loading=lazy, forms, videos. Fix order: 1) tighten conditions to the pages that contain the opener (Singular > Pages > specific) and exclude checkout/booking; 2) strip media, videos and fonts from popups (text + button only); 3) replace footer/contact-form popups with a Contact page link; 4) only as last resort use a third-party Ajax popup (JetPopup 'Loading content with Ajax', see separate finding).
findings.breaks_when: A popup opened by `Open By Selector`, a link action (`#elementor-action:action=popup:open`) or a Form 'Actions After Submit' sits on a page you excluded from the popup's conditions: the click then does nothing (showPopup returns). Always include every page that contains an opener.
findings.how_to_apply: In Elementor > Templates > Popups > (popup) > Publish Settings > Conditions: replace `Entire Site` with `Include > Singular > Pages > <the pages that open it>`; add `Exclude > Singular > Pages > Checkout/Booking`. In the audit, list popups via `SELECT p.ID FROM wp_posts p JOIN wp_postmeta t ON t.post_id=p.ID AND t.meta_key='_elementor_template_type' AND t.meta_value='popup'` and read `_elementor_conditions` + `_elementor_popup_display_settings`. Public-HTML check per URL: `curl -sL <url> | grep -o 'data-elementor-type="popup"[^>]*' | wc -l`.
findings.how_to_verify: After narrowing conditions: curl the home page and confirm 0 `data-elementor-type="popup"` wrappers and no `elementor-post-<popupid>-css` link; click every opener on the pages that keep the popup and confirm it opens (DevTools console shows no error, `elementorFrontend.documentsManager.documents[<id>]` exists). Re-run mobile Lighthouse: fewer stylesheets, lower 'Reduce unused CSS'.

findings.claim: Inside a pre-rendered (display:none) popup, `` is not downloaded by Chrome, Safari or Firefox, but non-lazy images, CSS background images and the popup's post-N.css are; Elementor's Optimized Image Loading makes most popup images lazy, while the Site Logo widget and LiteSpeed/FlyingPress lazy-load placeholders behave differently.
findings.detail:
web.dev 'Browser-level image lazy loading' (last updated 2024-08-13): 'Chrome, Safari, and Firefox don't load images using display: none; styling, either on the image element or on a parent element. However, other image hiding techniques, such as using opacity:0 styling, still cause the browser to load the image.' phpied.com test (2024-01-01, Chrome/Firefox/Safari): 'All non-lazy images are loaded no matter how their containers are hidden'; 'Lazy images inside a display: none or
do not load'; 'visibility: hidden is the worst'. On onar the popup 6302 contains `` with no loading attribute (theme-site-logo widget) → downloads on every page even though the same logo is also in the header; the other popup image was rewritten by LiteSpeed to a data: SVG placeholder (`data-lazyloaded="1"`), which also does not download. Popup CSS files reference fonts (onar post-6302.css: 'Noto Serif Display', 'Open Sans', 3 global typography vars) and, on pallada, the header CSS post-4565.css (7.2 KB) carries a `url(.../pexels-orlovamaria-4946875.webp)` background image. Not verified live in this session (no Chrome in the container): whether a @font-face used only inside a display:none popup is fetched (expected: no, fonts load on first rendered glyph).
findings.breaks_when: Nothing breaks; the only trap is the reverse: an image that must be visible the instant a popup opens (hero in a full-screen popup) flashes in late when lazy. Set that one image to Lazy Load: No deliberately.
findings.how_to_apply: Audit: inside each `data-elementor-type="popup"` wrapper count `<img` without `loading="lazy"` and `background-image`/`url(` in that popup's post-N.css; flag site-logo/image widgets in popups. Fix: remove images, logos and background images from popups (mobile-menu popups do not need a second logo); keep popup text-only; if an image is essential, let Elementor's Optimized Image Loading leave it lazy.
findings.how_to_verify: DevTools > Network > Img filter on a fresh load with the popup closed: no request for the popup's image files; open the popup and confirm they load then. For CSS backgrounds check Network for the popup's `url(...)` assets before opening.

findings.claim: Pro 4.3 popup triggers and advanced rules are stored in the `_elementor_popup_display_settings` post meta as `{triggers:{...}, timing:{...}}` and echoed into `data-elementor-settings`; `triggers: []` means a manual-only popup (Open By Selector, link action or form action), and the exact option names are documented in the June 2026 help article.
findings.detail: Verified read-only on marakaki.com (Pro 4.3.1): class constant `\ElementorPro\Modules\Popup\Document::DISPLAY_SETTINGS_META_KEY` = `_elementor_popup_display_settings`; popup 65879 stores `{"triggers":{"page_load_delay":2},"timing":{"times_times":1,"times_period":"day"}}`, popups 37731/33768/33310 store `{"triggers":[],"timing":[]}`. Trigger keys seen in Pro 4.3.1 JS: page_load, scrolling, scrolling_to, click, inactivity, exit_intent; timing (advanced-rule) keys: page_views, sessions, times, url, sources, logged_in, devices, schedule. Help 'Configure a popup' (Last Update June 19, 2026) option names: Triggers — 'On Page Load', 'On Scroll' (Up/Down, % down / px up), 'On Scroll To Element' (CSS ID), 'On Click' (number of clicks), 'After Inactivity' (seconds), 'On Page Exit Intent'; Advanced Rules — 'Show after X page views', 'Show after X sessions', 'Show up to X times' (Count: On Open / On Close, stored in Local Storage), 'When arriving from specific URL' (Show/Hide, Regex), 'Show when arriving from' (search engines / external / internal), 'Hide for logged in users' ('For websites with cache, this feature might not work properly'), 'Show on devices' (Desktop/Tablet/Mobile). Settings tab: 'Avoid Multiple Popups: If the user has seen another popup on the page he visits, hide this popup by selecting Yes', 'Open By Selector: Enter a list of selectors that will manually trigger the popup (CSS IDs, classes or data-elements)', 'Prevent Closing on Overlay', 'Prevent Closing on ESC Key', 'Disable Page Scrolling'. Note 'Popups cannot be displayed more than once if the page is not reloaded'. Pro changelog 3.34.4 (2026-01-29): 'Fix: Avoid Multiple Popups control does not work in Popups'. 'Show on devices' is evaluated in JS, so a desktop-only popup is still downloaded on mobile. Help 'Conditions, triggers, and advanced rules' (Last Update August 27, 2026) confirms the three-layer model (Conditions = where, Triggers = user actions, Advanced Rules = non-user conditions).
findings.breaks_when: not known to break (read-only audit field). Caveat: `Show on devices` and `Hide for logged in users` are client-side filters and never reduce the HTML payload.
findings.how_to_apply: audit.php: for each popup read `get_post_meta($id,'_elementor_popup_display_settings',true)`; classify `triggers==[]` as manual-only (needs an opener on every included page), `page_load_delay`/`scrolling*`/`exit_intent`/`inactivity` as automatic (a UX decision; on mobile prefer none), `timing.devices` present as device-filtered (payload still ships to all devices). Report `avoid_multiple_popups` from `_elementor_page_settings`.
findings.how_to_verify: Compare the meta with the `data-elementor-settings` attribute on the live page wrapper (they must match after saving); for a device-filtered popup load the page with a mobile UA and confirm the popup HTML is still present (expected) so the payload claim holds.

findings.claim: A popup or Theme Builder template with an empty `_elementor_conditions` meta never renders and any link/selector/form action pointing to it silently does nothing, so such popups are dead weight to delete; conversely a popup with `include/general` ships on every page.
findings.detail: marakaki.com (Pro 4.3.1): 4 published popups — 65879 'Stock Offers popup' (page-load trigger 2 s, once per day) and 33310 'Product Filter' have no `_elementor_conditions` meta → never rendered (home HTML has 0 popups despite hasPopUps:true); 37731 'mobile menu categories' = `include/woocommerce/product_archive`, 33768 'Single Product swatches' = `include/woocommerce/product`. Also published with no conditions: headers 52610 'header backup En' and 52615 'header backu el' (8 widgets each, nav-menu + menu cart). Novamira's ability description states the same rule: 'A template with no conditions renders nowhere.' onar: popup 6529 'BOOK ENGINE POPUP' is a draft (ignored by Pro). Condition string format confirmed live: `include/general` (Entire Site), `include/singular/front_page`, `include/woocommerce/product`, `include/product_archive/product_cat`, `exclude/product_archive/product_cat/3688`, `exclude/product_archive/product_search`, `include/product/in_product_tag/7736`. Help 'Set conditions for site part templates' (Last Update October 1, 2026): Entire Site; Singular > All Singular / Front Page / Posts / In Category / In Child Categories / In Tag / Posts by Author / Pages / Landing Pages / Floating buttons; Archive; 'You can assign multiple conditions to a template'. Caveat for the delete rule: on multilingual sites translated templates have no conditions by design (next finding).
findings.breaks_when: The template is a translation (Polylang/WPML) of a conditioned template, or is referenced by a Template widget / Loop widget / DCE PDF template — then it is used despite having no conditions. Check translations and `template_id` references first.
findings.how_to_apply: audit.php field `templates_without_conditions`: `SELECT p.ID,p.post_title,t.meta_value type FROM wp_posts p JOIN wp_postmeta t ON t.post_id=p.ID AND t.meta_key='_elementor_template_type' AND t.meta_value IN ('header','footer','popup','single','single-post','single-page','archive','product','product-archive','search-results','error-404') LEFT JOIN wp_postmeta c ON c.post_id=p.ID AND c.meta_key='_elementor_conditions' WHERE p.post_type='elementor_library' AND p.post_status='publish' AND (c.meta_value IS NULL OR c.meta_value='' OR c.meta_value='a:0:{}')`; exclude IDs that appear in `pll_get_post_translations()` / WPML `icl_object_id()` of a conditioned template or in any `"template_id":"<id>"` inside `_elementor_data`. Present the rest as 'safe to trash (with OK)'. Trash (not delete) via the Elementor Templates screen so it is reversible for 30 days.
findings.how_to_verify: Before trashing: `curl -s <url> | grep -c 'elementor-<id>'` on the home page, a product page and an archive = 0; after trashing, re-crawl 5 key pages for 404 assets or missing header/footer; `wp elementor-pro theme-builder clear-conditions` then reload.

findings.claim: Pro caches resolved display conditions in the option `elementor_pro_theme_builder_conditions` (keys: header, footer, popup, single, archive, elementor_head, elementor_body_start, elementor_body_end); editing `_elementor_conditions` outside the editor has no effect until the cache regenerates (`wp elementor-pro theme-builder clear-conditions`), and multilingual query filters can corrupt the regeneration.
findings.detail: Read-only probe on marakaki (Pro 4.3.1): `get_option('elementor_pro_theme_builder_conditions')` is a 2,532-byte array; sample `"single":{"31823":["include/product"],"34965":["include/singular/project"],...}`, `"elementor_head":{"42899":["include/general"],...}` — Custom Code snippets share the same cache. developers.elementor.com CLI doc: 'All the conditions are cached. The Elementor CLI theme-builder clear-conditions command will clear the cached conditions to trigger a regeneration process.' Command: `wp elementor-pro theme-builder clear-conditions`. WPML erratum (resolved) shows the cache is rebuilt by a `WP_Query` with `'meta_key' => '_elementor_conditions'` in `elementor-pro/modules/theme-builder/classes/conditions-cache.php`; with a language filter active only one language's templates were cached and the original template 'stops loading completely' until `suppress_filters => true`. Element Caching (merged in Pro 3.32.0, 2025-09-15, Performance tab) is a separate HTML cache: help says containers/off-canvas/sections are always cached and 'Element Caching cannot be used on elements that contain dynamic tags'; it does not store conditions, but a stale element cache plus a stale page cache can hide a conditions change — purge both after editing conditions.
findings.breaks_when: Conditions are changed by a script/MCP and the cache is not regenerated → old header/footer/popup set keeps rendering; or a page cache (LiteSpeed/FlyingPress/W3TC) serves the old HTML. Also regenerating while WPML/Polylang filters are active in a CLI context can drop one language's templates (the WPML erratum pattern).
findings.how_to_apply: Always change conditions in the editor's Publish Settings or run `wp elementor-pro theme-builder clear-conditions` right after a programmatic change; then purge the page cache (LiteSpeed: Toolbox > Purge All; FlyingPress: Purge pages and preload; W3TC: Purge All Caches) and Elementor > Tools > Regenerate Files & Data. audit.php: compare the set of template IDs per location in the option with templates whose `_elementor_conditions` is non-empty and flag `conditions_cache_stale` when they differ.
findings.how_to_verify: After the change load a page in each language with `?nocache=1` (LiteSpeed) or logged out after purge and confirm the intended header/footer/popup IDs in `data-elementor-id`; `wp option get elementor_pro_theme_builder_conditions --format=json` lists the expected IDs under each key.

findings.claim: On multilingual sites one header/footer per language costs only the matching language's post-N.css on each page, but translated templates intentionally have zero conditions (Connect Polylang for Elementor swaps them; WPML's guide says to publish the secondary template without conditions), so the audit must join translations before calling a template unused, and WPML duplicates with a missing `_elementor_template_type` are broken copies.
findings.detail: limnoupolis.gr (Polylang): Novamira lists Header EN 46478 / Header EL 46479 / Footer EN 46480 / Footer EL 46481, each with 1 condition; the EN home loads exactly post-13852 (page), post-46472 (kit), post-46478 (header), post-46480 (footer) — the EL pair is absent. pallada.gr and onar-seaside-lounge.gr use `plugins/connect-polylang-elementor` (wordpress.org listing v2.5.5: 'Template translation and show in the correct language'): pallada 'Header el' 780 has 1 condition while 'Header en' 4565 (the one rendered on the EN home) has 0; onar header 6076 has 1 condition, 'Header-gr' 6880 has 0, popup 6302 'Mobile-Menu' has 1, 'Mobile-Menu-GR' 8038 has 0. WPML guide 'Creating different Elementor templates per language' (October 17, 2024): set Display Conditions on the default-language template, create the secondary-language template and 'Connect with translations'. marakaki.com (WPML 5.1): Novamira flags 10 Greek-titled library posts (e.g. 40753 'κατηγορίες μενού για κινητά', 40742 'Αναζήτηση - Αναδυόμενο παράθυρο', 40757 'Προεπιλεγμένο κιτ') with `type: null`, `library_term: ''`, `type_mismatch: true` — WPML duplicates that lost `_elementor_template_type`; pallada has 2 (4524 loop-item stored under term 'page', 4519 archive under 'page').
